items.title: Adult phenotype of genetically confirmed Dravet syndrome: diagnostic challenges and clinical red flags from a multicenter Polish cohort.
items.abstract: Aim of the study To characterize the clinical phenotype of adults with clinically diagnosed and genetically confirmed Dravet syndrome (DS), with particular emphasis on seizure evolution, cognitive and motor impairment, and diagnostic delay. Clinical rationale for the study An increasing number of individuals with DS survive into adulthood and require long-term neurological care. However, the adult phenotype differs from the classical childhood presentation and remains underrecognized in adult neurological practice. Recognition of an age-evolving seizure phenotype, together with intellectual disability, gait and postural abnormalities, and extrapyramidal features, may provide important diagnostic clues and prompt molecular testing in previously undiagnosed adults. Material and methods We conducted a multicenter retrospective case series of nine adults (six females and three males) fulfilling clinical diagnostic criteria for DS and carrying a pathogenic or likely pathogenic SCN1A variant. Clinical data were obtained from medical records, neurological examinations, seizure diaries, and psychological assessments performed as part of routine care. Seizure history and evolution, status epilepticus, cognitive and communication impairment, motor phenotype, and treatment history were analyzed. Results The mean age at evaluation was 27.8 years (range 21-37 years). Seizure onset occurred at a mean age of 6 months, whereas the mean age at molecular diagnosis was 13.2 years, corresponding to a mean diagnostic delay of 12.7 years. Febrile seizures occurred in eight of nine patients and persisted beyond the age of 18 years in three. Generalized tonic-clonic seizures persisted into adulthood in all patients, whereas status epilepticus occurred after the age of 18 years in only one. Intellectual disability was present in all patients and was severe or profound in six; communication impairment was observed in eight. Motor abnormalities were prominent, including gait impairment (9/9), ataxia (8/9), postural abnormalities (8/9), bradykinesia (5/9), hypomimia (5/9), and parkinsonian features (3/9). All patients had been exposed to sodium channel-blocking antiseizure medications before molecular diagnosis, with seizure worsening documented in eight of nine patients. Conclusions and clinical implications The adult phenotype of DS combines persistent drug-resistant epilepsy with intellectual and communication impairment and prominent motor dysfunction. Although generalized tonic-clonic seizures may persist, other features of the epileptic phenotype, particularly status epilepticus, become less prominent with age. Gait, postural, cerebellar, and extrapyramidal abnormalities may provide important diagnostic clues in adults with infantile-onset epilepsy and intellectual disability. Recognition of this age-evolving phenotype may facilitate molecular diagnosis and support syndrome-specific management in adult neurological practice.

items.title: Cave ecosystems as drivers of viral diversity, endemism, and ecological function at a global scale
items.abstract: Caves are subterranean ecosystems that host diverse microbial communities involved in key biogeochemical processes. Yet, the diversity and ecological roles of viruses within these systems remain poorly understood. Here, we analyzed metagenomic data collected from 30 globally distributed cave systems, identifying 8,176 viral operational taxonomic units (≥ 10kb size) that have little representation within a recent database of environmental viruses. In addition, cave-specific environmental fingerprints are shown to be a strong driver of viral distribution, reflected in a high degree of endemism both within and across cave systems. Viral-host associations suggest that viruses are primarily associated with Pseudomonadota and Actinomycetota lineages, the most abundant groups across all samples and involved in diverse carbon, sulfur, and nitrogen metabolisms. The high proportion of lytic viruses targeting these groups suggests strong top-down viral control, with virus-mediated microbial turnover likely contributing to organic matter recycling. This is further supported by lytic viruses carrying the majority of auxiliary metabolic genes (AMGs), with functions related to enhancing viral progeny production by increasing resource availability and reallocating cellular resources toward viral replication. In this study, we highlight how cave environments shape viral ecology and unveil a still yet unknown component of the subsurface virosphere.

items.title: Identifying the metacommunity scale reconciles deterministic and stochastic assembly in a natural mainland–island microbial system
items.abstract: Disentangling the deterministic and stochastic processes that shape microbial communities remains a central challenge in microbial ecology. The framework proposed by Vellend---selection, drift, dispersal and speciation---offers a natural conceptual scaffold, but testing these processes in natural communities is technically demanding, and analyses are often narrowed to a single process, which can lead to seemingly contradictory conclusions. Here we illustrate the promise and the pitfalls of a comprehensive application of this framework by re-analysing a temporally resolved dataset of microbial communities inhabiting water-filled tree-holes at the base of a single beech tree, a natural mainland--island system for which both neutral assembly and strong selection have been reported. We show that these views are compatible once unsupervised compositional clustering is used to identify the scale at which assembly processes should be tested. Treating each compositional cluster as a set of local communities that receive immigrants from a distinct metacommunity, we applied neutral, phylogenetic and null-model tests of selection and dispersal, metagenomic prediction and association inference. Selection operated chiefly as environmental filtering at the metacommunity level, associated with tree-hole size and shape, whereas local communities were statistically indistinguishable from stochastic assembly. Variable selection and dispersal limitation acted between metacommunities, whereas homogenizing dispersal prevailed within them. Association networks recapitulated metacommunity structure, indicating that co-occurrence largely reflects shared environment rather than interactions. In summary, performing some analyses while excluding others leads to misleading conclusions: comprehensive analyses and identifying the intrinsic scale in which selection may operate are needed to move beyond the deterministic--stochastic dichotomy.

items.title: Major Limitations on the Use of the UK Centre for Ecology & Hydrology Land Cover Map to Interpret Habitat Partitioning at the Holy Loch, Argyll, Scotland
items.abstract: This short communication critiques the uncritical reliance on the UK Centre for Ecology & Hydrology (UKCEH) Land Cover Map for fine-scale habitat analysis, using the head of the Holy Loch, Argyll, Scotland, as a case study. Ground-truthing reveals nine major categorical and spectral deviations—including misclassified algal mats, wild radish, and complex estuarine dynamics. By highlighting these severe remote sensing artifacts in a paraglacially inherited, dynamic system, this paper establishes a foundational methodological baseline for upcoming companion studies detailing the fully mapped vegetation, structural investigations, and historical-geology of the Holy Loch

items.title: 2',3'-Cyclic nucleotide monophosphates modulate quorum sensing and virulence in Ralstonia solanacearum via multiple signaling pathways.
items.abstract: It has been demonstrated that 2',3'-cGMP modulates the physiology of Ralstonia solanacearum by inhibiting the regulatory activity of the transcriptional regulator RSp0980. Here, we report that 2',3'-cyclic nucleotide monophosphates (2',3'-cNMPs), including 2',3'-cAMP, 2',3'-cGMP, 2',3'-cCMP, and 2',3'-cUMP, which are synthesized by the RNase T1 homolog RSc2766, play a critical role in the modulation of R. solanacearum virulence through another receptor. 2',3'-cNMPs specifically bind to the LysR-type transcriptional regulator RSc2761 and thus increase the regulatory activity of RSc2761 on the transcription of target genes. Intriguingly, the 2',3'-cNMP-RSc2761 signaling system also regulates the transcription of phcA , which encodes the master regulator of the quorum-sensing (QS) network, and subsequently controls the production of QS signals and virulence in R. solanacearum . Together, our work provides new insights into the regulatory mechanisms of 2',3'-cNMPs through multiple signaling pathways, suggesting that R. solanacearum utilizes a complex and precise signaling network to control its pathogenicity.IMPORTANCE Ralstonia solanacearum is a plant pathogen that causes destructive bacterial wilt and leads to severe crop losses worldwide. This study deciphers the synthetic pathway of the intracellular second messengers 2',3'-cNMPs in R. solanacearum . In addition, we demonstrate that 2',3'-cNMPs specifically act on the transcriptional regulator RSc2761, which in turn controls the pathogenicity of R. solanacearum by regulating the transcription of phcA and other target genes. Our findings unveil a novel 2',3'-cNMP-mediated pathogenicity regulatory pathway in R. solanacearum and provide potential targets for the control of bacterial wilt disease.

items.title: Out of the cradle: secondary expansion from a source lake is associated with loss of morphological distinctiveness in endemic Kamchatkan charrs (Salvelinus).
items.abstract: The contribution of postglacial adaptive radiations to regional freshwater fish biodiversity remains debated. To test whether such radiations can give rise to new populations in neighboring ecosystems, we reconstructed the evolutionary history of the endemic Salvelinus malma assemblage of Lake Kronotskoe (Kamchatka). We traced the dispersal of endemic lineages from the lake into adjacent basins and quantified morphological divergence between lacustrine charrs and their derived populations. Using SNPs from SLAF-seq loci, we analyzed phylogeny, genetic differentiation, contemporary hybridization and historical gene flow among eleven charr groups, and complemented these analyses with morphometric comparisons. Our results indicate that the lacustrine-addfluvial predatory and benthivorous lineages of the Lake Kronotskoe basin colonized small peripheral waterbodies via temporary riverbed connections during the Holocene. These lineages also continue to disperse downstream from the lake, which is isolated by rapids, and hybridize with anadromous S. malma. These migrations have given rise to three new isolated populations and one hybrid anadromous population. Morphological evolution in the derived populations was independent of their phylogenetic history and converged on a generalized morphology typical of pelagic or riverine fish. Thus, postglacial expansion of adaptive morphs from the source lake enhances regional diversity, while migrants can rapidly lose ancestral adaptive traits in new habitats.

items.title: Persistence revisited: Partitioning rather than media-specific reactivity dominates persistence in the environment.
items.abstract: Current regulation identifies environmentally persistent chemicals often using thresholds defined for single-media half-lives. This approach ignores the large and even dominating impact of multimedia partitioning on the (bio)availability of compounds that undergo degradation, and accordingly may underestimate the chemical lifetimes by orders of magnitude. This is demonstrated through comparing chemical half-lives in water with overall persistence (Pov) in terms of environmental lifetimes calculated through a steady-state multimedia mass-balance model. While Pov depends on the entrance compartment, Stroebe's τE, the temporal-remote-state expected environmental lifetime, is less sensitive to the initial entry compartment. Thus, τE appears most suited for the prediction of chemical persistence. In this study, a stepwise Ordinary Least Squares (OLS) regression analysis showed that only four chemical properties, log values of Kow (hydrophobicity), kdeg,w and kdeg,a (degradation rate constants in water and air, respectively), and Pv (vapour pressure), are sufficient to estimate τE. But this analysis also showed non-linear error patterns despite overall good statistics, unraveling peculiarities of the non-linear log-log dependence of τE on compound properties. A machine-learning k nearest neighbors (kNN) regression model operating in the property space yields even more accurate and linear results. Application to existing data sets demonstrates the usefulness of this approach. In particular, it shows that the reduction of bioavailability due to multimedia partitioning may cause compounds classified as "readily biodegradable" to be identified as persistent when they have sufficiently high hydrophobicity (e.g. phenanthrene with log Kow = 4.5: lifetime > 30 years). The developed tools (SimpleRisk4REACH enabling τE calculation through Stroebe's mathematical procedure; kNN regression model for τE prediction) are made available to the public.

items.title: Evolutionary rewiring of the Drosophila melanogaster accessory gland by the RNA-binding protein gene, Marf1.
items.abstract: Gene expression evolution can take several forms, including changes in isoform usage, transcript abundance, and patterns of tissue- or cell type-specific expression. Using comparative and population-level transcriptomic analyses in the melanogaster subgroup of Drosophila, we previously documented the gain of Marf1 expression in the main cells of the D. melanogaster accessory gland, which produces most of the seminal fluid proteins in the species. Marf1, an RNA-binding protein, is ovary biased in the female and accessory gland biased in the male. It is required for female fertility, but its potential male functions are unknown. We investigated the possible male function of this gene using genetic, genomic, transcriptomic, and organismal analyses. We found that despite its very young expression phenotype in the male accessory gland, Marf1 has become integrated into the accessory gland gene regulatory network. We also found that its novel accessory gland expression is correlated with a fixed transposon fragment that is also associated with species-specific open chromatin in the accessory gland. Because Marf1 is located in the pericentromeric region of chromosome 2, which is riddled with repetitive DNA and characterized by low recombination rates and strong effects of linked selection, we hypothesize that novel accessory gland expression of this gene was deleterious and an incidental effect of centromeric hitchhiking effects, followed by compensation and integration of this gene into a novel gene regulatory network in the D. melanogaster accessory gland.

items.title: Improving the ecotoxicity impact assessment methodology for chemical mixtures: a case study on antibiotics.
items.abstract: When chemicals such as antibiotics are released into the environment, they can harm aquatic species by interfering with their growth, reproduction, and other biological processes. To protect aquatic wildlife, a good understanding of the ecotoxicity impact of chemical mixtures on freshwater ecosystems is required. Traditional ecotoxicity models used in life cycle assessment, such as USEtox, simply add up the impact of all individual substances and ignore interactive mixture effects that may occur between substances. This paper aims to present a novel methodology to quantify the freshwater ecotoxicity impact of chemical mixtures on aquatic species. For this purpose, concentration addition was applied at species level to develop an impact assessment model that is theoretically more consistent with the original concentration addition concept. Moreover, a species impact distribution was introduced to quantify the overall freshwater ecotoxicity impact. Binary interactions were also taken into account based on the cumulative risk assessment framework of the United States Environmental Protection Agency (US EPA). A Swiss antibiotic-emitting hospital was selected as a case study to demonstrate this new approach. When binary interactions are not included, the traditional freshwater ecotoxicity model overestimates the impact of antibiotic mixtures on freshwater ecotoxicity. For instance, for the norfloxacin-erythromycin mixture, the impact is 23% lower using the novel method compared to the traditional method. When binary interactions are included into the novel method, a 4% decrease in the freshwater ecotoxicity impact is found for the norfloxacin-ciprofloxacin mixture, while a 4% increase is found for a norfloxacin-erythromycin mixture. A sensitivity analysis shows that the calculated environmental impact can strongly (up to 400%) vary when interaction parameters are changed.

items.title: Accelerating plastic pollution mitigation in Vietnam: A circular economy policy and implementation roadmap.
items.abstract: Plastic pollution poses significant environmental and public health risks in Vietnam, driven by rising consumption and inadequate waste management. As one of the leading contributors to marine plastic leakage, the country faces challenges linked to linear economic practices and weak recycling systems. This study applies a structured narrative review protocol to synthesize evidence from policy, scientific, and institutional sources in the manuscript corpus. The analysis examines circular economy strategies and evaluates them using a comparative prioritization framework based on impact potential, implementation feasibility, and time-to-effect. The article identifies high-priority interventions for Vietnam (extended producer responsibility enforcement, source segregation, and reuse systems), highlights major barriers (fragmented governance, informal-system exclusion, and weak data systems), and proposes an actionable research and policy agenda for the transition to a circular plastics economy.

items.title: Neutral thorium(IV)-di-palladium(II)-cacodylate-bridged-complex.
items.abstract: Herein, we report on the synthesis and structural characterization of a neutral palladium(II)-cacodylate-bridged complex containing a thorium(IV) ion and cacodylate capping groups, [Th IV PdII2{(CH 3 ) 2 AsO 2 } 8 ] (1). Complex 1 was synthesized using a simple one-pot technique in aqueous medium at pH 7. The thorium ion is sandwiched by two palladium(II) ions creating a unique Pd II ⋯Th IV ⋯Pd II core, which is bridged by eight cacodylate ligands.

items.title: Phenotypic Integration at a Small Geographic Scale: Parallel Shifts in Morphology, Signaling, Behavior, and Hormones in the Italian Wall Lizard.
items.abstract: Selection often acts on trait integration across multiple organizational levels, producing parallel shifts in suites of traits that determine performance. Understanding how selective pressures generate these coordinated shifts over fine geographic scales is central to evolutionary and functional ecology. Using mainland and islet populations of the Italian wall lizard under similar macroclimatic conditions, we tested whether divergence in body size, color signaling, and melanism parallels shifts in intraspecific aggression, sociability, and baseline and stress-induced steroid hormone levels. Mainland lizards were larger and exhibited stronger sexual dimorphism, with males possessing higher body condition than islet males. Lateral head coloration was prevalent and conspicuous on the mainland, while islet lizards showed higher melanism on head and flank and more blue ocelli on flank scales. These characteristics matched behavior: islet males showed social indifference and no aggression, while mainland males exhibited aggression and showed stronger attraction to conspecifics. Endocrine profiles paralleled these shifts: mainland males had higher baseline testosterone, whereas islet males had higher baseline corticosterone. Stress-induced levels of either hormone did not differ between populations. These shifts indicate divergence in an integrated functional phenotype, consistent with alternative strategies along an axis of competitive investment: a mainland "proactive territorial strategy" (large size, conspicuous head coloration, aggression, and high baseline testosterone) versus an islet "tolerance strategy" (smaller size, increased melanism and blue ocelli, reduced aggression, and high baseline corticosterone). By combining behavioral ecology, endocrinology, and functional morphology, we provide a comprehensive, mechanistic framework for understanding phenotypic divergence at small geographical scale.

items.title: The politics of stasis and change: The motivational roots of conservatism in party platforms and citizens' own words
items.abstract: A central question in political psychology concerns the motivational roots of ideological differences between left and right. A common approach explains right-wing thinking as reflecting heightened sensitivity to threat and a motivation to protect the status quo. We argue that this approach rests on an incomplete model of goals, which overlooks the motive to conserve. Building on the ternary goal model, we examine whether the right is better characterized by maintenance (sustaining a valued present) than by protection (responding to threats). Using a multilingual classifier validated on human-rated statements, we measured goals in a top-down manner, in 892 party platforms from 11 countries, and bottom-up, in the goals spontaneously reported by 2,333 citizens in six countries and in citizens’ support for platform statements that differed in goal orientation. Top-down, right-wing parties were more maintenance-oriented than left-wing parties, and in recent decades less progress-oriented. Protection orientation did not differ by side but was higher in opposition and at the ideological margins. Bottom-up, citizens showed a similar pattern. Progress orientation was strongest on the left. Maintenance orientation followed a curve that peaked among moderate conservatives. Its linear rise with conservatism was suppressed by institutional trust, which was lower on the right. In support ratings, progress-oriented statements appealed more to the left and maintenance-oriented statements more to the right, whereas protection-oriented statements favored neither. The left–right divide thus sets two constructive aims – to progress and to maintain – against each other, while protection marks those in opposition and at the margins.

items.title: The Effectiveness of Specialized Behavioral Psychology-Based Training in Reducing Cyberloafing among Perioperative Nurses
items.abstract: Abstract Introduction: Cyberloafing, defined as the non-work-related use of the Internet during working hours, can negatively impact the productivity of perioperative nurses and patient safety. The high psychological stress and the need for sustained concentration in surgical environments underscore the importance of targeted interventions to reduce this behavior. Behavioral psychology-based training, by strengthening self-control and time management skills, is one of the novel approaches in this field. Aim: To evaluate the effectiveness of specialized behavioral psychology-based training in reducing various cyberloafing behaviors among perioperative nurses in educational–therapeutic hospitals in Ilam Province. Methods: This quasi-experimental study with a pre-test–post-test control group design was conducted in 2025 on 40 perioperative nurses (20 in the experimental group and 20 in the control group) selected through simple random sampling. Data were collected using the standard Cyberloafing Questionnaire, which includes four subscales: “personal messaging/email,” “social networks,” “online shopping and financial activities,” and “online entertainment/multimedia.” The Cronbach’s alpha of the Persian version was 0.87. The intervention consisted of four 90-minute behavioral psychology-based training sessions over two weeks for the experimental group. Data were analyzed using paired t-test, independent t-test, and Cohen’s d effect size (α = 0.05). items.title: Leading System Transformation Through a Quality Standard Development Process for the Child and Youth Mental Health and Addictions Sector.
items.abstract: Quality standards can improve service quality, accountability, and equity. Their development in Community-based Child and Youth Mental Health and Addictions (CYMHA) settings requires sector-specific guidance and processes. Few standards are tailored to Ontario's CYMHA sector, and research on developing such standards remains scarce. This article presents the development, implementation, and evaluation of the Knowledge Institute on Child and Youth Mental Health and Addictions (KI) Standard Development Process (SDP) for quality standards in the CYMHA sector. Drawing on experience developing standards and reviewing other approaches, the KI formalized a methodology that foregrounds collaboration with youth, families, service providers, and system leaders. The process follows four phases-scoping, drafting, mobilizing, and maintaining-and integrates implementation science, evaluation, and meaningful engagement. This article details the SDP development and pilot. It highlights the value of a replicable, evidence-informed approach and multi-partner collaboration in developing relevant, meaningful, standards and achieving system-wide implementation.

items.title: Seasonal Symptoms Are Related to Rumination and Habitual Negative Thinking.
items.abstract: Seasonal affective disorder (SAD) is a mood disorder with a seasonal pattern that emerges usually in the winter and remits in summer. In the present study, we aimed to investigate the role of rumination and habits of negative thinking as vulnerability factors in elevated sensitivity to seasons and the potential change of these factors over seasons. A total of 185 participants completed a digital survey about seasonal patterns (SPAQ), ruminative response style (RRS), habits of negative thinking (HINT), and symptoms of depression (PHQ-9); 169 participated in a mood induction task, and 133 were followed up longitudinally with assessments in summer and winter. SPAQ scores correlated significantly with PHQ-9 scores, RRS scores, and HINT scores (all p < 0.001). Participants with a SAD diagnosis and elevated seasonal symptoms differed significantly on these scales from people with low seasonal symptoms. Longitudinal analysis revealed that only participants with a SAD diagnosis showed significant increases in their depression scores from summer to winter, while group differences on all other scales did not change significantly across seasons. In a mood induction task, we found baseline differences in mood and rumination, but no increased propensity of experiencing sad mood or state rumination among individuals with a SAD diagnosis or elevated seasonal symptoms as compared to participants with low levels of seasonal symptoms. Psychological factors such as rumination and its habitual features might be present all year round as a trait-like cognitive vulnerability, contributing to the development of seasonal symptoms and SAD.

items.title: Stability and change in loneliness among older Europeans: a trait-state-occasion analysis of SHARE data.
items.abstract: Background Loneliness in later life is a prevalent psychological experience that reflects both stable individual differences and changing social circumstances, yet little is known about the relative contribution of these components over time. The aims are: a) to partition the variance of loneliness into trait vs. occasion (state); and b) to accommodate covariates related to social contact (received and given help). Method Data comes from three waves of the Survey of Health, Aging and Retirement in Europe. Loneliness was measured with UCLA-R Scale. Results The trait component accounted for approximately 60% of the latent variance, whereas the occasion component accounted for approximately 40%. The TSO model was extended to include covariates. Received help was positively associated with trait-like loneliness, whereas given help was negatively associated with it. Associations with occasion-specific components were generally weaker and mostly non-significant, with two statistically significant exceptions. Conclusions Most of the loneliness seems to be trait-like. The time-varying loneliness was smaller in size, but relevant. Helping exchanges were more consistently associated with the stable component of loneliness than with occasion-specific variability.

items.title: Implementing LGBTQ+ Inclusive Mental Health Care Into Practice: Barriers and Facilitators in an Australian Local Health Network.
items.abstract: Mapping implicit barriers to and facilitators of care in ways that are sensitive to LGBTQ+ people's needs within health systems is key to improving LGBTQ+ mental health care. We conducted such a mapping within an Australian local health network's mental health services ("the Network"). Ethnographic fieldwork (in which we captured researcher impressions of the service-sites and the views of staff), was analyzed using reflexive thematic analysis. To help us more effectively evidence and target findings specific to actors within different levels of the Network, we further broke down themes and subthemes using the five domains of the i-PARIHS framework- Innovation, Recipients, Local Context, Organisational Context , and the Outer Context . Two primary themes were developed: 1) affective responses to the intended change, including resistance to change, embarrassment about current inadequate practices , and a desire for change ; and 2) facilitators of pathways to change, including means of leveraging existing resources, contextual safety signals , and participants voicing a call for knowing what to do . The findings suggest clear barriers to improving LGBTQ+ inclusivity alongside goodwill to support change. Our findings and novel usage of the i-PARIHS framework show promising applicability to other LGBTQ+ mental health-care equity settings.

items.title: Comparing multivariate cognitive change in unimpaired older adults to those with questionable impairment or mild dementia: a NACC study.
items.abstract: Introduction We explored how frequently unimpaired older adults show declines across multiple cognitive measures and examined the extent to which their rates of multivariate cognitive change compared to older adults with questionable impairment or mild dementia. Method Two-year change scores were calculated for 1208 participants in the National Alzheimer's Coordinating Center (NACC) database. The number of declines in performance falling below the 5 th percentile in the natural distribution of change scores (the total change count) among the unimpaired participants ( n = 742) was compared to those with questionable impairment ( n = 389) and those with mild dementia ( n = 77). Results Only 9.9% of the cognitively unimpaired participants obtained two or more significant declines in performance, compared to 27.5% of the questionably impaired participants and 49.4% of those with mild dementia. The total change count demonstrated significant discriminative ability for distinguishing between cognitively unimpaired participants and those with questionable impairment (AUC = .621) or mild dementia (AUC = .759). The threshold of two or more declines maintained high specificity (90.1%) for identifying atypical cognitive decline. In a multinomial logistic regression, a change count of two or more was a robust predictor of both questionable impairment (OR = 3.47) and mild dementia (OR = 8.55), beyond the effects of demographic covariates (age, gender, education, race/ethnicity). Conclusions Less than one tenth of cognitively unimpaired older adults show two or more significant declines in their performance on 13 measures from the NACC UDS 3.0 neuropsychological test battery. Individuals who exhibit two or more significant declines in their raw scores across this battery are likely experiencing atypical cognitive decline. Establishing longitudinal base rates of cognitive change across a test battery offers a viable, empirically grounded approach to identifying progression along the dementia continuum.

items.title: Ideal sleep duration as a potential explanation of the bimodal chronotype: An exploratory study.
items.abstract: Regarding circadian typology, the existence of a fourth category, the bimodal types, was previously proposed. Bimodal types would be those answering some questions as morning types, while others as evening types, resulting in a different sleep-wake cycle compared to intermediate types. The aim of this study was to further explore the plausibility of this new circadian typology category, attempting to determine whether it qualifies as a genuinely new category of individuals or merely a byproduct of another individual difference, namely ideal sleep duration. To this end, we reanalyzed data previously collected from 1583 children and adolescents (817 females, mean age of 13.13 ± 1.96) and 2115 adults (1144 females, mean age of 44.50 ± 5.64) who completed the Morningness-Eveningness Questionnaire for Children and Adolescents (MEQ-CA) and the MEQ, respectively. The open-ended questions on the ideal bedtime and get-up time were used to compute the ideal total sleep time that was later grouped into three categories: short- (≤6 hours), medium- (6 < x < 12 hours), and long sleepers (≥12 hours). In children and adolescents, bimodal types were overrepresented in both short and long sleepers and underrepresented among medium sleepers; separately considering the gender variable, the same pattern of results was detected in males only. Regarding adults, an overrepresentation of bimodal types was observed among long sleepers and their underrepresentation among medium sleepers; this same distribution was replicated only in males. It seems that the suggested fourth category of circadian typology, that of bimodal types, may be considered as a byproduct of the individual difference in ideal sleep duration.

items.title: "Woven into the fabric of life": young adults' normalisation of stress in contemporary Aotearoa.
items.abstract: Objective This research explored 'lay' or everyday sense-making of young adults in Aotearoa New Zealand around stress. Stress has become a widely understood and commonly experienced phenomenon, with associated physical and mental health consequences. Contemporary understandings around stress are produced by and within context. Currently Aotearoa is dominated by neoliberal ideology, and an acceptance of 'hustle culture', with social media and digital technology increasingly embedded in daily life. Methods and measures We generated data using nine focus groups (online and in person), with 29 young adults (mean age 27), recruited through a range of strategies. Most participants identified as Pākehā or NZ European (20), two as Indian, and the remaining each identified as different ethnicities, including one as Māori. Taking a critical, social constructionist approach, we used reflexive thematic analysis to develop patterns in how stress is made sense of by young adults. Results: The analysis we report here focuses on the normalisation of stress. This analytic interpretation was conveyed through four themes: the pervasiveness of stress; (modern) life is stressful; but stress is the way you win; and stress as poison, and as medicine. Conclusions Stress was framed as a normal, natural, and universal experience, accepted as part of everyday life, and even desirable within the neoliberal contemporary context.

items.title: The Indonesian General Population's Perception of Help-Seeking in Mental Healthcare: A Survey Study.
items.abstract: Background Indonesia struggles with low help-seeking rates, limited mental health literacy, treatment gaps, stigma, and cultural beliefs, underscoring the need to understand public perceptions for better service acceptance for mental health problems. We aim to examine how mental health literacy and self-stigma of seeking help relate to attitudes toward seeking professional psychological help, with specific attention to the role of clinical psychologists. Methods Three hundred nine participants from the general population in three Indonesian regions completed a survey between June and August 2023. The survey included seven case vignettes of mental disorders, followed by questions on their perceived severity, causes, and sources of help. Additional measures assessed knowledge about clinical psychologists, self-stigma of seeking help, and help-seeking attitudes. Data analysis involved correlations, ANOVAs, and multiple regression, whereas qualitative thematic analysis was conducted on open-ended responses. Results Participants perceived most mental health issues as moderate to severe. Biological and intrapersonal factors were commonly cited as causes, with friends, family, and clinical psychologists seen as the most helpful sources. Although participants reported prior experience and knowledge about clinical psychologists, familiarity varied. Regression analysis showed that perceived severity of mental health problems and knowledge of clinical psychologists were positively associated with attitudes toward seeking help, while self-stigma was negatively associated with these attitudes, explaining 24% of the variance. Conclusion Mental health literacy seemed to be on an adequate level, and family and friends were rated as the most helpful sources, followed by clinical psychologists. Greater perceived severity of mental health problems and more knowledge of the clinical psychologist's role were associated with more favorable attitudes toward seeking professional psychological help, whereas higher self-stigma of seeking help and stronger reliance on informal support were associated with less favorable attitudes.

items.title: Breaking the cycle of urban rat infestations: An integrative strategy incorporating knowledge, goals and risks of citizens, pest professionals, public health policymakers and researchers
items.abstract: Wicked problems (WPs) involve multiple stakeholders with conflicting incentives and fragmented knowledge, while attempts to solve one part of a problem create new problems elsewhere. Global urban rodent infestations are the epitome of generational WPs, remaining deeply rooted for centuries. Rising demand for rodent control across 195 countries, along with insurance claims and public complaint data, suggests worsening trends. Rodents contribute to an estimated 400 million rodent-related zoonoses per annum. Additionally, they contaminate foods and cause building fires, disabled vehicles, and structural damage. Annual costs may reach US$40–60 billion and could escalate with climate change and urbanization. Building off examples from mosquito and wastewater surveillance, as well as the few promising rat-control programs, we construct a model for addressing this issue. WPs are resolved by identifying stakeholders and acknowledging their incentive:risk profiles. We name the four most common stakeholders: property owners, pest management professionals (PMPs), researchers and public health agencies, then map their profiles and identify how they impede one another’s progress. For instance, PMPs possess detailed knowledge of local infestations but have little incentive to share proprietary data or access to potential research sites. In a collaborative relationship, they could provide site access to researchers while being incentivized by client heat maps and science-validated control tools. This can facilitate cross-platform data sharing. Researchers could then better support public health agencies with ecological and pathogen data, helping shift responses from enforcement toward education and prevention. Property owners benefit from reduced risks of stigma, fines, illness, and property damage. Sometimes the best science is not a new technology or tool, but recognition of stakeholder interests and a commitment to exchanges that benefit each group without increasing its risks. Breaking knowledge silos and aligning incentives may allow even the most entrenched urban rodent problems to be addressed. Our framework shows that effective One Health approaches to urban rodent infestations depend on aligning stakeholder incentive: risk profiles.

items.title: Correcting misconceptions and shaping preferences about energy with reinforcement learning
items.abstract: Addressing the climate crisis requires citizens to make informed choices about sustainable energy policy, yet public debates are often shaped by inaccurate beliefs about the environmental and health impacts of different energy sources. Misconceptions about key features of energy sources, such as their greenhouse gas emissions, mortality rates, and contribution to electricity production, are particularly dangerous for this debate, as they risk systematically distorting public support for effective decarbonisation strategies. Here we investigate whether a brief reinforcement‑based intervention can correct such misconceptions and influence societal investment preferences. Across seven countries, we reveal systematic misbeliefs, such as overestimating the emissions and mortality of nuclear power and under‑estimating the mortality of biomass, which were corrected by our intervention across all features and countries. Furthermore, correcting beliefs led to shifts in preferences towards objectively cleaner and safer energy mixes, and these changes were consistent across countries. Follow‑up assessments indicated that most of our intervention’s effects were detectable after 14 weeks. These results demonstrate a three‑step actionable pathway, from behavioural feedback, through belief correction, to preference change, and suggest that short, reinforcement‑based interventions could be a scalable tool for improving public decision‑making in climate policy and other domains where misconceptions pollute the debate.

items.title: The Unseen Shift: A Phenomenological Study of Mothering Experiences in Nurses During COVID-19
items.abstract: Abstract Background Infectious disease outbreaks and pandemics constitute a major global public health challenge, exerting profound adverse effects on healthcare workers who are mothers and on their children. This study aimed to describe and interpret the lived experiences of mothering among nurses caring for young children during the COVID-19 pandemic. Methods This qualitative hermeneutic phenomenological study explored the lived experiences of 12 female nurses caring for infants or toddlers, purposively recruited in 2025 from hospitals affiliated with Ardabil University of Medical Sciences in Iran. Individual semi-structured interviews (40–60 minutes each) were conducted by the principal investigator via telephone or videoconference to explore participants' experiences of caring for young children during the COVID-19 pandemic. Data collection continued until saturation was reached. Data were analyzed using Diekelmann's hermeneutic phenomenological method. Results Thematic analysis of the qualitative data revealed four main themes: 1) role conflict and existential exhaustion, (2) motherhood behind masks and infection control measures, (3) social isolation and the collapse of support networks, and (4) the lifeworld of fear, guilt, and resilience. Conclusions The findings revealed that participating nurses experienced motherhood through the formidable barriers of alcohol-based disinfectants, double-layered masks, hospital corridors, and isolation rooms, all while enduring profound social isolation. Despite these overwhelming challenges, they demonstrated remarkable self-sacrifice and resilience, persistently striving to safeguard their families' health and well-being.

items.title: Similarity Theory of Epidemic Waves: From Universal Dynamics to Peak Hospitalization
items.abstract: Abstract During infectious disease outbreaks, healthcare managers require rapid tools to project peak hospital workloads without heavy computer simulations. This paper introduces a simple mathematical method that treats epidemic waves as natural, self-limiting events. By converting absolute case numbers into relative percentages, our framework completely removes structural differences associated with regional geography and population size. We demonstrate that the universal shape of a wave is independently governed by only two driving forces: the biological spreading power of the virus and the behavioural contact reduction rate of the population. Under this transformation, complex disease trajectories from highly diverse regions flatten and merge symmetrically into a single, predictable pattern. Combining public behaviour metrics with hospital discharge rates yields a straightforward formula to calculate peak bed demand. The results prove a major operational asymmetry: public contact reduction provides significantly higher immediate protection for hospitals during acute growth phases than accelerating vaccine distribution. This approach allows health authorities to monitor a small pilot group and scale the findings to project national capacity needs in real time.

items.title: Do Traffic Congestion Indicators Improve PM2.5 Forecasting? Evidence from Machine Learning Models in Kampala
items.abstract: Abstract Air pollution remains a major environmental and public health challenge in Kampala, Uganda, where PM 2.5 concentrations frequently exceed World Health Organization (WHO) guidelines values. Although traffic emissions are widely recognized as contributors to urban air pollution, limited empirical evidence exists on whether traffic-congestion indicators improve PM 2.5 forecasting beyond information provided by meteorological and temporal variables. This study evaluated the predictive contribution of traffic-congestion indicators to PM 2.5 using machine learning models. PM 2.5 , temperature, and humidity observations were obtained from the AirQo monitoring network, while traffic data were collected along the Jinja Road transport using the Google Routes API. After preprocessing and temporal synchronization, a dataset consisting of 696 hourly observations was used to implement Random Forest and HistGradientBoosting forecasting models. Environmental baseline models were compared with traffic-enhanced models incorporating mean speed, travel duration, and Traffic Performance Index (TPI). Model performance was evaluated using Mean Absolute Error (MAE), Root Mean Squared Error (RMSE), and the coefficient of determination (R 2 ). Results showed that the best environmental baseline model, HistGradientBoosting, achieved superior performance (MAE = 15.28, RMSE = 21.40, R 2 = 0.5752) compared with the best traffic-enhanced model (MAE = 23.16, RMSE = 31.70, R 2 = 0.4753). Correlation and feature-importance analysis further indicated that traffic-congestion indicators exhibited weak relationships with PM2.5 concentrations and contributed substantially to less predictive information than temporal and meteorological variables. An additional analysis incorporating lagged PM 2.5 variables achieved the highest explanatory performance (R 2 = 0.6245), highlighting the importance of historical pollution measurements in forecasting future PM 2.5 concentrations. The findings suggest that, within the study context, corridor-level congestion indicators provided limited incremental forecasting value, while temporal patterns, meteorological conditions, and historical PM 2.5 measurements were more influential predictors. The study contributes empirical evidence for evaluating predictor relevance in machine-learning based air-quality forecasting and provides insights for the design of efficient forecasting systems in rapidly urbanizing cities.

items.title: Time to initiation of Antenatal care and its predictors among pastoral pregnant women in madawalabu district public health facilities, southeastern Ethiopia, 2024: retrospective follow-up study
items.abstract: Abstract Background: Timely initiation of antenatal care within the first trimester is critical for reducing maternal morbidity and mortality through early detection of complications and provision of key preventive interventions. Pastoralist communities, however, face substantial geographic and sociocultural barriers that may delay antennal care initiation, and empirical evidence on these determinants remains limited. Objective: To assess time to initiation of antenatal care and its predictors among pastoral pregnant women in Madawalabu district, southeastern Ethiopia. Methods: A facility‑based retrospective follow‑up study was conducted among 475 pregnant women who received antenatal care services at public health facilities in Madawalabu district in 2024. Participants were selected using systematic random sampling. Data were collected using checklists and structured interviewer‑administered questionnaires, entered into Epi‑Data 4.6.0, and analyzed with Stata 15. Time to first ANC contact was estimated using Kaplan–Meier survival analysis with log‑rank tests. Predictors of antenatal care initiation were identified using Cox proportional hazards regression; model adequacy was assessed using Cox–Snell residuals. Results: The mean survival time to antenatal care initiation was 7.4 months (95% CI: 7.08, 7.76). Earlier initiation was independently associated with higher maternal education (AHR = 1.65; 95% CI: 1.21, 2.25), urban residence (AHR = 1.96; 95% CI: 1.07, 3.59), having received counseling on antenatal care (AHR = 3.17; 95% CI: 1.18, 8.54), and good knowledge of antenatal care (AHR = 1.64; 95% CI: 1.14, 2.36). Longer delays were observed among women from female‑headed households (AHR = 0.46; 95% CI: 0.26, 0.81) and those with no prior exposure to obstetric ultrasound scans (AHR = 0.12; 95% CI: 0.04, 0.32). Conclusion and recommendation: Pregnant women in this pastoralist setting initiate antenatal care substantially later than World Health Organization recommendations. Educational attainment, place of residence, counseling, and antenatal care‑related knowledge were predictors of earlier initiation, whereas female‑headed household status and lack of prior ultrasound exposure contributed to delays. Targeted strategies including strengthening community-based health education tailored to pastoralist livelihoods, improving access in remote areas, expanding counseling services, supporting female‑headed households, and promoting ultrasound use are urgently needed to improve timely antenatal care uptake.

items.title: Towards real-time wastewater pollution tracking: Evaluating the performance of instrumentation-based wastewater pollution proxies in an urban estuary
items.abstract: Abstract Wastewater pollution poses risks to both ecosystem and public health via the introduction of pathogens, excessive nutrients, and chemicals of emerging concern to the aquatic environment. Typical monitoring to alert the public of elevated fecal bacteria levels and potential wastewater pollution relies on discrete water samples and 24-hr culturing of indicator bacteria, which leads to alerts being posted no earlier than 1–2 days after pollution impacts. Discrete sampling can also miss acute wastewater impacts from storms or spills. Therefore, there is interest in real-time proxies to provide earlier public alerts and track wastewater pollution inputs to water bodies at a finer time scale. Emerging proxies include real-time monitoring of dissolved organic fluorescence, particularly tracking fluorescence wavelengths similar to optical brighteners (a component of laundry detergent) and tryptophan (an amino acid) that have been demonstrated to be enriched in wastewater. In this study, we examined the ability of in situ, real-time-capable sensors to predict wastewater-associated fecal indicator bacteria concentrations in the Ala Wai Harbor, Honolulu, HI. A fluorometer measuring “optical brightener” fluorescence and “tryptophan” fluorescence was deployed alongside an existing long-term monitoring sensor package measuring temperature, salinity, turbidity, and chlorophyll-a fluorescence. Discrete bottle samples were analyzed for fecal indicator bacteria, sucralose (a conservative wastewater tracer), nutrients, and 3-D scans of fluorescent dissolved organic matter. A positive correlation was observed between culture-based counts of the fecal indicator bacteria Enterococcus spp. and sucralose, which is found only in human waste, indicating consistent wastewater contamination in the Ala Wai Harbor. Dissolved fluorescence measurements in the wavelengths associated with optical brighteners were found to be the best instrumentation-based predictor of Enterococcus spp. concentrations, alone or in combination with other parameters (R 2 = 0.71–0.72). The best-specified categorical models to predict Enterococcus spp. exceedances of the Hawaiʻi state threshold of 130 colony forming units (CFU) /100 mL included both optical brightener fluorescence and salinity with > 95% sensitivity and ~ 75% specificity. The addition of the optical brightener fluorescence channel doubled the explained variance in fecal indicator bacteria by real-time sensors when compared to the existing suite of temperature, salinity, and turbidity (R 2 =0.36–0.38). Our results demonstrate that real-time measurements of optical brightener fluorescence could provide instantaneous warnings of wastewater spills and elevated fecal bacteria levels in waterways at risk of wastewater pollution, and this data stream could be integrated into existing outflow plume models and forecasts to provide better real-time estimates of water safety for ocean users in the surrounding marine areas.

items.title: Support Systems in Renal Care: A Qualitative Assessment of Patient Perceptions and Their Role in Managing Kidney Failure
items.abstract: Abstract Background Managing kidney failure in Ghana is complicated by high comorbidity rates, restricted treatment access, and catastrophic out-of-pocket expenses. Objective This study qualitatively assessed patient perceptions of available formal, informal, and institutional support systems and their influence on condition management and treatment adherence. Methods Using an interpretive phenomenological design, 15 adults undergoing hemodialysis at a private center in Kumasi and a public hospital in Sunyani were purposively sampled. Semi-structured interviews conducted in Twi were transcribed verbatim and analysed via manual reflexive thematic analysis underpinned by Social Support Theory. Findings: Three major themes emerged: Awareness of Support Systems, Healthcare Treatment and Support, and Family and Social Support. Participants reported a severe informational deficit driving late clinical presentation. Frontline clinicians provided vital emotional and appraisal support, but a breakdown in formal instrumental support due to prohibitive dialysis costs forced an unsustainable reliance on multi-generational family networks. This domestic burden induced severe caregiver fatigue, occasionally causing relational fragmentation or abandonment. Conversely, workplace and religious networks functioned as critical secondary stress buffers. Conclusion Managing kidney failure requires transitioning from fragmented, family-dependent models to integrated institutional frameworks. The National Health Insurance Authority should expand coverage to fully subsidise ancillary medications, decentralise regional renal units, and integrate clinical psychosocial support to safeguard vulnerable patients.

items.title: Researching adaptations in equitable, diverse, and inclusive co-design practice during and beyond the pandemic: innovations in a design research realist synthesis
items.abstract: Abstract Background During the COVID-19 pandemic, public health requirements for physical distancing and restrictions on physical gathering significantly altered how co-design could be conducted in health care contexts, especially negatively affecting projects engaging individuals from marginalized communities. Rapid adaptations were made with varied levels of success. A conventional strategy for understanding these adaptations would have been a review of published literature. However, few detailed accounts had been published at the time, and many co-designers were still actively exploring how to adapt their methods. Objectives This research investigated co-design practices to learn what adaptations were successful in engaging marginalized communities, what adaptations might be applied in other contexts, and what might be sustained post-pandemic. Design The overall research design was a realist synthesis, focusing on what works, for whom, and in what circumstances. An initial framework of co-design principles that contribute to equitable, diverse and inclusive (EDI) participation was developed to structure the analysis of adaptations that were made. However, with changes still underway and many adaptations not published, innovations to realist methods were necessary. In addition to a literature scan, design research approaches (workshops, interviews, a Community of Practice, webinars, a Winter School, and conference presentations) were used to generate data and validate findings iteratively. Setting and participants The data collection and analysis took place mostly online. Design researchers, health researchers and design practitioners from three continents were engaged in the various activities over time. Results Adding design research approaches to the realist synthesis identified many adaptations that would otherwise not have been recorded or noticed. Substantively, there were significant numbers of successful adaptations aligned with four initial EDI principles, and three additional categories of adaptations were identified. Conclusions Adapting realist methods to include design research approaches can be fruitful, especially when the evidence and experience under investigation are actively in development. Many of the adaptations that were made during the pandemic can potentially be carried into post-pandemic co-design practice, increasing opportunities for engagement with individuals from marginalized communities. Disseminating these findings in ways that are useable by co-designers is the next step in this research.

items.title: Physicians Assign Themselves More Responsibility Than the General Population when AI Fails in Healthcare: A Swedish Cross-Sectional Survey
items.abstract: Abstract Background: The integration of Artificial Intelligence (AI) into clinical decision-making creates uncertainty regarding responsibility and accountability when adverse outcomes occur. Despite this, data regarding stakeholder perspectives remain scarce, especially quantitative data comparing physician and public views on responsibility allocation and transparency. This study aims to evaluate and compare how physicians and the general population in Sweden attribute responsibility for negative medical outcomes when AI is used to support healthcare decisions in primary care, as well as their views on the necessity of transparently disclosing AI use to patients. Methods: A nationwide, cross-sectional, mixed-methods survey was conducted in Sweden between February and May 2025. The survey targeted two distinct cohorts (N = 500 per group): licensed physicians under 70 years, sampled from the National Board of Health and Welfare register, and adults aged 18 or older sampled from the Swedish population registry. The survey used case vignettes as background for multiple-choice questions, with complementary open-ended free-text responses. The data was evaluated using comparative statistical analysis and reflexive thematic analysis. Results: Physicians were significantly more likely than the general population to assign responsibility to the physician (92\% vs. 74\%) and to favor a shared responsibility model involving the physician (48\% vs. 35\%). In contrast, the general population more frequently selected non-physician actor combinations (26\% vs. 8\%) and assigned greater responsibility to the patient in a scenario involving direct patient-AI interaction without a physician involved. Neither group broadly assigned responsibility to the AI itself (1.3\% physicians vs. 10\% general population). The reflexive thematic analysis reinforced these results, identifying a shared accountability framework where all actors share responsibility, but where the physician serves as the ultimate safeguard. A majority of the general population (68\%) affirmed the patient's right to always know if AI was used, in contrast to only 23\% of physicians who exhibited a polarised distribution. Conclusion: Respondents endorse a shared responsibility model among actors involved in implementing and using AI for medical decisions. The physician is viewed as the essential human-in-the-loop, bearing ultimate accountability for adverse outcomes of AI-assisted medical decisions according to a vast majority of respondents. Divergent perspectives regarding transparency emphasise the need to clarify informed consent standards for AI deployment in healthcare.

items.title: Factors associated with surgeons’ dual practice in mixed health systems. A hierarchical modelling study from Brazil
items.abstract: Abstract Background Physician dual practice, whereby public doctors engage concomitantly with private healthcare services, is widespread in mixed and fragmented health systems. For surgical services, dual practice may be particularly important because surgeons depend on hospital infrastructure, operating facilities and multidisciplinary teams, while their distribution across sectors can influence the availability, organisation and geographical accessibility of specialist care. Brazil combines a tax-funded universal health system with a large private healthcare sector, creating substantial opportunities for surgeons to work across multiple organisations. We examined employment arrangements among Brazilian surgeons and factors associated with dual practice. Methods We conducted a national cross-sectional survey of 1,544 practising surgeons affiliated with the Colégio Brasileiro de Cirurgiões between September 2024 and February 2025. Respondents were classified as public-only, private-only or dual practitioners. Two hierarchical binary logistic regression models compared private-only and public-only surgeons with dual practitioners, sequentially incorporating personal characteristics, labour-market factors, organisation and characteristics of surgical practice, and psychosocial variables. Results Dual practice was the predominant employment arrangement, reported by 1,092 (70.7%) surgeons, compared with 332 (21.5%) working exclusively in the private sector and 120 (7.8%) exclusively in the public sector.

items.title: Catalysing system reforms in Pakistan’s Healthcare and Health Professions Education: National Stakeholder priorities for strengthening policy and system Governance
items.abstract: Abstract Objective Pakistan has broadened its medical and dental education sphere, yet apprehensions last about undergraduates’ competence, impact of regulation, international acknowledgment of qualifications and retention of the health workforce. This study explored multi stakeholder perspectives on training capacity, quality of education, governance, regulation and acknowledgment of health professions education in Pakistan, and identified prime reforms. Methodology: A qualitative descriptive study was conducted using hybrid focus group discussion held on 4 August 2026 as part of national Health and Education Summit Pakistan (HESP) 2026. Fourteen purposively sampled stakeholders participated in discussion guided by 16 semi structured questions. Data were analysed using Framework Method, and Health Policy Triangle was applied as an interpretive lens. Results Nine themes were identified across three domains. Educational quality and competence : undefined and unenforced competency standards; deficits in clinical training infrastructure; faculty development and continuous quality improvement; and cautious, purpose-specific integration of artificial intelligence. Governance, regulation and recognition : fragmented, input-oriented governance; private-sector representation and public–private imbalance; and international recognition and global alignment. Workforce and equity : equity in workforce planning; and workforce sustainability, security and dignity. Participants identified main barrier to reform is not in an absence of policy but in weak implementation, input based accreditation and poor coordination among regulatory bodies. Conclusion Stakeholders called for a shift from input based to outcome-based accreditation built on a nationally agreed definition of competence, a shared inter agency governance platform, documented clinical supervision and simulation, and workforce protection measures.

items.title: Policy Attention Reconfiguration across Three Generations of Canadian Sport Policy
items.abstract: Abstract Research question: How does policy attention change across successive generations of national sport policy? This study develops the Policy Attention Reconfiguration Model (PARM) to examine how attention to institutional, operational, and normative policy components is reconfigured over time. Research methods: Longitudinal qualitative document analysis compared three generations of Canadian Sport Policy (2002, 2012, and 2025–2035). Hybrid deductive–inductive coding generated 31 analytical nodes across six dimensions and 3,592 coded references. Agreement between the original and reviewed coding versions was assessed using policy-equal, character-level Cohen’s kappa (κ = 0.8256). Results and findings: The three policy generations exhibited overlapping but distinct configurations of policy attention. Governance structures and policy actors received their greatest relative emphasis in CSP1, while policy goals and instruments peaked in CSP2. CSP3 placed greater emphasis on policy discourse and values, alongside increased attention to health, participation, inclusion and equity, marginalised populations, and sport as a public good. Overall, policy attention shifted from system organisation through implementation coordination toward broader public purposes, while established priorities remained present. Implications: PARM demonstrates how continuity in policy components can coexist with changes in their relative emphasis. By connecting policy attention with policy design and sport governance, the framework provides a structured approach for examining how the priorities through which sport systems are organised, implemented, and justified change over time.

items.title: Identification and Characterization of Linear B-Cell Epitopes in Plasmodium falciparum MSP9 Protein for Potential Application in Malaria Serodiagnosis
items.abstract: Background: Malaria remains a major global public health problem, causing millions of cases and thousands of deaths each year. Without an effective antimalarial vaccine, diagnosis remains a key strategy for disease control. However, false-negative results due to the emergence of P. falciparum populations with deletions in the Pfhrp2/3 genes may compromise case management. Thus, this study aimed to identify and characterize linear B-cell epitopes of the MSP9 protein to evaluate new targets for developing high-precision biotechnological tools for malaria diagnosis. Methods: We mapped MSP9 epitopes using a peptide microarray strategy, followed by epitope screening with bioinformatics tools and ELISA validation. Results: We identified 31 MSP9 epitopes through SPOT synthesis, 16 of which were in regions exhibiting low structural or chemical similarity to homologous proteins from other Plasmodium species. ELISA analysis revealed that the peptides PfMSP9/IgG/23, PfMSP9/IgG/27, and PfMSP9/IgG/30 exhibited sensitivities of 44.81%, 87.23%, and 46.81%, and specificities of 81.82%, 95.74%, and 89.74%, respectively. Conclusions: Our findings indicate that the PfMSP9/IgG/27 peptide, owing to its high sensitivity and specificity, enabled the differentiation of individuals infected with P. falciparum from those infected with P. vivax. Despite the low sensitivity of the other peptides, their high specificity allowed us to differentiate between the two organisms. We believe that using additional MSP9 epitopes and applying the same approach to other P. falciparum proteins will make it possible to develop a chimeric antigen for serological diagnosis of malaria.

items.title: Clinical Nurses' Perceptions of Interruptive Clinical Decision Support Alerts: A Qualitative Study.
items.abstract: Interruptive clinical decision support (CDS) alerts are intended to improve patient care and outcomes, increase efficiency, and reduce errors, yet they are frequently overridden by clinicians. Inpatient nurses receive disproportionately high alert volumes. The purpose of this study was to understand how interruptive CDS alerts affect clinical decision-making and support or hinder the practice of inpatient clinical nurses. Interpretive description guided this qualitative study, which included 14 semistructured interviews with a convenience sample of inpatient clinical nurses. Through iterative thematic analysis, 4 themes were constructed from the data: (1) disrupting nursing care, where persistent, inaccurate, irrelevant alerts disrupt care; (2) revamping alert design, where alerts are too confusing, similar, and have limited options; (3) acting as the middleman, where alerts require nurses to notify prescribers or resolve issues outside their scope; and (4) enhanced support and safety, most evident in medication administration where alerts are actionable and appropriately timed. Findings support involving clinical nurses in the design, testing, and implementation of CDS alerts and establishing nursing CDS governance. Organizational leaders should examine how the number and behavior of alerts impact clinical nurses and position nurses as intermediaries between the electronic health record and prescribers. Education and electronic health record development are necessary to accomplish this work.

items.title: A Meta-Research Review of Statistical Practices for Image-Reliant AI Tools Predicting Lung Cancer Outcomes.
items.abstract: AbstractAI models using medical images are increasingly proposed to support clinical decision-making in lung cancer, motivating assessment of their methodological rigor and transparency. To assess how these models are developed, evaluated, and reported, and to identify gaps in best statistical practices, we conducted a cross-sectional meta-research review of OpenAlex-indexed studies (January 1, 2023, to June 30, 2025) that developed image-based AI tools for lung cancer risk prediction, detection, or prognosis. Thirty-six studies met our inclusion criteria. Convolutional neural networks were used in most studies (27 studies, 75%), and area under the curve (AUC) was the most frequently reported evaluation metric (29 studies, 81%). Although 23 studies (64%) reported some form of uncertainty quantification, most were limited to presenting confidence intervals for global performance metrics (e.g., AUC, sensitivity, and accuracy) rather than individual prediction- or risk-level uncertainty. Common limitations included limited external test set use (14 studies, 39%), insufficient subgroup analyses (10 studies, 28%), and limited adherence to established prediction-model reporting guidelines. Overall, future research should prioritize standardized reporting, use of external test sets, and model performance assessment across clinically relevant subpopulations. The coexistence of increasingly powerful AI-based prediction models with inconsistent study design, evaluation, and reporting practices emphasizes the urgent need to implement more rigorous and transparent methodological standards in this field. items.title: Electronic Health Record-Integrated Quality Dashboard for Diabetes Care in Public Primary Health Care: Development and Usability Study.
items.abstract: Background Quality dashboards are essential tools in health care, providing integrated and visualized data to support decision-making. Continuous monitoring of key indicators is crucial for managing chronic diseases such as diabetes mellitus and improving outcomes. Objective This study aimed to develop and evaluate an interactive diabetes quality dashboard integrated within the public health care system of Tandil, Argentina, to support monitoring and decision-making in primary care. Methods A participatory and multidisciplinary approach was used to design and implement the dashboard. Development consisted of two phases: (1) indicator selection and visualization design and (2) dashboard development and iterative testing. This study was conducted between October 2024 and May 2025. Indicators were initially identified from national clinical practice guidelines and Healthcare Effectiveness Data and Information Set standards and refined through 2 in-person workshops with 10 stakeholders (a health system decision-maker, primary care physicians, nurses, researchers, and IT specialists) who were purposively selected by the research team and local primary health care authorities based on their institutional role and involvement in diabetes care, chronic disease management, or health information systems and were personally invited to participate. Six virtual group sessions were then conducted with the same stakeholders to iteratively refine the dashboard based on their feedback. The dashboard was integrated into an existing electronic health record system and developed using Apache Superset. Usability was assessed using the System Usability Scale following an exploratory evaluation in which participants independently explored the dashboard without predefined tasks. Results Stakeholder workshops and iterative testing informed the dashboard's content and design. The final dashboard integrated 29 indicators across 6 tabs in 3 sections for population-level monitoring of adults with diabetes. Among 9 health care professionals participating in the usability assessment, the mean System Usability Scale score was 78.7 (SD 9.4), and 8 (88.9%) scored above the standard benchmark of 68. All participants considered the dashboard useful for health decision-making, 7 suggested further data disaggregation, and 3 recommended benchmarking capabilities. Conclusions The dashboard received favorable usability scores and may support population-level monitoring of diabetes care in public health settings. Its integration into an existing electronic health record system and participatory development were key strengths. Future research should assess its impact on care processes and clinical outcomes and explore its adaptation to other health care systems.

items.title: Preoperative hippocampal volume, resection extent, and 5-year stability of seizure freedom after temporal lobe epilepsy surgery.
items.abstract: Objective To examine whether preoperative ipsilateral hippocampal volume modifies the association between hippocampal resection extent and durable 5-year seizure freedom after temporal lobe epilepsy surgery. Methods We performed a retrospective secondary analysis of the public Imaging Database for Epilepsy And Surgery. Patients undergoing temporal lobectomy or temporal lesionectomy were eligible. The exposure was ipsilateral hippocampal resection fraction, the modifier was preoperative ipsilateral hippocampal volume z-score, and the outcome was International League Against Epilepsy class 1 at every annual assessment from years 1 through 5. Multivariable logistic regression included their interaction and pathology, procedure type, preoperative focal-to-bilateral tonic-clonic seizures, age, epilepsy duration, antiseizure medication count, sex, and operative side. Results Among 353 patients undergoing temporal surgery, 220 had all five annual outcomes and 210 had complete primary-model data. Durable seizure freedom occurred in 82 of 210 patients (39.0%). The resection-by-volume interaction odds ratio was 1.49 (95% confidence interval, 1.01-2.21; p = .045). Model-based probabilities increased with greater resection when hippocampal volume was preserved but not with marked atrophy. The estimate was similar in temporal lobectomy alone (odds ratio, 1.74; 95% confidence interval, 1.07-2.83) and attenuated after inverse-probability weighting (odds ratio, 1.43; 95% confidence interval, .95-2.13). Significance In this cohort, the association between measured hippocampal resection overlap and seizure outcome varied across preoperative hippocampal volumes. The pattern was most apparent when seizure freedom was assessed across 5 years rather than at a single postoperative visit.

items.title: Safety Assessment for Ingested N-acetylcysteine Exposure: A Systematic Review.
items.abstract: N-acetylcysteine (NAC), an amino acid precursor, is an approved drug in the United States and sold in products represented as dietary supplements. Currently, NAC is excluded from the statutory definition of a dietary supplement because of its approved drug status. The U.S. Food and Drug Administration (FDA) has the authority to remove this exclusion by regulation. As part of evaluating whether to pursue rulemaking, FDA has considered NAC's safety profile. Adverse effects (AEs) from investigational uses of NAC include gastrointestinal symptoms, such as nausea and vomiting, plus rash with or without fever. However, similar AE reports on use of NAC as a dietary supplement were unavailable. To address this data gap, a systematic review (SR) was conducted to assess AEs associated with NAC, as it relates to an expectation of safety for NAC as a dietary supplement. The SR identified 41 high-quality studies from 149 studies reviewed. One study identified a statistically significant increase in nausea in patients with ulcerative colitis at a dose of 800 mg/day for 16 weeks. The remaining high-quality studies found no corresponding increase in AEs with high doses (up to 9000 mg/day) and long durations (up to 3 yrs). NAC doses in clinical studies were comparable to recommended servings of available NAC-containing products represented as supplements, indicating similar exposure levels and, therefore, a similar safety profile. Based on that similarity and the minimal level of concern for AEs associated with NAC, this review concludes a reasonable expectation of safety for NAC as a dietary supplement.
