items.title: Understanding parental perspectives on chemotherapy side effects in children with cancer at Bugando medical centre, Mwanza, Tanzania: A descriptive cross-sectional study.
items.abstract: IntroductionChildhood cancer treatment often involves chemotherapy, which is associated with adverse drug reactions/side effects that require close monitoring. Parents and guardians play a critical role in identifying and managing these reactions in children. This study assessed the awareness, attitudes, and proactive monitoring practices of parents/guardians regarding chemotherapy-related adverse drug reactions among children with cancer at a tertiary referral hospital in Tanzania.MethodsA descriptive cross-sectional study was conducted among 200 parents/guardians of paediatric cancer patients receiving chemotherapy at Bugando Medical Centre, Mwanza, Tanzania. Data were collected using a semi-structured questionnaire and analysed using Stata version 16. Descriptive statistics, chi-square tests, and logistic regression analyses were performed.ResultsMost participants demonstrated low awareness of chemotherapy-related adverse drug reactions (80.5%). However, positive attitudes (58.5%) and proactive monitoring practices (69.0%) were observed. Female caregivers were more likely to demonstrate proactive monitoring practices than male caregivers (AOR = 1.97, 95% CI: 1.05-3.68, p = 0.03). Participants who were aware of chemotherapy-related adverse drug reactions were also more likely to demonstrate proactive monitoring practices (AOR = 3.19, 95% CI: 1.22-8.35, p = 0.02).ConclusionsDespite limited awareness, parents and guardians demonstrated positive attitudes and self-reported proactive monitoring of their children for chemotherapy-related adverse drug reactions. Strengthening caregiver education and communication during cancer treatment may improve awareness, facilitate early recognition, reporting and appropriate management of adverse reactions.Clinical trial NumberNA.

items.title: The β-ladder domain of TMUV NS1 enhances viral replication in avian cells by modulating its interaction with the NS4A-2K-NS4B complex.
items.abstract: Tembusu virus (TMUV), a mosquito‑borne flavivirus, represents a major threat to waterfowl farming in East and Southeast Asia. In vivo studies have noted distinct viral loads and viremia between ducklings infected with mosquito‑derived TMUV (mTMUV) and duck‑derived TMUV (dTMUV), yet the viral elements driving such phenotypic divergence remain unknown. The multifunctional nonstructural glycoprotein NS1 participates in flavivirus replication, secretion, and immune regulation. Here, we generated a panel of chimeric TMUV viruses with full‑length NS1 exchanges and NS1 domain substitutions based on mTMUV and dTMUV backbones. Our results demonstrated that NS1 modulates TMUV phenotypes in a strain-, dose-, and genetic background-dependent manner. Subcutaneous inoculation mimicking natural mosquito transmission amplified inter‑group phenotypic discrepancies, verifying NS1 as a pivotal modulator of TMUV‑triggered viremia. Since duck peripheral blood mononuclear cell (PBMC) infection underpins in vivo local viral establishment, an in vitro PBMC infection model validated the key contributory roles of NS1 and its functional domains in sustaining viral infection. We further utilized duck embryo fibroblasts (DEFs) to dissect the function of candidate NS1 domains. Domain swapping identified the β‑ladder domain as a major contributor to enhanced viral replication. Mechanistically, this replication enhancement effect correlates with strengthened interaction between NS1 and the NS4A-2K-NS4B replication complex. Collectively, our results identify the NS1 β-ladder domain as a critical determinant for TMUV infection. By modulating the interaction between NS1 and the NS4A-2K-NS4B complex, this domain regulates viral RNA replication efficiency in different hosts and consequently modulates viral dissemination and pathogenicity of TMUV. Importance Tembusu virus (TMUV) severely threatens waterfowl production across East and Southeast Asia. Noticeable phenotypic differences exist between mosquito-derived and duck-derived TMUV; however, the viral determinants responsible for this variation remain poorly understood. Although flavivirus NS1 is a multifunctional glycoprotein, how it mediates TMUV host-specific phenotypes remains incompletely characterized. Using chimeric and mutant viruses, this study demonstrates that the NS1 β-ladder domain enhances viral replication by strengthening the interaction with the NS4A-2K-NS4B replication complex. This domain governs TMUV replication efficiency across hosts, thereby controlling viral dissemination and pathogenicity. Our findings uncover a key molecular basis for TMUV host adaptation and provide insights into flavivirus mosquito-to-waterfowl transmission.

items.title: Novel wounded porcine skin ex vivo methicillin-resistant Staphylococcus aureus and Pseudomonas aeruginosa infection models.
items.abstract: Chronic wounds are a growing challenge in clinical practice and can be associated with infection by antimicrobial-resistant bacteria. With increasing demand for pathophysiology research and therapeutic technology development, biologically relevant platforms like infected swine skin explants are used; however, explants are not typically studied in conjunction with normal microbiota, which recapitulates the clinical scenario. The current study generated 1- and 8-cm diameter wounded swine skin explants from shaved, sanitized swine skin harvested immediately after euthanasia. Tissue morphology was evaluated over 9 days using a custom histological grading scale and growth dynamics of skin microbiota monitored. Explant viability decreased after 3 days in association with a peak in normal microbiota of varying diversity. Stable co-colonization of wound beds with clinical Pseudomonas aeruginosa and methicillin-resistant Staphylococcus aureus isolates alongside microbiota over 3 days was demonstrated. In summary, the presented 1- and 8-cm explant models maintain normal microbiota and are suitable for microbiome and/or wound infection treatment or prevention studies.

items.title: Sarcopenia Beyond the Clinic: A Community-Based Pilot Screening Study Among Elderly Kuwaitis.
items.abstract: Objective This pilot study screened community-dwelling elderly Kuwaitis for sarcopenia using Asian Working Group for Sarcopenia (AWGS) 2019 criteria to inform public health strategy. Material and methods In this unfunded cross-sectional pilot study, 61 Kuwaiti nationals aged ≥60 years were recruited in Al Asimah Governorate. Handgrip strength and physical performance (Short Physical Performance Battery [SPPB]) were assessed in all participants. Possible sarcopenia was defined as low handgrip strength or impaired physical performance; screen-positive participants underwent multi-frequency bioelectrical impedance analysis (BIA) to confirm sarcopenia by muscle mass. Groups were compared with chi-square/Fisher's exact and t-/Mann-Whitney tests; 95% confidence intervals (CI) used the Wilson score method. Results Possible sarcopenia was identified in 33 of 61 participants (54.1%, CI 41.7-66.0%), rising from 21.4% (CI 7.6-47.6%) at 60-69 years to 90.9% (CI 72.2-97.5%) at ≥80 years (p Conclusion This pilot study provides the first community-based evidence of a high possible-sarcopenia burden among elderly Kuwaitis, with muscle-mass confirmation in nearly one-third of screen-positive cases and marked age and gender gradients. These findings warrant a larger, nationally representative validation study and support two-step sarcopenia screening in routine geriatric care. .

items.title: Cancer Incidence and Mortality Patterns in Central Asia in 2022 and an Assessment of the Future Burden in 2045.
items.abstract: Central Asia is undergoing rapid epidemiological transition, yet internationally comparable assessments of cancer profiles in the constituent countries (Kazakhstan, Kyrgyzstan, Tajikistan, Turkmenistan and Uzbekistan) remain limited. We aimed to describe patterns of cancer incidence and mortality across the region and to project the future cancer burden through 2045. Cancer incidence and mortality estimates in 2022 were obtained for the five countries from IARC's GLOBOCAN database. Age-standardised incidence and mortality rates were compared by country, sex and cancer type. The future cancer burden was projected by applying age-specific cancer rates to population projections, assuming stable rates over time. In 2022, an estimated 92,665 new cancer cases and 56,110 cancer deaths occurred across Central Asia. Kazakhstan had the highest overall incidence and mortality rates, whereas the lowest rates across most major cancer sites were consistently estimated for Tajikistan. Breast cancer was the most common cancer among women, and lung cancer among men. The regional cancer profile was characterised by the coexistence of infection-related cancers alongside those linked to socioeconomic transition. Assuming stable rates, the annual number of new cancer cases is projected to increase by approximately 65%, reaching 152,000 by 2045, while cancer deaths are projected to increase by 73% to nearly 97,000 deaths. Cancer patterns in Central Asia suggest that regional cancer control planning should be nuanced to reflect each country's profile and resources, balancing prevention of infection-related cancers with early detection and effective management of common cancers associated with ongoing socioeconomic transitions.

items.title: Fragment End Motif Analysis of Microbial Cell-Free DNA Improves Detection of Pathogens over Noise from Contaminants and Commensals.
items.abstract: Background Circulating plasma microbial DNA (mDNA) is a promising biomarker for sepsis, but its accuracy is hindered by the low abundance of pathogen DNA and the presence of contaminants and commensals. mDNA enrichment using a selection of short fragments and single-stranded DNA (ssDNA) library preparation can improve pathogen yield but also increases background noise. Since nucleotide representation at mDNA fragment ends is biased by enzymatic digestion in vivo, we hypothesized that analysis of 5' and 3' mDNA fragment end motifs in enriched ssDNA libraries could improve pathogen detection. Methods We performed deep metagenomic sequencing of size-selected ssDNA libraries from 38 plasma samples, including 20 samples from 5 sepsis patients, 18 samples from 6 patients without infection, and 6 no-template controls. Across these samples, we compared observed-to-expected ratios for end motifs in mDNA fragments from candidate pathogens and contaminants. For each candidate pathogen, we evaluated the accuracy of combining end motifs with microbial abundance for detection of infection. Results mDNA fragments from infection-causing pathogens were biased in the nucleotide motifs at both fragment ends compared with contaminants, with the highest enrichment observed in the GG dinucleotide at the 3' end (P Conclusions mDNA end motif analysis improves signal-to-noise ratio beyond microbial abundance alone and improves pathogen detection in plasma metagenomic sequencing.

items.title: Climate change anxiety and insomnia in nursing students: implications for health promotion?
items.abstract: Background Climate change is not only an environmental crisis but also an emerging mental health concern. This study investigated the relationship between climate change anxiety and insomnia severity among nursing students in the Mediterranean Region of Turkey. Methods A descriptive cross-sectional survey was conducted with 512 participants between December 2024 and January 2025. Data were collected using the Descriptive Information Form, the Climate Change Anxiety Scale (CCAS), and the Insomnia Severity Index (ISI). Results The mean CCAS score was 1.63 ± 0.69 and the mean ISI score was 13.20 ± 4.18. Correlation analysis revealed a moderate positive relationship between climate change anxiety and insomnia severity ( r = 0.372, p Conclusions Climate change anxiety is associated with increased insomnia severity among nursing students, highlighting the mental health implications of climate-related psychological stress. Health promotion initiatives within universities should incorporate resilience-building, sleep hygiene education, and mental health support to address climate-related anxiety. Further longitudinal and multicenter studies are warranted to confirm these findings and guide effective public health interventions.

items.title: High-throughput simultaneous determination of 51 herbicide residues in drinking water by online solid-phase extraction coupled with ultra-performance liquid chromatography-tandem mass spectrometry.
items.abstract: An online solid-phase extraction coupled with ultra-performance liquid chromatography-tandem mass spectrometry (online SPE-UPLC-MS/MS) method was developed for the simultaneous determination of 51 herbicides, including triazines, sulfonylureas, amides, and phenylureas, in drinking water. Water samples were filtered through a 0.22 µm hydrophilic polytetrafluoroethylene (PTFE) membrane, adjusted to pH 6, enriched on an Oasis hydrophilic-lipophilic balance (HLB) online solid-phase extraction (SPE) column with 0.1% formic acid in water as the loading solution, and separated on an ACQUITY UPLC HSS T3 column using 0.1% formic acid in water-acetonitrile. Detection was performed in positive electrospray ionization (ESI + ) and multiple reaction monitoring (MRM) mode. The method showed good linearity for all analytes, with correlation coefficients greater than 0.995. The limits of detection and quantification were 0.146-0.833 ng L -1 and 0.487-2.778 ng L -1 , respectively. Mean recoveries at 5, 10, and 50 ng L -1 ranged from 68.0% to 118.9%, with intra-day and inter-day RSDs of 0.2-9.5% and 1.0-19.9%, respectively. Matrix effects were weak for forty-seven compounds, moderate for three, and strong for one. The method was successfully applied to 84 real samples from 28 water treatment plants in southeastern China. Overall detection rates decreased from raw water to finished water and tap water, with triazines and amides as the predominant detected classes. This analytical method provides reliable technical support for drinking water quality surveillance and health risk assessment.

items.title: Patient Selection and Outcomes After Percutaneous Cholecystostomy for High-Risk Acute Cholecystitis: A 10-Year Cohort Study.
items.abstract: Background Percutaneous cholecystostomy (PC) is used for acute cholecystitis when immediate cholecystectomy is unsafe. We evaluated selection, treatment response, drain morbidity, subsequent surgery, and survival in a quaternary referral practice. Methods Adults undergoing PC from January 2016 to August 2025 were retrospectively reviewed, with follow-up to September 2026. Analyses assessed operative risk, Tokyo severity, 72-h response, drain outcomes, surgery and mortality, distinguishing planned interval from acute/rescue cholecystectomy. Results Eighty-one patients underwent PC over 9.7 years; 56.8% were interhospital transfers. Median age was 74.2 years; 97.5% were American Society of Anesthesiologists (ASA) Grade 3 or higher, 82.7% had American College of Surgeons National Surgical Quality Improvement Program (ACS NSQIP) predicted mortality ≥ 10%, 72.8% had Tokyo Grade III disease and 51.9% were in septic shock. Clinical improvement within 72 h occurred in 91.4%. Drain complications occurred in 21.0% and recurrent biliary events in 17.3%. Forty patients (49.4%) underwent cholecystectomy: 32 planned interval and eight acute/rescue procedures. Median time to planned interval surgery was 108 days. Lower NSQIP risk and documented bridge-to-surgery intent were independently associated with planned interval cholecystectomy. One-year mortality was 28.8% (23/80); failure to improve within 72 h was associated with 85.7% one-year mortality versus 23.3% after improvement (p = 0.002). Conclusion PC was used in a highly selected, severely unwell population and usually achieved early improvement, but drain morbidity and competing mortality remained substantial. Approximately two in five patients progressed to planned definitive surgery, supporting selective PC use when index operative risk is prohibitive.

items.title: Surgery rates in Japan around market-entry milestones of advanced therapies for Crohn's disease and ulcerative colitis: an interrupted time-series study using a large-scale Japanese claims database.
items.abstract: Objective Whether the market entry of newer advanced therapies is associated with changes in surgery rates for inflammatory bowel disease in routine clinical practice remains unclear. We aimed to describe surgery rates for Crohn's disease and ulcerative colitis in Japan around the market-entry milestones of advanced therapies. Methods This interrupted time-series study used a large-scale, outpatient-inclusive health insurance claims database from Japan (2012-2020). Prespecified intervention points were the market-entry months of ustekinumab for Crohn's disease (May 2017) and vedolizumab for ulcerative colitis (November 2018). The primary outcome was monthly surgery rates, modeled using segmented Poisson regression with an offset for patients at risk. Results The cohorts included 5,411 patients with Crohn's disease and 37,052 with ulcerative colitis. Surgery rates declined during the pre-intervention period (incidence rate ratios [95% confidence intervals]: Crohn's disease, 0.993 [0.988-0.999]; ulcerative colitis, 0.994 [0.988-1.001]). No evidence of a level or post-intervention trend change was observed at the intervention points (Crohn's disease: level change, 0.924 [0.708-1.202]; trend change, 1.000 [0.984-1.015]; ulcerative colitis: level change, 0.883 [0.588-1.309]; trend change, 1.008 [0.984-1.032]). Conclusion Surgery rates showed a gradual pre-existing decline with no detectable level or trend change around these market-entry milestones. These findings suggest that changes in surgical rates may occur gradually rather than as an abrupt shift around a single market-entry milestone.

items.title: A fuzzy set approach to assessing catastrophic health spending: an application to data from Nigeria.
items.abstract: Catastrophic health spending (CHS) is conventionally assessed as a crisp set, in which a household either incurs CHS or does not. Arguably, this does not reflect reality, particularly because households often cannot determine with certainty when they transition to financial catastrophe. This paper argues that this transition is gradual and can be modelled as a fuzzy rather than a crisp set. This paper develops a fuzzy set approach to assess CHS, using a fuzzy membership function and introducing novel statistics, including closeness and vulnerability to CHS. Under the fuzzy set approach, CHS headcount adds the conventional headcount to the novel headcount of vulnerability to CHS. Data come from Nigeria, where out-of-pocket health spending is the predominant form of health expenditure. At the 10% budget share threshold, Nigeria's CHS headcount increased from 20% under the conventional approach to 42% under the fuzzy set approach, with the CHS vulnerability headcount exceeding that under the traditional approach. Focusing solely on out-of-pocket health spending, as is traditionally done in assessing CHS, the fuzzy set approach highlights the significant burden households face, which is often overlooked by conventional methods, and this is a pertinent issue for health financing policy.

items.title: Charting the Course: Examining 75 Years of SOPHE's History Through Presidential Addresses.
items.abstract: The Society for Public Health Education (SOPHE), one of the leading professional organizations in health education, has worked to advance professional standards, strengthen credentialing opportunities, and promote health equity for more than 75 years. At each annual conference, the outgoing SOPHE president addresses the audience, reflecting on the organization and field of health education, which provides insights into SOPHE's history and evolving priorities over time. This study is the first analysis of the available SOPHE presidential addresses over three quarters of a century. Such historical analyses are valuable for informing new organizational leaders, members, students, and staff on how the organization has been influenced by and responded to societal events over different eras and provides lessons for navigating future challenges. Presidential addresses were obtained through SOPHE's archives, published in the organization's oldest journal or directly requested from living past presidents. A thematic analysis of the available presidential addresses ( n = 28) identified five themes: (a) Organizational Structure and Changes, (b) Health Education Priorities, (c) Equity and Advocacy, (d) Collaborations, and (e) Public Health Priorities and Events. An analysis by decade showed how SOPHE's focus shifted from building a professional foundation toward addressing inequities, fostering collaboration, and responding to public health challenges. The findings offer insights to inform future organizational priorities and highlight the importance of preserving future presidential addresses as a historical resource to guide SOPHE moving forward.

items.title: A Blessing in Disguise: The Long-Term Effects of Childhood Exposure to the Boll Weevil on Old-Age Male Longevity.
items.abstract: The infamous agricultural pest, the boll weevil, spread across southern US counties between 1892 and 1920. It had devastating impacts on cotton production, a highly child-labor-intensive crop. This study examines how the arrival of the boll weevil and the subsequent reductions in child labor affect later-life mortality outcomes. Using Social Security Administration death records linked with the 1940 census, we document that the staggered spread of the boll weevil improved the longevity of exposed male children. Full exposure to the boll weevil is associated with an intent-to-treat effect of 1-3 months of higher longevity. We show that the estimated effects are robust across a wide array of specifications, are not driven by sociodemographic and socioeconomic compositional change in the final sample, and are not associated with pre-existing trends in the outcome. Further, we find larger impacts among Blacks, children of lower educated mothers, whose fathers work in the farming industry, and those born in high cotton intensity counties. Moreover, the effects appear to be substantially larger among children in states with less restrictive child labor policies, implying the role of these policies in reducing the adverse effects of child labor in the absence of the boll weevil in cotton production counties. Affected children are more likely to migrate, and their destination counties are more likely to be urban and have higher socioeconomic scores. The 1940 census suggests that the exposed children attain higher levels of education and have higher socioeconomic scores. We discuss the policy implications of these results in relation to child labor and school attendance policies in developing countries.

items.title: Association of Planetary Health Diet with decreased risk of cardiometabolic diseases, multimorbidity, and its progression: a prospective cohort study.
items.abstract: Background Lifestyle factors account for most of cardiometabolic diseases (CMDs) and progression to cardiometabolic multimorbidity (CMM). Yet, whether adherence to the Planetary Health Diet (PHD) is related to a lower risk of CMDs, CMM, and CMD progression is less known. Methods We used large cohort data that included over 100,000 participants. Adherence to the PHD was measured by the Planetary Health Diet Index (PHDI) and CMDs were ascertained by linkage to national registries through 1 September 2023. Cox proportional hazards models or weighted Cox regression models were employed to analyse the relationship between the PHD and the risk of CMDs. CMD progression in relation to the PHD was estimated by multi-state modelling with Cox regression. Results After a median follow-up of 12.5 years, greater adherence to the PHD was associated with a decreased risk of stroke (hazard ratio (HR) = 0.973, 95% confidence interval (CI) = 0.951-0.997) and type 2 diabetes (0.968, 0.952-0.984). The association of the PHDI with type 2 diabetes showed significant nonlinearity ( p = 0.04), with the lowest risk occurring when the PHDI reached 84 points. Compliance with the PHD was inversely related to the risk of transitions from baseline separately to first CMD and to death, with an HR (95% CI) of 0.89 (0.84-0.94) and 0.81 (0.73-0.89) among adults in the highest adherence group, respectively. Conclusion Our findings support the PHD as a modifiable factor for the primary prevention of CMDs and the PHDI at 84 points being linked to the lowest type 2 diabetes risk.

items.title: METTL8 orchestrates TFH cell differentiation through m³C-mediated TCF1 regulation in infection and cancer models.
items.abstract: T follicular helper (TFH) cells are critical for humoral immunity against infections and correlate with immunotherapy efficacy, whereas immune checkpoint inhibitor therapy can drive their aberrant expansion, underscoring the need to understand the regulators controlling TFH cell fate. However, the epitranscriptomic regulation of their differentiation remains poorly understood. Here, we identify the 3-methylcytosine (m³C) methyltransferase METTL8 as a key regulator of TFH cell differentiation in both viral infection and cancer. METTL8 was preferentially expressed in CXCL13hi TFH cells, and its deficiency impaired TFH differentiation and germinal center responses in the lymphocytic choriomeningitis virus infection model and following anti-PD-1 immunotherapy in tumor models. Mechanistically, METTL8 exerted dual functions: it bound and stabilized Tcf7 mRNA through m³C modification, and it interacted with TCF1 protein to regulate chromatin accessibility and 3D genome organization at key TFH-associated loci, including Cxcr5 and Il6ra. Notably, ginkgolic acid treatment suppressed TFH responses without compromising the antitumor efficacy of anti-PD-1 therapy, an effect associated with METTL8. Collectively, our findings identify METTL8 as an epitranscriptomic regulator linked to RNA modification, TCF1-associated transcriptional control, and chromatin architecture during TFH differentiation and suggest that modulation of this pathway may provide a strategy to tune TFH-driven immune responses.

items.title: The Long-term cognitive and mental health impacts of pandemic-induced social isolation: a trajectory analysis.
items.abstract: Objectives The COVID-19 pandemic imposed social deprivation on older adults, offering a natural experiment to test trajectories of cognitive vulnerability and psychological resilience. Guided by a Dual-Pathway Framework, we investigated how pandemic-era community-based social participation trajectories predicted 2022 cognitive and mental health outcomes, and whether childhood adversity (CA) moderated these effects. Methods We analyzed nationally representative longitudinal data from the Health and Retirement Study, with final analytic samples of 2,457 for depressive symptoms and 1,679 for cognitive function. Survey-weighted multivariable regressions using baseline-adjusted change scores evaluated how 2016-2020 social participation trajectories (Consistently Isolated, Pandemic Drop-off, Consistently Engaged, Pandemic Initiators) predicted changes in cognitive function and depressive symptoms from 2016 to 2022. Models adjusted for 2016 baselines, sociodemographic disadvantages, and physical health constraints, while testing moderation by cumulative CA. Results Compared with Consistently Engaged peers, the Pandemic Drop-off cohort showed significant cognitive decline by 2022, resembling the Consistently Isolated. This drop-off did not predict worsened long-term depressive symptoms. CA independently predicted poorer mental health. Binary models showed no moderation, while continuous sensitivity analyses suggested a potential protective interaction between late-life social initiation and cumulative early-life trauma for cognitive preservation. Pandemic Initiators preserved cognitive function comparable to consistently engaged adults. Discussion Findings support the Dual-Pathway Framework: the aging mind demonstrates emotional adaptation, whereas the aging brain may show accelerated aging after abrupt community-level social deprivation. Social participation may be important for cognitive health. Mitigating post-pandemic cognitive decline may require treating social isolation as a clinical vital sign and supporting social prescribing.

items.title: Nurse Practitioner Practice in Nurse-Managed Health Clinics: A Cross-Sectional 6-State Study.
items.abstract: Nurse-managed health clinics (NMHCs) are settings in which the rapidly growing workforce of nurse practitioners (NPs) can serve as the main providers of primary care services. Depending on state requirements, NMHCs may operate with little or no physician involvement. If NMHCs promote NP recruitment and retention, they may help address critical primary care shortages in underserved areas. Assessing this potential requires evidence on the practice characteristics, practice patterns, work environments, and job outcomes for NPs practicing in NMHCs. To examine these factors, we compared NPs practicing in NMHCs ( n = 48) to NPs practicing in clinics not identified as NMHCs ( n = 1196) using data from a 6-state study. NPs in NMHCs had greater independent practice support (3.81 vs. 3.46; p p p p = .0033), performance feedback (0.47 vs. 0.62; p = .0150), and after-hours care (0.28 vs. 0.42; p = .0330). We found comparable rates of burnout, job dissatisfaction, and likelihood of leaving the job among NPs in NMHCs and other settings ( p > .05). NPs in NMHCs spent more time performing leadership (4.0 hr vs. 1.9 hr; p = .0026) and quality improvement activities (3.5 hr vs. 1.9 hr, p = .0231). Findings suggest that NPs in NMHCs experience favorable work environments and comparable job outcomes, while engaging in leadership and quality improvement activities. Lower structural capabilities in these settings may be related to their smaller size. Thus, NMHCs may support primary care NP recruitment and retention in underserved areas.

items.title: Incidence and predictors of hypertensive heart disease among hypertensive patients: A retrospective cohort study in South Gondar Zone Hospitals, Ethiopia.
items.abstract: Background Hypertensive heart disease, including left ventricular hypertrophy and heart failure, is a neglected chronic disease in sub-Saharan Africa, causes a significant increase in morbidity and premature mortality. Despite this problem, studies on early development, incidence, and potential biochemical and behavioural predictors in Ethiopia, particularly in the study area, are scarce. Methods An institution-based retrospective cohort study was conducted on 531 hypertensive patients in selected South Gondar Zone hospitals in Ethiopia from September 2019 to June 2024. Data were collected using a structured checklist-based chart review. EPI data version 4.2 for data entry and STAT version 17 for analysis were used. Kaplan-Meier and log-rank tests, as well as Cox proportional hazard regression models, were used for survival data analysis. Result The incidence rate of hypertensive heart disease was 14.93 (95% CI: 12.94-17.23) per 1000 person-months of observation. The median survival time for the development of hypertensive heart disease was 18 months (IQR, 12-24 months). Older age group (≥60 years) (AHR = 1.82, 95%CI:1.12,2.97), obesity (AHR = 1.90,95%CI:1.29,2.79), low HDL (AHR = 1.78, 95%CI:1.21,2.64), and high non-HDL cholesterol level (AHR = 2.22,95%CI:1.51,3.25) were significant predictors of early development of hypertensive heart disease as compared to their counterparts. Conclusion Hypertensive patients in this setting had a high incidence rate and short survival time to develop hypertensive heart disease. In this study, existence of hypertensive heart disease as a common and rapidly progressing complication of hypertension was confirmed and the prognosis was poor. Routine screening for early cardiac remodelling in older patients, integration of weight management into hypertension care, and attention to lipid abnormalities should be considered as part of serious public health response, though causal conclusions require further prospective research.

items.title: Thrombo-Occlusive Vasculopathy and Dual-Excipient Granuloma Secondary to Subcutaneous Injection of Crushed Codeine Tablets.
items.abstract: Skin popping refers to the subcutaneous injection of drugs, including crushed oral tablets modified into injectable solutions. Pharmaceutical excipients such as microcrystalline cellulose and polyvinylpyrrolidone (PVP) are deposited into the tissue, provoking foreign body reactions. A 44-year-old man presented with bilateral painful ulcerated lesions on the extensor forearms. He was otherwise healthy with no history of renal impairment. Histopathological examination revealed epidermal necrosis with thrombo-occlusive vasculopathy, pan-dermal fibrosis, and granulomatous inflammation containing two morphologically distinct foreign materials: polarizable, colorless, fiber-like material consistent with microcrystalline cellulose, and spherical spaces containing nonpolarizable, bluish material positive for mucicarmine, colloidal iron, and Alcian blue, consistent with the soluble form of PVP. Following the identification of foreign material, the patient admitted to repeated subcutaneous injection of crushed codeine tablets. The thrombo-occlusive vasculopathy observed may reflect inadvertent intravascular delivery of excipients during the inexact process of skin popping and/or local vascular injury from the surrounding foreign body response. This case highlights the co-identification of two morphologically distinct excipients on routine histopathology as a diagnostic clue for injection of crushed oral medications and illustrates the spectrum of ischemic and inflammatory tissue injury encountered in skin popping.

items.title: Gastroesophageal reflux disease in chronic obstructive pulmonary disease and asthma: Results from the China Pulmonary Health study.
items.abstract: Background Gastroesophageal reflux disease (GERD) is a common comorbidity of chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD) and asthma. However, limited information is available on GERD among community-sourced patients with COPD and asthma in China. This study aimed to assess the prevalence of GERD and its association with respiratory symptoms and airway reversibility in these patients from the general population. Methods The China Pulmonary Health (CPH) study, a national cross-sectional survey, enrolled 57,779 adults aged ≥20 years from June 2012 to May 2015. Participants completed standard questionnaires and underwent pulmonary function tests. GERD was defined using the Gastroesophageal Reflux Disease Questionnaire (GerdQ). Airway reversibility was assessed via post-bronchodilator pulmonary function changes. Multivariate regressions examined the association of GERD with respiratory symptoms and airway reversibility. Results In total, 47,226 participants were included in the final analysis. The prevalence of GERD was 6.62% (95% confidence interval [CI]: 5.89-7.34%) in patients with COPD, and 13.73% (95% CI: 12.19-15.27%) and 12.38% (95% CI: 9.84-14.93%) in patients with asthma and asthma with airflow limitation, respectively. GERD was associated with nasal symptoms, cough, sputum, wheezing, and dyspnea in patients with COPD. GERD was also associated with nasal symptoms and dyspnea in patients with asthma. After adjusting for confounders, the asthma group with GERD had smaller postbronchodilator changes in forced expiratory volume in 1 s (FEV1) compared with those without GERD (B = -0.030, 95% CI: -0.055 to -0.005, P = 0.018), and the association remained after further adjusting for respiratory symptoms (B = -0.033, 95% CI: -0.058 to -0.008, P = 0.009). But postbronchodilator changes in FEV1 or forced vital capacity (FVC) did not differ between COPD patients with and without GERD. Conclusions GERD is prevalent and significantly associated with respiratory symptoms in patients with COPD and asthma. In patients with asthma, those with GERD had worse airway reversibility.

items.title: 2025 Annual Australian Measles and Rubella Genotyping Surveillance Program Report.
items.abstract: Molecular characterisation is a critical component of Australia's measles and rubella surveillance systems, supporting outbreak investigations, identifying sources of infection, and providing evidence for the continued maintenance of Australia's measles and rubella elimination status. This annual report summarises measles and rubella molecular epidemiology in Australia during 2025 and evaluates the utility of whole genome sequencing (WGS) for measles surveillance. In 2025, there were 181 confirmed measles cases notified in Australia, representing a 217.5% increase on the number notified in 2024. Measles virus genotypes B3 and D8 were detected, together with 21 vaccine-associated genotype A cases. Genotype B3 predominated during the first half of the year and was largely associated with importations from Vietnam, whereas genotype D8 predominated during the second half of the year and was primarily associated with importations from Indonesia. Thirty-one epidemiologically confirmed outbreaks were identified, comprising 13 genotype B3 outbreaks and 17 genotype D8 outbreaks. The discriminatory power and concordance with epidemiological data in the context of outbreak investigations was substantially greater for WGS data than for conventional N450-based genotyping. Viruses sharing the same N450-based distinct sequence identifier (DSid) differed by up to 33 single nucleotide polymorphisms (SNPs) for genotype B3 and 36 SNPs for genotype D8, whereas genomes obtained from epidemiologically linked cases differed by a maximum of four SNPs. Despite increased national case numbers in 2025, available molecular and epidemiological evidence indicated that cases were associated with importations or import-related transmission events, with no evidence of sustained endemic measles transmission. Rubella activity remained extremely low, with no rubella virus detections identified among 157 specimens tested by polymerase chain reaction (PCR) and only two notified cases nationally, neither of which had material available for genotyping. These findings support the continued absence of endemic measles and rubella transmission in Australia and highlight the value of WGS for enhancing measles surveillance and outbreak investigations.

items.title: Child Sexual Abuse, Sexual Function, and Sexual Distress in Couples Coping with Sexual Interest/Arousal Disorder: A Dyadic Longitudinal Study.
items.abstract: Sexual interest/arousal disorder (SIAD), characterized by low sexual desire and high sexual distress, is the most common sexual dysfunction among women. Although current theoretical models support interpersonal conceptualizations of sexual desire, distal interpersonal factors that may underlie the sexual well-being of couples coping with SIAD, such as child sexual abuse (CSA), have not been thoroughly documented. Yet, difficulties with sexual desire and arousal are among the most frequently reported sexual dysfunctions among CSA survivors. Using a one-year longitudinal design among couples with SIAD, this study examined the associations between both partners' CSA and their sexual function and distress. Individuals with SIAD (N = 263; M age = 34.16) and their partners (N = 263; M age = 35.71) completed validated questionnaires at baseline, 6 months, and 12 months. Dyadic latent growth curve analyses were conducted within a structural equation model. Results showed that greater CSA among individuals with SIAD was associated with their own higher initial levels of sexual distress. Moreover, higher levels of non-SIAD partners' CSA were unexpectedly associated with lower initial levels of sexual function difficulties for individuals with SIAD. However, non-SIAD partners' CSA predicted greater increases in sexual function difficulties over time for individuals with SIAD. No other significant associations were found. Findings highlight the role of CSA in the sexual function and distress of couples coping with SIAD and point towards the value of couple-based interventions that acknowledge both partners' histories and their impact on mutual sexual experiences.

items.title: Extracellular vesicles and their role in neurodegenerative diseases.
items.abstract: Extracellular vesicles (EVs) are membrane-bound nanoparticles that enable intercellular communication in the nervous system by transferring proteins, lipids and nucleic acids between cells. In neurodegenerative diseases (NDDs), evidence from cellular and animal models, together with emerging human data, implicates EVs in several interconnected processes: altered vesicle biogenesis and endolysosomal trafficking; selective loading of pathogenic cargoes (including amyloid-β, tau, α-synuclein, TDP43 and PrP Sc ); and dissemination of misfolded proteins in ways consistent with prion-like seeding and spread. EVs also modulate neuroinflammation by relaying cytokines and regulatory microRNAs among neurons, glia and the neurovascular unit and by engaging the blood-brain barrier to shape CNS-periphery crosstalk. These same properties underpin a growing translational interest: brain-derived EV populations in blood and other biofluids offer a minimally invasive window into early pathology and disease trajectories, and native or engineered EVs are being developed as delivery vehicles or as targets to curb pathological propagation. This Review integrates mechanistic and clinical advances, highlights key sources of biological and methodological variability, and defines priorities for standardization, cell-of-origin assignment and clinical validation required to realize EV-based diagnostics and therapeutics for NDDs.

items.title: Causal role of human hippocampus in relational structure learning and inference.
items.abstract: When meeting new individuals or known individuals in new circumstances, we intuitively map out their relationships-not merely through direct experience, but by inferring new connections on the basis of prior relational knowledge. How such relational knowledge is represented and used in the brain remains a long-standing question in cognitive neuroscience. Here, using a behavioural task and computational modelling, we show that participants (N = 36) leveraged existing knowledge of relational structures to infer new relationships, facilitating adaptation in changing environments. Whole-brain neuroimaging identified consistent representations of relational structure in the hippocampus. To investigate the causal link between hippocampal representations and inference, we used neural network simulations to predict the behavioural effects of disrupting such representations. Consistent with this prediction, transcranial ultrasound stimulation of the human hippocampus (N = 20), transiently modulating its activity, disrupted structure-based inference (P < 0.001, Cohen's d = -0.89, 95% confidence interval -1.41 to -0.36), providing empirical evidence for a causal role of hippocampus in relational-structure learning and structure-based inference.

items.title: Distinct prelimbic microcircuits control sensory and affective dimensions of neuropathic pain.
items.abstract: The microcircuit mechanisms underlying deactivation and altered output of the medial prefrontal cortex (mPFC), a common feature of several chronic pain conditions, are poorly understood. Here, using unbiased in vivo longitudinal multiphoton imaging in the mouse prelimbic cortex (PrL), we show that nerve injury induces sensitization of all classes of GABAergic interneurons and a phenotypic switch from unimodal to polymodal responses. Through circuit interrogation, we identified functions for caudal geminal eminence-derived Prox1 + interneurons and revealed that distinct classes of inhibitory and excitatory neurons in the PrL have different functions in promoting neuropathic pain. In addition, we show that the sensory and affective dimensions of neuropathic pain engaged two distinct microcircuits, PV + -Rbp4 + neurons and Prox1 + -Cux2 + /Ntsr1 + neurons, respectively, to control distinct projection outputs. These findings provide a mechanistic basis for how mPFC guides actions to avoid or overcome pain and how prefrontal deactivation exacerbates neuropathic pain.

items.title: Automated retinal layer thickness segmentation in neovascular age-related macular degeneration: a comparison of two algorithms.
items.abstract: Purpose To evaluate the consistency of retinal measurements provided by two automated segmentation algorithms in eyes with neovascular age-related macular degeneration (AMD). Design Retrospective cohort study. Participants Fifty patients with neovascular AMD. Methods Retinal thickness was measured using a Heidelberg Spectralis HRA + OCT spectral-domain device. Measurements were automatically averaged across ETDRS grid subfields centered on the fovea using both the Spectralis built-in software (version 1.10.4.0) and the Orion automated OCT segmentation software (Voxeleron, version 3.0.0). Main outcome measures Differences in quantitative retinal thickness metrics between the two algorithms. Results For inner retinal thickness, the mean difference was 8.97 μm in the central fovea (R² = 0.32), with larger variability in the inner (22.09-28.73 μm; R² = 0.32-0.80) and outer circles (16.02-29.50 μm; R² = 0.45-0.41). Outer retinal thickness showed smaller differences, with a mean of 21.51 μm in the central fovea (R² = 0.36) and modest variation across subfields. The neurosensory retina demonstrated a mean difference of 0.13 μm centrally (R² = 0.66), increasing across ETDRS subfields, with an overall mean difference of 45.30μm (R² = 0.82). Total retinal thickness differed by 43.54 μm centrally (R² = 0.61), with smaller differences across the grid (mean 18.16 μm; R² = 0.60). Conclusions While correlations between the two segmentation algorithms were moderate to strong for several metrics, clinically meaningful mean differences were observed in specific compartments, most notably for central neurosensory and total retinal thickness. These findings indicate that the two algorithms should not be used interchangeably.

items.title: Neurodegeneration with brain iron accumulation - from gene discovery to therapeutic strategies.
items.abstract: Precision therapeutics are emerging for various neurological disorders, most notably single-gene disorders. Development of breakthrough treatments typically requires insight into the earliest pathogenic changes, which enables intervention before irreversible damage to cell function has occurred. At the extreme, presymptomatic gene therapy could subvert entire disease processes. The neurodegeneration with brain iron accumulation (NBIA) disorders exemplify progress from Mendelian disease gene discovery to the era of precision neurotherapeutics. These disorders highlight the opportunities and challenges in developing precision therapeutics for single-gene neurological disorders. In this Review, we discuss the most common NBIA disorders to highlight how the study of genetic disorders can provide insight into basic neuroscience and the brain's regional vulnerability. We discuss in detail the biology of pantothenate kinase-associated neurodegeneration (PKAN), which underscores the complex and poorly understood biochemistry of this apparently simple inborn error of vitamin metabolism, and also forges a path for novel interventions. The progress in understanding of and therapeutic development for PKAN exemplifies the beginning of a rise in breakthrough therapies for genetic neurological disorders.

items.title: A systematic review and meta-analysis exploring the effects of tDCS on metabolic syndrome parameters in adults.
items.abstract: Background Metabolic syndrome is a group of health conditions associated with obesity, increased risk of type 2 diabetes, cardiovascular disease and mortality. Interventions, including lifestyle changes, pharmacological treatments, and surgical interventions, have limited long-term efficacy, and do not adequately address some underpinning factors in overweight/obesity, such as cognitive/inhibitory control related to eating behaviours. There is emerging evidence for the successful use of neuromodulation techniques, such as transcranial direct current stimulation (tDCS), as potential adjunctive therapies for eating and weight disorders. This systematic review and meta-analysis have investigated the potential effects of tDCS on weight and metabolic parameters, in adults with or without excess body weight. Methods In accordance with the Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses (PRISMA) statement, a systematic search of Embase, PsychInfo and PubMed electronic databases was performed to identify randomised clinical trials (RCTs) of tDCS which reported at least one metabolic syndrome parameter. Primary outcomes were weight, body mass index (BMI), waist circumference, blood pressure, blood glucose, insulin, and lipid profile. Results A total of 28 studies (1129 participants) were included. tDCS protocols varied in stimulation sites, current intensity, and number and duration of sessions. Meta-analyses showed small but statistically significant weight loss (MD = -1.16 kg, 95% CI: -2.29 to -0.02; p = 0.04) and waist circumference reduction (MD = -0.67 cm, 95% CI: -1.14 to -0.19; p = 0.02) following active tDCS compared to sham. A non-significant reduction in food cravings traits was observed (SMD = -0.21, p = 0.06). Effects on glucose and blood pressure were variable. Conclusion The modest positive effects of tDCS on weight and waist circumference, nonetheless, highlight its potential clinical relevance for treating obesity and metabolic syndrome. Well-powered RCTs using standardised assessment procedures are essential to clarify the therapeutic mechanisms of tDCS and to identify optimal dosing for this population.

items.title: Principles and assumptions underlying domain detection in spatial transcriptomics.
items.abstract: Spatial-omics technologies simultaneously measure feature expression and locations within tissues, providing an unprecedented opportunity to study tissue structures. The first key step in analyzing these high-dimensional datasets is identifying biologically relevant clusters, yet the large number of spatial-omics clustering (SOC) methods makes method selection challenging. Here we comprehensively review 47 SOC methods and extract information on 108 variables across 26 groups of method characteristics and applicability. This revealed substantial diversity in the underlying algorithms, affecting the suitability of methods to different tissues and biotechnologies. Based on this, we provide an analytical decision tree to help data analysts select methods based on their data types and research questions, and we highlight knowledge gaps to help bioinformaticians identify new avenues for method development. We thus hope to pave the way for more effective applications in a diverse methodological landscape and guide future method development.

items.title: Selective and spatially biased activity remodeling following adult-onset sensory loss.
items.abstract: Cross-modal brain plasticity after sensory loss allows an organism to utilize the remaining senses to guide behavior. Two distinct mechanisms support such adaptation: cross-modal recruitment and compensatory plasticity. Cross-modal recruitment refers to the deprived sensory areas gaining responsiveness to the spared senses, while compensatory plasticity indicates enhanced functionality of the spared sensory areas. Widespread synaptic and circuit-level plasticity has been reported to support such cross-modal plasticity. Here we combined whole-brain clearing, light-sheet imaging, and activity labeling using a cFosTRAP2 mouse line to examine the spatial distribution of highly active cells across brain areas following acute sensory manipulations in adult mice of both sexes. Adult-onset vision loss led to an initial decrease in the density of activity-labeled cells in visual areas, including the primary visual cortex (V1), and a parallel increase in the spared primary auditory (A1) and somatosensory barrel (S1BF) cortices. V1 and some higher-order visual areas (HVAs), but not the visual thalamus, exhibited a partial rebound in activity after a week of vision loss. The activity rebound in visual cortices and the enhanced activity observed in A1 were spatially biased. Passively exposing adult-onset blind mice to sound did not further alter activity levels, except for a decrease in the claustrum. Conversely, adult-onset deafening significantly reduced the activity-labeled cell density in auditory and auditory-related areas without clear signs of compensatory plasticity in the spared areas. Our results indicate that adult cross-modal plasticity is largely observed in sensory cortices with rather specific within-area spatial bias, suggesting selective functional adaptations. Significance Statement This study examined the spatial profile of how the adult brain adapts when one sense is lost. In mice, vision loss caused brain activity to drop in visual areas followed by partial recovery over time, suggesting gradual recruitment of these areas by non-visual information. In parallel, the brain areas for hearing and touch became more active, a sign of compensation. Activity changes were not widespread but limited mainly to sensory areas with some local spatial bias. In contrast, the same duration of hearing loss produced much less evidence of compensation in the spared sensory areas. These findings suggest that the adult brain can reorganize after sensory loss, but this adaptation is selective and region-specific, implying targeted functional compensation.

items.title: RAI1 loss produces cell type-specific transcriptomic, circuit, and behavioural consequences across mPFC GABAergic interneuron subtypes.
items.abstract: Haploinsufficiency of RAI1 ( retinoic acid-induced 1 ) causes Smith-Magenis syndrome (SMS), a neurodevelopmental disorder characterized by intellectual disability, maladaptive behaviours, and social deficits. RAI1 is a transcriptional regulator broadly expressed across multiple brain cell types, yet the cell type-specific transcriptional consequences of Rai1 haploinsufficiency remain unknown. Behavioural experiments used mice of both sexes. Our spatial transcriptomic assays in Rai1 +/- mice identified dysregulated genes across isocortical cell types, with synaptic organization and activity-dependent programs affected in a subtype-specific manner among GABAergic interneurons. To explore RAI1 function in these cells, we conditionally deleted Rai1 from parvalbumin (PV), somatostatin (SST), and vasoactive intestinal peptide (VIP) interneurons. In the social dominance tube test, PV- and SST-specific Rai1 loss reduced winning rates, whereas VIP-specific loss increased winning. Rai1 ⁺/⁻ mice showed social competition-induced PV/VIP cFos activation in the medial-prefrontal cortex. Overall mPFC cFos activity was increased in VIP mutants but was decreased in PV and SST mutants. Monosynaptic rabies tracing revealed RAI1-dependent, subtype-specific remodeling of long-range inputs onto mPFC interneurons. Chemogenetic inhibition of Rai1 -deficient mPFC PV or VIP interneurons normalized the social competition phenotypes. Together, our findings reveal that Rai1 haploinsufficiency induces cell-type-specific transcriptional and anatomical reorganization of prefrontal interneurons, which bidirectionally biases social behaviour output and is acutely reversible by targeted activity modulation. By resolving how a broadly expressed gene produces divergent consequences across interneuron classes, our work clarifies the cellular origins of social deficits in SMS and points to subtype-selective interneuron modulation as a therapeutic strategy i SMS and GABAergic disorders. Significance statement Social behavioural deficits are a prominent feature of SMS, a neurodevelopmental disorder caused by haploinsufficiency of the transcriptional regulator RAI1 GABAergic interneuron subtypes in the medial prefrontal cortex are critical for social behaviour, but the transcriptional programs governing their functional development and maturation are largely unknown. Here we show that Rai1 loss causes subtype-specific transcriptomic and anatomical input reorganization, and altered Fos activity in PV, SST, and VIP interneurons, culminating in divergent social competitive outcomes. The net social deficit likely arises from competing cell-type-specific perturbations. Notably, acute modulation of interneuron activity normalizes social behaviour, highlighting a potential therapeutic opportunity. Our findings emphasize the need for subtype-specific interventions and provide a cell-type-resolved framework for understanding GABAergic dysfunction in neurodevelopmental disorders.

items.title: A dorsoventral gradient of synaptic dynamics across columns of the midbrain periaqueductal gray.
items.abstract: The midbrain periaqueductal gray (PAG) is an evolutionarily conserved, highly interconnected brain region that coordinates diverse physiological and behavioral responses essential for survival, including pain modulation, autonomic and cardiovascular regulation, and defensive responses to threat. The PAG is anatomically and functionally subdivided into longitudinal columns that generate divergent behavioral and physiological responses. However, little is known about how distinct synaptic properties of neurons in each column support column-specific information processing. To address this gap, we made whole-cell voltage-clamp recordings from unlabeled neurons in the ventrolateral (vl), lateral (l), and dorsomedial (dm) columns of PAG in adult male and female C57BL/6J mice. Our results demonstrate that many features of synaptic processing are conserved across columns, including the relative balance of synaptic inhibition/excitation as well as stable paired pulse ratios across a wide range of interstimulus intervals. Despite these commonalities, high frequency stimulation revealed significant cross-column differences in synaptic integration mechanisms. Specifically, phasic EPSC amplitudes remained stable in the vlPAG and, to a lesser extent, the lPAG. In stark contrast, high frequency stimulation resulted in pronounced temporal summation in the dmPAG, due to, in part, slower EPSC kinetics. This profile resulted in the generation of an envelope/slow current during high-frequency trains which counteracted more pronounced phasic EPSC depression observed in the dmPAG. Together, these results identify column-specific strategies to preserve excitatory signal transfer across the PAG, providing a synaptic basis for how distinct columns process information to support their specialized functional roles. eNeuro Assessment The study investigates synaptic properties of periaqueductal grey (PAG) neurons in distinct divisions. The authors report convincing data for division-specific synaptic dynamics. The experiments are rigorously designed, the data are of high quality, and the statistical power and analyses are appropriate. The results provide important information about region-specific response properties within the PAG and have implication for the interpretation of the contribution of this circuit to behavior.

items.title: Speech and Language Abnormalities in Putative Brain-First Versus Body-First Parkinson's Disease.
items.abstract: The α-synuclein origin model proposes brain-first and body-first Parkinson's disease (PD) subtypes, with speech potentially revealing their distinct neurodegenerative patterns. We aimed to analyze the possible speech and language differences between untreated PD patients with premotor (putative body-first) and without (putative brain-first) rapid eye movement sleep behavior disorder. Speech samples of reading passages and monologues were automatically analyzed using acoustic and linguistic features. We enrolled 23 body-first and 35 brain-first de novo PD patients compared with 35 healthy controls. Brain-first patients showed greater speech impairment severity compared with body-first patients (P = 0.002) and controls (P < 0.001), whereas body-first patients showed greater language impairment severity compared with brain-first patients (P < 0.001) and controls (P < 0.001). Putative brain-first subtype had more motor speech abnormalities whereas body-first subtype manifested greater language impairment. Thes finding is consistent with motor-dominant nigrostriatal involvement in brain-first and broader non-motor/cognitive involvement in body-first PD. © 2026 The Author(s). items.title: Distinct patterns of activity in the prelimbic cortex track task-related differences for cocaine and water reinforcers.
items.abstract: The pursuit of drugs is a fundamental element of substance use. Different tasks assess drug pursuit in the face of effort, punishment, or the absence of the drug, and recent studies have suggested that a shared latent variable may drive behavior across these tasks. The prelimbic cortex (PL) is implicated in these behaviors, but it is unknown if its role is driven by distinct neural ensembles. We recorded PL activity using in vivo endoscopic calcium imaging in 32 male and female Sprague-Dawley rats as they completed cocaine or water self-administration, extinction, progressive ratio, and punished self-administration. We found that behavior across tasks covaried in water, but not cocaine rats. We also found that slow, sustained neural excitations following response for reward were lower in extinction. Furthermore, exploratory analysis suggests that those individual rats that had more responsive neurons also had significantly higher levels of reward pursuit in the extinction task. Notably, this relationship was true across cocaine and water rats, suggesting a general role independent of reward type. Thus, our findings suggest that extinction behavior is tracked by a distinct neural pattern in the PL.

items.title: Nature, Nurture, and Early Childhood Development: Emerging Evidence and Opportunities for Pediatrics.
items.abstract: Early childhood represents a unique window of biological vulnerability and developmental opportunity 1 . Brain plasticity during the first years of life suggests that environmental exposures and relational experiences may exert profound and lasting effects on cognitive, emotional, and physical health throughout the lifespan 2,3 . Within the framework of contemporary developmental neuroscience, pediatric research has increasingly focused on how physical surroundings, particularly green spaces and natural environments, interact with socio-emotional experiences to shape early developmental trajectories. A major research initiative recently announced in Europe, by the Royal Foundation Centre for Early Childhood 4 , brings this intersection to the forefront. This commentary authored by members of the working group on Social Pediatrics of the European Pediatric Association, Union of National Pediatric Societies and Associations (EPA-UNEPSA), briefly explores current evidence across environmental psychology and pediatric developmental research, reporting recent parental survey data, with the aim to highlight the opportunities and methodological challenges this initiative may present for social and preventive pediatrics.

items.title: Comparing the acute neurophysiological effects of 10 Hz monophasic cTMS and biphasic rTMS in healthy adults.
items.abstract: Background Neurophysiological responses to repetitive transcranial magnetic stimulation (rTMS) are highly variable across individuals. Monophasic stimulation using controllable pulse parameter TMS (cTMS) has been shown to enhance corticospinal excitability and increase responder rates in patterned protocols. However, it remains unclear whether these advantages extend to conventional 10 Hz stimulation. Objective To compare the acute effects of 10 Hz monophasic cTMS and biphasic rTMS on corticospinal excitability and short-interval intracortical inhibition (SICI), and to examine the influence of sex and brain-derived neurotrophic factor (BDNF) genotype. Methods Thirty-three healthy adults completed three randomized sessions of 10 Hz cTMS, rTMS, and sham stimulation. Motor evoked potentials (MEPs) and SICI were assessed at baseline and 10 min post-stimulation. Responders were classified based on changes in MEP amplitude. Results No significant changes in MEP amplitude or SICI were observed following cTMS, rTMS, or sham. Exploratory analysis detected no significant effects of sex or BDNF genotype. Exploratory responder analyses revealed substantial variability, with similar proportions of facilitation following cTMS (61%) and rTMS (64%). Across real stimulation, facilitation was observed in 57% of Val/Val and 68% of Met carriers, with no clear differences between genotypes. Conclusion No significant differences were detected between 10 Hz monophasic cTMS, biphasic rTMS, and sham in MEP amplitude or SICI at 10 min post-stimulation. Exploratory analyses detected no clear effects of sex or BDNF genotype.

items.title: Beta 1 -adrenergic receptor regulation of VMN growth hormone-releasing hormone neuron lactate, estrogen, and counterregulatory transmitter receptor gene expression in male versus female rats.
items.abstract: The metabolic-sensitive hindbrain transmitter norepinephrine (NE) controls ventromedial hypothalamic nucleus (VMN) growth hormone-releasing hormone (Ghrh)/steroidogenic factor-1 (SF1) neuron counterregulatory neurotransmission via beta1-adrenergic receptor signaling. Ghrh neurons assimilate nutrient, hormone, and neurochemical cues that affect counterregulation. Current research employed in vivo ADRβ1 gene silencing technology to examine whether NE imposes sex-specific regulation of VMN Ghrh neuron receptivity to these stimuli during eu- and/or hypoglycemia. VMN ADRβ1 gene knockdown respectively up- or down-regulated Ghrh neuron GPR81 lactate receptor gene expression in vehicle- versus insulin-injected male rats, yet this mRNA was decreased (euglycemia) or unaffected (hypoglycemia) in females. Gene silencing suppressed estrogen receptor (ER)-alpha, ER-beta, and G protein-coupled ER-1 (GPER) transcripts in euglycemic females but negatively only a subset of these mRNAs in males. β1-AR knockdown did not modify ER gene expression in insulin-treated female rats but inhibited GPER transcripts in hypoglycemic males. Eu- and hypoglycemic animals of each sex exhibited down-regulated Ghrh neuron gamma-aminobutyric acid (GABA)-A receptor mRNA after VMN ADRβ1 siRNA pretreatment, whereas gene silencing correspondingly decreased or increased GABA-B receptor subunit-2 transcripts in hypoglycemic males versus females. ADRβ1 gene knockdown caused opposite changes in guanylate cyclase-1 soluble subunit alpha2 mRNA in vehicle- versus insulin-treated males but down-regulated this mRNA in females. Results suggest that sex-dimorphic β1-AR control of VMNdm Ghrh/SF-1 neuron transmission may involve regulation of cell sensitivity to convergent extrinsic stimuli that influence neural regulation of glucose homeostasis. Data moreover disclose that the direction of receptor control of distinctive receptor genes is glucose status-dependent.

items.title: Acupuncture alleviates post-stroke depression by inhibiting proline-driven ferroptosis in hippocampal neurons.
items.abstract: Background Post-stroke depression (PSD) represents a prevalent stroke complication with scarce therapeutic interventions. Acupuncture has shown clinical efficacy in PSD, but the underlying mechanisms remain unclear. This study investigates whether acupuncture alleviates PSD by regulating proline metabolism-mediated ferroptosis. Methods We generated a rat PSD model via common carotid artery ligation coupled with chronic unpredictable mild stress (CUMS). Acupuncture at GV20, GV26, GV24, and GV14 was administered for four weeks. Behavioral tests, TTC and Nissl staining, ELISA, qPCR, western blot, amino acid metabolomics, and hippocampal neuron cultures with proline intervention were performed. Results Acupuncture robustly rescued depression-like phenotypes and mitigated hippocampal neuronal injury in PSD rats. Acupuncture decreased serum levels of iron ions, malondialdehyde (MDA) and reactive oxygen species (ROS), increased glutathione (GSH), and reversed the aberrant expression of ferroptosis-related proteins (GPX4, SLC7A11, ACSL4, TFR1) in the hippocampus. Amino acid metabolomics revealed elevated serum proline in PSD rats, which was normalized by acupuncture. Exogenous proline administration aggravated depressive behaviors and hippocampal ferroptosis. In cultured hippocampal neurons, high-dose proline directly induced ferroptosis and reduced cell viability. Conclusion Acupuncture ameliorates PSD by inhibiting hippocampal neuronal ferroptosis through regulation of proline metabolism, revealing a novel mechanism for acupuncture treatment.

items.title: Chitosan nanoparticles for the slow release of synthetic RARβ agonists.
items.abstract: The sustained and local delivery of drugs to the central nervous system, is a challenge for treatments of neurodegenerative diseases and traumatic injuries. In order to avoid repeated injections after spinal cord injury (SCI), we have developed a delivery platform for the slow release of two synthetic agonists of the retinoic acid receptor β (RARβ). The drugs, EC23 and ellorarxine, are incorporated in and delivered with chitosan nanoparticles (CsNp). These were prepared by ionic gelation using formulations with water-soluble [CsNp(w)] and acidic chitosan [CsNp(ac)], and were characterized by scanning electron microscopy, dynamic light scattering, and particle size distribution analysis. Both formulations produced nanoscale particles, with CsNp(ac) showing a more homogeneous size distribution compared with CsNp(w). Drug incorporation was highly efficient, and release experiments demonstrated that both EC23 and ellorarxine were released in a sustained manner over 15 days, with release kinetics depending on the CsNp formulation and the encapsulated RARβ-agonist. The results indicate that drug release from CsNp was governed by a combination of decreasing ionic interactions between drugs and the polymer, particle erosion and diffusion. Biological effects of drug release from CsNp were investigated in vitro and in vivo. We confirmed induction of RARβ-target genes, nuclear localization of RARβ and neurite outgrowth with PC12 cells. The study presents a new formulation of CsNp as a delivery system of synthetic RARβ-agonists, which is potentially relevant not only for the treatment of subacute SCI but also for other pathologies of the central nervous system where local and sustained pharmacological activity is desired.

items.title: Modeling postpartum depression in rodents: from established paradigms to emerging methodological innovations.
items.abstract: Background Postpartum depression (PPD) is a complex and heterogeneous disorder that cannot be fully explained by a single pathogenic mechanism. Rodent models have been instrumental in dissecting the contribution of endocrine dysregulation, stress exposure, and altered maternal adaptation. However, their translational value may be limited when these factors are studied separately. New method This narrative review examines how classical PPD animal models can be complemented by emerging approaches that better capture the multiple biological pathways underlying postpartum vulnerability. Recent models have focused on neurosteroid-sensitive GABAergic signaling, immune and metabolic alterations, developmental stress exposure, and the biological determinants of individual susceptibility. Results Genetic, epigenetic, and circuit-level approaches offer new opportunities to investigate the mechanisms contributing to PPD-like phenotypes and to clarify why similar perinatal challenges may lead to different outcomes across individuals. Comparison with existing methods Emerging approaches should not replace classical models but rather complement them. Traditional single-trigger paradigms are useful for isolating specific mechanisms, including hypothalamic-pituitary-adrenal axis dysregulation, impaired neuroplasticity, and altered maternal behavior. Used alone, however, they lack construct validity for PPD unless combined with pre-existing susceptibility factors. Newer models are better suited to capturing the heterogeneity and multifactorial nature of PPD. Nonetheless, their diversity and limited standardization continue to hinder cross-study comparisons. Conclusions Future research should integrate established and emerging models within mechanism-based, multi-hit designs. Combining behavioral assessment with endocrine, immune, metabolic, molecular, and circuit-level measures may improve translational validity, facilitate biomarker identification, and support the development of more targeted preventive and therapeutic strategies for PPD.

items.title: Correlative mapping of fiber architecture and myelin organization across length scales using X-ray scattering and polarized light imaging.
items.abstract: We combine scanning small- and wide-angle X-ray scattering (SAXS/WAXS) with three-dimensional polarized light imaging (3D-PLI) to establish a correlative framework for probing myelin-rich brain tissue in sagittal sections of a blue-and-yellow macaw (Ara ararauna). From the lamellar Bragg peaks of compact myelin, SAXS provides quantitative maps of a myelin-related peak area, the local repeat distance, and the in-plane fiber orientation extracted from the azimuthal anisotropy of the myelin peak. 3D-PLI provides high-resolution maps of in-plane fiber orientation together with a retardation-based contrast. After alignment and resolution matching, we find strong agreement between the SAXS- and 3D-PLI-derived orientation fields in white-matter regions. This agreement anchors the scattering-derived parameters in the context of nerve tissue. Beyond orientation validation, the correlative dataset separates complementary myelin descriptors across length scales: SAXS maps the myelin-related peak area and nanoscale repeat distance, while WAXS in the cerebellar region of interest adds an additional descriptor of lipid-chain packing. Combined with layer-dependent low-q scattering contrasts that reflect mesoscale density fluctuations, these maps link tract architecture to myelin ultrastructure and molecular order. STATEMENT OF SIGNIFICANCE: Myelin is a multilayered biological membrane whose function depends not only on how nerve fibers are arranged but also on nanoscale membrane spacing and lipid packing. These features are usually measured separately. Here, we combine three-dimensional polarized light imaging with scanning small- and wide-angle X-ray scattering in the same brain sections. We find agreement between the optical and X-ray estimates of in-plane fiber orientation and obtain complementary maps of myelin-related peak area, lamellar repeat distance and lipid-chain packing signatures. By relating these structural measurements to the same fiber tracts, the approach provides a basis for studying how myelin organization changes during development, aging and neurological disease.

items.title: Spine shortening osteotomy improves gait quality after one year in tethered cord syndrome: a retrospective case series.
items.abstract: Objective Tethered cord release (TCR) remains the gold standard treatment for tethered cord syndrome (TCS), yet repeat TCRs often fail to restore neurological function. Spine shortening osteotomy (SSO) has been proposed as an alternative for revision untethering or complex tethering anatomies, but its effect on ambulatory performance has not been quantified. This study evaluates whether SSO improves walking function in patients with recurrent or complex TCS using instrumented gait analysis (IGA). Methods A retrospective cohort of all patients undergoing SSO at Amsterdam Medical Centre between 2012 and 2022 was assembled. Indications were revision surgery or anatomically complex tethering. Preoperative and 12-month postoperative gait assessments employed two-dimensional IGA. Standardized video recordings yielded the Edinburgh Visual Gait Score (EVGS), walking speed, and kinematic variables . Results SSO was performed in 12 patients (mean age 38 ± 14 years); complete gait data were available for nine. Median EVGS improved significantly from 13 to 7 (Wilcoxon signed-rank test, z = -2.38, p = 0.018). Walking speed increased not significantly by 0.10 m.s -1 (z = -1.661, p = 0.097), four patients (44%) experienced a clinically meaningful gain >= 0.1 m.s -1 . No significant changes were observed in secondary kinematic parameters. Conclusions SSO provided improvement in gait quality in patients with recurrent or complex TCS, while effects on speed are heterogeneous. Limitations include the small, heterogeneous cohort and reliance on 2-D analysis. Larger, multicenter studies are needed to confirm these findings, refine patient selection, and inform guideline development for SSO in TCS.
