items.title: Switching between singleton-detection and feature-search mode in visual search.
items.abstract: There has long been a debate in visual search about whether attentional capture is determined by top-down search settings or by the structure of the search process itself. We addressed this issue in two experiments in which participants searched for the same target shape, while the dominant trial context biased the search mode toward either feature search or singleton detection. To assess whether multiple items were processed in parallel or more serially, we also included a two-target compatibility manipulation, in which some trials contained two targets associated with either compatible or incompatible responses. In Experiment 1, most trials (10/11) contained heterogeneous displays, which required participants to adopt the feature-search mode to locate the target. In Experiment 2, most trials contained homogeneous displays, allowing participants to rely on singleton detection to locate the target. On a minority of trials (1/11), the opposite display type was presented, allowing us to test whether the dominant search strategy would persist across changing displays. The results showed strong contextual persistence. When heterogeneous displays predominated, search was slow, Target-Target Compatibility effects were absent, and salient distractors failed to capture attention, even on homogeneous display trials in which singleton-detection mode could in principle be used. When homogeneous displays predominated, allowing singleton-detection mode to be adopted, search was faster, compatibility effects emerged, and salient distractors captured attention across trial types. These findings suggest that attentional capture depends on the mode of processing induced by the predominant display context, rather than on the properties of the current display alone. items.title: Social sharing of emotions: Links between emotion regulation strategies and diurnal cortisol.
items.abstract: Daily social sharing of emotions during self-disclosure with close others is crucial for understanding social emotion regulation. Cortisol, the end product of the hypothalamic-pituitary-adrenal axis, is closely linked to social stress and emotion regulation processes. This study examined the associations between diurnal cortisol and multiple context-specific emotion regulation strategies (reappraisal, co-rumination, and suppression) reported during in-person social sharing of emotions with close others in daily life. We analyzed data from a larger study (September 2022-April 2024) of 153 friendship dyads (Mage = 20.01, SD = 2.65; 71% female; 82% White) who provided daily self-reports and morning and nighttime saliva samples for 1 week. Analyses revealed divergent patterns across levels of analysis. At the between-person level, those who reported higher suppression when socially sharing emotions across the study period displayed lower average night cortisol. In contrast, at the within-person level, greater-than-usual suppression when socially sharing emotions was characterized by higher night cortisol and, consequently, a flatter diurnal cortisol slope. Neither co-rumination nor reappraisal was linked to diurnal cortisol. All results were robust after controlling for relevant covariates. The current findings highlight the importance of assessing multiple emotion regulation strategies in the context of socially sharing emotions with close others in daily life and their associations with diurnal cortisol at between- and within-person levels over time. Future work is warranted to examine underlying mechanisms and extend the generalizability of the current findings. (PsycInfo Database Record (c) 2026 APA, all rights reserved).

items.title: Feasibility of the iQuit mindfully smoking cessation app among adults with low socioeconomic status.
items.abstract: This study evaluated the feasibility and acceptability of the iQuit Mindfully app for smoking cessation among adults with low socioeconomic status (SES). In this 12-week feasibility study, 62 adults with low SES (58% female, 94% annual household income <200% federal poverty level, 48% White, 39% Black, Mage = 48) who smoked cigarettes and wanted to quit were randomly assigned to iQuit Mindfully (n = 38) or the National Cancer Institute QuitGuide app (n = 24). Whereas participants in both conditions provided positive feedback, iQuit Mindfully participants uniquely highlighted the benefits of mindfulness for managing stress and cravings. Benchmarks for retention (80%; actual 93%) and acceptability (7 on a 1-10 scale) were exceeded. iQuit Mindfully participants were more likely to recommend the app (M = 8.5 vs. 7.6) and perceived greater app helpfulness (M = 7.4 vs. 6.5) compared to QuitGuide. The benchmark for iQuit Mindfully app module completion (75% to complete five of eight modules) was not met (58%), and participants suggested more notifications, reminders, and interactivity. Among participants with expired carbon monoxide data, 21.2% of iQuit Mindfully participants (seven of 33) achieved 7-day abstinence at Week 8 versus 13.6% of QuitGuide participants (three of 22). At Week 12, 28.1% of iQuit Mindfully participants (nine of 32) and 22.7% of QuitGuide participants (five of 22) achieved carbon monoxide-confirmed abstinence. Results support the acceptability of the iQuit Mindfully app for adults with low SES. Participant feedback will be used to improve the app with the long-term goal to provide accessible smoking cessation support for low-SES adults. items.title: Major depressive disorder involves motivational conflicts in emotion regulation in daily life.
items.abstract: What do individuals with major depressive disorder (MDD) want to achieve when regulating their emotions? The answer has not been clear, given that some evidence suggests they are more motivated and other evidence suggests they are less motivated to feel better, than healthy controls are. Tracking emotion regulation in an ecological momentary assessment study in individuals with MDD (N = 94) and in healthy individuals (N = 90), and using multilevel modeling, we demonstrated that compared with healthy individuals, those with MDD were more likely to experience motivational conflicts (i.e., they endorsed competing goals) in emotion regulation in daily life. Joint frequency analyses showed that compared with healthy individuals, individuals with MDD wanted to both decrease and increase unpleasant emotions more frequently. They were also more motivated to increase and decrease pleasant emotions. Such motivational conflicts carried negative implications. The more individuals with MDD experienced motivational conflicts in emotion regulation, the more severe their clinical symptoms became over time. In follow-up semistructured interviews on experienced conflict and attraction to sadness, individuals with MDD explicitly reported experiencing conflict in emotion regulation more often than healthy individuals, and being more attracted to sadness. Thematic analyses validated by a large language model revealed that, when individuals with MDD were attracted to sadness, they were more likely to describe it as self-consistent. Healthy individuals were more likely to describe sadness as appropriate or useful in the situation. Motivational conflicts in emotion regulation may exacerbate distress and impair success in emotion regulation in MDD. (PsycInfo Database Record (c) 2026 APA, all rights reserved).

items.title: Experiences of Breastfeeding and Body Image for New Mothers Who Restrict Their Diet to Lose Weight in the United Kingdom - A Qualitative Exploration.
items.abstract: This qualitative study explored the experiences of mothers who breastfed whilst restricting their diet. Online semi-structured interviews were conducted with 10 UK-based mothers who had given birth in the last 3 years and had breastfed their child/ren while restricting their diet to lose weight. Data were analysed using interpretative phenomenological analysis, and three group experiential themes were developed. Navigating internal and external expectations of body image explores the divergent experiences of body image during pregnancy and the societal and cultural pressures to return to a pre-baby body. Balancing maternal and infant needs examines the ways in which the demands of motherhood limited the mothers' opportunities for diet and exercise. It also illustrates the ways in which the mothers navigated feelings of hunger and how they balanced the nutritional requirements of breastfeeding and their desire to restrict their food intake. Unmet health needs and a search for information evidences the limited opportunities that women had to discuss dietary restriction with healthcare professionals and how they engaged in self-directed research. It is argued that proactive, individualised, and non-judgemental healthcare is required to support women who restrict their diet whilst breastfeeding.

items.title: Multi-country RCT of a Systematically-Optimised, Remotely-Delivered Five-Session Parenting Intervention with Parents of Young Children with Conduct Problems.
items.abstract: Parenting programs are a recommended strategy to improve parenting skills and reduce disruptive behaviours but access to services is limited in North Macedonia, Republic of Moldova and Romania. We adapted a parenting program to this context, systematically optimized it and predicted positive change on child disruptive behaviours and several secondary domains compared to a lecture-only group. We conducted a multi-site randomized controlled trial of a remotely delivered group-based parenting intervention (5 sessions, n = 415 caregivers) against an online group lecture (1 session, n = 408 caregivers) in these three countries with 823 (primarily female) caregivers of children aged 2-9 years with elevated levels of behavioural difficulties (ClinicalTrials.gov: NCT04721730, https://clinicaltrials.gov/study/NCT04721730). We randomized with a 1:1 ratio; partially masked outcome assessors, data analysts and 4 assessment points; pre: between 7 December 2020 and 17 May 2021, followed by program delivery with 4-month post-intervention assessment (25.0% dropout), and 12-month follow-up-assessment (35.0% dropout). Intention-to-treat analyses demonstrated small positive post-intervention effects on primary outcomes: reduced child aggressive behaviours (ß =0.15, SE = -1.40, p = .026, d = -0.30, 95% CI [-0.57, -0.04]), Oppositional Defiant Disorder/Conduct Disorder rates (4/135 [3.0%] vs. 5/112 [4.5%] in lecture group, rate ratio = 0.66, 95% CI [0.18, -2.46]), and a larger change in slope in the last 24-hour daily reports during intervention (p = .004, d = -0.37, 95% CI [-0.62, -0.11]). Primary outcome effects were not sustained at 12-month follow-up implying effort is needed to determine how to sustain effects longer-term of digitally delivered interventions in low resource contexts.

items.title: Sensorimotor impairment and cognitive function across the Alzheimer's disease continuum and major depressive disorder.
items.abstract: Sensorimotor impairments are associated with cognitive decline, but their cumulative burden across clinical subgroups is not well characterized. To test whether sensorimotor burden is associated with baseline cognition and modifies subgroup-related cognitive differences. We analyzed 511 community-dwelling older adults. Participants were classified as cognitively normal, preclinical Alzheimer's disease (Clinical Dementia Rating score of 0 with amyloid positron-emission tomography positivity), mild cognitive impairment, or major depressive disorder. Cognition was measured with the Preclinical Alzheimer Cognitive Composite. A Sensorimotor Index summed impairments in grip strength, gait speed, reaction time, hearing, vision, and olfaction and was categorized as low (0-1) or elevated (≥ 2). Multivariable linear regression assessed subgroup, index, and subgroup-by-index terms, adjusting for age, sex, race, education, apolipoprotein E ε4 status, and neighborhood deprivation. Without interactions, elevated burden was associated with lower cognitive scores (β =- 0.374; 95% confidence interval, - 0.508 to - 0.240; p < 0.001). In the interaction model, the mild cognitive impairment-by-elevated-index (β =- 0.647; 95% confidence interval, - 0.981 to - 0.313; p < 0.001) and major depressive disorder-by-elevated-index terms (β =- 0.440; 95% confidence interval, - 0.759 to - 0.120; p = 0.007) were significant; the preclinical Alzheimer's disease interaction was not. Dose-response analyses showed progressively lower cognitive scores at higher index levels. Greater sensorimotor burden was associated with lower cognition, with stronger adverse associations in mild cognitive impairment and major depressive disorder. Multidomain sensorimotor assessment may improve characterization of cognitive heterogeneity in older adults.

items.title: The Co-Development of Socioeconomic Trajectories and Mathematics Motivation in Adolescence.
items.abstract: Moving beyond prior research that has primarily focused on socioeconomic differences in the development of academic motivation, this study examined how socioeconomic and motivational trajectories co-develop across adolescence and whether this co-development varies across different dimensions of SES and forms of motivation. Five-year longitudinal data were drawn from 3,684 Chinese students (at baseline: Mage = 9.73, SDage = 0.54; 48.0% female), who were tracked across three assessment waves in Grade 4, Grade 6, and Grade 9. Parallel latent growth models were used to examine changes in objective SES (indexed by household income) and subjective SES (indexed by perceived standing relative to classmates) alongside intrinsic motivation, identified regulation, and controlled motivation in mathematics. Results showed that increases in objective SES were not associated with changes in any form of motivation. In contrast, slower declines in subjective SES co-occurred with slower declines in autonomous forms of motivation (i.e., intrinsic motivation and identified regulation), but not controlled motivation. Rather, controlled motivation was more closely associated with adolescents' initial socioeconomic position, with socioeconomic differences in controlled motivation becoming less pronounced over time. These findings highlight that socioeconomic trajectories and mathematics motivation did not uniformly co-develop; rather, developmental co-variation was particularly evident between subjective SES and the autonomous forms of motivation, suggesting that interventions on educational inequality must actively target how youth interpret their social standing and academic opportunities.

items.title: Validation and Likelihood-Ratio Calibration of the Italian Ritvo Autism Asperger Diagnostic Scale-Revised (RAADS-R).
items.abstract: Italian psychometric evidence on the RAADS-R has been limited. This case-control validation examined the reliability, structure, and measurement invariance of the Italian RAADS-R, its discrimination between autistic and non-autistic adults with candidate cut-offs and likelihood-ratio (LR) bands, subscale contributions, gender differences, and AQ convergence. Sample 1 comprised 376 autistic adults referred to a specialized adult-autism service and diagnosed by blind multidisciplinary assessment, compared with 376 self-declared non-autistic community adults; Sample 2 comprised 354 adults with self-reported previously established diagnoses and 354 comparison adults, matched on age within gender. Analyses covered reliability, CFA/bifactor/ESEM structure, invariance, ROC analysis with cross-sample threshold application, LR bands, a Group × Gender MANCOVA, and AQ convergence. Internal consistency was excellent (ω = 0.98); a strong general factor (ωh = 0.96-0.97) indicated that the DSM-5 subscales describe content rather than distinct dimensions. In Sample 1, AUC was 0.91 and the candidate cut-off of 92 gave sensitivity 0.89 and specificity 0.81; Sample 2 yielded 104 (sensitivity 0.94, specificity 0.77). Across samples, 92 favored sensitivity and 104 specificity. Four LR bands graded the score (≤ 70, 71-91, 92-136, ≥ 137). Autistic women reported higher sensory scores than men, with item-level invariance supported. RAADS-R and AQ totals correlated strongly (r = .86). The Italian RAADS-R is a reliable screening aid within multidisciplinary assessment. Because accuracy was estimated against community adults, the cut-offs and LR bands are preliminary, require validation in consecutive clinical samples, and should not be used to rule out autism when clinical suspicion exists.

items.title: Semantic flexibility across adulthood: a novel polysemy-based task and preliminary reference data in Italian adults.
items.abstract: Semantic cognition requires access to stored conceptual knowledge and flexible retrieval according to contextual demands. Conventional verbal fluency tasks do not directly assess the ability to generate multiple meanings of the same lexical item. This study developed a novel polysemy-based task and examined demographic influences on semantic flexibility in healthy Italian adults. One hundred and fifty neurologically healthy adults aged 20-69 years, evenly distributed across five age groups and balanced by sex, generated distinct meanings for 12 familiar Italian polysemous words. Outcomes included a Global Score, total valid meanings, completion time, Single-Meaning Responses (SMRs), and errors. Age, education, and sex effects were examined using ANCOVA and multiple regression. Preliminary demographic adjustments and Equivalent Scores were derived. Education was the strongest predictor of Global Score and total meanings. Age showed a small positive association with both measures, whereas sex was not significant. Completion time showed a non-linear age pattern. SMRs varied with age and education, while other error categories showed limited demographic variability. The age- and education-based model explained 25.0% of Global Score variance and was used to derive preliminary adjusted reference values. The polysemy-based task provides a novel approach to assessing flexible retrieval of alternative meanings within the same lexical item. Performance was mainly influenced by education, with no age-related decline in overall semantic production. The study represents an initial reference-data step rather than a clinical validation; therefore, Equivalent Scores should not be interpreted as diagnostic cut-offs. Further psychometric and clinical validation is required before diagnostic use.

items.title: Preparing Rather Than Predicting: The Role of Psychosocial Assessment in Adolescent Bariatric Surgery.
items.abstract: BackgroundPsychological assessment is a standard component of adolescent metabolic and bariatric surgery (MBS) evaluation. Contemporary guidelines emphasize psychosocial assessment as a tool to identify vulnerabilities, assess readiness, and guide individualized support rather than predict surgical success. We sought to evaluate associations between preoperative psychosocial questionnaire scores and short-term postoperative outcomes after MBS.MethodsWe performed a retrospective cohort study of adolescents undergoing MBS at a single institution between 2018 and 2023. Patients completed validated psychosocial assessments including the SCL-90-R, BESAA, and TRAQ as part of routine preoperative evaluation. Associations between questionnaire scores, demographics, and postoperative outcomes were evaluated. Six-month percent total body weight loss (%TBWL) was analyzed as a continuous outcome with linear regression and binary outcomes with modified Poisson regression.ResultsEighty adolescents met inclusion criteria (median age 16.9 years; 67.5% female; median BMI 51.5 kg/m2). Six-month weight was available for 45 patients (56%). In exploratory analyses, nominal associations were observed between demographic characteristics and psychosocial questionnaire findings; however, none remained significant after adjustment for multiple comparisons (lowest q = 0.079). None of the questionnaire scores was associated with six-month %TBWL, loss to follow-up, or postoperative vitamin adherence (all P ≥ 0.13).ConclusionPreoperative psychosocial questionnaire scores were not associated with short-term postoperative outcomes after adolescent MBS. These findings support the evolving role of psychosocial assessment as a mechanism for identifying vulnerabilities and informing individualized behavioral health support rather than predicting surgical success.

items.title: Documented Human Implementation of NIH SBIR/STTR-Funded Neurosurgical Technologies: A Retrospective Cohort Study
items.abstract: Background: Federal small business awards from the National Institutes of Health fund neurosurgical devices and procedural technologies, but how often the specific funded capability reaches human use is unknown. We determined how often these technologies had documented human implementation and in which settings. Methods: We assembled a retrospective public-source cohort of technologies supported by Small Business Innovation Research and Small Business Technology Transfer awards from fiscal years 2005–2020 by keyword filtering and funded-purpose review. Confirmation required living-human use of the funded capability or a supported direct extension after a qualifying same-technology award, with public evidence by October 8, 2026. Exploratory comparisons examined program, observed phase, award era, and cumulative support. A 500-family random sample assessed screening omissions. Results: The cohort comprised 209 technologies, 221 award families, and 453 applications receiving $206,825,343. Human implementation was documented for 31/209 technologies (14.8%; Wilson 95% confidence interval, 10.7%–20.3%); evidence was not located for 156 and was indeterminate for 22. Confirmed settings were neurosurgical-scope care (26), other clinical care (2), mixed surgical cohorts (1), and nonclinical human evaluation (2). Confirmation was more frequent with observed Phase II support than Phase I only (21/98 vs 10/111; difference, 12.4 percentage points; company-component bootstrap 95% confidence interval, 2.8–22.4). None of four conventional tests met a Holm-adjusted .05 threshold. Screening scenarios estimated 40–76 omitted families. Conclusion: Approximately one in seven included technologies had documented human implementation. Linking individual awards to implemented capabilities provides an empirical benchmark for early neurosurgical translation and a practical foundation for tracking subsequent clinical evaluation.

items.title: Beyond National Averages: Social Contact Patterns in the Upper Midwest
items.abstract: Background: Social contact surveys measure how individuals interact with each other, which directly influences disease transmission dynamics. The COVID-19 pandemic substantially altered how people live and work, highlighting the need for up-to-date and sub-national estimates of social contact patterns to inform disease modeling and public health planning. Methods: The Midwest Analytics & Disease Modeling Center (MADMC) conducted an opt-in social contact survey of upper Midwest residents, with about 60% of participants drawn from Minnesota. Participants reported all interpersonal contacts during the previous day, including the age of their contacts allowing for the analysis of mixing patterns. Detailed demographic information about the participants was also collected, allowing for additional subgroup analyses of contact patterns. Results: Participants in our sample had an average of 6.8 contacts per day (IQR: 2.0 - 8.0), which is within the range of recent post-pandemic US national and European estimates. Contacts varied across demographic groups, with those attending work or school in-person reporting the highest number of contacts. Mixing across most age group pairs was a little lower than in comparable national survey except for younger age groups, who had substantially higher rates of contact with same-age peers. Differences in the contact matrices alone were associated with a 6.7% difference in estimated basic reproduction number(R0). Near the epidemic threshold, even this modest difference could meaningfully affect transmission dynamics. These effects may be amplified or attenuated by pathogen-specific age patterns of susceptibility and infectiousness, leading to larger or smaller differences in R0 estimates derived from national versus regional mixing patterns. Conclusions: These findings provide empirical evidence on post-pandemic social contact patterns in the United States and highlight the potential implications of regional variation in social mixing for infectious disease transmission. The mean 6.8 daily contacts is consistent with evidence of persistent changes in daily routines following the pandemic. Incorporating contemporary, region-specific contact patterns into transmission models may improve their ability to capture geographic variation in transmission risk and inform epidemic forecasting.

items.title: Mobile money vendors as a community channel for adolescent condom provision and sexual health information in Uganda: a type-II hybrid effectiveness-implementation study
items.abstract: Purpose: Unmarried adolescents in Uganda have limited access to sexual and reproductive health (SRH) services, and conventional programs have struggled to reach them sustainably. Mobile money vendors (MMVs) are ubiquitous in young people's daily lives. We assessed the feasibility of an MMV-based intervention to provide condoms and SRH information to adolescents. Methods: In this type-II hybrid effectiveness-implementation study in Eastern Uganda, 30 MMVs provided oral and printed information, free condoms, and referrals for four months in 2024. Feasibility was assessed using the Bowen framework, drawing on service logs, baseline and endline surveys of adolescents aged 15-19 years (n = 1,204), three focus group discussions with MMVs, eight key informant interviews, a post-intervention MMV survey, and supervision reports. Results: MMVs recorded 104,849 adolescent customer visits; oral information was provided at 54,365 visits and condoms at 21,056 visits. Condom use in the intervention arm increased from 67.3% to 77.7% (p = 0.04), and the proportion obtaining condoms from MMVs rose from 0% to 64.6%. Adolescents valued the service's convenience and confidentiality. Initial resistance from some community adults largely diminished, although referrals remained few (210 cases). All MMV shops completed the intervention without disrupting business, and customer numbers and sales rose 1.64- and 1.50-fold. Suggested adaptations included vendor identification and services for girls, integration with public health systems for scalability. Conclusions: The MMV-based approach was feasible and reached hard-to-access unmarried adolescents with condoms and SRH information. For scale-up, improvements for adaptation and large-scale evaluation are necessary.

items.title: How Far to Perinatal Care? Open Drive-Time Measures to Delivering Hospitals, Perinatal Substance Use Treatment, and Health Centers for Every U.S. County, with Rural and Frontier Estimates
items.abstract: Counting facilities inside county lines does not show how far a pregnant or postpartum woman must travel for care. We built the Rural and Frontier Perinatal Care Access Layer, an open, versioned dataset that measures, for all 3,144 counties of the 50 states and the District of Columbia, the share of women aged 15–44 who live more than 30 and more than 60 minutes’ drive from three types of care: a hospital providing inpatient labor and delivery care (2,424 hospitals confirmed in Centers for Medicare & Medicaid Services, CMS, maternal health data), a substance use disorder (SUD) treatment facility with a program for pregnant or postpartum women (4,600 FindTreatment.gov listings), and a federally funded health center site (11,769). Drive times run from 239,741 population-weighted Census block group centers over a national OpenStreetMap road graph of 24.4 million points, using the speed rules of the Open Source Routing Machine (OSRM) car profile and an exact multi-source shortest-path search, and are weighted by the 66.0 million women aged 15–44 counted in the 2020–2024 American Community Survey. Nationally, 91.0% of women live within 30 minutes of a delivering hospital and 99.0% within 60 minutes, but the median frontier woman drives 43.3 minutes and 34.1% of frontier women live more than an hour away. Perinatal SUD treatment is the least accessible of the three: 13.3% of rural and 53.4% of frontier women live more than an hour from it, and in 556 rural or frontier counties most women do. 108 counties, 101 of them frontier, have most women more than an hour from all three care types. Because CMS does not report delivery status for many critical access hospitals, we also bound the hospital measure from above; the upper bound roughly halves the frontier share beyond an hour (15.8%). A check of 450 randomly drawn trips against the public OSRM server on the same roads gave a median time ratio of 0.992 and 99.1% agreement on the 60-minute cutoff, and the national mean drive to a delivering hospital (14.0 minutes) matches a published estimate from a commercial network (14.1 minutes). The data, code, routing method notes, and quality report are openly released (doi:10.5281/zenodo.24206837).

items.title: Clustering of Maternal and Perinatal Complications Following Fresh and Frozen Embryo Transfer in First-Time Mothers: A Population-Based Cohort Study.
items.abstract: To assess how often women who give birth following frozen-thawed embryo transfer (frozen-ET), fresh embryo transfer (fresh-ET) and natural conception (NC) have pregnancies without maternal and perinatal complications, develop a single complication, or experience multiple complications. A population-based cohort study. Denmark (2008-2014), Norway (2008-2015) and Sweden (2008-2015). Restricted to singleton pregnancies among first-time mothers, this study included 6634 deliveries after frozen-ET, 25 660 after fresh-ET and 523 277 after NC. The following complications were studied: stillbirth, neonatal death (0-27 days after delivery), preterm birth (gestational age +22% from the expected birthweight according to sex and gestational age), low birthweight (< 2500 g), macrosomia (≥ 4500 g), Apgar score < 5 at 5 min, major birth defects, hypertensive disorders in pregnancy, placenta previa and placental abruption. In first-time mothers, three of every four singleton pregnancies after frozen-ET and fresh-ET were without maternal and perinatal complications, compared to four of every five pregnancies after NC. In pregnancies with neonatal survival ≥ 28 days (99.3% after frozen-ET, 99.3% after fresh-ET, and 99.5% after NC), two or more complications affected one in 11 pregnancies after frozen-ET and fresh-ET, compared to one in 16 after NC. In this study, we observed that most first-time mothers experienced pregnancies without maternal and perinatal complications following ART, and when complications occurred, they were typically without additional complications. Although single and multiple complications were more common following ART than after NC, the absolute differences were small. These findings may help set realistic expectations when counselling people who consider ART treatment, or those already in treatment.

items.title: Rapid forensic THC determination in cannabis plant material: A proof-of-concept study of low-power microwave drying.
items.abstract: Forensic laboratories frequently require quantification of THC in seized cannabis plant material on a dry weight basis, but conventional air drying may require prolonged preparation times, delaying forensic reporting. This paired pilot study evaluated whether low-power microwave drying could provide neutral THC measurements showing agreement with conventional oven drying while substantially reducing preparation time. Fresh material from 20 cannabis plants was split into matched aliquots and dried by ambient air, laboratory oven (80°C, 10 min), or microwave (70 W, 2-3 min). Samples were analyzed by GC-MS (identification) and GC-FID (quantification). The analytical endpoint was neutral THC; THCA and total potential THC were not determined. Mean THC percentages were 0.898% (air), 0.829% (oven), and 0.802% (microwave). Drying method effect was significant (Friedman χ2 = 10.47, p = 0.0053; ANOVA F(2,38) = 13.19, p < 0.001). For microwave versus oven drying, the mean difference was -0.027 percentage points (95% CI -0.057 to 0.003; p = 0.073). Bland-Altman bias was -0.027 with 95% limits of agreement from -0.152 to 0.098, and ICC(A,1) was 0.975 (95% CI: 0.938-0.991). Strict equivalence within ±0.05 percentage points was not established (TOST p = 0.061). Microwave drying substantially shortened preparation time and produced neutral THC measurements showing close agreement with oven drying under the tested conditions, although equivalence was not established. It may be useful for rapid preliminary assessment, but prospective validation-including residual-moisture determination, temperature monitoring, broader cannabinoid profiling, and full analytical validation-is required before confirmatory forensic use.

items.title: Australian and New Zealand Living Guidelines for Cochlear Implantation in Adults: A Consensus-Based and Evidence-Informed Guideline Adaptation Process.
items.abstract: Cochlear implantation is an established, effective intervention for adults with moderately severe to profound hearing loss. Despite strong evidence of benefit, access to adult cochlear implantation in Australia and New Zealand (ANZ) has been limited and inconsistent, with variation in referral practices, candidacy evaluation, and outcome assessment. In 2023, the Global Living Guidelines for adult cochlear implantation were published and provided a framework for regional adaptation. The ANZ Hearing Health Collaborative (ANZ HHC) convened a multidisciplinary working group to adapt the Global Living Guidelines for the ANZ context. Over 18 months, the group used an ADAPTE-informed process and a modified Delphi approach across five virtual workshops, incorporating multidisciplinary representation, lived experience input, anonymous voting, peer review, public consultation and endorsement. The adapted ANZ Living Guidelines provide consensus-based, evidence-informed recommendations across four domains: referral for cochlear implant (CI) evaluation, CI evaluation, candidacy recommendation and outcome evaluation. The recommendations retain alignment with the global evidence base while incorporating ANZ-specific service delivery, funding, and workforce considerations. Final endorsement exceeded 80% agreement across hearing health respondents. The ANZ Living Guidelines for Cochlear Implantation in Adults are the first regionally endorsed consensus framework for adult CI care across ANZ. This adaptation process provides a transparent and reproducible model for contextualising global living guidelines while supporting equitable, standardised, patient-centred care.

items.title: Polish Cross-Cultural Adaptation and Preliminary Psychometric Evaluation of the Left Ventricular Assist Device Self-Care Behaviour Scale: A Cross-Sectional Study.
items.abstract: To cross-culturally adapt the Left Ventricular Assist Device Self-Care Behaviour Scale into Polish and obtain preliminary evidence on its psychometric properties in patients supported with a left ventricular assist device. Cross-sectional, single-centre psychometric evaluation study. Following forward-backward translation, multidisciplinary expert review and cognitive debriefing, the Polish version of the 20-item scale was administered to 48 adult patients supported with a left ventricular assist device. Internal consistency was assessed using Cronbach's alpha and McDonald's omega. Item-level construct evidence was explored using multitrait scaling, inter-subscale correlations and exploratory known-groups comparisons with correction for multiple testing. Confirmatory factor analysis was not performed because of the limited sample size. Monitoring and device self-care showed acceptable internal-consistency point estimates, whereas heart failure self-care was borderline. Item-level evidence was mixed, with cross-domain overlap for several items and inter-subscale associations provided only limited support for domain separation. Pronounced ceiling effects were present, particularly for device-related items. Education-related differences in heart failure self-care and total score remained significant after correction for multiple testing, whereas differences by support duration and therapeutic indication did not. This study provides a developer-approved Polish cross-cultural adaptation of the scale with preliminary psychometric evidence. Larger multicentre studies are needed to establish factorial validity, temporal stability, external convergent validity and responsiveness before the scale is used as a validated longitudinal outcome measure. The translated scale may support structured assessment and discussion of self-reported self-care behaviours in clinical follow-up, but repeated scores should not yet be interpreted as reliable longitudinal change or treatment effect. What problem did the study address? No Polish-language version of the scale had published psychometric evidence, limiting standardised assessment of self-care behaviour in patients supported with a left ventricular assist device. What were the main findings? Internal consistency was acceptable for Monitoring and device self-care and borderline for heart failure self-care; item-level construct evidence was mixed and ceiling effects in device-related items were pronounced. Where and on whom will the research have an impact? The findings are relevant to nurses, clinicians and researchers caring for Polish-speaking patients supported with a left ventricular assist device by providing a standardised translated version for structured assessment and further psychometric evaluation. This study adhered to the Strengthening the Reporting of Observational Studies in Epidemiology (STROBE) reporting guideline. No Patient or Public Contribution.

items.title: Rising rates of young people not in education, employment, or training explained by higher prevalence of self-reported ill health and psychological distress: a 15-year UK study.
items.abstract: Rising rates of young people Not in Education, Employment, or Training (NEET) in the United Kingdom (UK) have recently coincided with declining youth physical and mental health but no study has asked whether this reflects a growing proportion of young people with health problems (prevalence) or those with health problems becoming more likely to be NEET (penalty). Using 15 years of Understanding Society data (2009-23), we analysed 15,242 respondents aged 16-24 (66,160 observations). We employed three complementary approaches: descriptive trends, Blinder-Oaxaca-Kitagawa (BO) probit decomposition comparing 2009-2013 and 2019-2023 against a 2014-2018 reference period, and within-person Poisson models with lagged health status. Exposures included self-reported health conditions or disability (SRHD), psychological distress, diagnosed conditions and socio-demographic factors. NEET rates were lowest in 2014-18 (10.5-11.5%) and higher in 2009-13 (12-15%) and 2019-23 (15-16%). Higher prevalence of SRHD, psychological distress, diagnosed depression and multimorbidity explained changes in NEET prevalence across both the 2009-13 to 2014-2018 and 2014-18 to 2019-23 periods. No change in penalty was observed for any health variable across periods, except for an increase in the penalty for SRHD between the 2009-13 to 2014-18 periods. Rising NEET rates among UK youth are driven largely by more young people having physical and psychological ill health. Whilst labour market and education accommodations remain important, reducing NEET rates will require reversing the decline in youth health, not just accommodating it.

items.title: Community awareness, knowledge, attitudes, preventive behaviors, and intended responses to Ebola virus disease in Burao, Somaliland: implications for outbreak preparedness.
items.abstract: Understanding public awareness and responses to Ebola virus disease (EVD) may inform risk communication in settings without documented transmission. We assessed prior awareness among adults in Burao, Somaliland, and knowledge, attitudes, current behaviors, and hypothetical outbreak responses among those who had previously heard of EVD. A community-based cross-sectional survey was conducted from 2 June to 21 July 2026 among adults aged 18 years or older who had lived in Burao for at least 6 months. Of 788 consenting adults, all contributed to the awareness and perception analyses; 387 who had previously heard of EVD completed detailed modules. Scores were analyzed continuously using multivariable linear regression and sensitivity analyses using interviewer-clustered standard errors and fractional logistic models. No design weights or verified sampling primary sampling unit identifiers were available. Of 788 consenting adults, 387 (49.1%) had previously heard of EVD. Only this previously aware subgroup (n = 387) completed the knowledge, attitude, current-behavior, and intended-response modules. Their mean knowledge, favorable-attitude, and intended-response scores were 60.6% (SD 24.1), 67.0% (SD 14.0), and 73.3% (SD 19.6), respectively. Post-secondary education was associated with prior awareness (adjusted prevalence ratio 1.87, 95% CI 1.52-2.31). Recent EVD information and formal EVD education were associated with higher knowledge scores. Knowledge was positively associated with the favorable-attitude score, and both were associated with intended-response scores; these primary patterns persisted in interviewer-clustered and bounded-outcome sensitivity analyses. Of all 788 consenting adults, 602 (76.4%) supported additional public EVD education. Approximately half of respondents had previously heard of EVD. Knowledge, attitude, current-behavior, and intended-response estimates apply only to those with prior awareness and must not be interpreted as community-wide measures or verified outbreak readiness. Findings identify communication priorities but do not establish causal relationships or predict behavior during an outbreak.

items.title: Association of antiretroviral regimen changes and tuberculosis preventive therapy with all-cause mortality among adults on ART in a high-mobility primary care setting in Northwest Ethiopia: a retrospective cohort study.
items.abstract: To assess the association of antiretroviral therapy (ART) regimen changes and tuberculosis preventive therapy (TPT) with all-cause mortality among adults on ART at a primary health center in a high-mobility setting in Northwest Ethiopia. Retrospective cohort study. This study was conducted from October 31, 2013 to October 31, 2024 in Northwest Ethiopia, Chagni town. This town serves as a delivery point for a population characterized by mobility, including seasonal and migrant workers, and main route to the Grand Ethiopian Renaissance Dam. It has one primary hospital and one health center that provide health services, including free ART and preventive therapies for people living with HIV. Primary outcome was all-cause mortality. Time to event was measured from ART initiation to death or censoring. Secondary outcomes (determinants) were assessed using survival analysis. Multivariable Cox regression was applied to identify associations of variables. A total of 337 participants were included, with a mean (standard deviation) age of 40.32 (± 11.13) years. 44 (13.05%) died with incidence rate of 1.98 (95% CI 1.47-2.65) per 100-persons years of observation. The overall survival probability at the end of follow-up was 85.25%. In multivariable Cox regression analysis, no regimen changes (AHR: 12.68; 95% CI 4.2-38.2), non-receipt of TPT (AHR: 6.89; 95% CI 3.4-13.80), unsuppressed viral load (AHR: 4.25; 95% CI 1.87-9.65), and CD4 count (AHR: 0.996; 95% CI 0.994-0.998) were significantly associated with all-cause mortality. All-cause mortality remains substantial in this high-mobility primary care setting. Lack of documented ART regimen change and non-receipt of TPT were strongly associated with all-cause mortality. Unsuppressed viral load and low CD4 count were also independently associated with all-cause mortality. These findings highlight the importance of appropriate ART regimen management, TPT provision, and close monitoring of immunological and virological status in addition to conducting further longitudinal studies among adults on ART in high-mobility settings in Northwest Ethiopia.

items.title: Survival following 14% Plasmodium falciparum hyperparasitaemia: cerebral malaria and anaemic heart failure in a Nigerian toddler.
items.abstract: Malaria remains a leading cause of mortality amongst children under five in sub-Saharan Africa. Complicated Plasmodium falciparum malaria frequently presents with multiple life-threatening sequelae, including cerebral malaria, profound anaemia, and hyperparasitaemia. Although parasite densities exceeding 10% are independently associated with high mortality, achieving full recovery in a young child presenting with simultaneous extreme parasitaemia, deep coma, and severe malarial anaemia remains exceptionally noteworthy. We report the case of a 20-month-old male from Akoko, Ondo State, Nigeria, who presented with a five-day history of fever, cough, and diarrhoea, progressing to unconsciousness. Clinical examination revealed a Blantyre Coma Scale of 2/5, profound pallor, tachycardia (158 bpm), and tender hepatomegaly. Laboratory investigations confirmed an extreme 14% P. falciparum parasitaemia and a life-threatening packed cell volume of 8%. Cerebrospinal fluid analysis ruled out bacterial meningitis though an elevated protein level (71 mg/dL) supported the diagnosis of cerebral malaria. The patient was stabilised in the cardiac position to optimise venous return and alleviate signs of incipient heart failure, and was initiated on a multi-modal therapeutic regimen. Antimalarial therapy was commenced with intravenous artesunate (3 mg/kg), supported by two sessions of sedimented red blood cell transfusions and empiric IV Ceftriaxone. By the fourth day of treatment, the child regained full consciousness and was transitioned to oral artemether-lumefantrine. The patient was discharged in a stable condition on day seven with a recovered packed cell volume of 35%. This case highlights the critical importance of the "24-h window" in treating severe malaria. The successful outcome confirms the efficacy of intravenous artesunate and the necessity of aggressive supportive care-including blood transfusion-in managing the severe triad of hyperparasitaemia, cerebral sequestration, and severe anaemia in paediatric patients within endemic regions. This report emphasises the need for public health initiatives that educate caregivers on the early recognition of malaria symptoms to facilitate prompt care. Furthermore, it reaffirms that urgent microscopic evaluation remains the gold standard for the immediate diagnosis of hyperparasitaemic cases in resource-limited settings.

items.title: "I can definitely relate to that": leveraging peers with lived experience as interviewers in qualitative perinatal substance use research.
items.abstract: Peer interviewers are increasingly used in qualitative research to strengthen data collection, particularly when working with historically marginalized communities to foster trust and potentially elicit richer narratives. Yet the specific techniques by which peers shape the collection and quality of interview data remain underexplored. This study aims to examine how trained peer interviewers influenced the interview process across two perinatal substance use research studies. We conducted a secondary analysis of qualitative interview data from two U.S. studies (2021-2025) in which peer interviewers completed forty semi-structured interviews with pregnant, postpartum, and parenting people of color with a history of substance use disorder. Research coordinators independently reviewed all transcripts to identify exchanges where interviewer-interviewee dialogue included moments of rapport-building, emotional resonance, or personal reflection. Using a reflexive thematic analysis framework, we developed and refined a codebook, applied it across all excerpts, and integrated peer interviewer reflections to finalize themes. Three overarching themes appeared regarding the techniques peer interviewers used. First, peer interviewers built rapport and connection by referencing shared identities and experiences, using colloquial language, and pausing to check in on participant comfort. Second, peer interviewers used both empathetic validation (drawing on personal experience) and sympathetic validation (offering affirmation without explicit disclosure) to affirm participants' experiences or encourage deeper reflection. Third, peer interviewers proactively disclosed aspects of their identity either to clarify interview questions or to prompt more detailed participant responses, with personal disclosures frequently facilitating richer answers to questions. By describing specific interviewer techniques, specifically validation, disclosure, and rapport-building, we identified concrete, actionable guidance for future qualitative research teams seeking to integrate peer interviewers. These findings support the expansion of community-based participatory models that center lived experience and underscore the need for peer interviewer training programs that explicitly cultivate and reinforce these practices.

items.title: Bridging the gap in One Health: challenges at the diagnostic interface - laboratory insights on sample quality and stewardship.
items.abstract: The aim was to conduct an interface analysis to assess the sources and frequency of errors in the diagnostic workflows involved in handling human and animal microbiological samples. A web-based cross-sectional survey was conducted among German-speaking healthcare workers in human and veterinary medicine between 7th October 2022 and 14th July 2023. The data evaluated in this study focus on perceptions of microbiology laboratory staff responsible for specimen reception, processing, and interpretation (sample recipients, SR) in human and veterinary laboratories across both outpatient and inpatient settings in German-speaking countries. Based on the questionnaire sent out using the snowball method, 20 of the 166 questions were tailored to recipients of diagnostics and used for descriptive and statistical (t-tests, chi-square tests) data analysis. A total of 2,464 valid responses were analysed; 372 (15.1%) were identified as SR, with the largest group working in human medicine (HM) (n=166, 44.6%). Respondents estimated that 18.5 samples per 100 were incorrectly requested by HM, compared with 15.4 by veterinarians and 14.8 by medical technicians (MT). All professional groups consistently cited swabs as the most error-prone material. Respondents with over 10 years of experience more frequently reported that requests took over 60 minutes of post-processing time per day. However, this was not statistically significant. SR face substantial challenges due to insufficient information, communication gaps, and inconsistent sample quality. Effective diagnostic stewardship requires addressing these issues through interprofessional education, digital decision-support, and standardised test-requesting processes.

items.title: Designing a Locally Adapted Kader Educational Program to Improve Social Support for Women with Metastatic Breast Cancer in Indonesia.
items.abstract: The community-based program in Indonesia was established in 1970s through community health volunteer system, called Kader. Many efforts have been made to increase Kader's capacity for cancer care, yet existing programs are often short-term and unstructured, and they do not address the unique needs of people living with cancer. Despite the increasing number of people living with cancer, cadres' knowledge and confidence in supporting women with breast cancer in the community are low. This paper, part of the COMMUNICATED (community care for metastatic breast cancer), aimed to strengthen social support for women with breast cancer through Kader education. It describes the program development and some components of the first action phase. The program development involved three stages: (1) defining five competencies and introducing the term Kader TATAK (Tangguh dan Tanggap Kanker, Resilience and Responsive to Cancer) to strengthen role identity; (2) developing training program and materials; and (3) designing recruitment strategies and multisectoral collaboration. The first stage of action phase involved training facilitators and nurses buddies. It was followed by Kader training using a flipped learning approach. A total of 112 Kader from Yogyakarta and Bali participated. Kader's knowledge increased from 7.27 (SD = 1.81) to 8.89 (SD = 1.27) of 10 (Z = -7.19, p < 0.001), and self-confidence scores from 54.51 (SD = 14.82) to 66.06 (SD = 13.19) out of 85 (Z=-7.35, p < 0.001). The findings suggest that the program has potential to prepare Kader to provide social support for women with breast cancer in community settings. Further evaluation is needed to assess feasibility, transferability, and scalability across diverse settings.

items.title: Mental health care utilization among young black sexual minority men living with HIV at Ryan-white funded HIV care centers in Atlanta, Georgia.
items.abstract: Young Black sexual minority men (YB-SMM) living with HIV experience disproportionate mental health burdens, exacerbated by systemic inequities, stigma and structural determinants. Despite high rates of mental health symptoms, mental health service utilization remains low. We examined factors associated with mental health service utilization among YB-SMM receiving HIV care. We conducted a cross-sectional survey among 100 YB-SMM living with HIV recruited from two Ryan White-funded HIV clinics in a large Southeastern U.S. city. Participants completed validated measures assessing mental health care utilization, psychosocial factors and demographics. Logistic regression analyses examined associations with lifetime mental health provider use, desire for services in the past year and provider referral. Participants had a mean age of 25 years; 78% identified as gay, 49% experienced housing instability and 50% reported a history of incarceration. Overall, 51% had ever seen a mental health provider, 53% wanted mental health services in the past year; 40% received a provider referral; however, only 22% of the total sample attended a visit following referral. Lower income was associated with greater mental health service utilization among multiple outcomes. Greater non-organizational religious activity was associated with lifetime mental health provider use, depressive symptoms were associated with desire for services and higher trust in physicians was associated with provider referral. Mental health service interest was common, while provider and mental health service attendance were reported by fewer participants. Future work should examine how referral practices, provider availability and other service-level barriers influence mental health care engagement among YB-SMM living with HIV.

items.title: Barriers and Inequities in Access to Obstetric Analgesia during Labour: Implications for Latin America from a Scoping Review.
items.abstract: Equitable access to evidence-based pain relief during labour is a fundamental component of respectful maternity care. However, women in Latin America continue to face structural, sociocultural and health system barriers that limit access to desired pain management options. Evidence gaps remain in several countries. A scoping review was conducted following JBI methodology and PRISMA-ScR guidelines. Five electronic databases were searched for English and Spanish language publications from January 2010 to May 2026, complemented by snowball searching. The 2010 threshold was selected to capture contemporary health system reforms, with one earlier landmark study included by exception. Studies addressing access to obstetric analgesia in Latin America and conceptually relevant international evidence were included. Twenty-two studies were included. Evidence consistently identified that access to obstetric analgesia is conditioned by sociocultural, institutional, structural, and economic factors. Major barriers included shortages of trained personnel, socioeconomic inequalities, linguistic and cultural barriers, discrimination, and limited access to information. Across studies, women's childbirth experiences were strongly influenced by autonomy, respectful care, and participation in decision-making. Improving equitable access to labour pain relief requires policies that strengthen health system capacity, ensure informed choice, and promote respectful maternity care. Region-specific research is needed to inform equitable maternal health policies across Latin America.

items.title: Who Consumes What? Characterization of Violent Pornography Consumers in the Young Adult Population Living in Spain.
items.abstract: Studies about violent pornography consumers until now could be biased by social desirability. This study aimed to explore violent pornography consumption in young adults in Spain with an instrument that minimized social desirability. A cross-sectional study was conducted with 3607 women and men aged 18-35 years. By using multinomial logistic regression models, we identified the sociodemographic characteristics associated with the consumption of different types of pornography, considering consumption frequency and social desirability. In the last year, 84.6% of men and 45.2% of women have viewed pornography, and 82.2% of men and 74.4% of women have viewed violent pornography. Sexual orientation was associated with the likelihood of viewing pornography with degrading/humiliating practices without physical violence (OR_gay_bisexual: 1.92; OR_lesbian_bisexual: 2.36) and with the likelihood of viewing pornography with physical violence (OR_gay_bisexual: 2.38; OR_lesbian_bisexual: 3.15). In women, the place of origin was associated with consuming pornography with physical violence (OR_stranger: 1.92). In women, both associations were explained by consumption frequency. In men, the association of sexual orientation did not depend on consumption frequency (Degrad/humi: OR_gay_bisexual: 1.75; Physical: OR_gay_bisexual: 1.96). The higher the social desirability, the lower the consumption of pornography with physical violence (OR_men: 0.87; OR_women: 0.91) and degrading/humiliating practices without physical violence (OR_men 0.93). The type of pornography consumed is defined by sexual orientation in men and by the frequency of consumption in both sexes.

items.title: Fully Automated Segmentation of Chronic Total Occlusion Lesions on Coronary CT Angiography Using Deep Learning.
items.abstract: Reliable quantitative assessment for chronic total occlusion (CTO) lesions depends on accurate segmentation of coronary computed tomography angiography (CCTA) images. However, incomplete contrast opacification and complex lesion morphology make precise delineation particularly challenging. We developed an Atrous Attention U-Net (AAU-Net) for CTO segmentation and integrated it into a fully automated workflow comprising heart localization, CTO localization, and lesion segmentation. This retrospective study included 565 CTO lesions from 551 patients who underwent prospectively ECG-gated CCTA at three centers. Standalone segmentation used reference-mask-derived lesion-containing slices and regions of interest, whereas the automated workflow used predicted localization without reference-mask information or manual correction. Under reference-defined localization, AAU-Net achieved a Dice score of 0.8421 and intersection over union of 0.7312 in the internal test set, although performance varied by anatomical location and center. Performance decreased in the fully automated workflow, with Dice scores of 0.6922 in the internal test set, 0.5822 in external test set 1, and 0.6480 in external test set 2, potentially reflecting localization errors and differences between the separately trained segmentation models. In an exploratory locked-model radiomics analysis, features derived from automated segmentations showed numerically lower predictive performance than those derived from manual segmentations. Overall, AAU-Net showed favorable segmentation performance under reference-defined localization, but the fully automated workflow demonstrated lower performance that varied across centers. The radiomics findings demonstrate technical feasibility rather than established clinical utility. Further optimization and larger prospective multicenter validation are required before clinical deployment.

items.title: Environmental Exposures and Diagnosed Dyslipidemia Among Middle-Aged and Older Adults in China.
items.abstract: Dyslipidemia is shaped not only by biological aging but also by historically structured social and environmental conditions experienced across cohorts and periods. Rapid urbanization, environmental degradation, and population aging in China provide a critical context for examining how life-course processes intersect with contemporary exposures to influence dyslipidemia risk. Drawing on Age-Period-Cohort (APC) analysis, this study investigated how age, birth cohort, and period-specific environmental conditions jointly structured dyslipidemia among middle-aged and older adults. Individual-level data were drawn from five waves (2011-2020) of the China Health and Retirement Longitudinal Study (CHARLS). City-level environmental characteristics were compiled from the Google Earth Engine and China City Statistical Yearbook to construct measures of physical and social environments. Multilevel models incorporating APC specifications were used to estimate age, period, and cohort effects, and to assess associations between environmental exposures and the risk of dyslipidemia. Results reveal a nonlinear age pattern, with dyslipidemia risk peaking in the mid-50 s before declining in later life. Period effects indicate rising prevalence across survey waves, consistent with broader nutritional, behavioral, and diagnostic transitions. Cohort disparities were observed: later-born cohorts exhibited substantially lower risk than earlier-born cohorts (born in 1949 and earlier). Environmental exposures further structured these inequalities. Summer land-surface temperature showed a U-shaped association with dyslipidemia, while winter temperatures demonstrated inverted U-shaped relationships. Air pollutants were positively associated with risk in largely monotonic patterns. Importantly, cohort-stratified analyses revealed greater environmental susceptibility among earlier-born cohorts, suggesting cumulative disadvantage across the life course. These findings demonstrate how early-life conditions interact with contemporary environmental stressors to produce intergenerational disparities in cardiometabolic health. Integrating life-course perspectives with environmental governance may be essential for reducing chronic disease burdens in rapidly aging and ecologically transforming societies.

items.title: Global Challenges, Local Meaning: Methods and Lessons from a Global Public Health Partnership Measuring the Interplay of Built and Food Environments with Climate Hazards in African Cities.
items.abstract: Non-communicable diseases (NCDs) are increasing on the African continent, where rapid urbanization, built environments not conducive to healthy diets or active living, and climate-related stressors co-occur as "syndemic hazards" that may interact to amplify NCD risk. We detail the novel concepts and methods employed to quantify these syndemic hazards, co-designed through a global public health partnership of academics collaborating closely with stakeholders in four African cities: Cape Town and Soweto (South Africa), Lagos (Nigeria), and Yaoundé (Cameroon). We developed and implemented a multi-scalar data collection framework, combining adapted versions of the Microscale Audit of Pedestrian Streetscapes (MAPS-Global) and the Environmental Profile of a Community's Health (EPOCH) with secondary data on climatic hazards identified and prioritized through stakeholder engagement. We report the implementation of the framework across 633 audited routes, including instrument adaptations and strategies used to overcome field challenges. Our approach demonstrates how standardized environmental audit tools can be adapted through partnership-based processes to generate comparable yet contextually meaningful data on syndemic hazards, supporting policy-relevant urban health research in under-represented settings.

items.title: Clinical outcomes of Thunder-fire moxibustion with or without Yiqi Wenyang Tincture for cancer-related fatigue: a randomized controlled trial.
items.abstract: Cancer-related fatigue (CRF) is a debilitating symptom with limited treatment options. This study evaluated whether thunder-fire moxibustion (TFM) combined with Yiqi Wenyang Tincture (YWT) could provide additional benefit for CRF beyond conventional integrative management (control). In a three-arm randomized controlled trial, 255 cancer patients were allocated (85 per group) to TFM alone, TFM plus YWT (TFM + YWT), or conventional integrative management (control). The primary outcomes were the Revised Piper Fatigue Scale (PFS-R) total score and EORTC QLQ-C30 global quality-of-life score at week 6. In conservative intention-to-treat analyses using baseline observation carried forward for five missing week-6 assessments, with ANCOVA adjusted for baseline score and HC3 robust standard errors, TFM + YWT had lower PFS-R scores than TFM alone (adjusted mean difference, -0.459; 95% CI, -0.793 to -0.126; Bonferroni-adjusted p = 0.021) and higher global quality of life (2.552; 0.589 to 4.515; Bonferroni-adjusted p = 0.033). Exploratory outcomes were analyzed in the complete-case set. TFM, particularly when combined with YWT, may provide incremental clinical benefit for CRF; confirmation in larger trials with matched attention controls and longer follow-up is warranted. items.title: Impact of heat alerts on mortality and emergency ambulance dispatches in Japan.
items.abstract: Heat-health warning systems are important measures used worldwide to mitigate heat-related illness, but evidence on their effectiveness remains inconsistent. Japan has seen a rise in heatstroke cases in recent years, prompting the implementation of a heat alert system to prevent health risks. This study evaluates the impact of Japan's heat alert system on mortality and emergency ambulance dispatches (EADs). We collected daily time-series data on mortality, EADs, and Wet Bulb Globe Temperature (WBGT) across Japan's 47 prefectures for June-September 2020 and May-September 2021-2023; mortality data were available only through 2022. For both mortality and EADs, data were collected for all-cause, circulatory, respiratory, and genitourinary outcomes. Additionally, EADs were collected for heatstroke. Heat alert days were matched with non-alert days with similar WBGT levels. A conditional Poisson regression model was used to evaluate the association between heat alerts and health outcomes. Of 2,715 heat alert days between 2020 and 2023, 1,310 had matched non-alert counterparts, resulting in 2,620 observation days. EADs increased on heat alert days: all-cause by 3.11% (95% confidence interval (CI): 1.74%, 4.50%), genitourinary by 5.82% (95% CI: 0.07%, 11.9%), and heatstroke by 31.1% (95% CI: 21.2%, 41.8%) compared to matched non-alert days. No significant associations were observed for mortality or other EAD outcomes. These patterns may be associated with heightened public awareness, diagnostic shifts, or behavioral responses. Further research should explore public engagement with alerts and behavioral changes in response to heat alerts.

items.title: Plasma proteomics identifies insulin resistance signatures predictive of cardiometabolic disease risk.
items.abstract: Insulin resistance drives cardiometabolic disease, yet its molecular signatures and tissue origins remain incompletely characterized. Here we define a circulating protein signature that enables scalable assessment of insulin sensitivity. We applied multiworkflow proteomics to plasma from 161 individuals spanning the insulin sensitivity spectrum defined by the hyperinsulinaemic-euglycaemic clamp and identified 488 proteins associated with insulin sensitivity, capturing contributions from liver, adipose tissue and immune cells. A subset of these proteins shifted towards a more insulin-sensitive profile following an exercise intervention in men. We further developed a model combining 13 proteins, including IGFBP1, LEP, GDF15, PON3 and LDLR, with clinical variables (sex, HbA1c and the triglyceride-to-high-density lipoprotein cholesterol ratio) to predict insulin sensitivity (R2 = 0.67). In ~20,000 UK Biobank participants, the model outperformed the triglyceride-to-high-density lipoprotein cholesterol ratio in predicting type 2 diabetes (concordance index, 0.86 versus 0.74) and, unlike HbA1c, predicted hepatic, renal, cardiovascular and respiratory disease. In an independent cohort of 1,700 individuals, the model also showed greater predictive utility than fasting insulin resistance indices, including the homeostatic model assessment of insulin resistance. Together, these findings establish a tissue-resolved plasma proteomic framework for characterizing insulin resistance and provide a scalable approach to precision cardiometabolic risk stratification.

items.title: The impact of structured care versus usual care on service uptake and distress among distressed callers to a cancer telephone support service: outcomes of the START stepped wedge trial.
items.abstract: Up to 45% of people with a cancer diagnosis and 44% of caregivers experience distress. Evidence-based guidelines recommend psychosocial screening with structured referrals in all settings. To identify whether the implementation of a co-designed distress screening and structured referral intervention at Cancer Information and Support (CIS) telephone services resulted in increased referral uptake and reduced distress for people with cancer and caregivers versus those receiving usual care. As part of the stepped wedge trial, caller distress was measured using the Distress Thermometer (DT) and Generalised Health Questionnaire-28 (GHQ-28) and uptake of referrals offered by the CIS were recorded. Referral uptake and GHQ-28 scores were assessed using generalised linear mixed models (GLMMs) with fixed effects for the intervention period and structured care. Subgroup analyses were also performed to assess the difference between caller type (patients vs caregivers) and previous mental health treatment. This study of 2348 patients and caregivers found insufficient evidence to support increased referral uptake or decreased distress in the structured care group, or a relationship between referral uptake or distress by caller type (patient/caregiver) (p > .05 for adjusted ORs in each comparison). Although the structured care model did not improve referral uptake or distress, these findings should be interpreted cautiously due to a lack of intervention fidelity. Recommendations for improving intervention fidelity and future co-design research strategies are discussed.

items.title: Development of treatments for sarcopenia: new challenges, opportunities and perspectives.
items.abstract: Sarcopenia is characterized by loss of muscle mass, strength and function, and is associated with decline in physical function, falls, fractures and premature mortality. Despite increasing recognition of its clinical and societal burden, progress in translating advances in sarcopenia research into approved pharmacological therapies has remained limited. Potential barriers include heterogeneity in trial design regarding eligibility criteria, follow-up duration and outcomes, as well as limited regulatory harmonization. Given advances in sarcopenia research, the continued absence of approved treatments and the need to integrate perspectives that have emerged since the 2020 ESCEO recommendations for the conduct of sarcopenia clinical trials, this Perspective provides up-to-date expert perspectives on the development of treatments for sarcopenia, informed by discussions held by a working group convened by the World Health Organization Collaborating Centre for Epidemiology of Musculoskeletal Conditions and Ageing. Developments in the definition of sarcopenia, the regulatory landscape and therapeutic approaches are presented, together with considerations for the design of pharmacological trials, including target populations, the selection and assessment of trial outcomes (including digital health measures and patient-reported outcome measures), trial duration, use of biomarkers and patient expectations of treatments.

items.title: Patient acceptability on the use of teleconsultations for colorectal cancer surveillance care.
items.abstract: Despite evidence supporting the role of teleconsultation for surveillance of colorectal cancer (CRC) patients, implementation remains challenging. This study examined the perception, receptibility and acceptance of the care delivery models amongst elderly CRC patients. This mixed methods study involved a self-administered survey on 100 patients who were asked to rank their preferred communication method (physical hospital/general practitioner consultation, telephone and video call) for the various CRC care scenarios (pre-operative counselling, post-operative review, delivering normal/abnormal histology, imaging or blood test/scan results). Semi-structured interviews were conducted with 18 patients to explore reasons for acceptance and non-acceptance. Chi-square analyses revealed that patients were not accepting of teleconsultation for postoperative reviews of major conditions and delivery of abnormal test and/or scan results (all p < .05). However, there were no differences in teleconsultation acceptance for preoperative counselling and postoperative reviews of minor conditions, and more patients were accepting of teleconsultations for delivery of normal histology, imaging scan and blood test results (all p < .001). Content analysis showed that teleconsultation acceptance was mainly due to perceived equivalence in communication modalities as well as convenience, while non-acceptance was due to the limitations of telecommunication. It is evident that patients prefer a face-to-face physical consultation when their surveillance trajectories suggest more serious implications. However, our findings highlighted the opportunity for teleconsultations to be used selectively with particular patients and situations where patient outcomes remain normal. It remains uncertain if this hybrid model for CRC surveillance will be cost-effectiveness and acceptable.

items.title: Comparative Evaluation of Intranasal Simvastatin-Loaded Transbilosomes Versus Oral Simvastatin Suspension in Attenuating Heart Failure in Rat Models Induced by Doxorubicin and Ischemia/Reperfusion.
items.abstract: Simvastatin (SMS) has profound lipid-independent "pleiotropic" effects that benefit heart failure (HF), but its poor solubility and bioavailability limit its efficacy. This study developed nasal simvastatin-loaded transbilosomes (SLT) to improve drug solubility and bioavailability and mitigate HF. To develop an optimal SLT formulation, the Box-Behnken design was employed. The effectiveness of the nasal SLT was evaluated in vivo using rat models of HF induced by either doxorubicin or ischemia/reperfusion. Relative to free SMS, the optimal SLT achieved a release increase of 3.81-fold, increased bioavailability by 6.35-fold, enhanced permeation by 7.46-fold, and increased the cardiac accumulation by 1.96-fold. Compared to the oral SMS group, the nasal SLT group exhibited significantly lower levels of triglycerides, cholesterol, LDL, CK-MB, LDH, troponin I, NT-proBNP, NO, MDA, and heart rate, being 1.49-fold, 1.47-fold, 1.40-fold, 1.48-fold, 1.42-fold, 1.59-fold, 1.42-fold, 2.0-fold, 1.90-fold, and 1.99-fold lower, respectively. Conversely, HDL, GSH, SOD, ejection fraction, and fractional shortening increased by 1.5-fold, 1.95-fold, 1.48-fold, 1.48-fold, and 1.42-fold, respectively. Histopathology examination validated the efficacy of the nasal SLT formulation. While these findings represent nasal SLT as a promising insight in alleviating HF, future work is recommended to fully elucidate the distinct contribution of isolated vehicle and route controls.

items.title: Child emotional competence: a conceptual organizing framework and parent-report measure of emotion reasoning, emotion stability, emotion regulation, and empathy
items.abstract: Introduction Emotional competence (EC) plays a vital role in children's development, well-being, and mental health outcomes. However, the field lacks consensus on definitions and measurement approaches, leading to inconsistencies and limitations in understanding and assessing EC. Methods This paper presents a conceptual organizing framework for EC that integrates and clarifies the various components of emotional functioning. Additionally, a new measure, the Emotional Competence Inventory for Children (ECIC), was developed and validated to assess EC among children ages 3–12 years based on the proposed framework. The study involved two separate samples ( N = 695) recruited through Amazon's Mechanical Turk. Data analysis included exploratory and confirmatory factor analyses, measurement invariance testing, and assessments of reliability and validity. Results Results supported the four components of EC: Emotion Reasoning, Emotion Stability, Emotion Regulation, and Empathy. Subscales of Emotion Reasoning and Emotion Stability were identified, providing nuanced insights into emotional development. The ECIC demonstrated promising psychometric properties, including evidence of measurement invariance across several demographic groups, although full scalar invariance was not established across all groups. The unique associations of ECIC scales/subscales shed light on their differential associations with child health outcomes, aiding precision-medicine approaches and intervention efforts. Discussion The validated ECIC measure offers an important tool for assessing EC and informing future personalized treatment research and assessment strategies. This conceptual organizing framework and accompanying measure contribute to advancing our understanding of EC, supporting children's emotional development, and promoting their overall well-being. Future research should further validate and refine the framework while investigating its applicability in diverse populations and treatment settings.
