items.title: Sesamin Ameliorates Insulin Resistance in Association With Gut Microbiota Remodeling and ICA-AhR-GLP-1 Signaling in Diabetic Mice.
items.abstract: Type 2 diabetes mellitus (T2DM) is closely associated with insulin resistance and gut microbiota dysbiosis. Here, we identified a microbiota-associated indole-3-carboxaldehyde (ICA)-AhR-GLP-1 pathway that contributes to the glucose-lowering effect of sesamin (Ses), a major sesame lignan. In db/db mice, Ses improved hyperglycemia and insulin resistance, while remodeling the gut microbiota and enriching Ligilactobacillus. Fecal microbiota transplantation from Ses-treated donors partially transferred these metabolic benefits. Integrated bacterial isolation, Ses-based fermentation, fecal metabolomics, and clinical LC-MS/MS analysis identified ICA as a Ses-responsive microbiota-associated metabolite. Serum ICA levels were reduced in newly diagnosed patients with T2DM and negatively correlated with FBG, HbA1c, and HOMA-IR. Oral ICA reproduced key metabolic effects of Ses and enhanced intestinal Gcg expression and GLP-1 production. Mechanistically, ICA bound to AhR, promoted AhR nuclear translocation, increased AhR occupancy at the XRE-containing region of the Gcg promoter, and stimulated GLP-1 secretion in STC-1 cells and intestinal organoids. AhR inhibition reduced Ses-induced GLP-1 production and partially attenuated its metabolic effects, whereas acute GLP-1R blockade blunted Ses- and ICA-induced improvements in glucose tolerance and early insulin secretion. Together, these findings support a model in which Ses improves glucose homeostasis in association with gut microbiota remodeling and engagement of an ICA-AhR-GLP-1 pathway.

items.title: Understanding Experiences With Feared Food Exposures: A Qualitative Study of People With Eating Disorders.
items.abstract: Objective Feared food exposures are a core eating disorder treatment component entailing eating an anxiety-eliciting food without engaging in compensatory behaviors. These exposures reduce eating-related anxiety and symptom severity; however, high treatment dropout and relapse rates in eating disorder populations suggest these benefits vary across participants. Understanding patients' experiences with this intervention may reveal factors that hinder or support positive outcomes, yet remain insufficiently understood. Therefore, we qualitatively explored how individuals with eating disorders experience feared food exposures. Method We interviewed Canadian adults (N = 19; M age = 30.84) who met DSM-5 criteria for an eating disorder and had completed a feared food exposure within treatment. Participants described a particularly salient feared food exposure that was planned with a clinician but completed without clinician involvement. Interviews explored the dynamic unfolding of urges, behaviors, motives, thoughts, and feelings before, throughout, and after the exposure. Results We identified four superordinate themes through template analysis. Control was experienced as both distressing and empowering, as greater autonomy added meaning to experiences while also increasing guilt. Distress extended beyond food and body image to encompass other concerns, such as social fears, and intensified with self-presentational or competitive motivations, such as wanting to be viewed favorably. Individuals adapted exposures to align with their perceived coping capacity, such as by adjusting their attunement to the experience. Discussion Results illustrate the complex and nuanced experience of feared food exposures. Clinicians and patients may benefit from considering autonomy, sources of distress, interpersonal motives, and current coping capacity when planning and implementing exposures.

items.title: Cortical Macro- and Microstructural Alterations in Multiple System Atrophy and Their Clinical Correlates.
items.abstract: Background Multiple system atrophy (MSA) is primarily characterized by subcortical neurodegeneration. However, neuropathological evidence indicates that cortical neurodegeneration is also part of the disease. Conventional neuroimaging measures, such as cortical thickness (CTh), have been used to assess cortical macrostructural alterations, but findings remain limited and inconclusive. In this context, cortical mean diffusivity (cMD) has emerged as a promising marker of microstructural integrity, capturing alterations beyond macrostructural changes in other neurodegenerative disorders. However, its role in MSA remains largely unexplored. Objectives The objective of the study was to characterize cortical macro- and microstructural alterations in MSA and assess associations with clinical severity and cognitive performance. Methods T1-weighted and diffusion magnetic resonance imaging (MRI), clinical, and neuropsychological assessments were obtained in 29 patients with MSA and 35 age- and sex-matched controls (HCs). Cortical macro- and microstructural alterations were evaluated using CTh and cMD, respectively. Group comparisons and correlations between MRI-derived cortical measures and clinical, cognitive, and neurodegeneration biomarkers were conducted (P Results Patients with MSA exhibited widespread increases in cMD, predominantly affecting the frontal and temporal cortices. This pattern partially overlapped with cortical thinning, although cMD alterations extended to rostral-lateral, rostral-medial, and inferior-medial regions. In MSA, increased cMD was associated with global cognitive impairment, whereas cortical thinning correlated with disease severity. Conclusions MSA involves concurrent macro- and microstructural cortical alterations, with microstructural changes potentially preceding overt atrophy and indicating early pathology. Distinct cMD and CTh patterns suggest partially independent processes, whereas differential clinical associations highlight their complementarity. Together, these markers improve the characterization of cortical degeneration and disease heterogeneity. © 2026 The Author(s). items.title: Self-Awareness and Career Decision-Making: Evidence From Adolescents in Arunachal Pradesh, India.
items.abstract: Career decision-making is an important developmental task during adolescence, yet evidence from geographically understudied regions remains limited. This study examined the associations between self-awareness and career decision-making among adolescents in Arunachal Pradesh, India. A cross-sectional school-based survey included 564 adolescents aged 14-19 years enrolled in secondary and higher secondary schools in the Itanagar Capital Region of Arunachal Pradesh, India. Participants completed standardized measures of self-awareness and career decision-making. They also completed open-ended questions on perceived strengths, career aspirations and sources of career guidance. Pearson correlations, simple and multivariable linear regression, and content analyses were used. Adolescents reported high self-awareness and career decidedness (r = 0.40, p< 0.001), but not with career indecision (r = -0.08). Self-awareness accounted for 15.8% with career decidedness in the bivariate model (R2 = 0.158, f2 = 0.19) and remained modestly associated after adjustment for gender, community, school type and age (β = 0.37, p < 0.001). Content analysis indicated that medical and technical professions were the most preferred career aspirations, while some adolescents reported uncertainty regarding their career interests. Many participants relied on parents and teachers for career guidance. Self-awareness showed a modest association with career decidedness and should be understood as one developmental resource operating alongside family, school and community influences. The findings contribute to adolescent career development in an understudied Indian context and highlight the importance of fostering self-awareness to support career decision-making.

items.title: Symptom burden and patient activation in maintenance hemodialysis patients: chain-mediating effects of illness perception and self-regulatory fatigue.
items.abstract: This study examined the association between symptom burden and patient activation in maintenance hemodialysis patients and tested the mediating roles of illness perception and self-regulatory fatigue.A cross-sectional questionnaire survey was conducted among 265 patients receiving maintenance hemodialysis at a tertiary hospital in China from November 2025 to March 2026. Data were collected using a general information questionnaire, the Dialysis Symptom Index, the Brief Illness Perception Questionnaire, the Self-Regulatory Fatigue Scale and the Patient Activation Measure. Descriptive statistics, Pearson correlation analysis, multiple linear regression, Harman single-factor test and structural equation modeling were performed. Bias-corrected bootstrapping with 5000 resamples was used to test mediating effects. Symptom burden had a significant direct effect on patient activation, accounting for 53.58%of the total effect. Illness perception, self-regulatory fatigue and the sequential pathway from illness perception to self-regulatory fatigue also mediated the relationship between symptom burden and patient activation, accounting for 29.28%, 11.84%and 5.30%of the total effect, respectively. Symptom burden was associated with patient activation both directly and indirectly through illness perception and self-regulatory fatigue. These findings suggest that illness perception and self-regulatory fatigue may help explain the association between symptom burden and patient activation in patients receiving maintenance haemodialysis.

items.title: Profiles of emotion regulation difficulties in the transition to menopause: a latent profile analysis.
items.abstract: The menopausal transition is associated with heightened psychological vulnerability, yet individual differences in emotion regulation (ER) during this period remain poorly understood. This study applied latent profile analysis to identify distinct ER difficulty profiles in women during menopause transition and examined attachment anxiety and avoidance as predictors of profile membership. A sample of 455 women aged 40-60 years at different stages of the menopausal transition (late reproductive, perimenopausal, and postmenopausal) participated in this cross-sectional study. Four profiles were identified: High ER Difficulties (11.2%), Moderate ER Difficulties (48.1%), Emotional Clarity Deficit (11.4%), and Low ER Difficulties (29.2%). Profiles differed significantly on depression, anxiety, stress, menopause-specific somatic and psychological symptoms, and personal burnout (all p < .001, with large effects), with one key exception: the Emotional Clarity Deficit profile did not differ from the Low ER profile on any outcome despite presenting the highest lack of emotional clarity scores in the solution. Attachment anxiety and avoidance both predicted membership in the High and Moderate ER profiles, whereas only attachment avoidance uniquely predicted the Emotional Clarity Deficit profile. These findings provide initial person-centered evidence of ER heterogeneity in the menopausal transition. The Emotional Clarity Deficit profile, which was statistically associated with attachment avoidance, represents a configuration not captured by severity-based approaches; however, its clinical significance and stability remain to be established through replication in independent samples and longitudinal research.

items.title: Hidden in Plain Sight: A Qualitative Study of Lived Experience Disclosure in the Workplace Among Eating Disorder Clinicians.
items.abstract: Background Up to half of eating disorder clinicians report personal lived experience of an eating disorder. However, there is limited research examining experiences of eating disorder clinicians' disclosure of an eating disorder in the workplace. We aimed to analyze qualitative responses about disclosure of an eating disorder in the workplace among eating disorder clinicians. Method Australian eating disorder health professionals responded online to an open-ended question where respondents (N = 103, 95.15% female, M age = 36.98 years) were asked about personal or colleagues' experiences of eating disorder disclosure in the workplace. Responses were analyzed using reflexive thematic analysis. Results Four themes were developed through analysis: (1) stigma, prejudice, and discrimination; (2) supportive inclusivity, hope and understanding; (3) disclosure policy and practice uncertainty, and (4) disclosure agency and context. Responses highlighted negative assumptions made about a clinician's fitness to practice, from collegial interactions through to recruitment and supervision practices. Discussion Findings suggest that eating disorder clinicians with lived experience of an eating disorder report significant stigma and discrimination within the workforce. Results highlight the urgent need for the eating disorder sector to create psychologically safe workplaces, which has the potential to improve clinician and client wellbeing. Continued research into building a mentally healthy eating disorder workforce should include development of ethical practice guidelines to help supervisors, managers, and colleagues support clinicians with lived experience of an eating disorder.

items.title: Persistent Gaps in the Reporting, Representation, and Assessment of Sociodemographic Sample Characteristics in United States Eating Disorder Psychotherapy Trials: An Invited Interim Update.
items.abstract: Objective Present an interim update on the reporting and representation of sociodemographic data in eating disorder psychotherapeutic treatment trials in the United States from 2021 to 2026 and discuss challenges that arose during screening and data synthesis. Provide recommendations to improve trial reporting to facilitate ongoing systematic evaluation of representation. Method PRISMA guidelines for systematic reviews were followed. Eligible studies were randomized controlled psychotherapeutic eating disorder treatment trials in the efficacy or effectiveness stage with at least one US site published from 2021 to mid-2026. Two independent raters screened and extracted data. We calculated pooled estimates to evaluate representation. Results Our search yielded 1343 studies for screening; eight were deemed eligible. Screening challenges arose due to participant location ambiguity, lack of by-country demographic data, and ambiguity in intervention development stage. Trials were predominantly focused on young adult, female populations and disproportionately targeted binge-eating spectrum disorders and high weight. Sexual orientation and diverse gender identities were not assessed. We observed some indication of increased racial diversity, but Black participants remained markedly underrepresented. Discussion Representation estimates should be interpreted with caution due to small sample size. We observed some signals of progress in sociodemographic representation, but also continued areas of stagnation (e.g., age diversity). To facilitate future evaluation of sociodemographic representation, we provide recommendations for clinical trial conduct and reporting, including improved transparency in participant location and intervention stage.

items.title: Disordered Eating Attitudes and Behaviors in Individuals With BMI > 27 kg/m<sup>2</sup> Treated by Semaglutide: A 60-Week Randomized Placebo-Controlled Trial.
items.abstract: Objective To examine disordered eating attitudes and behaviors in individuals treated with semaglutide 2.4 mg or placebo for 60 weeks. Methods Individuals seeking obesity treatment (n = 120) randomized (3:2) to semaglutide or placebo, both with lifestyle intervention, were assessed at baseline and Weeks 20, 40, and 60. At each assessment, clinicians evaluated binge eating and eating disorder psychopathology (Eating Disorder Examination), and questionnaires measured loss of control (Loss of Control Over Eating Scale), drive for thinness [Eating Disorder Inventory (EDI)], body dissatisfaction (EDI and Body Satisfaction Scale), and mood (PHQ-9). Following multiple imputation, ANCOVAs compared the groups in change at each assessment, controlling for baseline. Results Mean reductions from baseline in loss of control, global eating disorder pathology, weight and shape concern, drive for thinness, and body dissatisfaction were significantly greater with semaglutide compared to placebo at several timepoints. The groups did not differ significantly in binge frequency reductions. However, participants reporting baseline binge episodes (n = 31) and those who had full or subthreshold binge-eating disorder (n = 18) were more likely to achieve abstinence with semaglutide compared to placebo. Reliable deteriorations in eating psychopathology, new onset of binge eating, and compensatory behaviors were rare, and symptom emergence did not seem higher with semaglutide. Discussion Semaglutide reduced eating disorder psychopathology and improved body image relative to placebo at 20 to 60 weeks of treatment for obesity management. Semaglutide also increased remission in those with binge eating. Disordered eating behaviors were rare but did occur, suggesting the need for periodic monitoring in at-risk individuals. items.title: Divergent effects of memory suppression on food reward evaluation: devaluation in normal-weight versus rebound in females with overweight/obesity.
items.abstract: Previous research has shown that satiety-related inhibition of food reward memory retrieval is a key process in appetite regulation, with impairments in this function promoting overeating and weight gain. Building on this literature, the present study examined whether externally cued active suppression of food-related memory retrieval via the Think/No-Think (TNT) paradigm can directly modulate subjective food reward evaluations, including liking and wanting, across individuals with varying body mass index (BMI) levels. Fifty-seven female university students, including those with normal weight and those living with overweight/obesity, completed a food-specific Think/No-Think task, wherein participants were instructed to actively retrieve certain food-related words while deliberately suppressing others. Self-reported measures of liking and wanting for each food item were employed to assess how memory suppression influences food reward evaluations. All participants, regardless of BMI status, demonstrated significantly lower recall accuracy for suppressed items compared to retrieved items ([-0.079, -0.031], p < 0.001) and baseline items ([-0.070, -0.018], p = 0.001). However, reward evaluations differed markedly. Individuals with healthy weight exhibited a significant reduction in wanting for No-Think items ([0.013, 0.426], p = 0.038), indicating successful devaluation. Conversely, participants with overweight or obesity exhibited heightened desire for suppressed items ([-0.324, -0.029], p = 0.021). Further analyses revealed that restrained eating behaviors mediated these divergent responses ([-0.589, -0.079], p = 0.011). Active memory suppression not only reduces food memory accessibility but also significantly devalues subjective food reward evaluations, particularly subjective wanting for food items. Maladaptive eating behaviors like dietary restraint appear to generate a "rebound effect" rather than devaluation. These findings suggest that memory suppression holds potential for regulating food responses and obesity-prevention interventions.

items.title: Cannabis Use Modalities and Their Associations with Cannabis Use Disorder Severity.
items.abstract: Cannabis continues to be the most common illicit substance used in the United States. Increases in cannabis use prevalence are associated with increases in cannabis use disorder (CUD) risk. With changes in legalization, potency, and social acceptability, very little research has examined the potential usage modalities and their association with CUD. The purpose of this study is to determine the classes of cannabis users and examine each class' probability of being associated with current CUD in an undergraduate sample. The sample included 431 self-identifying African American undergraduate students (Women = 71.70%) with a mean age of approximately 19.55 (SD = 1.64) years. After giving consent, participants were asked to complete an online self-reported survey, including the Daily Sessions, Frequency, Age of Onset, and Quantity of Cannabis Use Inventory (DFAQ-CU). The DFAQ-CU contains an item inquiring about the participant' primary cannabis consumption method. Upon completion of the online survey, participants were administered a semi-structured interview that included the Mini International Neuropsychiatric Interview (MINI). The MINI assesses psychological disorders, including CUD ( n = 144). Employing Latent Class Analysis, we identified three classes: 1) Unlikely Users ( n = 247), Joints/Blunts ( n = 159), and Multi-users ( n = 25). Multinomial regression analysis revealed that Joints and Blunt users were more likely to have mild, moderate, and severe CUD. Multiusers were also more likely to have mild or moderate CUD, with higher likelihood than their Joint/Blunt counterparts. The three-class model underscores the increased risk of CUD associated with multi-use and predominant joints/blunts usage.

items.title: Differential neural mechanisms of hypnosis and progressive muscle relaxation in reducing social anxiety symptoms.
items.abstract: Background Hypnosis (HYP) and progressive muscle relaxation (PMR) are effective for social anxiety disorder (SAD), but their neural mechanisms remain unclear. This study compared their effects on brain activity and connectivity during emotional face processing. Methods Forty-five participants with high social anxiety symptoms were randomized to HYP (n = 24) or PMR (n = 21) and assessed before and after 6 sessions using the Liebowitz Social Anxiety Scale and fMRI. 23 matched healthy controls (HC) served as baseline controls. Brain activation and generalized psychophysiological interaction (gPPI) analyses were conducted. Results At baseline, SAD group versus HC showed higher LSAS scores, slower emotional face RTs, and reduced activation in occipital, postcentral, prefrontal/temporal regions, caudate, putamen, and thalamus. After intervention, both groups had lower LSAS scores. PMR increased RTs while HYP did not. HYP selectively decreased activation in the left superior frontal gyrus (lSFG) for negative stimuli and in the right superior temporal gyrus for neutral stimuli, whereas PMR showed no such effects. Both interventions reduced activation in the caudate, putamen, and thalamus. gPPI revealed that HYP increased lSFG-posterior cingulate cortex connectivity under negative stimuli, while PMR decreased this connectivity. Conclusions Both interventions alleviated SAD symptoms via limbic modulation; however, HYP more strongly targeted fronto-temporal regions and cognitive-attentional networks, suggesting partially distinct neural mechanisms from PMR. Clinical trials registration Chinese Clinical Trial Registry (ChiCTR1900022651).

items.title: N-Terminal Propeptide of Procollagen Type III (PIIINP) as a Biomarker for Liver Fibrosis Severity: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis.
items.abstract: The invasive nature of liver biopsy, the gold standard for liver fibrosis assessment, underscores the critical need for robust noninvasive biomarkers. The N-terminal propeptide of procollagen Type III (PIIINP), a direct marker of fibrogenesis, is one such candidate. Despite numerous primary studies, there has been no definitive meta-analysis to quantitatively summarize its diagnostic performance across different fibrosis stages and etiologies. This systematic review and meta-analysis was therefore conducted to precisely determine the pooled diagnostic accuracy of PIIINP for detecting and staging liver fibrosis and cirrhosis. We conducted a comprehensive literature search across PubMed, Scopus, Web of Science, and Embase. Eighteen studies, comprising 4639 individuals, were included for qualitative assessment and meta-analysis. Study quality was generally high (15 studies), with two rated as fair and one as low. A total of 30 substudies were analyzed from these 18 publications, as several studies reported multiple outcome measures. The primary aim was to evaluate the diagnostic accuracy of PIIINP for detecting and staging liver fibrosis and cirrhosis. The pooled diagnostic metrics for PIIINP in determining liver fibrosis severity were as follows: sensitivity, 72.29% (95% CI: 64.72-79.87); specificity, 79.34% (95% CI: 74.02-84.66); positive predictive value, 61.70% (95% CI: 49.49-73.90); negative predictive value, 81.29% (95% CI: 73.14-89.43); area under the curve, 0.75 (95% CI: 0.70-0.81); and overall accuracy, 73.29% (95% CI: 70.53-76.05). At a cutoff value of 7.34 ng/mL, PIIINP demonstrated a sensitivity of 67% (95% CI: 59-75) and a specificity of 77% (95% CI: 72-82) for differentiating advanced fibrosis or cirrhosis from milder stages. PIIINP demonstrates clinically useful accuracy as a noninvasive biomarker for assessing liver fibrosis severity, independent of underlying etiology. Its strong negative predictive value is particularly valuable for ruling out advanced disease. Future research should focus on validating disease-specific cutoffs and integrating PIIINP into standardized diagnostic algorithms for targeted patient populations.

items.title: Economic Burden of Neonatal Intensive Care Unit Admissions in Public Hospitals of Sidama Regional State, Ethiopia, 2024.
items.abstract: Neonatal intensive care unit (NICU) admission imposes a significant economic burden on parents, particularly in low-resource settings such as Ethiopia. Understanding the financial impact of NICU care is of paramount importance for improving healthcare delivery and reducing out-of-pocket expenses for parents. The aim of this study was to assess the economic burden of NICU admissions and associated factors in public hospitals in Sidama Regional State, Ethiopia. A total of 446 parents of neonate admitted to NICUs in six government hospitals in Sidama regional state. A cross-sectional study design was executed. Structured questionnaire and medical record reviews were used to collect the data. Expenses of the parents were categorized in to direct cost like medicine and laboratory test and indirect costs like food, transportation, and others. Regression analysis was applied to identify factors associated with the overall economic burden. Median total cost of NICU admission was 2007 ETB ($34.76), of this the indirect costs was account for 67.8%. The highest portion 81.8% of the indirect costs was constituted by food expense. Medicine cost accounted 54.4% of the direct costs which was the highest. More than half of the parents (51.3%) covered costs using their current income, while 24.7% resorted to borrowing. Duration of hospital stay (adjusted exp(β) = 1.02, 95% CI: 1.01-1.03) was significantly associated with higher economic burden, while admission to a general hospital, relative to a primary hospital, was significantly associated with lower economic burden (adjusted exp(β) = 0.21, 95% CI: 0.14-0.99). Economic burden of NICU admissions is substantial, with indirect costs, particularly food expenses, being the largest contributor. Prolonged hospital stays and admission to primary hospitals were associated with higher costs. Interventions to reduce out-of-pocket expenses, such as improving access to medical insurance and strengthening primary healthcare facilities, are recommended.

items.title: Acute and Early HIV Infection Among Key Populations in Rwanda: A Multisite Cross-Sectional Study to Inform Targeted Testing and Case-Finding, 2025.
items.abstract: Acute HIV infection is highly transmissible yet often missed by antibody-only rapid tests. Rwanda adopted fourth-generation antigen/antibody (Ag/Ab) tests in 2016, but routine p24 antigen documentation remains limited, limiting acute/early infection estimates. This study characterized acute/early HIV infection among key populations, including female sex workers (FSW), men who have sex with men (MSM), and people who inject drugs (PWID), to inform targeted testing and prevention interventions. We conducted a cross-sectional study in 2025 across 25 health facilities in 12 Rwandan districts. Individuals aged ≥ 15 years with unknown HIV status from FSW, MSM, PWID, and adolescent girls and young women (AGYW) were recruited via snowball sampling. Structured RedCap questionnaires captured socio-demographic, behavioral, and HIV testing history data. HIV testing followed the national serial algorithm using fourth-generation Determine HIV Early Detect rapid tests; acute/early infection required p24 antigen positivity regardless of antibody status. Among 1341 participants (median age 25 years, interquartile range [IQR]: 21-30), 864 (64%) were FSW, 177 (13%) were MSM, 58 (4.3%) were PWID, and 242 (18%) were AGYW; 66% had only primary education and 55% resided in rural areas. In the prior 4 weeks, 52% reported multiple sexual partners and 35.5% reported consistent condom use. One-third (416, 32.8%) were aware of pre-exposure prophylaxis (PrEP), and 34.7% (141/406) had ever used it. Overall HIV positivity was 5.0% (67/1341); acute/early HIV infection yield was 0.45% (6/1341), with two-thirds of cases (4/6) among MSM, all from Kigali City. Half (3/6) of acute/early cases reported inconsistent condom use and none reported PrEP use. Acute and early HIV infections appear more common among MSM in Kigali, potentially associated with ongoing risk behaviors and low PrEP uptake, although this observation is based on a small number of cases. Priorities include strengthened acute HIV surveillance via fourth-generation and self-testing, rapid antiretroviral therapy (ART) initiation, and scaled-up tailored prevention, especially PrEP.

items.title: Vaccinated parents are more likely to vaccinate their children.
items.abstract: Vaccines are the most effective way to prevent the spread of infectious diseases. Parental vaccination status may influence acceptance of vaccination for their children. The COVID-19 pandemic provided us an opportunity to learn about parental factors that impact the vaccination of children. We conducted a multilingual online survey in rural California to assess parental and child vaccination status. Our study found that parents who are vaccinated with either the flu or COVID-19 vaccine were likely to report that their child had received a COVID-19 vaccine. Parental vaccination was associated with child vaccination in unadjusted analysis.

items.title: Defeating Multidrug-Resistant ESKAPEE Pathogens With Polymer Nanomaterials.
items.abstract: The clinical efficacy of antibiotics has progressively declined over the past decades as a consequence of the global spread of antimicrobial resistance, a phenomenon that is particularly pronounced among the so-called ESKAPEE pathogens: Enterococcus species, Staphylococcus aureus, Klebsiella pneumoniae, Acinetobacter baumannii, Pseudomonas aeruginosa, Enterobacter species, and Escherichia coli. Collectively, these bacteria are responsible for more than 50% of infection-related deaths worldwide, and multidrug-resistance is highly prevalent among them. This alarming trend poses a critical threat to global public health and underscores the urgent need for innovative therapeutic strategies. One such approach involves the use of polymers as drug delivery systems for both conventional antibiotics and novel antimicrobial compounds, in the form of nanoparticles or polymer prodrugs, to circumvent resistance mechanisms. Other promising strategies are polycations with intrinsic antibacterial activity that act through mechanisms not yet widely exploited and polymers exerting photodynamic and photothermal effects. In this review, we summarize and discuss the current evidence for the efficacy of polymer-based strategies against drug-resistant ESKAPEE infections.

items.title: Sex-Based Differences in Procedural Success and One-Year-Outcomes After Percutaneous Coronary Intervention for Chronic Total Occlusion.
items.abstract: Evidence regarding sex-related differences in outcomes and procedural characteristics of percutaneous coronary intervention for chronic total occlusion (CTO-PCI) remains limited, particularly in Japanese populations. This study investigated sex-based differences in procedural success, complications, and 1-year clinical outcomes in patients undergoing CTO-PCI and examined the clinical implications of sex-specific risk factors. A total of 11,147 patients who underwent CTO-PCI between January 2014 and December 2022 were analyzed from the Japanese CTO-PCI expert registry. Baseline clinical, angiographic, and procedural characteristics were compared between women and men. Study endpoints included technical success, in-hospital procedural complications, and 1-year major adverse cardiovascular and cerebrovascular events (MACCE), defined as all-cause death, nonfatal myocardial infarction, and stroke. Multivariable logistic regression identified predictors of procedural failure, and Cox proportional hazards models identified predictors of 1-year MACCE. Among 11,147 patients, 1,579 were women (14%) and 9,568 were men (86%). Women were older, had a lower body mass index, and more frequently had heart failure and chronic kidney disease, whereas men had higher rates of smoking, prior myocardial infarction, and reduced left ventricular systolic function. Women exhibited significantly lower procedural success rates and higher incidences of procedural complications. Female sex was independently associated with procedural failure. In women, older age, hemodialysis, and procedural failure were independently associated with an increased risk of 1-year MACCE. Clinically significant sex-based differences exist in procedural success, complication rates, and determinants of adverse outcomes after CTO-PCI. These findings highlight the importance of incorporating sex-specific factors when selecting patients and formulating procedural strategies. Sex-based differences in outcomes after percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI) for chronic total occlusion (CTO) remain controversial, and data from Japanese populations are lacking. Using a large Japanese multicenter registry, we examined sex-specific differences in clinical characteristics, procedural success, complications, and 1-year major adverse cardiovascular and cerebrovascular events (MACCE). Women undergoing CTO-PCI were older and had a higher burden of comorbidities, including heart failure and chronic kidney disease. Procedural success rates were significantly lower and complication rates were higher in women. Importantly, predictors of 1-year MACCE differed between women and men, highlighting the need for sex-specific considerations when considering the procedural strategies for CTO-PCI.

items.title: Rabies Control in Guangdong Province: Epidemic Trend and Prevention Strategies.
items.abstract: To characterize the epidemic trends of human rabies in Guangdong Province from 1951 to 2024 and to summarize the historical practices and outcomes of rabies control programs. Descriptive analysis and Joinpoint regression were employed to analyze the temporal trends of rabies cases. Spearman's rank correlation analysis was used to examine the relationships between gross domestic product (GDP) and rabies cases, as well as the correlation between the number of human exposures recorded by rabies post-exposure prophylaxis clinics (PEP) and rabies cases. Guangdong experienced two major epidemic peaks, with the highest annual number of cases reaching 1,629 in 1980. Integrated strategies, including dog management, mass dog vaccination, PEP, and public health education, reduced annual cases to sporadic levels (<10 since 2019). The association between GDP and human rabies cases followed a biphasic trajectory: a significant positive correlation in Phase I (1951-1980; ρ = 0.75, p < 0.001) followed by robust negative correlations in Phase II (1981-2005; ρ = -0.63, p < 0.001) and Phase III (2006-2024; ρ = -0.99, p < 0.001). Since PEP clinic establishment in 2005 in Guangdong, a significant negative correlation was found between rabies exposures reported by PEP and human cases (ρ = -0.961, p < 0.001). Integrated control strategies have successfully reduced human rabies to a low endemic level in Guangdong. This decline coincided with progressive economic development and expanded PEP. However, elimination has yet to be attained. Eliminating canine-mediated human rabies requires sustained investment in dog vaccination and PEP and robust One Health collaboration.

items.title: Body mass index, waist circumference and association to surgical margins after radical prostatectomy.
items.abstract: To investigate obesity in association with risk of positive surgical margins (PSM) after radical prostatectomy (RP) for prostate cancer. We used data from Swedish cohorts and registers linked to the National Prostate Cancer Register to identify men who had undergone RP between 2007 and 2021. Relative risks of PSM according to pre-diagnostic body mass index (BMI) and waist circumference were estimated using logistic regression models. Explorative analyses were conducted by time from diagnosis to surgery, prostate cancer risk category, and calendar period. Of 1344 men with BMI data (measured on average 10 years before diagnosis) who underwent RP, 651 also had waist circumference measurements. Overall, 28% of these men had PSM. Higher BMI and waist circumference were associated with increased risk of PSM; the relative risks were 1.33 (95% confidence interval [CI] 1.08-1.65) per 5 kg/m2 increment of BMI and 1.26 (95% CI 1.01-1.56) per 10 cm increment of waist circumference. No clear associations were found in the explorative analyses. High BMI and waist circumference were associated with increased risk of PSM. These findings highlight the potential relevance of body size for surgical outcomes and the need to explore possible diagnostic, surgical, and clinical explanations for the observed association.

items.title: Non-invasive physiotherapy interventions for autistic children and adolescents using the F-words Lens Tool: A scoping review.
items.abstract: To map non-invasive physiotherapy interventions for individuals with autism spectrum disorder, using the F-words Lens Tool to summarize the main components of these interventions. We searched PubMed, Web of Science, PEDro, Embase, the Central Register of Controlled Trials, and Scopus for studies published between 2001 and 2026 involving autistic children and adolescents. Intervention components were analysed using the Rehabilitation Treatment Specification System and linked to the F-words through the F-words Lens Tool framework. The review was co-developed with patient and public involvement. Forty-eight studies were included. Most interventions were delivered by physiotherapists (71%), whereas 29% were interdisciplinary. Twenty-eight distinct interventions were identified, with ingredients covering five F-words domains: Functioning (e.g. structured and repetitive motor task practice; 67.96%); Fitness (e.g. aerobic and resistance exercises; 60.7%); Friends (e.g. group activities and facilitation of social interaction; 35.71%), Family (e.g. parent training and adaptation of routines; 20.8%); and Fun (e.g. meaningful and motivating activities; 14.3%). No components related to the Future domain were identified. Interventions mainly focused on functioning and fitness, with limited attention to the Future domain. The F-words Lens Tool helped identify important gaps and support more comprehensive, person-centred approaches.

items.title: Smoking and fibrosis risk progression: a retrospective cohort study.
items.abstract: Around 40% of patients with chronic liver disease (CLD) have a history of tobacco smoking, but the impact of smoking on fibrosis progression remains unclear. This study investigates the association between tobacco smoking and Fibrosis-4 Index (FIB-4) risk progression high-risk FIB-4 in primary care patients with CLD. We conducted a retrospective cohort study of primary care patients with CLD and inputs for at least two separate FIB-4 calculations. Patients with an initial FIB-4 ≥3.25, or prior diagnoses of cirrhosis, hepatocellular carcinoma, or liver transplant were excluded. The primary outcome was time to FIB-4 ≥3.25, indicating a high-risk for advanced fibrosis. Tobacco smoking status (never, former, current) was the primary exposure. We used univariate and bivariate analyses to describe the cohort and unadjusted and adjusted Cox regression models to evaluate the association of tobacco smoking with time to FIB-4 ≥3.25. The cohort had 2547 patients, with 24%, 36%, and 41% identified as current, former, and never tobacco smokers, respectively. After a mean follow-up of 5.4 years, 24% of the cohort progressed to high-risk FIB-4. In unadjusted Cox models, former (HR 1.35; 95% CI 1.11-1.63) and current (HR 1.49; 95% CI 1.21-1.83) tobacco smoking were associated with an increased risk of progression to high-risk FIB-4. Current (HR 1.27; 95% CI 1.02-1.59), but not former (HR 1.18; 95% CI 0.97-1.43), tobacco smoking was significantly associated with time to a high-risk FIB-4 after adjusting for CLD etiology, cardiometabolic, and demographic variables. Current tobacco smoking is associated with progression to a FIB-4 at high-risk for advanced fibrosis in patients with CLD.

items.title: Use of transvaginal and transabdominal cerclage in the Nordic countries: A survey of incidences and indications.
items.abstract: Clinical guidelines for cervical cerclage vary in terms of indications and patient management. In this study, we investigated the incidence, indications, surgical techniques, timing of placement, and peri- and postoperative care for both transvaginal and transabdominal cerclage use in the Nordic countries. This study was a cross-sectional survey. An electronic questionnaire was developed and distributed via an electronic data capture system (REDCap) to an obstetrician from all birth units in Denmark, Finland, Iceland, Norway, and Sweden. The primary outcome was the reported incidence of transvaginal cerclage, both history- and ultrasound-indicated, and of transabdominal cerclage. The estimated incidence per 100 000 births of history-indicated transvaginal cerclage was 231 in DK, 70 in FI, 140 in IS, 133 in NO, and 166 in SE. For ultrasound-indicated transvaginal cerclage, the estimated incidence per 100 000 births was 166 in DK, 21 in FI, 140 in IS, 17 in NO, and 59 in SE. For transabdominal cerclage, the estimated incidence was 63 in DK, 7 in FI, 28 in IS, 31 in NO, and 18 in SE. There is substantial variation in the use of cervical cerclage between the Nordic countries. We advocate for a harmonized Nordic model of cerclage care to ensure equitable and consistent practice across countries, coupled with a Nordic research collaboration network that can drive knowledge generation and implementation across the region.

items.title: Diurnal Patterns of Accelerometer-Measured Physical Activity, Genetic Risk and Incident Obesity: A Cohort Study of 58 877 Participants.
items.abstract: To examine the associations of diurnal physical activity patterns with incident obesity and whether these associations vary by genetic susceptibility. This prospective study included 58 877 UK Biobank participants with accelerometer data. Functional principal component analysis (fPCA) was applied to derive diurnal physical activity (PA) patterns. Cox proportional hazards models were used to examine the associations of PA patterns with incident obesity and their interactions with a body mass index polygenic risk score (PRSBMI). During a median follow-up of 8.3 years, 1567 participants developed obesity. Four functional principal components (fPCs) accounted for 97.2% of the total variance. Greater overall activity (fPC1) was associated with lower obesity risk (HR per SD = 0.85, 95% CI: 0.80-0.89). After adjustment for total physical activity, greater central-daytime activity (fPC2) was also associated with lower risk (HR per SD = 0.93, 95% CI: 0.90-0.97). For fPC4, compared with a score of 0, HRs were 0.91 (95% CI: 0.83-1.00) at a score of 1 (greater morning and evening activity) and 0.92 (95% CI: 0.84-1.00) at a score of -1 (greater midday and overnight activity). The fPC1 association was similar across low, intermediate, and high PRSBMI levels (HR = 0.87 at each level). Our findings support prioritising overall physical activity for obesity prevention across levels of genetic susceptibility, while also considering greater concentration of activity during the daytime.

items.title: Trust Beyond Words: Why Public Health Cannot Communicate Its Way Into Rebuilding Trust With the Public.
items.abstract: Policy Points We challenge the assumption that communication failures are the central cause of declining trust. Amid a widely acknowledged crisis of trust in public health, we argue that an overemphasis on communication obscures deeper, upstream failures in the ability of public health to exercise authentic presence and accountability. Community listening and engagement should be a core metric of public health practice: Incentives for public health practice, such as program funding mechanisms, research funding, and leadership promotions, should expand or realign with a bias toward improving community engagement. The public health profession is experiencing a widely recognized crisis of trust among the communities it seeks to serve. Leading public health advocates have suggested that the roots of this crisis lie not in the inherent practices of public health, but rather in failures to communicate effectively with the public. Accordingly, they have proposed improved communication strategies as a primary response. Drawing on philosophical literature and applied public health examples, we argue that efforts to restore trust between public health and communities must center on cultivating trustworthiness-an internal quality of public health professionals and institutions-rather than simply developing more effective strategies for eliciting trust through communication. Trustworthiness is rarely established apart from concrete acts of patiently listening to and practically responding to the needs of communities. Without these practices of meaningful engagement, improvements in public health communication may simply reinforce a transmissive model of communication, one that seeks to cultivate public trust primarily to secure community adherence acceptance of public health priorities and interventions. This tendency toward transmissive communication is a subtle, yet pervasive feature of many contemporary proposals for addressing public health's crisis of trust. Restoring public trust requires more than improving how public health communicates about its science and interventions. It requires cultivating the values, practices, and institutional arrangements that enable public health professionals and institutions to be meaningfully present in the communities they serve. Rather than prioritizing one-way, transmissive unidirectional communication from at a distance, the profession must first develop the capacity to listen, respond, and demonstrate its trustworthiness through sustained engagement.

items.title: Trustworthy Crisis Mental Health Care: Key Values and Features.
items.abstract: Mental health crises are increasing in the United States. Local and national policy efforts have focused on increasing access to crisis services, but little attention has been given to the quality of services delivered, or their perceived trustworthiness by people who use them. While trust in health care has been well studied in general health care settings, there has been a gap in the context of crisis mental health care. This gap exists despite the central role of relationships in mental health care, the vulnerability of people experiencing crises, and the use of practices known to erode trust (e.g., involuntary hospitalization). Our aim was to develop a framework for conceptualizing values and features of trustworthy crisis mental health care. With ongoing consultation from an advisory board, we conducted seven semistructured 1.5-hour virtual focus groups with 27 adults with lived experience of crisis mental health care to understand how trust in services is shaped. Transcripts were analyzed abductively for emergent themes through a rigorous process of codebook development and validation. We identified four core values underpinning beliefs in a trustworthy crisis mental health care system (human connection, autonomy, transparency, and respect), and four supporting values (personalization, benevolence, competence, and access). A trustworthy crisis mental health care system that expresses these values would exhibit a range of features across relational, organizational, systems, and societal levels. Participants emphasized the need to invest in non-medical, alternative crisis models. A central tension in current services emerged between risk management (e.g., concern over liability and physical safety) and therapeutic benefit, undermining trustworthiness at all levels. Beliefs in trustworthy crisis mental health care are unique to this setting. While we have outlined values and features of trustworthy crisis services, future work is needed to identify appropriate strategies to operationalize these values, as well as ways to address salient tension points that compromise trustworthiness.

items.title: Donor-Site Morbidity After Buccinator Myomucosal Flap: A Multicenter Cohort Study.
items.abstract: Buccinator myomucosal flaps (BMF) are increasingly used for reconstruction of small- to medium-sized intraoral defects because they replace oral mucosa with similar tissue. However, donor-site morbidity and its determinants remain poorly defined. This study aimed to evaluate donor-site morbidity after BMF harvest and identify factors associated with unfavorable outcomes. A retrospective international multicenter cohort study was conducted across 11 centers (10 in Europe and one in India). Adult patients undergoing reconstruction with BMF after oncologic resection and a minimum follow-up of 6 months were included. Donor-site morbidity was assessed during dedicated follow-up visits using a standardized clinical scoring system evaluating mouth opening, oral commissure symmetry, vestibular restoration, cheek lining reconstruction, and cosmetic outcome. A total of 340 patients were included (mean age 58.6 ± 13.9 years; 50% female; mean flap area 14.6 ± 6.2 cm2). The mean donor-site outcome score was 10.7 ± 3.4. At multivariable linear mixed-effects analysis accounting for center, adjuvant radiotherapy or radiochemotherapy and donor-site closure by secondary healing were independently associated with lower scores, whereas the buccal artery myomucosal island flap and the tunnelized facial artery myomucosal island flap were associated with higher scores. Wound dehiscence was the most frequent complication (9.1%). In 223 patients with available data, higher adherence to rehabilitation exercises was associated with improved outcome scores, both with and without adjuvant radiotherapy. BMF provides reliable reconstruction with generally favorable donor-site outcomes. Morbidity is mainly influenced by adjuvant radiotherapy, donor-site management, flap design, and adherence to postoperative rehabilitation exercises.

items.title: Serological Evidence of Leptospira Infection in Sheep in Central Appalachia, United States.
items.abstract: Leptospirosis is a globally important zoonotic disease affecting diverse animal species, including sheep. Although multiple studies have reported leptospiral seroprevalence in wildlife, livestock and companion animals in the United States (US), data on sheep populations remain limited. To address this knowledge gap, the present study assessed serological evidence of leptospiral exposure in sheep from Central Appalachia. We conducted a descriptive study using 257 archived serum samples collected through convenience sampling from sheep with no history of vaccination against leptospirosis across 17 flocks in northeastern Tennessee and western Virginia, within the Central Appalachian region. The archived sera were tested for the presence of leptospiral antibodies using the microscopic agglutination test (MAT). Animal-level sample positivity and flock-level positivity were summarized using descriptive statistics. A total of 257 archived sheep serum samples from 17 sheep flocks were analysed; the mean number of samples was 15 and ranged from 9 to 18 per sheep flock. Katahdin (24%) and mixed-breed sheep (23%) were the most common breeds, and 99.6% of sampled sheep were female. Most samples were collected in 2024 (88%), primarily during October and November. Overall, 44/257 sheep (17%) were seropositive for leptospiral antibodies, and 15/17 flocks (88%) had at least one seropositive sheep. Among the MAT-positive sheep, serovars Pomona (6.61%; 17/257), Bratislava (5.90%; 15/257), and Icterohaemorrhagiae (5.45%; 14/257) were most prevalent. The detection of leptospiral antibodies in sheep from most sampled flocks indicates that exposure to Leptospira spp. occurred across multiple locations within the study area. Although the use of archived samples precludes interpretation of these findings as population-level prevalence estimates, the results provide evidence of leptospiral exposure among sheep in Central Appalachia and support the need for larger, representative studies to better define the prevalence, geographic distribution and potential epidemiological significance of leptospiral exposure in regional sheep populations.

items.title: Spatial and Temporal Patterns of Blacklegged Tick (Ixodes scapularis) Populations and Lyme Disease Cases in Ontario, Canada, From 2007 to 2019.
items.abstract: Lyme disease, caused by Borrelia burgdorferi sensu stricto, is a growing human and animal health concern in Canada due to the rapid range expansion of its vector, the blacklegged tick (Ixodes scapularis). Various forms of surveillance have been performed for Lyme disease in Ontario, including mandatory human case reporting, passive tick surveillance (tick submissions from the public), active tick surveillance (tick dragging), and canine seroprevalence (proprietary data). This study assessed and compared the temporal trends, seasonality, and spatial distribution of blacklegged ticks and Lyme disease in Ontario using data from four types of surveillance. Time series analysis was applied to visualize temporal trends, followed by a generalized linear auto-regressive moving average modelling approach to assess the trend and seasonal effects. Human Lyme disease incidence per 100,000, passive I. scapularis submission rate per 100,000, B. burgdorferi prevalence in I. scapularis from active surveillance, and canine B. burgdorferi seroprevalence were spatially displayed at the public health unit level. An increasing trend in human cases, I. scapularis collected via passive and active approaches, and canine seropositivity were observed over time. Ixodes scapularis counts from passive and active surveillance peaked in May and October. Human cases peaked in July, while canine seroprevalence peaked in May. Human case incidence, tick submission rate, B. burgdorferi infection prevalence in I. scapularis from active surveillance, and canine seroprevalence were highest in public health units in eastern Ontario, but this was not consistent from year to year. This study demonstrates a significant disparity in Ontario's yearly, seasonal, and spatial patterns of I. scapularis, human Lyme disease cases, and canine seropositivity, challenging the comparability of risk across regions. A One Health surveillance approach that systematically collects and integrates animal, human, and environmental data at finer spatial and temporal scales is proposed.

items.title: KRAS and endometriosis: A systematic review and meta-analysis.
items.abstract: BackgroundEndometriosis is a chronic gynecological condition affecting approximately 10% of women of reproductive age worldwide. Accumulating molecular evidence suggests that endometriotic lesions harbor somatic oncogenic mutations, including activating mutations in the KRAS gene. However, the prevalence of KRAS mutations across endometriosis subtypes and their clinical significance remain poorly defined.ObjectivesThis systematic review and meta-analysis aimed to estimate the prevalence of somatic KRAS mutations in endometriosis, characterize variant allele frequencies, and evaluate associations with clinical outcomes, including recurrence, infertility, and malignant transformation.MethodsA comprehensive search of PubMed/MEDLINE, Embase, and Web of Science/Scopus was conducted in accordance with the Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses 2020 guidelines (International Prospective Register of Systematic Reviews: CRD420261303629). Eligible studies included observational designs and molecular sequencing reports on endometriotic tissue. Pooled prevalence was estimated using a random-effects meta-analysis (DerSimonian-Laird model), with heterogeneity assessed using Cochran's Q and I2 statistics.ResultsSeven studies were included, covering deep infiltrating, ovarian, and superficial peritoneal endometriosis subtypes. The pooled KRAS mutation prevalence was 48% (95% confidence interval: 38%-58%), with substantial heterogeneity (I2 = 77%). Mutations were most frequent in deep infiltrating and ovarian lesions (50%-55%) compared with that in superficial peritoneal disease (∼30%-35%). Variant allele fractions were consistently low (<20%), reflecting clonal epithelial expansion. KRAS-positive patients demonstrated greater disease extent and surgical complexity, though associations with pain, infertility, and recurrence were not statistically significant.ConclusionPreliminary evidence suggests that KRAS mutations are common in endometriosis; however, findings should be interpreted cautiously owing to substantial study heterogeneity and limited available data. KRAS may hold biological significance as a biomarker; however, current evidence is insufficient to support routine clinical use.

items.title: Proteome-Wide Genetic Study Identified ENTPD5 as a Candidate Target for Obesity-Related MASLD.
items.abstract: This study aimed to discover causal plasma proteins for metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease (MASLD) using trans-ancestry genetic data. We performed proteome-wide Mendelian randomization (MR) for 1256 proteins and MASLD using genome-wide association data from East Asian (n = 85,124) and European (n = 500,348) populations. Colocalization was conducted to validate putative causal proteins for MASLD, followed by two-step MR assessing adiposity mediation. Longitudinal cross-lagged analysis in a bariatric surgery cohort (n = 53) was used to assess temporal associations. ENTPD5 and APOE showed consistent causal effects in both East Asians and Europeans, both supported by colocalization. Both proteins influenced MASLD risk through adiposity, with BMI mediating 15.7% of the ENTPD5 effect. Longitudinal analysis in the bariatric surgery cohort supported the temporal pathway "ENTPD5→BMI reduction→MASLD remission (assessed by the fatty liver index)," with 29.2% mediation by BMI. Phenome-wide MR revealed a broad pleiotropic profile of ENTPD5, warranting further evaluation of target safety and repurposing potential. These findings suggest that ENTPD5 and APOE are potential causal biomarkers for MASLD and may contribute to its pathogenesis. ENTPD5 represents a candidate target for obesity-related diseases, although its pleiotropic profile warrants further investigation.

items.title: Maximizing the utilization and impact of the Osteoarthritis Initiative (OAI): A comprehensive guide to data handling and analytic strategies.
items.abstract: The Osteoarthritis Initiative (OAI) is a cohort study with publicly available resources intended to accelerate osteoarthritis research by providing harmonized clinical data, imaging, and biospecimens for 4,796 participants aged 45-79 years at enrollment, who were followed longitudinally for up to 16 years. OAI resources are distributed across three repositories: 1) the National Institute of Mental Health Data Archive (NDA; original visit data, millions of images, secondary image assessment, and biospecimen project data), 2) the database of Genotypes and Phenotypes (dbGaP; genome-wide association study data), and 3) the OAI biospecimen repository. The breadth and depth of the OAI's complex data architecture - spanning multiple repositories, nested studies, and longitudinal data files - are strengths. However, they also present challenges for investigators, particularly those new to the OAI. This manuscript provides a practical, methods-oriented guide to using OAI data and resources to lower barriers to OAI use, with the hope of accelerating discovery in osteoarthritis and related fields. We describe the study's design and its three repositories. We offer detailed guidance on dataset structure, file formats, naming conventions, key-merging variables, and missing-data codes. We address common analytic considerations, including the handling of data from image assessment projects, contingent variables, informative missingness, and subcohort-specific eligibility criteria. We provide recommendations for transparent reporting and reproducibility. We also describe how the OAI Collaborative Osteoarthritis Research Enterprise (OAI CORE) Knowledgebase, a National Institute of Arthritis and Musculoskeletal and Skin Diseases (NIAMS)-funded initiative designed to promote and facilitate the use of OAI resources, can assist users.

items.title: Redefining BASDAI cut-offs in axial spondyloarthritis: implications for patients' eligibility for treatment with biologic disease-modifying antirheumatic drugs.
items.abstract: To compare a newly proposed Bath Ankylosing Spondylitis Disease Activity Index (BASDAI) cut-off for high disease activity (BASDAI≥2.5) with the corresponding Axial Spondyloarthritis Disease Activity Score (ASDAS) cut-off (ASDAS≥2.1) as an eligibility criterion for initiating a biologic disease-modifying antirheumatic drug (bDMARD) in routine care patients with axial spondyloarthritis (axSpA). Real-world patients with axSpA initiating their first bDMARD from 9 European registries were analysed. Patients were categorised into 4 subgroups according to the fulfilment of ASDAS and BASDAI criteria at baseline, and treatment effect was assessed at 6 months using several response and remission outcomes. Adjusted logistic regression analyses were performed to determine whether fulfilling ASDAS and BASDAI criteria was associated with achieving the treatment outcomes. Of 6,329 patients included, 90.9% fulfilled both ASDAS and BASDAI eligibility criteria at baseline, 2.5% and 2.7% fulfilled either ASDAS or BASDAI criterion alone, while 3.8% fulfilled neither. The subgroup fulfilling both criteria demonstrated the highest responses at 6 months, while the highest remission outcomes were observed in the subgroup fulfilling neither criterion. Fulfilling either criterion at baseline was significantly associated with achieving response outcomes at 6 months, whereas a negative association was observed for remission outcomes. In a multinational European cohort, a very large overlap between the BASDAI and the ASDAS eligibility criteria was shown, and the predictive ability of the two criteria to achieve treatment outcomes was comparable. These findings support the use of BASDAI≥2.5 as a criterion for initiating bDMARD therapy in axSpA, particularly when ASDAS is unavailable.

items.title: Eupnea in Severe Airflow Limitation Identifies a Favorably Clinically Distinct Phenotype.
items.abstract: In Chronic Obstructive Pulmonary Disease (COPD), as disease severity worsens, lung function declines and symptom burden increases. The characteristics of individuals with severe airflow limitation who report no dyspnea (eupnea) are not well described. To investigate whether eupneic individuals with severe airflow limitation exhibit different clinical and imaging characteristics compared to those who are dyspneic. We analyzed data from 1,713 COPDGene participants with GOLD 3-4, categorized by mMRC dyspnea scores: 0 (eupneic), 1-2, and 3-4. Baseline assessments included spirometry, CT imaging, six-minute walk, and symptom questionnaires. Longitudinal outcomes included FEV1 decline, exacerbation frequency, and mortality. We replicated the analysis in participants with GOLD 1-2, GOLD 0, and preserved ratio impaired spirometry (PRISm). Among GOLD 3-4 participants, 8.2% were eupneic. Compared to those with mMRC 3-4, eupneic individuals had lower prevalence of chronic bronchitis and worse health-related quality of life, better exercise capacity, and less CT emphysema, gas trapping, and PRMfSAD. They experienced fewer exacerbations [incidence rate ratio (IRR) = 0.54; 95% CI: 0.42-0.69; P < 0.001] and had lower mortality (HR = 0.62;95% CI 0.48-0.80). Rates of longitudinal FEV1 decline were similar across mMRC groups. We observed similar findings in the GOLD 1-2, GOLD 0, and PRISm analyses. A modest proportion of individuals with severe respiratory function impairment are eupneic, showing better clinical outcomes and less structural lung damage than their dyspneic counterparts. Our findings support a multidimensional COPD assessment that incorporates symptom burden alongside spirometry.

items.title: Association between per- and polyfluoroalkyl substances (PFAS) and vaccine-induced antibody concentrations in five-year-old children from the Odense Child Cohort, Denmark.
items.abstract: Per- and polyfluoroalkyl substances (PFAS) are persistent environmental chemicals associated with lower vaccine-induced immune concentrations in children. Vaccine-induced antibody concentrations correlate strongly with time since vaccination, likely contributing to large variability in previous estimates. We investigated associations between prenatal and childhood PFAS exposure and antibody concentrations shortly after the five-year tetanus and diphtheria booster, with precise vaccination timing. We included 259 children from the Odense Child Cohort, a background-PFAS-exposed Danish cohort. Exact vaccination dates from the Danish Vaccination Register determined time since vaccination. Child serum samples were collected a median of 5.9 weeks after the five-year booster (2015-2018). PFAS was quantified in maternal and child samples and antibodies in child samples. Generalized Linear Models were used to examine associations adjusting for maternal education and time since vaccination. Secondary analyses used logistic regression estimating odds of reaching protective antibody levels. Generally consistent inverse, trends between childhood PFAS exposure and antibody levels were found, although most were not significant. The strongest association was observed for perfluorooctanoic acid (PFOA), where a doubling was associated with a 38.4% lower tetanus antibody concentration (95% CI: -57.7%, -11.1%). The PFOS estimate was in the same direction, but weaker (-17.1; 95% CI: -37.6%, 10.2%). Similar non-significant associations were observed for other PFAS and diphtheria antibodies. Higher PFAS were associated with non-significantly lower odds of reaching protective antibody levels for both vaccines. No consistent patterns were observed for prenatal PFAS exposure. In this cross-sectional study of low-exposed children, PFAS exposure was associated with lower antibody concentrations against tetanus and diphtheria. All estimates were inverse although not all significant, and associations appeared larger than in previous studies without exact vaccination dates. This is of public concern, as lower vaccine-induced antibody concentrations are considered critical adverse effect of PFAS.

items.title: Inflammation and the Association of Early-stage Cardiovascular-Kidney-Metabolic Syndrome with Incident Cardiovascular Disease and All-cause Mortality: Findings from the CARDIA and MESA Cohorts.
items.abstract: Limited data exist on whether inflammation modifies the association between early-stage cardiovascular-kidney-metabolic (CKM) syndrome and clinical events. We included 9,894 participants free of cardiovascular disease (CVD) from the Coronary Artery Risk Development in Young Adults study (CARDIA, Year 20, 2005-2006) and the Multi-Ethnic Study of Atherosclerosis (MESA, Exam 1, 2000-2002). We examined whether interleukin-6 (IL-6; primary) and high-sensitivity C-reactive protein (hsCRP; ≥2 mg/L; secondary) modified associations of early-stage CKM syndrome (stages 2-3 vs 0-1) with incident CVD and all-cause mortality. IL-6 was dichotomized at cohort- and sex-specific medians. Cohort-stratified Cox models were adjusted for age, sex, race/ethnicity, education, smoking, and physical activity; multiplicative and additive effect modification were assessed. During follow-up, 1,635 atherosclerotic CVD events, 567 heart failure events, and 2,593 deaths occurred. After adjustment for CKM stage, IL-6 at or above the median was associated with higher risks of atherosclerotic CVD (hazard ratio, 1.48; 95% CI, 1.33-1.64), heart failure (1.69; 1.41-2.03), and mortality (1.48; 1.36-1.61); hsCRP associations were smaller. IL-6 showed additive effect modification with CKM stage for atherosclerotic CVD (relative excess risk due to interaction, 0.81; 95% CI, 0.17-1.46) but no multiplicative effect modification (P = 0.59), and no effect modification for heart failure or mortality. hsCRP showed no consistent effect modification. Higher IL-6 and hsCRP were each associated with higher cardiovascular and mortality risks independent of early-stage CKM syndrome. IL-6 showed additive effect modification with CKM stage for atherosclerotic CVD, indicating a positive relative excess risk due to interaction among adults with CKM stages 2-3.

items.title: Exposure to multiple cephalosporins and central obesity among rural Chinese adults: A population-based biomonitoring study.
items.abstract: Cephalosporins are commonly used in human and veterinary medicine. Urinary biomonitoring can capture internal exposure from medical, dietary, and environmental sources. However, evidence on cephalosporin exposure and adiposity in adults remains limited so far. A population-based cross-sectional study included 1044 adults from three rural communities in Zhejiang Province, China, between May and June 2023. Twelve urinary cephalosporins were measured by solid-phase extraction coupled with ultra-performance liquid chromatography-tandem mass spectrometry. In a restricted sample of 918 participants, estimated daily intake (EDI) was calculated for 10 cephalosporins, and hazard quotients (HQs) and hazard indices (HIs) were calculated for six compounds as exploratory comparisons with available acceptable daily intake (ADI) benchmarks. Logistic regression models examined associations between cephalosporin detection and WHtR-defined central obesity, with BMI-defined obesity and WC-defined central obesity examined as alternative outcomes. Sensitivity analyses excluded participants with recent antibiotic use and extreme urinary concentrations, and separately those with chronic diseases. At least one target cephalosporin was detected in 383 participants (36.69%). WHtR-defined central obesity, BMI-defined obesity and WC-defined central obesity prevalences were 60.54%, 6.90% and 28.74%, respectively. In the restricted sample, cumulative EDI for the 10 included compounds was <0.01 μg/kg/day in 86.93% of participants, and cumulative HI for the six included compounds exceeded 1 in two participants (0.22%). In fully adjusted models, exposure to human-use cephalosporins (OR = 1.41, 95% CI: 1.07-1.86) and cumulative exposure to total cephalosporins (OR = 1.40, 95% CI: 1.06-1.84) were associated with WHtR-defined central obesity. The positive associations were generally consistent in sensitivity analyses. No corresponding associations were observed for BMI-defined obesity or WC-defined central obesity. Adults from rural communities were exposed to multiple cephalosporins, although overall exposure levels were low and screening indices for the six assessed compounds were below 1 for most participants in Zhejiang Province, China. Urinary exposure to cephalosporins was associated with higher odds of WHtR-defined central obesity.

items.title: Dietary Sugar Intake and Risk of Cognitive Disorders: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis.
items.abstract: Although prior studies have linked excessive dietary sugar intake to adverse cognitive outcomes, the findings of individual studies remain inconsistent, and there is a lack of synthesis. The objective of this study was to comprehensively examine the association between dietary sugar intake and risk of cognitive disorders. The Cochrane, Embase, PubMed, ScienceDirect, and Web of Science databases were searched from inception to December 2025. Prospective cohort, nested case-control or case-cohort studies evaluating the association of dietary total sugar or its subtypes with the risk of cognitive disorders, including cognitive impairment and dementia (including Alzheimer's disease), in adults were reviewed. Details of the studies and main outcomes were extracted independently by 2 reviewers. Among 2171 records screened, 10 prospective cohort studies comprising 12 cohorts and 257 761 participants were included. The number of cohorts and participants for each exposure was as follows: total sugar: 5 (N = 200 812); sugar-sweetened beverages: 9 (N = 214 084); fruit juice: 2 (N = 194 847); fructose: 4 (N = 197 082); sucrose: 3 (N = 194 928); lactose: 3 (N = 194 928); maltose: 3 (N = 194 928); glucose: 3 (N = 194 928). Meta-analysis indicated that individuals with the highest total sugar intake were at a higher risk of cognitive disorders compared with those with the lowest intake (hazard ratio = 1.23, 95% CI = 1.10-1.38, low certainty). No significant associations were observed for any specific sugar subtypes examined, with certainty of evidence ranging from low to very low. The present review suggests that higher total sugar intake may be associated with an increased risk of cognitive disorders. In contrast, the current evidence does not support a clear association between specific sugar subtypes and cognitive disorders. Future studies should prioritize clarifying the dose-response relationship between total sugar intake and cognitive disorders. PROSPERO registration No. CRD42025640308.

items.title: Contemporary screen exposure among children under two: a representative survey, implications and perspectives.
items.abstract: Professional guidelines consistently recommend avoiding screen exposure in children under two years of age; however, international evidence indicates that early media use is widespread. This narrative review synthesizes contemporary data on screen exposure in infancy and toddlerhood, integrates findings from recent longitudinal research on developmental implications, and discusses expectations and intervention strategies across family, clinical, public health, and policy levels. Drawing on international cohorts and previously published representative Hungarian data (N = 2569), we describe high prevalence, substantial daily exposure, and marked socioeconomic gradients. Nearly half of Hungarian 18-month-olds were exposed to screens daily, and over one third exceeded one hour per day on a typical day. Synthesizing literature from the last ten years, we examine early screen use within a developmental-ecological framework. Evidence links higher exposure in the first two years to poorer language, cognitive, and self-regulatory outcomes, while also indicating bi-directional and transactional processes. Beyond total exposure time, displacement of interaction-rich activities and caregiver-driven "technoference" may alter the microstructure of early social exchange, with potential implications for attachment, co-regulation, and language development. Given that early communication and self-regulation form foundational systems for later academic achievement, socio-emotional functioning, and health behaviours, early screen practices may influence longer-term developmental trajectories. We conclude by outlining developmentally informed expectations, family-level strategies, clinical guidance, and emerging policy approaches, emphasizing the need to move beyond descriptive prevalence estimates and strictly restrictive guidelines toward integrated, evidence-based responses adapted to contemporary digital environments.

items.title: Ultrasound elastography of pediatric cervical lymph nodes: a systematic review of clinical potential and current limitations.
items.abstract: Cervical lymphadenopathy is common in children and encompasses reactive, inflammatory, infectious, and malignant conditions. Ultrasound elastography assesses tissue mechanical properties and may complement conventional ultrasonography. This systematic review aimed to critically evaluate the evidence on cervical lymph node elastography in pediatric patients. PubMed, Scopus, and Web of Science were searched on October 8, 2026. Reporting followed PRISMA 2020; the protocol was not prospectively registered. Risk of bias was assessed with QUADAS-2 in diagnostic accuracy studies, and findings were synthesized narratively. Five studies involving 484 pediatric participants were included. Three investigated benign-malignant differentiation and two evaluated inflammatory conditions, using strain elastography, acoustic radiation force impulse imaging, shear wave elastography, or point shear wave elastography. Studies addressing malignancy reported promising diagnostic performance, but numerical inconsistencies in two publications undermined confidence in their accuracy estimates. Four studies assessed with QUADAS-2 showed high or unclear risk of bias in at least one domain; the fifth, lacking diagnostic accuracy outcomes, was assessed descriptively. Increased stiffness occurred in both malignant and benign inflammatory or infectious lymphadenopathy, limiting its specificity for malignancy. Differences in clinical populations, techniques, diagnostic objectives, and reference standards precluded quantitative synthesis. Ultrasound elastography may complement conventional assessment of pediatric cervical lymphadenopathy, but current evidence does not support universal stiffness thresholds or standalone diagnostic use. Prospective pediatric studies with standardized protocols and external validation are needed to establish its incremental value beyond conventional ultrasonography.
