items.title: Adult predation shapes brain evolution in guppies (Poecilia reticulata).
items.abstract: Predation is a powerful evolutionary force shaping many traits of prey species. As the brain is the neural substrate of all behaviours, including essential anti-predator actions, its morphology is expected to be directly shaped by predation. However, while correlative evidence supports this relationship, causal evidence of predation driving brain morphology is currently lacking. Here, we investigated how predation pressure changes brain morphology in guppies (Poecilia reticulata) from replicated artificial selection lines for adult predation survival. We found that after three generations of selection, predation-selected females likely evolved relatively larger brains compared to control fish. In males, while brain size was not affected by predation selection, predation lines showed relatively larger olfactory bulbs. These results demonstrate that predation can directly shape the evolution of brain morphology, remarkably fast and in a sex-specific manner. Comparing our findings to those from natural populations with divergent predation pressures allows us to disentangle the direct predation effects from the indirect ecological effects of high predation pressure that drive brain evolution.

items.title: Plant-soil feedbacks and seed dispersal through space and time: toward an integrative framework.
items.abstract: Background Plants can modify soil microbial communities and nutrient conditions, creating soil legacies that influence the performance of future plants and generate plant-soil feedbacks (PSFs). These legacies are often studied at local scales, whereas seed dispersal and germination determine where and when offspring encounter them. Integrating these processes is essential for understanding how local soil interactions influence plant recruitment and broader ecological dynamics. Scope We develop an integrative framework linking PSF with seed dispersal through space and time by matching seed distributions with the spatial extent of soil legacies and seed persistence and germination timing with legacy duration. Negative PSF reduces subsequent plant performance, whereas positive PSF enhances it. Under negative PSF, spatial displacement or delayed germination may reduce exposure to harmful legacies; under positive PSF, the same shifts may reduce access to beneficial legacies. The framework integrates classical spatial escape mechanisms, including Janzen-Connell distance-dependent escape from enemies near conspecific adults, with temporal escape through delayed recruitment, while considering reciprocal effects of dispersal on PSF and shared ecological drivers. An illustrative synthesis of 216 species identifies candidate cross-species associations: greater spatial dispersal tends to be associated with more positive PSF, whereas longer seedbank persistence tends to be associated with more negative PSF, and the dormancy association weakens after phylogenetic control. These observational patterns do not resolve causal direction. Conclusions By connecting soil legacies with seed movement and timing, this framework provides a mechanistic basis for understanding how local belowground interactions contribute to coexistence, succession, invasion, and restoration. Rather than assuming a universal PSF-dispersal relationship, the framework shows that recruitment outcomes depend on how seed movement and germination timing match the spatial extent and temporal persistence of soil legacies. Embedding PSF in a spatiotemporal context clarifies how local soil legacies scale up through recruitment to shape population and community dynamics.

items.title: Cognitive-behavioral conjoint therapy for posttraumatic stress disorder: A systematic review of outcomes, mechanisms, and clinical applications.
items.abstract: Posttraumatic stress disorder (PTSD) is associated with interpersonal dysfunction, and including loved ones in treatment may benefit both PTSD symptom reduction and relationship functioning. Cognitive-behavioral conjoint therapy (CBCT) for PTSD is a manualized, trauma-focused psychotherapy delivered in a dyadic format, typically to an individual with PTSD and their intimate partner. We replicated and extended a systematic review published in 2020 to incorporate several studies published since then. Procedures for this preregistered systematic review were consistent with PRISMA guidelines. We identified 50 reports representing 41 unique studies: 19 main outcome studies (i.e., five randomized controlled trials [RCTs], four of which were published after the previous review; 12 uncontrolled trials; and two naturalistic outcome studies), 17 secondary analyses, and five ongoing RCTs. Overall, these studies indicate that CBCT for PTSD and its adaptations improve PTSD symptoms. Findings were mixed for relationship satisfaction, co-occurring psychiatric symptoms, and partner accommodation. Baseline relationship satisfaction moderated effects of CBCT for PTSD on relationship outcomes; partner accommodation and social support moderated PTSD outcomes. Adaptations designed to increase efficiency, accessibility, and potency include alternative formats of treatment delivery, modified content, and pharmacological augmentation. The evidence base for CBCT for PTSD has grown rapidly in recent years, but methodological limitations, including small sample sizes, insufficient evidence from well-controlled trials, lack of generalizability of samples, and limited evidence of mechanisms of action, remain. Several ongoing studies were designed and will be well-positioned to address these limitations.

items.title: The mental cost of urban living: neighbourhood deprivation, income, and depressive symptoms in Germany.
items.abstract: Objective This study investigates the established associations between neighbourhood socioeconomic deprivation, household income, and depressive symptoms in Germany, and assesses whether these associations differ across settlement structures. Building on the person-in-environment framework, we understand mental health as an emergent outcome of the interplay between individuals and their environments. Method We analysed cross-sectional data from the nationally representative German Health Update 2019/2020 wave of the European Health Interview Survey (GEDA 2019/2020-EHIS) ​ (N = 20,773). Depressive symptoms were measured using Patient Health Questionnaire-8 (PHQ-8). Polynomial regression models tested linear and quadratic associations of neighbourhood deprivation (German Index of Socioeconomic Deprivation, GISD) with depressive symptoms, and their interaction with household income quintiles. Whether settlement type (cities, urban, rural and sparsely populated counties) moderated these associations was tested explicitly using nested interaction models. Results Higher neighbourhood deprivation was associated with increased depressive symptoms, with a significant quadratic term indicating disproportionately higher symptom severity in highly deprived areas. Household income was inversely associated with depressive symptoms, though its moderation of the deprivation association was only partially supported. Settlement type significantly moderated the deprivation-depression association: the quadratic association was strongest in cities and attenuated, or shifted towards a concave pattern, in less densely populated settlement types. This settlement-related moderation was additionally associated with income, particularly in urban and rural counties, and less consistently in sparsely populated areas. Conclusions The psychological burden of socioeconomic deprivation is not uniform, but differs systematically by settlement context and, less consistently, by individual income. These associations were most pronounced, and most clearly evident, in major cities. Addressing mental health inequalities linked to neighbourhood deprivation may therefore benefit from strategies tailored to settlement-specific conditions, alongside broader efforts aimed at individual socioeconomic resources.

items.title: Functional electrical stimulation-assisted cycling therapy with virtual reality biofeedback for functional recovery in people with chronic spinal cord injury: a feasibility case series.
items.abstract: Study design Feasibility case series. Objectives To evaluate the feasibility and individual therapeutic effects of functional electrical stimulation (FES)-assisted cycling therapy combined with virtual reality (VR) biofeedback (the iCycle) on function and walking outcomes in people with chronic incomplete spinal cord injury (SCI). Setting London Spinal Cord Injury Centre, Royal National Orthopaedic Hospital, UK. Methods Participants undertook up to three 30-minute iCycle sessions weekly in 4-week blocks for up to 12 weeks. Participants were assessed at the end of each block and were given the option to opt-out or continue. FES was applied to lower-limb muscles during alternate pedal revolutions, enabling biofeedback of voluntary effort via the VR cycling platform (Zwift). Clinical outcome measures included International Standards of Neurological Classification of SCI (ISNCSCI) motor and sensory scores, Berg Balance Scale, Trunk Impairment Scale, Walking Index for SCI-II (WISCI-II), 6-Minute Walk Test (6MWT), 10-Metre Walk Test (10MWT) and voluntary power output during cycling. Results Five participants completed 8 or 12 weeks of training. Functional improvements were observed primarily after the first 4-week block. Two participants increased lower extremity motor scores (+3 to +4). Four participants demonstrated gains in walking endurance (6MWT +90-135 m), reduced 10MWT times, and improved WISCI-II scores. Balance and voluntary power output continued to improve for up to 12 weeks. Conclusion iCycle training was feasible for individuals with incomplete chronic SCI. Clinically meaningful improvements in walking, balance, and endurance were observed, most prominently within the first 4-week block. Sponsorship University College London.

items.title: Perceived housing quality and emotional distress among refugees living in camps: a cross-sectional study in Eastern Germany.
items.abstract: Background Housing quality as a key social determinant of health has received growing attention in public health research. Asylum seekers and refugees in European countries are frequently housed in institutionalized, camp-like facilities. These facilities are often characterized by overcrowding and limited privacy, safety, and autonomy. Such conditions constitute an important post-migration stressor and may be a particularly relevant determinant of mental health. This study aimed to examine the association between multiple dimensions of perceived housing quality and emotional distress among refugees living in camps in Eastern Germany. Methods We conducted a cross-sectional study among asylum seekers and refugees living in 16 camps across three federal states in Eastern Germany. Data were collected via a multilingual online survey; fieldwork took place in June and July 2025, and the survey remained accessible until the end of August 2025. As the primary outcome, we assessed emotional distress using the cross-culturally validated Refugee Health Screener-13 (RHS-13) as an indicator of common mental disorders in refugee populations. In addition, we assessed perceived housing quality using multidimensional indicators as well as relevant sociodemographic covariates. To examine associations between housing quality and emotional distress, we fitted multivariable linear regression models with housing quality indicators as exposures and the RHS-13 sum score as the outcome. First, each housing quality indicator was included separately in single-indicator regression models, which were adjusted for prespecified sociodemographic variables. We then included multiple indicators across different housing quality dimensions simultaneously in the main model, which was also adjusted for sociodemographic variables. Results Most participants scored at or above the cutoff for emotional distress (79%; RHS-13 ≥ 11), with nearly half scoring in the severe-distress range (48%; RHS-13 ≥ 25). Most assessed housing quality indicators showed associations with emotional distress when examined separately in adjusted single-indicator regression models. When multiple indicators across multiple housing quality dimensions were included simultaneously in the adjusted main model, safety, lighting conditions, autonomy, and feelings of boredom or imprisonment within the refugee camp remained associated with emotional distress, whereas crowding, frequent transfers between camps, and region did not. Conclusions Perceived housing quality is closely associated with emotional distress among refugees living in Eastern German camps. Psychosocial and institutional dimensions of housing quality appear particularly relevant to emotional distress. Housing policies for refugees in European countries should therefore consider not only the physical structure of housing but also its psychosocial and institutional dimensions, such as safety, autonomy, and daily-life restrictions, when addressing mental health inequalities in this population.

items.title: Case Study on Nursing Pain Interpretation and Residents' Ability to be Understood.
items.abstract: Introduction In long term care [LTC], the high prevalence of painful illnesses and dementia contributes to complex care needs and challenging pain management. What further complicates matters for residents in this context is the inability to be understood. Purpose In addition to not being understood in the expression of their pain, many residents with a cognitive impairment will exhibit behavioral and psychological symptoms of dementia [BPSDs]. Pain indicators may then resemble BPSDs and be interpreted and treated as such. Little is known about this interpretation and subsequent interventions by nurses. Design To explore the management of pain in the LTC context, a single-site retrospective case-study was conducted in a Canadian province using a predefined list of indicators drawn from validated observational pain assessment instruments and the pain literature. Methods These indicators guided the review of residents' charts by abstracting data from nursing documentation and medication administration records. Nursing interpretation of symptoms, as documented in their notes, as either pain or behavior, as well as their actions, were examined. Also explored were associations between the resident's ability to be understood and the nursing interpretation of their symptoms. Results The analysis discovered that many symptoms were more likely to be interpreted as behavior versus pain. Furthermore, a relationship was discovered between the resident's ability to be understood and the interpretation of some symptoms as behavior versus pain. Conclusions and clinical implications Recommendations are made to better support nurses with this important yet challenging role of pain and behavior interpretation with residents who cannot be understood.

items.title: Evaluation of a clinician and lived experience peer worker co-led suicide prevention aftercare program: A non-randomized controlled trial of Next Steps.
items.abstract: Objective Evidence is lacking for the effectiveness of suicide prevention aftercare programs incorporating the lived-experience peer workforce. A non-randomized controlled trial evaluated Next Steps, a community-based clinician and peer-worker co-led aftercare program for individuals following a suicide-related emergency department presentation. It was hypothesized that compared to treatment-as-usual controls, participants will be less likely to have a repeat suicide-related presentation to an emergency department, have lower rates of re-presentations to the emergency department, and be associated with fewer all-cause deaths, in a 12-month follow-up. Method The study included 81 participants and 1412 controls. Re-presentation to an emergency department was analyzed using a Kaplan Meier plot, rates of re-presentation were analyzed using a negative binomial regression, and all-cause mortality was analyzed using Chi-square and Fisher's exact tests. Results No significant differences between participants and controls were found on suicide-related re-presentation (29.6% and 19.8%, respectively), or rates of re-presentation (p = 0.333). No deaths were recorded in the intervention group compared to 17 deaths in controls (1.2%), with the null hypothesis retained. Conclusions Next Steps did not demonstrate superiority over treatment-as-usual following a suicide-related emergency department presentation. The program offers a viable alternative to treatment-as-usual and one that involves the lived-experience workforce in implementation. Further research of peer involvement in aftercare programs is strongly indicated, and a gap remains in evidence of effectiveness at the level of controlled research trials.

items.title: Early caregiving adversity is associated with elevated pro-inflammatory gene expression during adolescence.
items.abstract: Background Early life adversity (ELA) is thought to increase risk for poor health outcomes, in part through induction of a persistent pro-inflammatory phenotype. Though ELA has been consistently associated with elevated circulating markers of inflammation in varied adult populations, meta-analytic work has found mixed links between ELA and circulating protein markers of inflammation in adolescents, leaving the pathways by which the adult inflammatory phenotype emerges unclear. Here we examined whether alterations in pro-inflammatory and Type I interferon (antiviral) gene expression in circulating immune cells (the Conserved Transcriptional Response to Adversity; CTRA) might provide a more sensitive measure of ELA-linked phenotypes in adolescents. Methods We assessed pro-inflammatory (NF-κB) and anti-viral (Interferon Response Factor) transcription factor activity and downstream gene expression in peripheral blood samples from 18 internationally adopted youth who had experienced previous institutional caregiving (a profound form of ELA) and 34 comparison, non-adopted youth. Results Consistent with the CTRA, relative to comparison youth, youth with a history of ELA showed elevated pro-inflammatory (NF-κB) and decreased antiviral (IRF) transcription factor activity. We found no group differences on a priori downstream gene expression composites. Differentially expressed transcripts were preferentially derived from CD16 + and CD16- monocytes, responsible for coordinating the early inflammatory stages of immune responses. Conclusions These findings confirm ELA-linked inflammatory gene regulation in circulating blood cells during adolescence. Compared to plasma protein measures, functional genomic (RNA) measures of inflammation may provide more sensitive, early indexes of developmental trajectories of inflammation following adversity, prior to emergence of an adult ELA-linked inflammatory phenotype associated with disease.

items.title: <sup>1</sup>H MRS reveals impact of early adversity and age on neurometabolic profiles in women.
items.abstract: Exposure to early-life stress (ELS), including neglect or abuse, is known for its detrimental effects on brain health. This study investigated how ELS interacts with chronological age to impact on brain metabolism in middle-aged women using proton magnetic resonance spectroscopy ( 1 H MRS) at 3 T. High-quality spectra from the hippocampus (HC) and posterior cingulate cortex (PCC) from 75 women, including 53% with ELS exposure before puberty, were analyzed. Generalized additive models assessed non-linear effects of ELS severity and chronological age on neurometabolites related to neuroinflammation and neurotransmitter cycling. Significant interactions emerged for myo-inositol (Ins) in both regions and glutamine (Gln) in the PCC, where greater ELS severity was linked to age-related increases in Ins and Gln concentrations. These results were robust when additionally controlling for symptoms of depression, anxiety, and PTSD, as well as SES, education, menopause status, and smoking. The observed patterns suggest that ELS exposure before puberty, at the older age range, is associated with glial and glutamatergic alterations that are indicative of neuroinflammation, potentially reflecting vulnerability to adverse brain health outcomes.

items.title: Longitudinal multimodal MRI correlates of subclinical insomnia symptoms and depressive mood in young adults.
items.abstract: Background Insomnia symptoms and depressive mood often change together in young adults, but their longitudinal associations with diffusion tensor image analysis along the perivascular space (DTI-ALPS), an indirect index of perivascular-space diffusivity, and within-limbic functional connectivity remain unclear. Methods 308 university students (233 women; age 19.0 ± 0.9 years) completed the Insomnia Severity Index (ISI), Self-Rating Depression Scale (SDS), diffusion MRI, and resting-state fMRI at baseline and after 1.7 ± 0.5 years. Associations among change scores were tested with permutation-based general linear models with false discovery rate correction, followed by exploratory indirect-association models. Results ISI and SDS increased slightly (dz = 0.16 and 0.20), whereas DTI-ALPS and within-limbic connectivity decreased (dz = -0.59 and - 0.26). Greater ISI increases were associated with larger DTI-ALPS decreases (β = -0.31, 95% CI [-0.42, -0.21]). DTI-ALPS decreases were associated with decreases in within-limbic connectivity (β = 0.17 [0.05, 0.28]) and increases in SDS (β = -0.13 [-0.25, -0.02]); connectivity decreases were associated with SDS increases (β = -0.18 [-0.29, -0.07]). Full models, including covariates, explained 4-16% of the variance in change. The serial indirect association was small (β = 0.0052, 95% CI [0.0004, 0.0133]). An indirect association was also observed in the reversed model. Temporal precedence was not established. Conclusions In a nonclinical cohort, modest changes in insomnia symptoms and depressive mood covaried with changes in DTI-ALPS and limbic connectivity. These are candidate imaging correlates of subclinical symptom variation and should not be generalized to insomnia disorder or major depressive disorder.

items.title: Effects of Androstadienone on Women's Preferences for Male Facial Skin Color: The Moderating Role of Intrasexual Competition.
items.abstract: Previous studies have shown that androstadienone (AND) can influence women's preferences for male facial shape cues, but it remains unclear whether this effect extends to other visual dimensions of male faces, such as facial skin color. The present study examined whether exposure to AND influences women's preferences for male facial skin color and whether this effect is moderated by intrasexual competition. Eighty-three women completed a two-session within-subject experiment in which they were exposed to AND and a placebo solution on two consecutive days. In each session, participants completed a two-alternative forced-choice task using male facial stimuli manipulated along three CIE L*a*b* dimensions: lightness, redness, and yellowness. For each dimension, participants chose the face they perceived as more attractive in a long-term mate-choice context. Participants preferred increased redness and increased lightness in both conditions, whereas increased yellowness was selected below chance only in the AND condition. A trial-level binomial generalized linear mixed-effects model showed that AND selectively enhanced preference for increased lightness, whereas no significant AND effects were observed for redness or yellowness. This lightness-specific effect was moderated by intrasexual competition: AND increased preference for lightness primarily among women with lower levels of intrasexual competition, but not among women with higher levels of intrasexual competition. These findings suggest that AND may selectively modulate mating-related facial preferences across specific visual dimensions and that its effect depends on women's baseline competitive orientation.

items.title: Frontocentral theta oscillations bias perceptual judgments of ambiguous visual causality.
items.abstract: Human perceptual decisions frequently rely on incomplete, ambiguous sensory inputs resolved prior to stimulus onset. Prior electrophysiological work confirms pre-event frontocentral ERP components predict ambiguous visual causal judgments, yet the spectrotemporal signatures of spontaneous oscillatory biases remain uncharacterized. Frontocentral theta signals proactive cognitive control, but whether pre-event theta oscillation modulates high-order causal inference independently of stimulus-locked ERPs remains untested. Thirteen volunteers (16 recruited, 3 excluded) completed a staircase-calibrated Michotte launching task with 64-channel EEG recorded. Time-frequency decomposition, permutation tests, and ERP-subtraction controls isolated pre-coincidence oscillatory patterns distinguishing causal bouncing and non-causal streaming percepts under PSE level. Elevated pre-coincidence Fz theta power robustly biased observers toward causal reports, showing a negative linear relationship between theta magnitude and streaming response ratios. The theta bias survived single-trial ERP removal, proving oscillatory signals carry predictive information distinct from known ERP markers. These findings imply frontocentral theta pre-allocates anticipatory cognitive resources to support intuitive causal reasoning, separating theta's executive regulatory function from alpha's modulation of basic sensory awareness. This study constructs a novel spectrotemporal framework explaining how spontaneous frontal oscillations sculpt ambiguous causal perception.

items.title: Does the mirror have magic? The moderating role of self-awareness intensity on sharing behavior in 3- to 6-year-old children.
items.abstract: This study examined whether theintensityof self-awareness induction moderates sharing behavior in 3- to 6-year-old children. Two experiments employed distinct sharing paradigms. Experiment 1 used a dictator-game sticker-sharing task. Experiment 2 used a balloon-sharing task. Both adopted a between-subjects design that crossed three self-awareness conditions with two age groups. The three conditions were: anenhanced mirror-selfcondition (mirror plus self-relevant cues), amirror-selfcondition (mirror only), and a control condition (no mirror). The two age groups were 3-4 years and 5-6 years. The results showed that, in both tasks, children in theenhanced mirror-selfcondition shared significantly more than those in the control condition. In the balloon task, they also shared significantly more than those in themirror-selfcondition, whereas themirror-selfand control conditions did not differ. Meanwhile, children aged 5-6 years shared significantly more than those aged 3-4 years across both tasks. Among the 3- to 6-year-old preschoolers studied here, these findings indicate that the reliability of the mirror-self effect may depend on thestrengthof self-awareness induction. Higher-intensity self-awareness induction appears to more reliably promote prosocial behavior in preschoolers. The results support the continuity hypothesis of objective self-awareness theory, help resolve prior inconsistencies regarding the stability of mirror effects, and offer empirically grounded implications for fostering prosocial development.

items.title: The Perceived Suitability of Digitally Delivered Impulse-Focused Techniques in Binge Eating: A Qualitative Intervention Development Study.
items.abstract: Objective Impulsivity and inhibitory control difficulties are key mechanisms in binge eating behaviour in individuals with eating disorders. Digital interventions targeting these mechanisms are primarily developed for weight loss rather than the specific psychological and clinical needs of the population with binge eating, creating a gap in treatment. This study explored lived experience perceptions of digitally delivered impulse-focused techniques to inform future intervention development. Method Fourteen participants (2 males, 12 females) were recruited via social media for online semi-structured interviews. Participants viewed a short demonstration video of an existing impulse-focused dietary change intervention (ImpulsePal) and discussed the perceived suitability of its techniques for binge eating contexts. Data were analysed using Reflexive Thematic Analysis. Results Three overarching themes were generated regarding the perceived suitability and potential risks of digitally delivered impulse-focused techniques; designing for accessibility, personalisation, and supportive communication; and unmet needs extending beyond impulse management, including connection, reflection, and self-awareness. Initial Guiding Principles for future digital intervention development in binge eating contexts are presented. Conclusions With careful adaptation, an impulse-focused intervention like ImpulsePal could complement existing support pathways, but further development and feasibility testing are required before wider testing or use in people with binge eating.

items.title: Surprised Facial Expressions Strengthen Memory for Neutral Pictures Irrespective of Task Demands.
items.abstract: Facial expressions are crucial in social interaction. Previous studies have consistently demonstrated that positive and negative facial expressions affect memory for relevant faces and even other stimuli in different tasks. However, little is known about the role of surprised facial expressions on memory processes. Therefore, the present study aimed to investigate whether surprised facial expressions influence memory for emotional stimuli in different task demands. To address this issue, participants were presented with surprised or neutral facial expressions together with positive, negative or neutral pictures. Moreover, participants were asked to memorize the pictures or to indicate the emotional content of the pictures or the facial expression. Subsequently, participants completed an old/new recognition task regarding the pictures. Results showed that surprised facial expressions, as compared to neutral ones, resulted in better recognition of neutral pictures, irrespective of task demands. Surprised facial expressions also enhanced recognition of positive and negative pictures when the task involved facial expression processing, although this broader effect was not significantly different from that effect when facial expressions were task-irrelevant. These findings highlight the role of surprised facial expressions on memory for other stimuli.

items.title: A Pilot Study of the Neural Activation Associated with Convergence Subtypes in Individuals with Convergence Insufficiency.
items.abstract: Purpose The purpose of this pilot investigation was to assess the neural correlates of convergence eye movement subtypes in individuals with convergence insufficiency using functional magnetic resonance imaging (fMRI). Methods Data were gathered from six individuals with convergence insufficiency. Brain activation was assessed using fMRI while subjects made convergence eye movements in response to stimuli that primarily led to changes in: (1) accommodative convergence (monocular viewing through a -2.00 D lens), (2) proximal convergence (monocular viewing of Difference-of-Gaussian (DOG) targets at different distances) and (3) disparity convergence (step increases in the disparity of a random dot stereogram). Results Areas of brain activation were dependent on the convergence stimulus. Subjects with convergence insufficiency showed substantial activation in the frontal lobes and in other areas associated with visual attention in the accommodative convergence and proximal convergence conditions. In the disparity condition, brain activation was primarily found in the occipital cortex. Conclusion These results suggest that activation seen in fMRI studies with convergence eye movements is dependent on the stimulus used to induce convergence. In the accommodative and proximal convergence conditions, brain activation was greater in areas associated with visual attention. In the disparity convergence condition, brain activation was primarily found in the occipital cortex.

items.title: An Intrapersonal Network Approach to Acute Symptom Dynamics After Sport-Related Concussion.
items.abstract: Background Post-concussion presentations are heterogeneous, characterized by various nonspecific self-report symptoms. Historically complete rest was the standard recommendation for concussion care, but with relatively high rates of persistent symptoms, active domain-specific interventions have been popularized. Determining which intervention is warranted can be difficult when concurrent psychological and preexisting health factors exacerbate injury-related sequelae. Objectives We sought to apply within-person network analysis to an observational study to characterize temporal patterns in acute symptoms. Methods Participants were 403 collegiate student-athletes from the Concussion, Assessment, Research, and Education Consortium with sufficient data on the Sport Concussion Assessment Tool, Third Edition. We used seven serial symptom evaluations immediately post-injury to estimate intrapersonal partial correlation networks and derive centrality frequency and in-/out-strength magnitudes. Contemporaneous networks represent within-day symptom associations with undirected edge weights; temporal networks represent day-to-day symptom associations with edge weights directed temporally from t to t + 1. Results Sadness (mean [M] = 0.99) and more emotional (M = 0.96) were the most central symptoms in the contemporaneous network. For the temporal networks, fatigue/low energy (M = 0.53) and feeling slowed down (M = 0.47) had the greatest in-strength, while confusion (M = 0.84) and neck pain (M = 0.78) had the greatest out-strength. Conclusions After concussion, nonspecific cognitive complaints are common across presentations despite substantial heterogeneity in central symptoms. Vestibulo-ocular and cervicogenic symptoms frequently elicit next-day symptomatology and are associated with increased risk for persistent symptoms, though evidence-based treatments exist. Cognitive-/fatigue-related symptoms are likely to be exacerbated by other sequelae, highlighting the importance of active management and an early, graded return to physical activity that encourages symptom habituation.

items.title: Effects of the HeartSync Intervention on Depression, Anxiety, and Life Satisfaction in the USA.
items.abstract: HeartSync is an Inner Healing Prayer intervention that has been used mostly in Christian lay ministry since 2010. The purpose of this study was to examine the effectiveness of this inner healing approach for the treatment of symptoms of depression/anxiety in clinical settings in the United States. In this quasi-experimental study, participants (n = 31) were assessed for depressive symptoms before, during, at the end, and 90 days after 10 sessions of HeartSync treatment. The PHQ-9, CES-D, Satisfaction with Life Scale, and GAD-7 were administered at each time point. The results indicated that (1) the average PHQ-9 score decreased by 65%, with 77% of participants having symptoms that decreased by 50%; (2) the mean CES-D score decreased by 60%, with 68% of participants having symptoms that decreased by 50%; (3) the mean GAD-7 score decreased by 55%, with 61% of participants having symptoms that decreased by 50%; and (4) the mean Satisfaction with Life Scale score increased by 123%, with 68% of participants indicating improvements of 50% or more in life satisfaction. Patient-reported outcomes (PROs) were also assessed, yielding an effectiveness rating of 8.4 out of 10. These findings provide preliminary support for HeartSync as an effective intervention for the treatment of depressive and anxiety symptoms and warrants further testing in a randomized controlled trial against other standard treatments for emotional disorders.

items.title: Interventions to reduce perinatal suicidality: a global systematic review.
items.abstract: Introduction Perinatal suicidality (suicidal thoughts, behaviours, plans and attempts) is a risk factor for suicide. Evidence on interventions to reduce perinatal suicidality remains limited. This systematic review examined the effectiveness of non-pharmacological interventions to reduce suicidality in perinatal women. Methods This review was registered with PROSPERO (CRD420251081528). Seven databases were searched from 2010 to December 2025. Interventions assessing a reduction in perinatal suicidality as a primary, secondary, or safety monitoring outcome were included. Two reviewers independently screened articles. A narrative summary was compiled. Risk of bias was assessed using the Mixed Methods Appraisal Tool. Results Six studies were included: 5 randomised controlled trials (3 individually randomised, 1 cluster, 1 noninferiority) and 1 historical controlled trial. Three studies investigated suicidality as a primary or secondary outcome, and three studies collected suicidality data for safety monitoring. Of these, two investigated multidisciplinary community health programmes, and one evaluated a behavioural activation therapy. Two studies showed a reduction in suicidality, and one showed a significant reduction at 3-4 months postpartum, but not at 7-8 months. Three studies assessed suicidality as safety monitoring. These studies investigated eye movement desensitisation and reprocessing therapy, a practice-level intervention incorporated into obstetric practices, and an electronic mindfulness-based intervention. These studies were not adequately powered to assess a reduction in suicidality. Discussion Few studies have investigated suicidality as a primary or secondary outcome. Although some health system level and psychological interventions were associated with a reduction in suicidality, robust evidence from interventions specifically designed to reduce perinatal suicidality is needed.

items.title: Gifts for the dead: Maya children's developing theory of mind and their participation in Día de los Muertos.
items.abstract: To better understand the nature of Theory of Mind (ToM) and the cultural dynamics of its development, developmental research should consider new approaches to investigate its use in context. This study sought to understand how participation in Day of the Dead, a holiday involving both real and unseen minds, may involve ToM. Participants in this study were 50 indigenous Tzotzil Mayan children (range = 5-11 years, 46% female) and their caregivers. It was predicted that children with greater ToM would score higher in a gift-giving task where the object was to give a pretend spirit its preferred gifts. Children who passed a classic false-belief task were more likely to give the spirit its preferred gifts. Data were collected in June 2023.

items.title: Identifying voices using confidence judgments under deadline pressure.
items.abstract: Voice identification from categorical lineups can be error-prone. We tested whether Brewer and colleagues' radical alternative to categorical face lineups also improves classification accuracy for earwitnesses. This procedure requires witnesses to rate, under deadline pressure, how confident they are that each lineup member matches their memory of the perpetrator. Participants ( N = 803) attempted to identify a perpetrator from a categorical voice lineup, a confidence-based voice lineup with deadlines, or one without deadlines. Consistent with the findings of Brewer and colleagues, classification accuracy was higher for confidence-based procedures than for categorical lineups. Aligning with this result, discriminability, i.e., the ability to distinguish innocent from guilty suspects, was also higher in confidence-based than categorical lineups. We found some evidence that, for voice identification, it is beneficial to omit deadline pressure; time may support the formation of stable voice representations. Overall, our findings support the conclusion that confidence-based voice procedures are better able to identify guilty suspects than traditional categorical procedures.

items.title: Impact of mood and neurocognitive diagnosis on California Verbal Learning Test intrusions, repetitions and recognition.
items.abstract: Mood symptoms, including both depression and anxiety, have been shown to have differential patterns on neuropsychological test results. Specific patterns of mood impacting the outcomes of the California Verbal Learning Test (CVLT) have not been fully explored, especially as they may interact with cognitive diagnoses. This study analysed data from 402 adult participants across two sites who underwent outpatient neuropsychological assessment. Specific analyses included whether the interaction between depression symptomatology with cognitive diagnosis (no diagnosis, Mild Neurocognitive Disorder, or Major Neurocognitive Disorder) was associated with CVLT repetition, intrusions, recognition hits and recognition false positives covarying for age, gender, education and site. These analyses were then repeated for the interaction between anxiety symptomatology and cognitive diagnosis. Results identified patterns of predictability, with significant interactions between depression and cognitive diagnosis predicting intrusion errors (β = -11.770, p < .001) and false positive errors (β = -3.942, p = .006), such that significant depression symptoms and a cognitive diagnosis were associated with fewer intrusion and false positive errors. There were also main effects for depression predicting recognition hits (β = -.664, p = .005), cognitive diagnosis predicting recognition hits (β = -1.273, p < .001; β = -.813, p = .002) and anxiety predicting repetition errors (β = -.896, p = .044). These results show potential patterns for clinicians to analyse in their patient populations to help differentiate whether cognitive diagnosis, mood symptomatology and/or an interaction between the two may be present for their patients.

items.title: Anxiety sensitivity as a transdiagnostic factor in paediatric chronic pain and sleep disturbances: a systematic review.
items.abstract: Objective This systematic review sought to highlight what is known about paediatric anxiety sensitivity (AS), chronic pain, and sleep disturbances, with the goal of improving theories on chronic pain and sleep and identifying novel areas for intervention. Methods PubMed, SCOPUS, and PsycINFO were searched through June 2026. Inclusion criteria: samples aged 0-18, assessed AS in relation to either chronic pain, sleep, or both, and were accessible in English. Of the 26 articles that met inclusion criteria, nine examined AS and sleep and 17 examined AS and chronic pain. No articles examined all three variables in concert. Results Higher AS was associated with worse sleep quality and efficiency, longer sleep onset latency, and insomnia symptomatology. AS was also related to worse pain outcomes, particularly fear of physical arousal, and may relate to the development and maintenance of chronic pain. Conclusions This systematic review highlights what is known about AS and sleep disturbances and AS and chronic pain in paediatric samples. No articles have been published examining these variables together. A theoretical model is proposed suggesting that AS may be an important target in clinical interventions with the goal of improving both paediatric chronic pain and sleep problems.

items.title: Ethnicity- and gender-based social stressors and parental socialization in Korean Chinese adolescent adjustment.
items.abstract: Although extensive research has documented the adverse effects of social stressors, such as ethnicity- and gender-based discrimination, on adolescent development, much of this work has focused on Western contexts. This survey study was conducted with 267 Korean Chinese adolescents (59% female; M age = 15.24 years, SD age = 1.66, age range: 12-18 years), examining how three forms of perceived discrimination linked to adolescents' psychosocial and academic adjustment, as well as the roles of parental socialization practices. Perceived discrimination by South Koreans, but not by Han Chinese, was linked to more depressive symptoms and delinquency. Gender nonconformity teasing was associated with more depressive symptoms and suicidal ideation. Parental cultural socialization was associated with lower suicidal ideation and delinquency and higher school attachment. Parental gender norm socialization was positively associated with school attachment. These findings underscore the negative implications of ethnicity- and gender-based discrimination, highlight the positive developmental correlates of parental cultural socialization, and suggest that parental gender norm socialization might serve a context-specific adaptive function.

items.title: Assessing book-length reading comprehension through knowledge structures.
items.abstract: Background Book-length reading requires readers to continuously maintain, update and integrate information across extended texts. However, traditional comprehension assessments of book-length reading provide limited insight into readers' ability to organize textual information globally. Aims The present study examined whether knowledge structures can be used to assess students' comprehension of book-length texts and to evaluate the cross-genre applicability and diagnostic value of this approach. Methodology Knowledge-structure representations were collected from 209 students after they read a narrative novel or an expository science book. Bayesian regression models were used to predict reading comprehension. Additional comparisons were conducted to examine differences in knowledge structures between students with different levels of comprehension. Results Knowledge structures measured by semantic networks predicted book-length text comprehension in both genres. At the same time, the knowledge structures constructed by students after narrative reading tended to reflect a sequence-based structure organized by temporal and causal relations, whereas those constructed after expository reading tended to reflect a hierarchy-based structure organized by logical relations among concepts. In addition, high-performing readers constructed networks with higher transitivity and clustering coefficient, and greater similarity to the expert reference network, indicating stronger structural organization. Low-performing readers' networks showed weaker or more fragmented organization and lower similarity to the expert reference network. Conclusions This study extends the assessment based on knowledge structure to book-length reading and shows that semantic networks can capture the structural quality of students' understanding after extended reading. This approach offers a promising framework for diagnostic assessment and targeted reading instruction.

items.title: Manifestations of Mpox in Males: An Australian Case Series.
items.abstract: Background Mpox commonly presents with anogenital lesions, creating diagnostic overlap with other causes of male genital ulceration, pustulation and oedema. Recognition is particularly relevant for clinicians assessing penile, perianal or proctitic symptoms, where delayed diagnosis may result in complications and transmission. Objectives To describe the male genital and anogenital manifestations of mpox in an Australian case series, including lesion morphology, co-infections, diagnostic pitfalls and complications relevant to male genital dermatology. Methods We performed a retrospective review of 50 consecutive adults who presented to local health services between 15 July 2023 and 1 October 2025 and tested positive for mpox by nucleic acid amplification testing. Clinical notes, pathology results, immunisation records and available lesion photographs were reviewed. This analysis emphasises male genital and anogenital findings. Results All patients were men who have sex with men, with a mean age of 38.6 years. The anogenital region was the most frequently involved anatomical area: penile swabs were positive in 25/50 patients (50%) and rectal swabs in 14/50 (28%). Presentations included penile lesions, perianal or rectal symptoms, proctitis, localised penile or perianal swelling and, in five patients, rectal mpox detected despite no visible external lesions. Lesions were described as pustular, ulcerated, crusted, papular, vesicular, erosive or exudative, and were variably painful, painless or pruritic. Differential diagnoses included primary syphilis, genital herpes simplex virus, molluscum contagiosum and folliculitis. Ten patients had concurrent sexually transmitted infections, including one lesion positive for both mpox and herpes simplex virus and one lesion positive for both mpox and syphilis. Five patients required hospital admission; male genital complications included severe proctitis, sepsis with concurrent sexually transmitted infection, penile swelling, chronic penile ulceration and urinary retention requiring catheterisation. Conclusions Mpox is an important cause of male genital and anogenital disease. In this cohort it most often presented as acute penile or rectal disease, but could mimic more common sexually transmitted infections or, rarely, a chronic penile ulcer requiring biopsy to exclude malignancy. Male genital dermatology services should consider mpox in new penile, perianal or proctitic presentations in at-risk men, particularly where lesions are pustular, ulcerated, exudative or associated with oedema, lymphadenopathy or concurrent sexually transmitted infection.

items.title: Factors Associated With Successful In-Office Diagnostic Vitreous Aspiration.
items.abstract: Background and objective To identify demographic, clinical, and procedural factors associated with successful vitreous taps and aspirate volume to optimize candidate selection and technique for this procedure. Study design/patients and methods We performed a retrospective analysis of patients who underwent in-office diagnostic vitreous aspiration from January 2010 to December 2022. We reviewed patient demographics, clinical characteristics, and procedural factors and then performed univariate and multivariable regression analyses to identify factors associated with successful vitreous tap and aspirate volume. Results Among 101 eyes from 101 patients (64% aged 60 years or older, 37.6% female) who received diagnostic vitreous taps in clinic, 77.2% were successfully performed, while the remainder required aqueous sampling. Regression analyses showed that past vitrectomy ( p p = 0.001) were associated with successful taps, where eyes with prior vitrectomy had a 100% success rate as compared to 68% in eyes without prior vitrectomy. Interestingly, larger 25-gauge needles were less successful (68%) than 27-gauge needles (93%), likely due to documentation of only the largest needle gauge attempted. Eyes that underwent successful vitreous aspiration had a mean aspirate volume of 0.3 ± 0.1 mL, with higher volumes observed in phakic than pseudophakic eyes (0.3 ± 0.1 vs. 0.2 ± 0.1 mL, p = 0.034), as well as those with suspected or actual diagnoses of endogenous versus exogenous infectious uveitis (0.4 vs. 0.2 mL, p = 0.002 and 0.4 vs. 0.2 mL, p = 0.003, respectively). Conclusion In-office diagnostic vitreous taps are more likely to be successful in vitrectomized eyes but do not appear to be affected by other factors such as the patient's age, severity or type of intraocular inflammation, or larger needle gauge.

items.title: Dapagliflozin transfer in breast milk may be clinically insignificant-An opportunity for optimization of evidence-based management of heart failure in postpartum patients.
items.abstract: Background Dapagliflozin (DAPA), a sodium-glucose co-transporter inhibitor (SGLT2i), has been shown to prevent the development of heart failure and slow the progression of pre-existing heart failure; however, there are limited data published to demonstrate the safety of postpartum lactating individuals taking SGLT2is. Methods Lactating patients received two oral doses of 10 mg DAPA over a 48-h period. Breast milk and plasma were collected 2 h after the second dose. Samples were processed via liquid chromatography mass spectrometry (LCMS) analysis. Breast milk concentrations of DAPA were divided by plasma concentrations of DAPA (in ng/mL). The absolute (AID; i.e., daily infant dose) and relative infant doses (RID) were performed. An RID of 10% was considered the limit of acceptable exposure. Results Three of four participants were able to produce enough sample for assessment. Across three samples, the mean DAPA concentrations in plasma and breast milk were 77.6 ± 10.2 and 16.8 ± 3.1 ng/mL, respectively. Mean AID was 8.04 × 10 -3 ± 2.50 × 10 -3 mg/day and the mean RID was 7.73 ± 3.9%. Conclusions This study demonstrates that human breast milk collected at peak anticipated maternal concentrations of DAPA has a mean RID below 10%. This is the first report of human transfer levels for DAPA, generating preliminary lactation-specific pharmacokinetic data that are essential to support evidence-based treatment of breastfeeding individuals and reduce disparities in their representation within cardiovascular therapeutic research.

items.title: Knowledge and Attitudes Regarding Sickle Cell Anaemia and Genetic Testing Among Students of King Saud Bin Abdulaziz University for Health Sciences, Al-Ahsa.
items.abstract: Sickle cell anaemia (SCA) represents a significant global health challenge, especially in areas where the frequency of the sickle cell gene is high, as in Saudi Arabia. Millions of people globally suffer from this hereditary blood disorder. Genetic testing offers opportunities in prevention and personalized treatment approaches. Moreover, students at nursing and health colleges are the backbone of public education in the future. Hence, examining the levels of knowledge and attitudes regarding SCA and genetic testing among nursing and health sciences students has valuable implications for public health interventions, policy development, and community engagement initiatives. To assess the level of knowledge and attitudes regarding SCA and genetic testing among bachelor's students at King Saud bin Abdulaziz University for Health Sciences, Al-Ahsa, Saudi Arabia. This study employed a descriptive, cross-sectional design using convenience sampling among 309 students at King Saud bin Abdulaziz University for Health Sciences in Al-Ahsa. Data were gathered at a single time point via an online self-reported survey including: (1) Demographic and background information form. (2) Participants' knowledge assessment of SCA and genetic testing, which consisted of 13 items (score range 0-13). Scores ≥ 7.8 (≥ 60%) were classified as satisfactory; < 7.8 as unsatisfactory. (3) Participants' attitudes towards SCA and genetic testing, which were measured on a 12-item, 3-point Likert scale (range 12-36). Scores ≥ 21.6 (≥ 60%) were positive; < 21.6 were negative. The participants' ages ranged from 17 to 23 years. Most of the participants were female (70.9%). Approximately 72.2% showed a satisfactory level of knowledge about SCA and genetic testing, with a total mean knowledge score (x̄ ± SD = 7.96 ± 2.527). The majority (90.6%) of the participants exhibited a positive attitude towards SCA and genetic testing, with a total mean attitude score (x̄ ± SD = 28.4 ± 4.6). Although this study demonstrated satisfactory knowledge and positive attitudes towards SCA and genetic testing, the findings are derived from a single university sample, constraining their broader generalizability. Future research should employ longitudinal designs to assess how knowledge and attitudes evolve and how they influence professional behaviour after graduation.

items.title: Factors Associated With Satisfaction and Perceived Change Among University Students After Implementing Care Practices to Address Psychological Distress.
items.abstract: Introduction Entering university symbolizes a sudden transition for most students, who are faced with an unfamiliar environment, new demands, and adaptations associated with individual and collective expectations regarding entry into higher education, which may be linked to the onset of psychological distress. Objective To analyze the factors associated with the repercussions of satisfaction and perceived change among university students after implementing care practices to address psychological distress. Method A cross-sectional study involving 540 students from a public federal university in Brazil. The assessment was conducted using the Patient Satisfaction with Mental Health Services Scale and the Perceived Change Scale. The analysis included descriptive statistics and multiple linear regression models, with p Results Higher scores for satisfaction and perceived change were associated with participation in activities such as Circle Dance and psychological counseling, as well as with sense of belonging to the campus. In contrast, students who self-identified as Indigenous, of "Other" gender, in their fourth year of study and those who required housing assistance and social services had lower mean scores on the scales. Conclusion Participating in care practices promotes well-being and adaptation. However, initiatives must account for the pre-existing vulnerability of minority and socioeconomically disadvantaged groups, whose continued enrollment requires ongoing institutional support.

items.title: A cross-study single-cell atlas reveals heterogeneous transcriptional states in PMA-differentiated THP-1 cells.
items.abstract: THP-1 cells are widely used to model human monocyte-to-macrophage differentiation, yet the transcriptional states associated with the labels "undifferentiated" and "differentiated" may vary among studies. We uniformly reprocessed six public THP-1 single-cell RNA-sequencing datasets comprising 149,648 cells from two studies of undifferentiated cells and four studies of PMA-differentiated macrophage-like cells. A Harmony-based joint embedding was used for visualization, while state-associated expression was interpreted primarily through effect sizes and consistency across datasets because differentiation status was confounded with study background and cells were not independent biological replicates. The two undifferentiated sources shared high S100A8, S100A9, LYZ and VCAN expression. In contrast, differentiated datasets retained these markers to different degrees, demonstrating that the "differentiated" label did not denote a uniform transcriptional state. Undifferentiated cells also contained proliferative, interferon-responsive and inflammatory sub-states. Two independent bulk RNA-seq time courses showed progressive induction of CD14 after PMA exposure. Exploratory in-house bulk expression, immunostaining and nuclear morphometry were directionally consistent with a monocytic THP-1 phenotype but were not treated as replicated validation experiments. These results provide a cross-study reference for assessing THP-1 state heterogeneity and support direct measurement of differentiation markers in each experiment rather than reliance on protocol labels alone. Supplementary information The online version contains supplementary material available at https://doi.org/10.1007/s10616-026-01116-2.

items.title: Ethnic Origin, Self-Efficacy and Challenges in Cancer Information Seeking by Older Adults: A Cross-Sectional Study.
items.abstract: The purposes of this study were: to examine the association between older adults' confidence in their perceived ability to find cancer information when necessary (cancer information self-efficacy) and the two information seeking challenges: cancer information effort and frustration, and understand whether this link differs along ethnic/racial lines. These examinations were performed through the prism of the self-efficacy theory. The data were obtained from the Health Information National Trends Survey 5 Cycle 4 (2020). The sample included 836 adults aged 60 years and older who searched for cancer information on any source. The results show that negative association existed between cancer information self-efficacy and each of the challenges. Moreover, interaction between cancer information self-efficacy and ethnic/racial background was found with regard to both challenges. The results suggest that cancer information self-efficacy serves as an instrument that assists in mitigating the severity of the challenges older adults might experience when looking for this type of information. They also suggest that cancer information self-efficacy benefits older persons of various racial or ethnic background to a varying extent with respect to information seeking experience. The results may serve public health decision makers and health professionals in developing plans aiming at facilitating cancer information seeking process for older adults.

items.title: Estimating PM<sub>2.5</sub> Concentration in Ho Chi Minh City Using Sentinel-5P and Machine Learning on Google Earth Engine (GEE).
items.abstract: Fine particulate matter (PM 2.5 ) pollution poses serious public health risks in Ho Chi Minh City (HCMC), Vietnam, where monitoring infrastructure is limited to only four certified stations. This study integrates Sentinel-5P atmospheric composition products, ERA5 meteorological reanalysis, and MODIS-derived parameters within the Google Earth Engine (GEE) platform to capture both primary and secondary PM 2.5 formation processes. Four machine learning (ML) models were compared: multiple linear regression, random forest, gradient boosting, and XGBoost. The XGBoost model achieved the best predictive performance (R² = 0.784, MAE = 2.53 µg/m³), enabling spatially continuous PM 2.5 mapping across the city. The estimated annual mean concentration of 21.55 ± 0.92 µg/m³ exceeded the WHO air quality guideline (5 µg/m³) by a factor of approximately 4.3, confirming widespread exposure to hazardous levels. This scalable framework supports pollution monitoring and public health risk assessment in conditions of changing urban green space and thermal environment for the former HCMC.

items.title: Navigating the Chilling Effect: The Impact of Federal Policy Retrenchment on Undocumented Health Care Access in a Sanctuary City.
items.abstract: This study investigates how the intersection of federal, state, and local policies shapes health care access for undocumented immigrants in the San Francisco Bay Area. Through 15 in-depth interviews with health care experts, including physicians and advocacy leaders, conducted between 2024 and 2025, the research captures the impact of recent political shifts. We find that fear, which has long been a barrier to care, has been exacerbated by Trump administration actions, including the rescission of "protected areas" policies and the potential reinstatement of public charge rules. Together, these have had a "chilling effect" on the community. Even in a progressive "Sanctuary City," undocumented patients avoid services due to concerns that enrolling in programs like Medi-Cal will place them on a "list" for immigration authorities. Our research also highlights the continued importance of local safety-net programs. While California expanded Medi-Cal to all undocumented residents in 2024, subsequent 2025 state budget rollbacks and federal Medicaid cuts have introduced new premiums and enrollment freezes. Consequently, local safety-net programs like Healthy San Francisco (HSF) are more trusted and reliable alternatives because they are city-managed and have higher income eligibility thresholds. Regardless, information barriers, language challenges, and provider shortages persist. The study concludes that while local infrastructure provides a vital buffer, the health of undocumented populations remains highly vulnerable to federal retrenchment, requiring durable city-level protections and robust community trust-building.

items.title: Fentanyl Concentrations in Vancouver's Unregulated Opioid Supply after Drug Decriminalization: A Controlled Interrupted Time-Series Study.
items.abstract: In January 2023, the province of British Columbia, Canada, implemented a 3-year pilot to decriminalize personal possession of selected drugs below a cumulative threshold of 2.5 g. Concerns arose that pressure to carry less and remain under the legal limit could result in increased concentrations of the potent opioid fentanyl in unregulated opioids. We sought to examine if the onset of decriminalization was associated with changes to the average fentanyl concentration in unregulated opioids in the city of Vancouver. Using drug checking data from Vancouver and the jurisdictional control of Toronto, Ontario, we performed a controlled interrupted time-series analysis modelling the monthly ratio of median fentanyl concentrations in opioid samples (Vancouver divided by Toronto) as a single series over a 4-year period (February 2021 to February 2025). Across the study period, 20,331 drug checking samples were available from Vancouver and 3,145 from Toronto. At the time of policy implementation, the Vancouver-Toronto concentration ratio was estimated to immediately decrease by 0.68 (95% CI - 1.72-0.37, p = 0.20), though the result was not statistically significant. Similarly, there was no significant difference in the monthly rate of change in the ratio before versus after decriminalization (0.06, 95% CI - 0.05-0.17, p = 0.27). Multiple sensitivity analyses indicated robustness of results. Fentanyl concentrations in both cities followed aligned temporal patterns and the relative trajectory of fentanyl concentrations between Vancouver and Toronto did not meaningfully diverge following decriminalization. Findings suggest that decriminalization was unlikely to have altered the strength of the unregulated opioid supply.

items.title: What Traditional Assessments Miss: A Perspective on Invisible Assets in Community Health.
items.abstract: Community needs assessments (CNAs) have historically taken a deficit approach that reveals gaps in resource allocation and distribution, while not giving the same attention to the strengths that communities possess. Asset mapping has challenged that practice but remains underutilized as a necessary component in community health assessments. This perspective paper argues for pairing participatory asset mapping with CNAs to capture the emic perspectives. Additionally, this paper defines invisible assets, discusses why they matter for under-resourced communities, and the factors that contribute to their development. Rather than relying solely on tangible resources, systemic disinvestment compels these communities to develop alternative survival strategies. Traditional assessments miss this, generating an incomplete picture of community health by underemphasizing informal, place-based, community-driven solutions. Standardizing the identification of invisible assets shifts assessments toward strength-based models, guiding policymakers, public health professionals, and funding to reinforce existing local capacity rather than disrupting beneficial systems communities have already established.

items.title: Kimura versus Warshaw technique for distal pancreatectomy: a meta-analysis and systematic review.
items.abstract: Introduction Spleen-preserving distal pancreatectomy (SPDP) has emerged as the preferred approach for benign and low-grade malignant distal pancreas tumors. Two primary techniques exist: the Kimura technique (splenic vessel preserving) and the Warshaw technique (splenic vessel resection with short gastric vessel reliance). Despite widespread adoption, comparative evidence remains limited and methodologically inconsistent. The objective of this study is to systematically compare perioperative and clinical outcomes between Kimura and Warshaw techniques in SPDP, analyzing only studies with preoperative technique allocation to eliminate intraoperative selection bias. We hypothesize that the Kimura technique is associated with fewer postoperative adverse events compared with the Warshaw technique. Methods We conducted a systematic review and meta-analysis following PROSPERO registration (CRD420251046633). PubMed, MEDLINE, Scopus, Google Scholar, and Web of Science were searched through November 2025 for English and Spanish studies published within 15 years. Inclusion criteria required preoperative technique selection based on imaging and tumor characteristics, with statistical comparison of outcomes. Studies employing "Kimura-first" or intraoperative decision protocols were excluded. Two reviewers independently extracted the data, with disagreements resolved by a third reviewer. Meta-analyses used random-effects models. Results Six studies encompassing 1312 patients (839 Kimura, 473 Warshaw) met inclusion criteria. Compared to the Warshaw technique, the Kimura technique was associated with significantly lower odds of readmission (OR 0.66, 95% CI 0.57-0.76; P = 0.006) and splenic infarct (OR 0.20, 95% CI 0.09-0.47; P = 0.004). Overall complications, major complications, minor complications, reinterventions, and pancreatic fistulas showed no significant differences between techniques. Conclusion Although both the Kimura and Warshaw techniques demonstrated no significant difference in most of the postoperative outcomes for SPDP, the Kimura technique offers significantly lower odds of readmission and splenic infarction. Technique selection should be individualized based on patient anatomy, tumor characteristics, and surgeon or institutional expertise to optimize outcomes.

items.title: Cost-effectiveness of respiratory syncytial virus vaccines in post-marketing settings: a systematic review and meta-analysis.
items.abstract: Background Respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) is a leading cause of acute lower respiratory infections, hospitalizations, and deaths, particularly among infants and older adults worldwide. This study aims to summarize cost-effectiveness evidence by pooling incremental net benefit (INB) estimates of marketed RSV vaccines. Methods In this review, PubMed, Embase, Web of Science, and the Cochrane Library were searched through November 20, 2025. Grey literature and reference lists were also searched. Random-effects meta-analyses were conducted separately for older adults and infants. Potential sources of heterogeneity were explored using population-specific subgroup analyses and univariable meta-regressions. Results Of the 17 studies included in the systematic review, 11 contributed to the primary meta-analysis and one additional study to sensitivity analysis only. Among older adults, the pooled INB was USD 105.05 [95% confidence interval (CI): USD 41.89-168.21; I 2 = 93.2%]. For infants, the pooled INB was USD 5.81 (95% CI: USD - 35.44-47.07; I 2 = 89.4%). In the European subgroup, the pooled INB among older adults was USD 123.63 (95% CI: USD 41.23-206.02; I 2 = 89.4%), while that for infants was USD 15.00 (95% CI: USD - 4.33-34.34; I 2 = 43.4%). Leave-one-out sensitivity analyses showed robust pooled INBs among older adults, whereas infant estimates were sensitive to study exclusion. Conclusions At the thresholds used in the included studies, RSV vaccination might be cost-effective for older adults in post-marketing settings, while the evidence for maternal vaccination remained inconclusive. Descriptive findings suggested that age- and risk-based targeting in older adults and seasonal maternal vaccination may yield higher INB estimates. Substantial between-study heterogeneity warrants cautious interpretation of the pooled estimates and highlights the need to consider local epidemiology and implementation conditions when developing RSV vaccination policies.

items.title: Hospital pharmacy in Spain towards 2030: A national self-assessment of the baseline status and strategic challenges of the SEFH 2030 Project.
items.abstract: The 2030 Project of the Spanish Society of Hospital Pharmacy (SEFH 2030 Project) defines 20 strategic challenges for the development of the specialty, together with the standards that allow their achievement to be measured. The baseline degree of implementation of these strategic challenges in hospital pharmacy services in Spain was described, as well as its variability according to hospital type, size, ownership, teaching accreditation and geographical distribution. A cross-sectional observational study was conducted through a national self-assessment questionnaire addressed to the pharmacy services of 374 hospitals listed in the National Hospital Catalogue, categorised by type, ownership, teaching accreditation and size. The questionnaire was completed between May and December 2025 on a dedicated online platform and comprised 100 items corresponding to the 5 most representative standards for each challenge, with 4 response levels ranging from not planned to fully implemented. The 20 challenges were grouped into 4 thematic domains. The degree of implementation was calculated by standard, challenge, domain and overall, and analysed according to hospital category and autonomous community. A total of 199 hospitals responded (53.2%), with response rates ranging from 82.6% to 31.5% depending on hospital category. Overall implementation of the 100 standards was 45.4%. By thematic domain it reached 57.4% in transversal activities, training and research, 51.9% in comprehensive pharmaceutical care, 40.0% in people and professional teams and 34.2% in organisations and health systems. Leadership in clinical safety achieved the highest implementation (73.6%) and open innovation the lowest (18.1%). Implementation ranged from 61.7% in public teaching general hospitals with more than 999 beds to 31.1% in single-specialty centres, and from 53.7% to 28.8% depending on the autonomous community. Variability is observed according to size, ownership and geographical distribution, with consolidated areas (leadership in clinical safety or medicines compounding) alongside gaps in innovation, digital transformation and connection with patients and the community. Data derive from an unverified self-assessment, and the lower participation of private and smaller centres may overestimate overall implementation. These results provide an individual and collective reference for strategic planning and for prioritising improvement actions towards the 2030 horizon.

items.title: The need for entrepreneurship training and practice in public health.
items.abstract: Reductions in funding for public health services worldwide have led to corresponding cuts in jobs and services. Whilst resourcing for public health institutions and services may have reduced, the need for public health has not diminished. The solution may lie in public health reimagining itself beyond traditional career pathways and funding structures and adopting more entrepreneurial approaches. However, entrepreneurial training in public health education programmes and training curricula is patchy and limited. More formal entrepreneurial education, mentorship, supported opportunities, and networks are needed. The public health benefits of investing in entrepreneurship training could be immense - enhancing the creativity of the workforce and stimulating new ideas and solutions, as well as securing the resources needed, to meet the public health challenges of today and the future.

items.title: When It All Falls On the Physicians: A Qualitative Study of Physician Workforce Changes Post-Dobbs in Four States With Abortion Bans.
items.abstract: Objectives We aimed to explore how abortion bans in four highly restrictive states affected physician workforce dynamics among physicians of diverse specialties after the Dobbs v. Jackson Women's Health Organization decision. Methods The Medical Integrity Initiative conducted in-depth interviews with physicians in Alabama, Idaho, Oklahoma, and Tennessee, states with strict abortion bans and severe legal penalties for physicians. Participants included specialists in emergency medicine, maternal-fetal medicine, medical genetics, obstetrics, oncology, and reproductive endocrinology and infertility. We used stratified and snowball sampling and conducted interviews via Zoom from July to October 2024. Grounded theory methodology informed the inductive approach to data analysis. We began with open (descriptive) coding and followed it with axial (interpretive) analysis. Results Thirty-two physicians across all specialties reported new challenges following the Dobbs decision. We identified the following overarching themes: 1) heightened liability concerns, 2) shifting burden of care onto academic hospitals, 3) added advocacy responsibilities, 4) emotional strain and ethical dilemma of leaving the state, and 5) increased challenges regarding workforce size and workload. Challenges that participants described included colleagues' exodus, difficulty recruiting providers and trainees, and labor and delivery unit closures. Many reported that they considered leaving their state. Participants expressed a desire for their institutions to support evidence-based clinical practice. Conclusion Physicians experienced changes in workforce composition and responsibilities following the Dobbs decision. Collective action and robust occupational, legal, and mental health support from their institutions and medical societies might enable physicians to safely stay and sustainably advocate in states with abortion bans.

items.title: Microbiota transplant therapy improves ulcerative colitis symptoms independent of donor engraftment in a pilot randomized placebo-controlled trial.
items.abstract: Background Several clinical trials have assessed microbiota transplant therapy (MTT) in ulcerative colitis (UC); however, none have assessed a standardized MTT product. We developed a standardized, oral, lyophilized MTT product and previously reported the primary endpoint of engraftment at week 12. Here, we assessed clinical outcomes and the association with donor engraftment. Methods A single-center, randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled pilot trial of patients with UC with an endoscopic Mayo score ≥1, who received MTT or placebo for 8 weeks. Symptom and fecal assessments occurred at baseline and weeks 4, 8, and 12. Secondary outcomes included the partial Mayo score (pMS) and correlation to donor engraftment. Stool microbiota were assessed via 16S rRNA sequencing and donor engraftment measured using SourceTracker. Results Participants receiving MTT (n = 13) had significantly higher donor engraftment at all measured time points compared with placebo (n = 14). Compared with baseline symptoms, participants who received MTT had significantly lower pMS at weeks 4 and 8, while no significant changes in pMS were noted in those randomized to placebo. There was no correlation between donor engraftment and pMS or clinical response. There was no significant pattern in engrafting donor taxa in those that met the threshold of clinical response at week 4 vs participants that did not meet clinical response. Conclusions Daily dosing of encapsulated MTT for 8 weeks reduces symptoms of UC as measured by the pMS. However, donor engraftment did not correlate to pMS or clinical responses.NCT03948919, Fecal Transplant for Ulcerative Colitis, https://clinicaltrials.gov/study/NCT03948919.
