items.title: Optimizing nitrogen balance in facility cultivation for higher productivity and lower environmental losses under excessive N fertilization
items.abstract: Vegetable production under greenhouse often leads to severe nitrogen (N) surplus, driven largely by intensive fertilizer application and frequent nutrient supplementation to maintain higher crop yield, which holds significantly higher nitrogen input levels than that of paddy and upland fields. Less than half of N applied is absorbed by the crops, while the remaining half is surplus, causes numerous ecological issues, including increased N 2 O emissions and NH 3 volatilization, eutrophication, contamination of drinking water, damaging crop productivity. This study evaluated the effects of varying nitrogen (N) fertilization levels-low (238 kg N ha -1 ), medium (337 kg N ha -1 ), and high (720 kg N ha -1 ) on crop productivity, N uptake efficiency, and environmental losses in the facility-cultivated fields. Nitrogen inputs and outputs were quantified to determine the N balance and evaluate its potential implications for crop growth and the N losses. The N balance in facility cultivation varied from -20 to 301 kg N ha -1 depending on nitrogen input levels, primarily depending on the amount of nitrogen fertilizer applied. As N input increased, emissions of N 2 O and NH 3 to the atmosphere were also increased, while nitrogen leaching into water systems was also increased remarkably. Total yield significantly declined by 20% in the high N treatment compared to lower N applications levels, and NUE was decreased with decreasing N input. In conclusion, excessive nitrogen fertilization in facility cultivation systems poses a potential threat crop productivity, disrupt nitrogen balance and accelerate environmental concerns. These findings highlight the importance of optimizing nitrogen fertilization and maintaining a balanced N budget to minimize environmental N losses while ensuring sustainable crop production and long-term ecological sustainability of facility cultivations.

items.title: Global patterns of radial growth-structural heterogeneity relationships in forests
items.abstract: Classical theory predicts that environmental improvement intensifies competition and increases forest structural heterogeneity (variation in tree radial size). Whether warmer and wetter conditions drive convergence in stress-dominated regions remains unknown. Using a global tree-ring dataset ( > 900 sites, > 55,000 cores) with mixed-effects and mediation models, and accounting for Taylor’s law, we show that the negative growth–structure correlation is widespread, but its absolute slope increases along the stress gradient and becomes non-significant in low-stress regions (warm low-altitude, South Temperate, and tropics). Climate-to-structure pathways shift from growth-mediated in stress-dominated regions to non-significant in low-stress regions, with mediation strength increasing from temperate to alpine zones. On the Tibetan Plateau, warmer and wetter conditions are associated with homogenization via enhanced radial growth and reduced climate sensitivity. These findings challenge the classical expectation that environmental improvement inevitably increases structural heterogeneity, revealing a shift from stress-driven convergence to decoupling under low stress and providing a unified framework for predicting forest responses to climate change. Climate change can reshape forest size structure. Using tree rings from > 900 sites, the authors found warming and wetter conditions reduce tree-size inequality in high-stress regions but have little effect in low-stress forests.

items.title: deepSTRAPP : An R package to assess trait‐ and range‐dependent diversification dynamics over time
items.abstract: Abstract Understanding how diversification dynamics interact with species traits and geographical distributions over time remains a central challenge in macroevolution and biogeography. Yet the timing of these associations is rarely tested explicitly: existing approaches often focus on present‐day trait–rate relationships, or summarize over the whole history of a clade, overlooking variations in historical processes acting over deep evolutionary timescales. We introduce deepSTRAPP , an R package for assessing trait‐ and range‐dependent diversification across any temporal interval. deepSTRAPP models the evolution of traits or ranges independently of diversification rates on time‐calibrated phylogenies, extracts inferred values at user‐defined time steps and performs semi‐parametric STRAPP (Structured Rate Permutations on Phylogenies) tests based on block‐permutation to identify time windows in which diversification rates varied with species attributes. It handles continuous, categorical and biogeographic data, and includes visualization tools to explore the evolution of traits, ranges, diversification rates and the significance of their associations through time. Applied to empirical datasets, deepSTRAPP provided critical new perspectives to macroevolutionary questions inaccessible to currently available methods. It uncovered significant state‐dependent dynamics confined to restricted time windows that whole‐tree analyses overlooked, and tempered conclusions about present‐day associations that did not extend substantially back through evolutionary time. By explicitly testing for temporal variation in trait‐ and range‐dependent diversification, deepSTRAPP provides a robust framework to disentangle the relative contributions of past versus recent processes in shaping biodiversity patterns across broad phylogenetic and temporal scales.

items.title: From Multidimensional Biodiversity Patterns to Conservation Features in Systematic Conservation Planning
items.abstract: Systematic conservation planning (SCP) provides a rigorous framework for addressing conservation prioritization by combining explicit objectives, conservation features, representation targets, costs, and implementation constraints. In this article, we advocate incorporating multidimensional indices into the determination of planning-unit weights or soft penalties. Rather than directly treating the spatial patterns of multidimensional biodiversity as features within the SCP framework, this approach ensures that areas with high local genetic, phylogenetic, or functional diversity values are explicitly favored among solutions achieving comparable species targets.

items.title: Grizzly Bear Use and Selection of Ski Resorts
items.abstract: Like other anthropogenic disturbances, ski runs are both a potential source of forage and increased mortality risk for grizzly bears (Ursus arctos). To better understand how grizzly bears select for and use ski runs we assessed grizzly bear selection for ski runs, differences in use of ski areas between age-sex classes, and differences in use during nocturnal and diurnal periods. We hypothesized that bears would select for ski runs, however, due to social hierarchy between age-sex classes, the lower social classes (e.g., subadults or females) would predominately use ski runs and the area around ski lodges. We also hypothesized that to minimize risk of human interactions, use would be highest during nocturnal periods. To test the selection hypothesis, we used resource selection function (RSF) models that were developed using GPS collar data collected from 22 grizzly bears living near three ski resorts. Next, we tested for a difference in the distance of age-sex classes to ski runs and lodges and during diurnal versus nocturnal periods. Grizzly bears selected for ski runs in spring and summer. Adult females preferred to be closest to ski runs while adult males appeared to distance themselves from ski runs. Subadult males were located closer to ski lodges, while adult males were located the furthest. These results suggest ski runs provide grizzly bear habitat, but higher quality and/or more secure habitat is available elsewhere. Finally, bears were on average closer to ski lodges during nocturnal periods as compared to diurnal; however, the average difference was very small. Our results suggest that management actions implemented in the National Park and at ski resorts may be changing grizzly bear behavior as compared to previous studies. Successful management of recreational facilities to mitigate effects to grizzly bears is increasingly important as recreational facilities expand in popularity and footprint.

items.title: Spatial pattern variations in AI-generated urban park layouts under retained urban constraints
items.abstract: How generated urban park layouts respond to different conditional spatial constraints remains unclear. There are three research gaps in current research: (1) Most studies examine individual spatial elements separately and provide limited comparisons among different retained constraint types; (2) Existing park cases differ in site conditions, making it difficult to compare constraint-related spatial responses under comparable conditions; (3) How combined retained constraints modify the spatial responses associated with individual constraints remains unclear. To address these problems, we construct a constraint-conditioned comparative generative framework for urban park layouts: (1) First, establish a common environmental baseline condition and construct single- and multi-constraint generation conditions by progressively introducing internal roads, building footprints, and water bodies; (2) Secondly, use conditional GANs to generate park layouts under different constraint conditions; (3) Finally, evaluate the generated layouts using 15 Spatial Pattern Indicators and use statistical comparisons and effect-size estimation to characterize spatial responses across constraint conditions. The research results show that: (1) Differences among single-constraint configurations were most pronounced in the connectivity of walkable spaces and landscape pattern, particularly in RCC, ED, and SHEI. (2) Indicator sensitivity varied across constraint types, with some indicators showing limited responses under individual constraints but greater responses under selected combined conditions. (3) Responses to combined constraints depended on the baseline configuration, with some additional constraints producing limited changes under already constrained conditions.

items.title: Lithium, Environmental Impacts and High Andean Salt Flats in Argentina, Bolivia and Chile. An Integrative Review of Scientific Literature
items.abstract: This article reviews scientific literature on lithium mining's environmental impacts in Argentina, Bolivia, and Chile's salt flats, analyzing the period 1975-2024. The literature splits into two views: an optimistic one promoting lithium as vital for energy transition and global markets, and a critical one warning of irreversible damage to fragile ecosystems and local lifestyles. Despite growing socio-environmental interest over 50 years, knowledge gaps persist, the information on socio-environmental impacts is dispersed, with different levels of depth and rigor, and with uneven data distribution and capabilities among these countries. Chile’s Salar de Atacama, heavily researched due to mining influence, shows major impacts on water, biodiversity, and communities, yet lithium extraction continues despite insufficient data for responsible management. Additionally, much of this information does not reach local territories, and the treatment of impacts perceived by local communities remains limited, exacerbating inequalities. Unless significant innovations are made, the extraction of lithium salts from high Andean salt flats is paradoxically accelerating the socio-environmental degradation of these fragile ecosystems.

items.title: Evaluating the sustainability of shrimp aquaculture in Vietnam: stakeholder perceptions across production intensification systems
items.abstract: Purpose This study examines stakeholder perceptions of the importance of 21 sustainability themes across 4 Vietnamese shrimp farming systems. It also assesses associations between respondent characteristics and a separate ranking of perceived system sustainability. Design/methodology/approach Using the Sustainability Assessment of Food and Agriculture Systems (SAFA) Guidelines, 94 respondents each rated 21 themes across 4 systems, yielding 84 ordinal ratings per respondent. Questionnaires were administered in person to 56 respondents and completed online by 38. Theme-specific Friedman tests accounted for repeated observations, with Benjamini-Hochberg adjustment across 21 omnibus tests and, separately, 126 paired Wilcoxon comparisons. Cumulative-link mixed models provided an ordinal sensitivity analysis. Ridge-penalised multinomial regression examined the separate ranking outcome. Findings Differences across systems were supported for 18 of the 21 themes after adjustment for multiple testing. Corporate ethics, rule of law and biodiversity showed no supported omnibus differences. Super-intensive farming generally received the highest ratings for the importance of addressing sustainability issues. These ratings concern perceived priorities rather than measured performance. First-rank counts were 27, 7, 5 and 55 for super-intensive, intensive, semi-intensive and extensive/improved extensive/integrated systems, respectively. Age and self-reported knowledge were positively associated with selected ranking contrasts. These associations provide secondary evidence because two outcome categories were small. Research limitations/implications The purposive sample comprised 52 consumers, 36 business stakeholders and 6 experts. Its size and composition limit generalisation. Survey mode, fixed question order, unmeasured familiarity with production systems, concentrated high ratings and seven uniform response profiles may have influenced the findings. Sparse ranking categories limit prediction and practical interpretation of the multinomial model. Social implications Promoting sustainable shrimp farming systems also aligns with MARD’s approved “Sustainable aquaculture development plan in the Mekong Delta to 2030” (Decision No. 3550/QÐ-BNN-TCTS, August 2021), which aims to develop regional aquaculture sustainably. Originality/value The study applies the SAFA themes to comparisons of shrimp farming systems rated by the same stakeholders. By distinguishing the importance assigned to individual issues from an overall sustainability ranking, it explains how these two forms of judgement contribute different evidence to sustainability assessment.

items.title: Floristic and Bioecological Analysis of Saxifraga L. Species Growing in the Territory of the Nakhchivan Autonomous Republic
items.abstract: The present study examines the floristic composition, ecological characteristics, geographical distribution, phenology, and potential utilization of species of the genus Saxifraga L. (Saxifragaceae) occurring in the Nakhchivan Autonomous Republic. The work is based on floristic literature, taxonomic sources, field observations conducted during 2024–2026, and comparison with updated nomenclatural information. Nine of the fourteen Saxifraga species reported for Azerbaijan were identified as occurring in Nakhchivan. The species are concentrated mainly in rocky habitats, crevices, stony slopes, subalpine meadows, and alpine belts. Ecological analysis classified five species as xerophytes, two as mesophytes, and two as xeromesophytes. The taxa were assigned to five areal classes, with Caucasian, European mountain, and Front Asian mountain elements predominating. The expanded interpretation emphasizes the relationship between species distribution, altitude, substrate lithology, slope exposure, and microclimatic variability. The study also outlines scientifically justified prospects for rock-garden design, ecological restoration, phytomelioration, ex situ conservation, and bioindicator research. The proposed scientific novelty lies in integrating floristic, ecological, chorological, and applied-conservation perspectives into a single regional framework, while identifying priorities for future population-genetic, molecular-taxonomic, and climate-resilience investigations.

items.title: ARTIFICIAL INTELLIGENCE APPLICATIONS FOR IMPROVING PRONUNCIATION SKILLS OF AUTISTIC PATIENTS: A CRITICAL REVIEW
items.abstract: Autism Spectrum Disorder (ASD) is a developmental disorder and individuals with ASD experience challenges in social relation, communication, as well as speech articulation. Many children with ASD have significant difficulty pronouncing words properly, presenting difficulties with learning at school and communicating in day-to-day situations. Recently, AI has demonstrated high potential and application value in many therapeutic and educational applications, speech and pronunciation training among others. AI systems typically integrate speech recognition, text-to-speech synthesis, automatic feedback and interactive learning environments. However, even with this progress, the existing solutions still have limitations such as limited vocabulary, lack of real-time interaction and poor adaptation to different dialects and cultural backgrounds. In this paper, a review of AI techniques that have been proposed to enhance pronunciation skills in children with ASD is offered. The review included 44 peer-reviewed articles obtained from Scopus database. We indicate current research trends, reflect existing gaps, and propose directions toward the development of more adaptive, inclusive, and cultural responsive AI-pedestal pronunciation training tools for improving communication skills and quality of life in children with ASD

items.title: Determination of the helium volume mixing ratio in Saturn’s atmosphere from a future atmospheric probe: methodology and uncertainty analysis
items.abstract: Abstract We present a methodology for determining the helium (He) volume mixing ratio (VMR) in Saturn’s atmosphere from measurements obtainable by a future atmospheric entry probe equipped with a tunable laser spectrometer (TLS) implementing wavelength modulated spectroscopy. The approach derives the He abundance as the residual of the total atmospheric pressure after accounting for molecular H 2 , CH 4 , and a small but unknown abundance of remaining trace gases. H 2 is measured via its electric quadrupole absorption lines near 2.1 μ m and CH 4 via its fundamental v 3 band near 3.3 μ m using a multi-bounce optical cavity of 10 m total path length. We develop closed-form analytical expressions for the He VMR and its propagated uncertainty, treating the trace gas contribution as a one-sided systematic bias and the measurement uncertainties on pressure, temperature, H 2 number density, and CH 4 number density as independent random errors. We demonstrate that the uncertainty budget is dominated overwhelmingly by the fractional measurement precision on the H 2 number density. For a representative probe sounding with conditions within the TLS measurement chamber at T = 200 K and P = 10 4 Pa, the total fractional uncertainty on the retrieved H 2 number density is approximately 1.2% for a single-line, single-measurement retrieval, comprised of a noise-limited contribution of ~0.33% (TLS minimum detectable fractional absorption of 10 -4 over a 10 m path), a HITRAN line-strength contribution of ≲1%, a mixture-dependent line-shape contribution of ~0.5%, and a path-length contribution of < 0.1%, combined in quadrature. With three-line profile-fit retrieval, the total error reduces to 0.8–1.1%, well within the ≲2.4% threshold needed to meet an absolute He VMR random uncertainty requirement of ≤0.02. The corresponding absolute He VMR uncertainties are $${\sigma}_{{f}_{\text{He}}}$$ ≈0.010 (single-line) and 0.007–0.009 (multi-line). These results confirm the viability of the TLS approach for He abundance determination and identify the HITRAN H 2 line-strength uncertainty and mixture-dependent line-shape physics (the latter not reducible by pre-flight calibration) as the leading systematic contributors to the residual He VMR uncertainty budget.

items.title: Implicit Surface Tension for Incompressible SPH Fluids with Interface Classification
items.abstract: Abstract In computer graphics and physics‐based animation, surface tension is an important factor in reproducing small‐scale fluid features. However, existing surface tension solvers often incur high computational costs and tend to become unstable under strong surface tension effects. To address this issue, we propose an SPH surface tension simulation method that combines geometric interface classification with an implicit solve. First, we construct a geometric criterion based on inter‐particle distances and neighborhood angles to identify liquid–air interface particles, liquid–solid interface particles, and bulk particles without relying on level sets or air‐phase particles. We further provide a threshold‐selection scheme independent of the particle radius. Building on this classification, we restrict the global pairwise cohesive interaction to an volumetric force applied only to interface particles and limit the degrees of freedom of the implicit system to interface particles. This design forms a pipeline that integrates particle classification, interface‐restricted cohesion solving, and pressure‐mediated force transfer. Experimental results show that our method significantly reduces computational cost, effectively reproduces surface‐tension‐induced fluid effects, and mitigates excessive local cohesion in canonical scenarios.

items.title: The Oxygen Reduction Reaction over Pt Nanoparticles Studied with First-Principles-Based Kinetic Monte Carlo Simulations
items.abstract: Abstract The oxygen reduction reaction is essential to reduce the dependence on fossil fuels. Although widely studied, the underlying reason for the onset overpotential of the reaction over Pt-based nanoparticles remains debated. Here, a first-principles-based kinetic Monte Carlo framework is developed to elucidate the main reaction mechanism, rate-determining steps, and the reason for the overpotential. Effects of the aqueous environment with directional hydrogen bonds are incorporated in the kinetic Monte Carlo simulations, and a framework for simulating linear sweep voltammetry is presented. We find that the overpotential originates from the high coverages of oxygen species (*O, *OH, and *H2O), which block sites for O2 adsorption. The kinetic simulations demonstrate that the effects of site-blocking can be tuned by the shape and size of the Pt nanoparticles. The lowest overpotential is obtained for particles in the size range between 3 and 6 nm with large fractions of (111) facets. The developed methods are general and facilitate the understanding and optimization of catalysts used in a range of electrochemical reactions.

items.abstract: Pembelajaran astronomi di Indonesia masih menghadapi keterbatasan baik dari sisi kurikulum maupun kompetensi guru, sehingga potensi astronomi sebagai entry point pembelajaran STEM belum optimal. Di sisi lain, pendekatan hands-on dapat meningkatkanpemahaman dan keterlibatan belajar sains. Kegiatan pengabdian kepada masyarakat internasional yang bekerjasama dengan Korean Astronomical Society (KAS) ini bertujuan untuk meningkatkan kompetensi guru IPA dalam bidang astronomi modern melalui workshop berbasis hands-on activity. Kegiatan ini melibatkan 28 peserta (guru dan calon guru) melalui sesi kuliah umum, hands-onactivity, dan sharing session. Evaluasi kegiatan dikumpulkan melalui kuesioner yang terdiri dari 10 item pernyataan tertutup berbentuk skala Likert dan 5 pertanyaan terbuka untuk mengevaluasi pengetahuan, keterampilan, serta kesiapan implementasi. Hasil menunjukkan peningkatan pemahaman konsep astronomi (M=4.75) dan relevansi aktivitas hands-on untuk pembelajaran di sekolah (M=4.79), serta tingginya motivasi dan kepercayaan diri peserta untuk mengimplementasikan pembelajaran di kelas.Temuan kualitatif menguatkan bahwa workshop mampu mengubah persepsi bahwa astronomi sulit menjadi lebih kontekstual dan aplikatif, meskipun masih terdapat tantangan dalam implementasi teknis dan integrasi dengan SDGs. Hal ini menunjukkan pentingnya dukungan lanjutan untuk memastikan transfer praktik ke kelas berjalan optimal. Secara keseluruhan, workshop berbasishands-on dengan kolaborasi internasional efektif sebagai model pengembangan profesional guru yang relevan dan adaptif di Indonesia.

items.title: The Forgotten Search for an LSD "Antidote".
items.abstract: This commentary reconstructs a neglected early clinical finding in psychopharmacology: The mid-1950s clinical observation that chlorpromazine partially antagonizes the subjective effects of Lysergic acid diethylamide (LSD). Here, we provide the first English translation of the foundational 1955 study by Giberti and Gregoretti. This early work, alongside some contemporaneous and ethically abusive human experimentation funded by the Central Intelligence Agency of the federal government of the United States (CIA) under its MKULTRA program, demonstrated significant pharmacological blockade. However, this line of inquiry was severed from the scientific literature following the suppression of psychedelic research in the 1970s. Consequently, this clear drug-drug interaction remained an isolated clinical fact without a mechanistic explanation for decades. Modern neuropharmacology has now elucidated the precise receptor-level basis: Chlorpromazine acts as an antagonist at the 5-HT 2A receptor, the primary molecular target of classic psychedelics like LSD. Thus, contemporary receptor knowledge validates and explains these prescient, premechanistic clinical insights.

items.title: AI in Neuro-Oncology: A Review in Neuroimaging.
items.abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) has become central to neuro-oncological imaging, impacting clinical and scientific workflows. In clinical practice, AI-based image reconstruction and noise reduction expedite the generation of advanced multiparametric MRI and PET scans. Automated segmentation and volumetric analysis improve reproducibility, speed, and standardization of tumor quantification and response assessment. In research, large language and multimodal models extract structured information from radiology reports and medical records. Collaborative initiatives, such as BraTS and FeTS, have established standardized, privacy-compliant frameworks for large-scale quantitative analyses. Tumor-specific applications include noninvasive molecular profiling in gliomas, grading and recurrence prediction in meningiomas, detection and response assessment in brain metastases, and pediatric-specific modeling aligned with RAPNO. However, AI models remain sensitive to technical and biological variations across institutions, limiting their clinical utility unless appropriate training and validation is performed. Nevertheless, progress is evident in prospective, biopsy-validated infiltration mapping, assessment of resection extent aligned with RANO-Resect, and standardization through AI-RANO. Emerging directions include foundation models, uncertainty estimation, federated learning, AI-enhanced ultra-low-field MRI, and dual-tracer PET. When used as a decision-support tool rather than a replacement for the imaging team, AI can increasingly improve the utility, reproducibility, and efficiency of quantitative, multiparametric imaging in patients with brain tumors.

items.title: A Two-Stage Approach to Detecting Differential Item Functioning: Combining Regularization with the Mantel-Haenszel Method (Reg-MH).
items.abstract: Test bias is a critical concern in educational and psychological measurement. Differential item functioning (DIF) is widely used to identify potential test bias. Although regularization methods have shown promise in DIF detection, interpreting the resulting DIF parameters remains challenging. This study proposes a two-stage approach, termed Reg-MH, that combines regularization with the Mantel-Haenszel (MH) method. Specifically, regularization is first used to select anchor items, followed by MH testing to identify DIF items, combining the anchor selection advantages of regularization with the interpretability of MH. A pilot simulation study examined alternative regularization-based anchor selection strategies and the number of anchor items. A main simulation study evaluated the performance of Reg-MH against traditional MH and regularized DIF (Reg-DIF) methods across varying sample sizes, DIF magnitudes, DIF proportions, and ability distributions. An empirical illustration using PISA 2012 data further demonstrated its practical application. The simulation results showed that Reg-MH generally achieved a more favorable balance between Type I error control and statistical power than the competing methods. Compared with traditional MH, Reg-MH reduced Type I error rates while maintaining higher statistical power than Reg-DIF. Type I error rates generally increased with sample size, DIF magnitude, and DIF proportion, whereas statistical power increased with sample size and DIF magnitude but decreased as DIF proportion increased. Overall, Reg-MH provides a promising approach to DIF detection by integrating regularization-based anchor selection with conventional statistical testing.

items.title: Accuracy of a difference in 24-hour physical behaviors between two groups: effects of balanced and unbalanced group sizes across scenarios with varying numbers of measurement days.
items.abstract: Background Too little data can lead to uncertain and potentially biased group differences in physical behaviors, while excess data may waste resources. In order to examine the trade-off between measurement efforts and study performance, we examined the accuracy (the combined effect of trueness and precision) of the difference in 24-hour physical behaviors between overweight and normal-weight office workers of the number of participants and the number of measurement days per participant in balanced and unbalanced data sets. Methods Time spent sitting, standing, moving, and sleeping was monitored for 7 days using a thigh-worn accelerometer in 103 overweight (BMI ≥ 25 kg/m 2 ) and 122 normal-weight ( 2 ) office workers. Using this parent dataset, we simulated, using bootstrap resampling, data collection strategies with 96 (8 × 4 × 3) combinations of the total number of participants (18, 36, 54, 72, 90, 108, 126, 144), working days per participant (1, 2, 3, 4), and balancedness (ratios 1:1, 1:2, and 2:1 between overweight and normal-weight participants). For each sampling strategy, trueness (the size) and precision (the 95% confidence interval width) of the group difference, both expressed in compositional space, was compared to the parent dataset, and the likelihood of obtaining statistically significant group differences was assessed as a measure of the combined effect of trueness and precision. Results Increasing the number of participants per group did not change the estimated behavior difference at a specific number of working days. Measuring only one day introduced bias to the difference, while more days produced estimates closer to the observed "true" difference in the parent dataset. Precision improved with more participants and days, and a balanced study generally yielded more precise estimates than an unbalanced study with the same total number of measurements. The likelihood of arriving at a significant group difference was influenced by the number of both participants and days. Conclusions Trueness (i.e., bias) was influenced by the number of days, but not the number of participants. In contrast, precision was influenced by the number of participants, days, and balancedness of the study population. Thus, it is important to consider the trade-offs between the number of participants, days and balancedness in future studies, and even to consider the costs of collecting data from more participants or more days per participant in either group. items.title: Facilitators and Barriers to Lifestyle Change Among Medical Students: A Longitudinal Lifestyle Medicine Intervention.
items.abstract: Lifestyle behaviors are major modifiable determinants of noncommunicable chronic diseases. Lifestyle Medicine promotes health through six pillars. Medical students are particularly vulnerable to unhealthy behaviors due to academic workload and stress. This study aims to identify facilitators and barriers to lifestyle change among medical students participating in a structured Lifestyle Medicine intervention. This longitudinal and interventional mixed-methods study followed six medical students from a Brazilian public university during a 4-month intervention including lifestyle education, self-assessment, goal setting, habit tracking, anthropometric assessment, and focus groups. Data were coded using the Consolidated Framework for Implementation Research and subsequently organized according to the Social Determinants of Health model. Self-efficacy emerged as the central facilitator, supported by organization, discipline, motivation, and self-monitoring. Other facilitators included social support, group engagement, and supportive environments. Barriers included emotional and motivational challenges, excessive smartphone use, academic workload, negative family influence, and social media pressure. Body weight and BMI remained stable, while mean muscle mass increased (+0.98 kg) and fat mass decreased (-1.07 kg). Lifestyle change among medical students is influenced by interacting personal, social, and environmental determinants. Integrating lifestyle education into medical curricula may benefit well-being and future patient counseling.

items.title: Contributions of lifestyle risk factors to socio-economic disparities in active and total life expectancy among older adults: A longitudinal cohort study.
items.abstract: Older adults of lower socio-economic position have a shorter active life expectancy (ALE) and total life expectancy (TLE). This study aimed to determine the extent to which these disparities could be explained by lifestyle risk factors. We used data (1998-2024) from 754 participants aged 70+ years of the Precipitating Events Project study in South Central Connecticut. Socio-economic indicators (i.e., years of education, income, and neighborhood disadvantage) and alcohol consumption were assessed at baseline only, whereas smoking, low physical activity, and obesity were updated at 18-month intervals. Disability was assessed monthly and defined as dependence in essential activities of daily living. We used discrete-time multistate modeling to estimate sex-specific ALE and TLE at age 70 years, and simulated elimination scenarios (in which the prevalence of the lifestyle risk factors was set to zero one-at-a-time and then jointly) to quantify the contributions of lifestyle risk factors to socio-economic disparities in ALE and TLE. Low physical activity made the largest contribution to disparities based on years of education (ALE: 35.4%; TLE: 54.5%) and neighborhood disadvantage (ALE: 49.4%; TLE: 53.4%) among men, and to disparities based on years of education (ALE: 67.4%; TLE: 93.4%), income (ALE: 39.9%; TLE: 55.3%), and neighborhood disadvantage (ALE: 23.8%; TLE: 20.1%) among women. The contributions of alcohol consumption, smoking, and obesity to disparities in ALE and TLE were negligible. To reduce socio-economic disparities in ALE and TLE in later life, priority should be given to policies and interventions designed to support more healthful behaviors.

items.title: State-space symmetry in Boolean network ensembles
items.abstract: Studies of evolving Boolean network systems have found that Boolean functions cluster into equivalence classes with a characteristic frequency distribution - a pattern governed by the Zyklenzeiger symmetry group - but the dynamical origin of this symmetry has remained unexplained. Here we show that it is a consequence of a fundamental symmetry of Boolean network dynamics itself. A Boolean network consists of nodes that update according to Boolean functions of their regulatory inputs; its global dynamics is encoded in a state-space network. We identify the dynamical symmetry group of ensembles of Boolean networks that average over random interaction topologies: for networks with $N$ nodes, it is the $N$-dimensional hyperoctahedral group, generated by node-flips and node-label permutations. These transformations are admissible for every Boolean network regardless of topology; for random-topology ensembles, including all ensembles of fixed in-degree $K<N$, they constitute the complete symmetry group. We also show that input-label permutations constitute a hidden gauge freedom of the dynamics. The Zyklenzeiger symmetry of Boolean functions follows directly from the node-flips of the hyperoctahedral group together with this gauge freedom. Boolean networks related by the hyperoctahedral group have isomorphic state-space networks and form its orbits, and Burnside's lemma gives the number of these orbits for any fixed network topology. It provides a symmetry reduction of the analysis of Boolean network dynamics and explains why the Boolean functions of evolved networks fall into Zyklenzeiger classes, and why these classes split in finite networks.

items.title: Midsagittal Corpus Callosum Parameterization: A Framework for Spatially Detailed Diffusion MR Imaging Analysis
items.abstract: The corpus callosum (CC) is the largest white matter structure in the human brain and plays a central role in interhemispheric communication. Diffusion MR imaging is widely used to investigate microstructural organization, but commonly used analysis approaches have important limitations. Voxel-based methods rely heavily on accurate inter-subject registration and smoothing choices, tract-based spatial statistics (TBSS) restricts the analysis to a narrow white matter skeleton, and parcellation approaches reduce spatial detail by averaging diffusion measures over relatively large regions. In this work, we introduce a parameterization framework for the analysis of the midsagittal CC that resamples the structure using a standardized grid of points, establishing a geometric correspondence across individuals without explicit inter-subject registration. In a test-retest dataset, the method provided stable measurements while covering most of the midsagittal CC, and sensitivity analyses showed that results in the central CC changed little under perturbations of the input CC mask, whereas peripheral regions were more sensitive. The framework was further evaluated in group analyses of aging and Alzheimer's disease in datasets that differ in acquisition protocol and spatial resolution. Effect-size maps and quantitative comparisons showed that its results were largely consistent with TBSS and parcellation-based analyses in the overall spatial pattern of effects, while also revealing additional spatially localized differences. These findings suggest that the parameterization provides a simple, computationally efficient, and spatially detailed approach for investigating midsagittal CC microstructure, offering a structure-specific complement to whole-brain and region-based methods.

items.title: Kepler as an accidental heliospheric imager: Thomson-scattered solar-wind structure in four years of background photometry
items.abstract: Kepler recorded several thousand dedicated sky-background pixels per detector output every 29.4 min from 2009 May to 2013 May while staring at a fixed 12-degree field at ecliptic latitude +65 degrees. From this archive we isolate a large-scale layer that measures brightness variations relative to an 8-day running median. This layer contains fluctuations of 0.02-0.1 electrons per second per pixel (about 1e-17 of the mean solar surface brightness) that sweep across the field in a day or less. Four lines of evidence show that these are sunlight Thomson-scattered by solar-wind electrons. (1) The sweeps propagate away from the Sun (84 percent within 45 degrees of the anti-solar direction; 25 percent expected by chance), and their direction follows the Sun through each quarter and across all 16 spacecraft rolls. (2) The field brightness correlates with the near-Earth (OMNI) proton density within a day of zero lag (r = 0.19, p < 1/150), but not with the energetic-proton flux. (3) Time-elongation maps show fronts moving outward at a median 15 degrees per day, as forward models of radially moving density structures predict. (4) The amplitude is about one third of a parameter-free Thomson-scattering prediction and varies by a factor of about 3 over the year, as predicted. Half of the scattered light comes from within 0.4-0.7 AU of the spacecraft. Fronts are strongest in slow wind. Kepler's background pixels thus provide a four-year, high-cadence, out-of-ecliptic record of solar-wind structure near 1 AU. Standard Kepler processing removes these signals, changing stellar light curves by less than about 1 ppm.

items.title: A new chemical network to explore the disequilibrium chemistry of silicates and iron in hot gas giants
items.abstract: Chemical equilibrium modeling of gas giant planet atmospheres has shown that the production and condensation of silicates plays an important role in shaping their final composition. However, no chemical kinetics network for these species are available, preventing the opportunity to analyze the impact of chemical disequilibrium processes. In this paper we present \texttt{SILANE}, a new chemical network that include Mg, Si, Fe and 15 carriers of these elements, including MgSiO$_3$ and Mg$_2$SiO$_4$, ready for use in the VULCAN code. We compare the results of our network with a chemical equilibrium model and discuss them in relation to previous results from literature. We then apply our new network to the analysis of a vertically mixed, Solar-composition atmosphere with equilibrium temperatures $T_{eq}$ in the [700, 1600] K range, finding that (i) rock-forming silicates disappears from the upper atmosphere already at 1100 K, (ii) SiH$_4$ reaches concentrations of $10^{-7}$ in the upper ($P\le 1.0$ bar) atmosphere for planets with $T_{eq}\in$ [800, 1100] K and (iii) the amount of oxygen in refractories decrease from 21\% at $T_{eq}$=700 K to essentially zero already at 1000 K, while in the classical equilibrium framework it remains constant up to $T_{eq}$=1300 K. By applying our network to the case of the young hot Jupiter YSES-1 c and comparing both the mixing ratios of volatile species and the enstatite fraction in the silicate mix, we find evidence of a well-mixed atmosphere, possibly with an average $K_{zz} \ge 10^{10}$ cm$^{2}$s$^{-1}$ up to the $10^{-4}$ bar level.

items.title: High-inclination Centaur or Captured Halley-Type Comet? Observational and Dynamical Characterization of C/2024 L1 (PANSTARRS)
items.abstract: The high-inclination (`high-i') Centaurs of the middle and outer Solar System are of uncertain origin. While many have been captured directly from the Oort Cloud, making them less-evolved analogues to the Halley-Type Comets, this process alone cannot produce the number of observed objects. The most discussed alternate origin is direct excitation of trans-Neptunian Objects into high-i orbits by the action of some unfound massive planet beyond Neptune. It is thus critical to find ways to discern the origins of these objects to provide new constraints on the various unfound planet hypotheses. This work assesses the only known active high-i Centaur: C/2024 L1 (PANSTARRS). Our dynamical investigations show that L1 has not decreased its semimajor axis in at least the past 1810 years, unlike all known TNO-derived active Centaurs at lower-i whose activity initiates after orbital changes. We also imaged L1 on five nights in the year before its April 2025 perihelion and found its brightness and optical colors to be stable and that its tail grew steadily. While this is like many Halley-type comets, few active low-i Centaurs have such stable activity. We thus propose that L1 is a captured Oort Cloud comet analogous to lower perihelion Halley-types and is thus a highly attractive target for large aperture follow up. The number and active fraction of these high-i objects should help us discern their origins and survey telescopes like Roman and Rubin could help us figure out where in the Outer Solar System the mystery lies.

items.title: The Lukashian Calendar: A universal calendar mechanism using variable-duration years and days for any human colony or settlement
items.abstract: Existing calendars, in particular the Gregorian calendar, have a complex structure which requires constant adjustment in the form of leap days and leap seconds in order to remain synchronized to the position of a planet in the Solar System. In addition, mean solar days can deviate up to 16 minutes from true solar days on Earth. On other planets, this discrepancy can be far greater: on Mars, it can be up to 51 minutes. Numerous Martian proposals ranging from Aitken (1936) to Gangale (1986) to Silin (2025) mimic the Gregorian calendar and do not address these issues. Moreover, many do not include a system for telling the time of day, or stretch the second beyond the standard SI second. This paper proposes a calendar mechanism that uses years and days with a variable duration, in order to accurately represent true solar years and days. In this mechanism, time of day is expressed as a proportion, rather than a number of fixed units, such as hours and minutes. This results in a simple and consistent structure that can universally be applied to any planet, moon or space station with a human presence. Furthermore, it allows analog missions on Earth to use the same calendar mechanism as future missions in space. This paper will outline the principles and details of this mechanism, using Earth and Mars as illustrative examples. Also discussed is the implementation of the mechanism on actual computers, which have a Unix time system clock based on discrete milliseconds.

items.title: Food co-purchasing networks encode geographic disparities in cardiometabolic health
items.abstract: Unhealthy diets are a major driver of cardiometabolic disease, yet the geospatial structure of dietary behavior and its links to population health remain poorly understood. While large-scale retail transaction data offer a unique view of population dietary behavior, conventional approaches reduce purchases to isolated items, not accounting for how foods are actually combined. Here, we analyze 51 million grocery receipts across 95 Danish municipalities using a statistically validated bipartite network framework to isolate co-purchases that product popularity alone cannot explain. We find that, although municipalities buy largely the same products, their co-purchasing networks reorganize along a continuous urban-to-peripheral gradient in how those products are combined. The network backbone can be resolved into modular dietary communities whose local cohesion allows us to predict cardiometabolic prescriptions, explaining a quarter to a half of the variance left after sociodemographic adjustment, beyond what product prevalence alone accounts for. Ultra-processed foods (UPFs) show no spatial gradient in prevalence and are located at the network periphery, where they share baskets with fresh foods but rarely form the combinations that hold the network together. Taken together, our findings show that geographic dietary differences are encoded not only in what people purchase, but in how foods are systematically combined within shopping baskets, offering a scalable network approach for population nutritional epidemiology.

items.title: OGLE-2018-BLG-0829L: A Microlensing System with a Planet Orbiting a Star Possessing a Brown-Dwarf Companion
items.abstract: We analyze the microlensing event OGLE-2018-BLG-0829, whose light curve exhibits a weak short-term anomaly in addition to the prominent caustic-crossing features of a binary lens. The anomaly cannot be explained by a binary-lens single-source (2L1S) model. We therefore investigate both binary-lens binary-source (2L2S) and triple-lens single-source (3L1S) interpretations and find that both models reproduce the additional anomaly, with the 3L1S model being favored by $Δχ^2=15.1$. Under the favored 3L1S interpretation, the anomaly arises from a caustic induced by a planetary-mass companion, whereas the prominent caustic-crossing features are produced by the underlying binary lens. Combining the measured event timescale, $t_{\rm E}=7.55\pm0.30$ days, and angular Einstein radius, $θ_{\rm E}=0.325 \pm 0.059$ mas, with a Bayesian analysis, we infer a lens system consisting of an M dwarf of mass $0.193^{+0.300}_{-0.098}\,M_\odot$, a possible brown-dwarf companion of mass $0.068^{+0.105}_{-0.034}\,M_\odot$, and a Saturn-mass planet of mass $0.337^{+0.522}_{-0.171}\,M_{\rm J}$. The companions have projected separations of approximately 3.6 au and 1.6 au from the primary, respectively. However, the physical interpretation remains tentative because potentially important higher-order effects have not been considered, and the dynamical stability of the proposed configuration remains uncertain. If confirmed, this would be the third star--brown dwarf--planet system identified through microlensing, highlighting the potential of microlensing to detect planets in complex multiple systems.

items.title: How to Agree Without Agreeing
items.abstract: Consensus lets institutions decide without a central authority, but a record of agreement reveals neither its basis nor its credibility. We model support, standing aside and veto as responses to a proposal. A proposal can pass without active support, and the member least willing to allow passage limits what can be adopted, however many members oppose the proposal. Letting proposers moderate their demands can ease agreement while undermining the prescribed punishment. Proposal restrictions or deviation costs can preserve that threat. Across the initialisations tested, learning agents agree frequently even though many reconstructed rules allow profitable departures. In our sample of Antarctic Treaty working papers, 80% of proposals revising existing arrangements were adopted at submission, against 38% of new proposals. Consensus can keep producing agreement on what already exists while new protection waits.

items.title: AI climate trajectories shaped by growth, power choices and decarbonization
items.abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) is emerging as a major source of electricity demand, yet its operational greenhouse gas (GHG) emissions remain difficult to resolve geographically. We develop a facility-level global inventory of AI-oriented data centers and extend it to 2030 using documented expansion plans and grid-policy scenarios. Under Current Policies, emissions increase from 20.4 MtCO$_2$e in 2024 to 68.7 MtCO$_2$e in 2030, with parameter-side Monte Carlo 5th--95th percentile ranges of 19.3--21.0 and 60.8--73.9 MtCO$_2$e, respectively. Only six geographies, representing less than 3% of projected capacity, avoid rising emissions. Grid decarbonization consistent with net zero by 2050 lowers projected 2030 emissions to 48.3 MtCO$_2$e, but fossil-based behind-the-meter generation erodes this benefit. Under that scenario, the U.S. behind-the-meter emissions penalty exceeds the combined AI-data-center emissions outside the United States. These findings support coordinated capacity planning, faster access to low-carbon electricity and limits on routine fossil-based behind-the-meter supply.

items.title: Detection of CH$_2$NH on Titan
items.abstract: Saturn's moon, Titan, presents a chemical environment where abiotic synthesis of organics essential for life -- including amino acids and nucleotide bases -- may naturally occur. The assessment of Titan's organic content begins with characterizing its atmospheric chemical inventory, where many predicted molecular species remain unidentified. Here, we present the definitive spectroscopic detection of CH$_2$NH (methanimine) on Titan from observations with the Atacama Large Millimeter/submillimeter Array. CH$_2$NH represents the first stable imine (C=N) to be detected on Titan, and may be integral for further biomolecule formation as a precursor to glycine and adenine. We find abundances of CH$_2$NH at the 0.1--1 ppb level in Titan's mesosphere through multiple valid vertical profile configurations, yielding total column densities ranging from $\sim0.9$--$3\times10^{13}$ cm$^{-2}$. Middle-atmospheric abundances are commensurate with recent photochemical model predictions. However, models with parameterized galactic cosmic ray (GCR) fluxes, which exhibit a secondary, stratospheric formation site, are shown to provide poor fits to the data. Thus, our results provide confirmation of predicted formation and destruction pathways for CH$_2$NH in the upper atmosphere, and demonstrate secondary formation mechanisms in the lower atmosphere require adjustments. The latter presents an important barrier for fully estimating Titan's lower atmospheric composition, as enhanced production by GCR is predicted for additional N-bearing species, such as NH$_3$ and CH$_3$NH$_2$ (methylamine). The detection of CH$_2$NH provides the motivation to search for additional species fundamental for prebiotic molecule formation, which will dramatically improve our understanding of complex molecular synthesis of relevance to astrobiology in CH$_4$-rich environments.

items.title: Shewanella oneidensis MR-1 facilitates pseudomonas aeruginosa PAO1 to degrade petroleum hydrocarbon through coordinated carbon metabolism and respiratory electron transfer.
items.abstract: Petroleum hydrocarbon biodegradation often slows after an initially rapid phase as degrader activity declines and electron-acceptor availability becomes limiting. Overcoming these kinetic and thermodynamic constraints is therefore critical for effective remediation of petroleum-contaminated soils. Here, we identified a metabiotic interaction between Pseudomonas aeruginosa PAO1 and Shewanella oneidensis MR-1 that enhanced n-hexadecane degradation. Although the relative abundance of MR-1 declined rapidly during co-cultivation, the co-culture achieved an apparent degradation efficiency of 100% within 9 d, compared with approximately 82% for PAO1 alone, without greater overall biomass accumulation. Experiments with non-viable MR-1 and riboflavin showed that MR-1-derived cellular and redox-active components contributed to this facilitation. Metabolomic and transcriptomic analyses revealed lower levels of hexadecanoic acid and acetyl-CoA, accompanied by coordinated responses in β-oxidation, TCA-cycle metabolism, cofactor supply, and respiratory electron transfer in PAO1. In nonsterile red soil, PAO1-MR-1 inoculation increased n-hexadecane degradation by approximately 47%. Together, these findings indicate that MR-1 acts as a redox-active facilitator rather than an independent hydrocarbon degrader, enhancing PAO1-mediated degradation through coordinated carbon metabolism and respiratory reprogramming. This study highlights metabiosis as a strategy for overcoming degradation bottlenecks and improving petroleum-contaminated soil remediation.

items.title: ROLE OF INSECTS IN AGRICULTURE AND ENVIRONMENT
items.abstract: Abstract: Insects are among the most ancient and successful organisms on Earth, having existed for over 400 million years. They form the most diverse group of living organisms, constituting more than 75% of all known animal species. Found in almost every habitat, insects play essential roles in agriculture, natural ecosystems, climate regulation, biodiversity maintenance, and food webs. Their interactions with plants, animals, and microorganisms create intricate ecological networks that support life on Earth. In the context of agriculture, insects occupy a unique dual position: they are both indispensable allies and challenging adversaries. Beneficial insects contribute to pollination, soil formation, nutrient cycling, and natural pest regulation, thereby facilitating sustainable agricultural productivity. Conversely, insect pests cause extensive crop losses, transmit plant diseases, and damage stored food, resulting in significant economic impacts globally. In an era of rapid climate change, land-use transformation, and pesticide overuse, the conservation and management of insect populations have become crucial. Understanding their ecological functions and integrating this knowledge into agricultural practices is a key step toward achieving sustainability, food security, and environmental resilience. items.title: Family environment, health risk behaviors, and mental health among chinese five-year vocational education students: a cross-sectional network analysis
items.abstract: Mental health problems, particularly depression and anxiety, pose a global public health challenge. Vocational education students are an understudied population, and the complex interrelationships among family environment, health risk behaviors, and psychological symptoms remain unclear. This study employed network analysis to examine these associations, aiming to identify central symptoms and potential gender differences. A total of 1,601 students enrolled in five-year higher vocational education programs were recruited from two vocational colleges in Nanning, Guangxi, using multistage cluster random sampling. Participants were aged 12–23 years, representing late adolescence and emerging adulthood. Family environment, health risk behaviors, and mental health status were assessed using the Family Environment Scale, the Student Health Status and Influencing Factors Questionnaire, and the Mental Health Scale for Middle School Students, respectively. The EBICglasso method was used to estimate networks and derive centrality indices, followed by the Network Comparison Test to evaluate gender differences. “Depression” and “Anxiety” showed the highest strength centrality. Family “Cohesion” and “Conflict” showed the highest bridge strength across domains. The relatively strongest edge was observed between “Sleep deprivation” and “Depression.” No significant gender differences were detected in network structure or global strength. Depression and anxiety were the most central symptoms in this network. Family cohesion and sleep deprivation were statistically prominent bridge nodes and may represent promising targets for future intervention research. Family-based emotional communication training and sleep health promotion warrant further investigation.

items.title: Risk factors for seizures in patients with brain metastases: integrating clinical features and molecular markers.
items.abstract: Brain metastases (BM) affect nearly 30% of patients with solid tumors. Despite this prevalence, the mechanisms underlying brain tumor-related epilepsy (BTRE) in this population remain incompletely elucidated. This study aims to investigate risk factors associated with seizure occurrence in patients with BM, focusing on histology and molecular markers of the primary tumor. We conducted a retrospective cohort study on 325 patients who underwent surgical resection of BM between 2014 and 2019. Clinical, radiological, and molecular data were analyzed using univariate and multivariable regression models to assess seizure risk factors. Overall Survival (OS) was assessed using Kaplan-Meier and Cox regression models. Seizures occurred in 32% of patients. Frontal (P<0.001) and parietal (P=0.05) locations were significantly associated with seizure occurrence. Ovarian cancer exhibited the highest seizure prevalence (80%, P=0.001), followed by melanoma (44%), breast (35%), and colorectal cancer (34%). Regarding molecular status, we found a significant association between seizures and both BRAF mutations in melanoma (P=0.03) and HER2 positive subtype breast cancer (P=0.01). Seizure occurrence at onset correlated with improved OS (P=0.01). Our findings suggest an association between seizure risk and molecular status of the primary tumor, specifically BRAF mutations in melanoma and HER2+ breast cancer subtype. Additionally, we found an improved OS in BM patients experiencing seizures at onset of disease. These findings are exploratory and warrant confirmation in larger cohorts; this could help refine seizure-risk estimation and prognostic assessment in surgically treated patients with brain metastases.

items.title: Longitudinal evolution of O-(2-[18F]-fluoroethyl)-L-tyrosine PET metrics in serial imaging during glioblastoma progression.
items.abstract: Most studies evaluating O-(2-[18F]-fluoroethyl)-L-tyrosine (FET) PET for glioblastoma progression rely on single-scan assessments, leaving diagnostic uncertainties in cases with borderline tracer uptake. We evaluated metabolic activity evolution during the transition of glioblastoma progression using serial FET PET to determine whether longitudinal parameter changes improve diagnostic certainty. Between 2016 and 2026, 182 patients with glioblastoma undergoing 690 dynamic FET PET scans (median, 3; range, 2-12) were retrospectively evaluated. Eligible cases required documented progressive disease according to RANO 2.0 criteria and serial FET PET at least 2 time points (at suspected progression and within a 6-month prior window). Static PET parameters, ie tumor-to-brain ratios (TBRmean, TBRmax) and metabolic tumor volume (MTV), and their longitudinal changes were evaluated according to PET RANO 1.0 criteria, alongside additional dynamic PET parameters (time-to-peak). Single-scan metrics and serial changes were compared in cases with borderline uptake. Ninety patients with 102 confirmed progression events met all selection criteria (median interscan interval, 2.7 months). At progression, TBRmean, TBRmax, and MTV increased significantly (P < .001). Median percentage increases were modest for TBRmean (+4%) and TBRmax (+17%), whereas MTV exhibited a substantial expansion (+182%). In cases with borderline uptake, applying a longitudinal MTV increase criterion of ≥40% per PET RANO 1.0 substantially improved progression detection to up to 89%, yielding a 14% higher diagnostic detection rate compared to single-scan thresholds. In glioblastomas with documented RANO 2.0 progression, integrating longitudinal MTV changes markedly improves diagnostic certainty over single-scan uptake metrics, particularly in challenging cases with borderline uptake.

items.title: Defining and managing NF1-related peripheral nerve sheath tumors at risk for malignant transformation: Consensus from the Atypical Neurofibroma Symposium.
items.abstract: People with neurofibromatosis type 1 (NF1) are at risk for developing peripheral nerve sheath tumors (PNSTs) ranging from benign neurofibromas to high-grade sarcomas. PNSTs known as atypical neurofibromas are at increased risk for malignant transformation. In 2017 the term ANNUBP (atypical neurofibromatous neoplasm of uncertain biologic potential) was proposed for PNSTs at increased risk for malignant transformation based on histopathologic features. Subsequently it was recognized that PNSTs not meeting ANNUBP criteria could still have concerning clinical, imaging and molecular features. A State of the Science conference addressed how to define these pre-cancerous PNSTs and reached consensus regarding clinical management and priority areas of research. Key recommendations from this symposium include: (1) using a combination of histologic, molecular and imaging features to define pre-malignant "at-risk" PNST; (2) recognizing that people with NF1 may be divided into "higher-risk" and "average-risk" for MPNST based on features such as their germline NF1 variant, internal tumor burden and history of malignancy or radiotherapy and; (3) the need to validate consensus screening and surveillance strategies based on personal and tumor-related risk factors. These recommendations will advance the ability to standardize care, and potentially fuel research that enables early diagnosis, prevention of malignant transformation and improved outcomes.

items.title: FLT3 Kinase Inhibition Reshapes the Neuronal Transcriptome to Suppress Seizures.
items.abstract: Approximately one-third of individuals with epilepsy are refractory to current anti-seizure medications, highlighting the need for new, mechanism-based therapeutic approaches. Fms-like tyrosine kinase 3 (FLT3), a receptor tyrosine kinase classically studied in hematopoiesis and leukemia, is also expressed in neurons, although its function in the brain remains largely unexplored. Our prior work identified small-molecule FLT3 inhibitors (FLT3i) as unexpected enhancers of potassium-chloride cotransporter 2 (KCC2), a neuron-specific chloride transporter essential for maintaining GABAergic inhibition. Here, we applied a functional genomics framework in mouse primary neurons and human stem cell-derived neurons to define FLT3i-induced transcriptional programs, revealing conserved gene networks governing synaptic function and ion channel regulation. A complementary CRISPR/Cas9-based screen of candidate transcription factors identified FLT3-responsive neuronal gene regulatory networks linked to epigenetic remodeling and neuroinflammatory signaling. We further demonstrate that KW-2449, an orally bioavailable FLT3 inhibitor, penetrates the blood-brain barrier, elevates KCC2 expression in vivo for up to 24 hours, and significantly reduces seizure susceptibility in a kainic acid-induced mouse model of epilepsy. Together, these findings reveal a previously unrecognized role for FLT3 in neuronal function and establish proof-of-principle for FLT3 inhibition as a mechanistically supported candidate strategy warranting further development as a next-generation anti-seizure therapy.

items.title: The 2026 Taiwan headache society guideline on the use of treatments targeting the CGRP pathway.
items.abstract: The introduction of CGRP-targeted therapy has markedly influenced migraine care in Taiwan, together with accumulating evidence and clinical experience. Therefore, the Treatment Guideline Subcommittee of the Taiwan Headache Society updated its 2022 consensus on preventive migraine therapy, with a specific focus on CGRP-targeted therapies. This updated guideline also provides evidence-based recommendations and practical guidance on the use of gepants following their introduction in Taiwan. After reviewing recent clinical trials, meta-analyses, and international guidelines, and integrating expert panel opinions, we developed this new guideline to update the treatment options, recommended populations, timing of initiation and discontinuation, and practical considerations for CGRP-targeted therapy, organised into ten clinical questions. According to the current consensus, preventive treatment is recommended for patients with ≥4 headache days per month, significant disability, failure of or contraindications to acute therapy, complicated migraine with severe aura (such as hemiplegic migraine or migrainous infarction), or when patient preference favours prevention after balancing potential benefits and risks. Currently, CGRP-targeted therapies for migraine prevention include anti-CGRP monoclonal antibodies, namely erenumab, fremanezumab, galcanezumab, and eptinezumab, as well as small-molecule CGRP receptor antagonists, including rimegepant and atogepant. In this 2026 updated guideline, CGRP-targeted therapy is listed as one of the first-line treatment options for both episodic and chronic migraine prevention. A history of failure of multiple preventive medications is not required before initiating CGRP-targeted therapy, as early initiation may provide better migraine control than delayed treatment. For both episodic and chronic migraine, the Taiwan Headache Society recommends that CGRP-targeted therapy may be continued for up to 12 months. This update is crucial for improving migraine care and highlights the importance of continuous CGRP-targeted therapy, rather than premature or unnecessary treatment interruption.

items.title: Branched optimal transport for stimulus to reaction brain mapping.
items.abstract: A central problem in systems neuroscience is to determine how an external stimulation is propagated through the brain so as to produce a reaction. Current deterministic and stochastic control models quantify transition costs between brain states on a prescribed network, but do not treat the transport network itself as an unknown. Here we propose a variational framework in which the inferred object is a graph/current connecting a stimulation source measure to a reaction target measure. The model is posed as an anisotropic branched optimal transport problem, where concavity of the flux cost promotes aggregation and branching. The support of an optimal current defines a stimulus-to-reaction routing architecture, interpreted as a brain reaction map. We prove existence of minimizers in discrete and continuous formulations and introduce a hybrid stochastic extension combining ramified transport with a path-space Kullback-Leibler control cost on the induced graph dynamics. This approach provides a mathematical mechanism for inferring propagation architectures rather than controlling trajectories on fixed substrates.

items.title: Influence of sex, puberty, and childhood psychopathology on developmental trajectories of the visual P300 across adolescence.
items.abstract: Research indicates the visual P300 decreases across adolescence due to maturation of neural attention networks. However, there is limited research examining whether assigned sex at birth and puberty influence this neurodevelopment. A blunted visual P300 has also been linked with internalizing and externalizing psychopathology, but it is unclear whether childhood psychopathology predicts changes in the P300 across adolescence. The present study examined whether sex, pubertal development, and childhood internalizing and externalizing symptoms predicted trajectories of the visual P300 across adolescence. The sample included 531 New York youth (45.5% female; 89.4% White; 19.7% Hispanic) who completed a flanker task to elicit the visual P300 at ages 9, 12, 15, 18, and 21 (2010-2025). Multilevel growth modeling indicated that the visual P300 was characterized by a quadratic decrease from late childhood to early adulthood; males showed a slower rate of change than females. Females with greater age 12 pubertal development showed a faster rate of change. Males with higher age 9 externalizing symptoms and depression symptoms had blunted baseline P300s. Age 9 internalizing and externalizing symptoms did not relate to slope. Results highlight the need to better understand the developmental of neural indicators of attentional processing that have been linked to future psychopathology.

items.title: A brief intervention highlighting counter-stereotypical role models changes children's gender stereotypes about values and careers.
items.abstract: Care-oriented values and careers are vital, yet men and boys remain less engaged with them. We tested a brief, preregistered role-model intervention to reduce children's gender stereotypes about communion (caring for others) and agency (achievement and independence). We also examined whether this intervention would narrow gender differences in children's own values and career interests. 7- to 10-year-olds from the U.S. and Canada (N = 244; 121 boys, 123 girls) viewed 6 animated vignettes about fictional children who grew up to choose careers aligned with their values. In the "stereotypical" condition, girls were communal and entered communal careers, while boys were agentic and entered agentic careers. In the "counter-stereotypical" condition, these pairings were reversed. A third, "counter-stereotypical + status" condition added wealth cues to both communal and agentic careers. Compared with the stereotypical condition, both counter-stereotypical conditions weakened children's gender stereotypes about communal and agentic values and careers. They also reduced gender differences in children's own communal values and career interests, although these effects were smaller and less consistent. Wealth cues did not strengthen the intervention. These findings suggest that counter-stereotypical role models are a promising, scalable method for combating stereotypes that steer boys away from communion-though likely one component of broader efforts.

items.title: Evo2VED: a database of DNA large language model-derived scores for variant interpretation.
items.abstract: The Evo2 Variant Effect Database (Evo2VED; https://dnallmved.org/) is a publicly accessible resource cataloging precomputed Evo2-derived variant effect scores, defined as allelic score differences, for 6.48 million human variants common in the gnomAD non-Finnish European population. Evo2VED includes scores from the 7B and 40B models under three scoring schemes, alongside annotations of variant function, evolutionary constraint, allele age, and disease associations. It integrates genome-wide association study (GWAS) data from UK Biobank, FinnGen, and the Million Veteran Program. Three complementary modules support variant-level interpretation, regional and region-set exploration, and trait-level analysis through flexible queries, interactive visualizations, and downloadable results. Evo2VED also catalogs associations between Evo2 annotations and per-SNP heritability across thousands of traits from these biobanks. A guided workflow connects GWAS with associated regions and individual variant evidence. Case studies of hypertension and depression illustrate how regional comparisons of Evo2 scores and GWAS signals can guide candidate variant prioritization. Evaluations using massively parallel reporter assays, molecular QTLs, fine-mapping probabilities, and clinical annotations assess associations with Evo2 scores alone and their added value beyond conservation and regulatory annotations. By providing accessible scores, contextual annotations, and comparative analyses, Evo2VED facilitates exploration and application of genomic language model predictions in human genetics research.

items.title: Association of Self-Reported Sleep and Circadian Variability and Moral Judgements and Decision-Making.
items.abstract: Sleep and social processes are bidirectionally interrelated. Circadian factors such as sleep duration, quality, and chronotype can influence social processing, including moral judgements and decision-making. We investigated the associations of self-reported sleep and circadian factors with measures of human moral and social judgements, including online vigilantism, aversion to causing and witnessing harm, and generosity. A total of 109 healthy adults (18-39 years) completed an observational online survey of self-report measures of sleep and circadian factors (quality, chronotype, sleep regularity, social jetlag), as well as self-report or behavioural measures related to moral concerns, such as willingness to engage in online vigilantism, aversion to causing and witnessing harm to others, and generosity (the Dictator Game). We found significant associations between increased online vigilantism and earlier chronotype, higher sleep regularity, and less social jetlag (r > 0.20, all p 0.20, all p 0.06). Hierarchical regression analyses identified moderate effect sizes for sleep regularity and (to a lesser extent) social jetlag as significant contributors to vigilantism and aversion to causing and witnessing harm (R2 > 0.21, all p < 0.05), after controlling for sociodemographic characteristics, mental health conditions, and medication intake. A small, non-significant effect size was identified for sleep quality and dictator game generosity (R2 = 0.13, p = 0.06). The findings highlight the importance of considering sleep and circadian regularity in human moral judgements and decision-making.

items.title: Day-to-day peer and family stress as proximal correlates of self-injurious thoughts during adolescence.
items.abstract: Theory and research both highlight interpersonal stressors as precipitants to self-injurious thoughts and behaviors (SITBs) during adolescence. Yet, little is known about near-term risk or which types of interpersonal stressors (e.g., peer and/or family) are most likely to precipitate adolescent SITBs. This study used an intensive longitudinal design to examine whether peer- and family-related stress were associated with adolescents' same- and next-day self-injurious thoughts. Participants were 154 female adolescents aged 12-17 years (77.3% White). Youth were oversampled for risk such that 73.4% ( n = 113) were at high risk for future SITBs. Youth completed a 30-day ecological momentary assessment procedure assessing interpersonal experiences and SITBs. Multilevel models showed that peer stress predicted same-day nonsuicidal self-injury urges and suicidal ideation (SI), whereas family stress predicted same-day nonsuicidal self-injury urges only. Neither peer nor family stress predicted next-day self-injurious thoughts. Exploratory models examining bidirectional effects showed that non-suicidal self-injury urges predicted next-day peer and family stress while SI predicted next-day family, but not peer, stress. Findings suggest that daily interpersonal stress is proximally associated with self-injurious thoughts during adolescence and underscore the importance of studying these processes in real time. Results may have implications for ecological momentary interventions to interrupt interpersonal risks for SITBs.

items.title: Prevalence and Correlates of Service-Connected Disability Among U.S. Military Veterans.
items.abstract: Objective Veterans with general medical or mental health conditions that were caused or exacerbated by military service may be eligible for U.S. Department of Veterans Affairs (VA) service-connected disability compensation, which entails financial support, access to health care, and long-term benefits. Using a contemporary, nationally representative sample of U.S. military veterans, the authors compared the sociodemographic, military, and clinical characteristics of veterans with and of those without service-connected disability and identified factors associated with receipt of benefits for mental health versus general medical conditions. Methods Data were analyzed from 2,636 U.S. military veterans who participated in the National Health and Resilience in Veterans Study. Participants reported service-connected disability status, disability rating, and primary service-connected conditions and completed assessments for sociodemographic characteristics, military status, trauma exposure, psychiatric disorders, and general medical conditions. Results Overall, 39% of veterans reported having a VA service-connected disability. Multivariable analyses indicated that younger age, longer military service, a greater number of deployments, lifetime psychiatric diagnosis, and greater medical burden were independently associated with increased odds of receiving service-connected disability benefits. Having a service-connected psychiatric disability was strongly associated with lifetime psychiatric diagnosis, a greater number of deployments, and military sexual trauma. Conclusions A substantial percentage of U.S. veterans receive service-connected disability benefits. Veterans receiving these benefits represent a clinically complex population with substantial cumulative service-related exposures and elevated mental and general medical health burdens. These findings may inform clinical care, resource allocation, and policies aimed at addressing the long-term health needs of veterans with service-connected disabilities.
