items.title: Investigating Incivility in Prelicensure Nursing Education: A Narrative Review of Faculty-to-Student Incivility.
items.abstract: Aim The aim of the study was threefold: 1) synthesize current research in undergraduate nursing education surrounding faculty-to-student incivility in the classroom setting, 2) construct a conceptual definition of faculty-to-student incivility, and 3) identify potential gaps in the current literature for future research purposes. Background Each dynamic of incivility in undergraduate nursing education has unique qualities that must be investigated. Faculty-to-student incivility can be identified in behaviors that negatively impact students' ability to progress through the program. Method A narrative review was performed on relevant articles from 2018 to the present across five databases. A thematic analysis was performed. Results Four key categories were identified in 14 articles: types of incivility, causes of incivility, consequences of incivility, and strategies to mitigate incivility. Conclusion Faculty-to-student incivility is an ongoing issue with profound consequences affecting student retention and the nursing profession. Addressing incivility through faculty education and institutional policies must be promoted.

items.title: Broadening global health knowledge: epistemic pluralism through Asian philosophical traditions.
items.abstract: Global health continues to operate largely within a biomedical epistemological framework that, while effective in addressing acute disease and advancing clinical care, remains limited in responding to complex challenges such as mental health, chronic illness, and persistent inequities. These limitations are not merely technical but reflect deeper epistemic constraints in how health and care are conceptualised. This article argues that selected Asian philosophical traditions, often interpreted through the lens of orientalism, offer an under-recognised resource for rethinking global health. Drawing selectively on Taoist, Confucian, and Buddhist traditions, we highlight how principles of relationality, adaptability, and compassion provide alternative foundations for understanding health beyond the absence of disease. These traditions offer distinctive conceptualisations of relationality, compassion and well-being that can be placed in dialogue with contemporary biomedical and public-health approaches. While contemporary global health systems have increasingly incorporated practices such as mindfulness-based interventions, this integration has often occurred without engagement with their broader philosophical and epistemological implications. Recognising these perspectives and their potential for integration has important implications for global health practice, including reorienting medical education toward reflective and relational competencies, strengthening person-centred and community-engaged care models, and addressing knowledge hierarchies that marginalise ancient philosophical traditions. Reimagining global health therefore requires moving beyond unidirectional knowledge transfer toward a more pluralistic and dialogic framework, in which diverse traditions contribute to more holistic, equitable, and contextually responsive health systems.

items.title: Dental solid waste management and associated environmental impacts in Australia: A mini-review.
items.abstract: Over the past century, global warming has become a major environmental issue. The healthcare sector, particularly the dental industry, has been responsible for generating significant amounts of solid waste, and consequently creating greenhouse gas emissions contributing to global warming. This mini-review collates evidence on the current global literature and Australian policy landscape on Australian dental solid waste management and associated environmental impacts. It involved a rapid literature review of global academic and grey literature and Australian policies on the management of dental solid waste. Seven academic articles, eight grey literature articles and three Australian policies were included for review. Key findings were tabulated and thematically coded into headings adapted from the 2018 Australian National Waste Policy framework for solid waste management. Solid waste generation should be reduced through actions such as oral health promotion and caries prevention activities, digitisation of dental administrative processes and streamlining of clinical processes. Waste management system design is important, including waste segregation and proper design of disposal and recycling systems. Knowledge sharing and staff education can help activate behavioural change towards the management of solid waste. Focusing on environmental sustainability, product stewardship and reducing single-use plastics and packaging can also improve solid waste management. Not all waste can be avoided in dentistry, and dental organisations should have alternative strategies to manage solid waste. Strong leadership and governance to support solid waste management strategies can ensure that organisations approach solid waste management at the highest level possible, reducing greenhouse gas emissions and their impact on climate change.

items.title: Toward a Definition and Differentiation of Secondary Traumatic Stress, Vicarious Trauma, Post-Traumatic Stress, and Compassion Fatigue in Relation to First Responders: An Integrative Literature Review.
items.abstract: This integrative review focuses on the psychological effects of direct and indirect exposure to trauma among first responders (firefighters, police investigators, police officers, paramedics, ambulance workers). The aim of this study is to provide conceptual clarification of the various terms used: secondary traumatic stress, vicarious trauma, compassion fatigue, and post-traumatic stress disorder. For this study, six databases were consulted: PsycINFO/ARTICLE; PubMed/Medline; Web of Science; Cochrane; Cairn; ScienceDirect, up to January 2026. To be included, articles had to be published in peer-reviewed scientific journals and concern an adult and professional population. Data extraction followed PRISMA guidelines, and 76 studies were included. Two researchers participated in data extraction and ensured the quality of the articles. The main results revealed conceptual porosity maintained by symptomatic overlaps and the limitations of measurement tools, often designed for other professional categories. The analysis also highlights the central role of organizational constraints in the emergence of trauma, the importance of considering the nature of exposure, cumulative burden, personal experience, and professional role in the study of traumatic responses. Finally, this review calls for exposure to trauma among first responders to be viewed as a public health issue.

items.title: How Can Local Food Environment Policies Reduce Socioeconomic Inequalities in Diet?
items.abstract: This commentary discusses the role of local municipal policies in addressing socioeconomic inequalities in diet and preventing diet-related noncommunicable diseases (NCDs). While national legal and fiscal instruments are essential, local governments possess unique tools, such as spatial planning and public procurement, to improve daily food environments. However, published examples do not establish the comparative effectiveness of municipal-level interventions or their effects on dietary inequalities. Improving physical access or relying on informational tools, like menu labelling, should not be assumed sufficient to reduce dietary inequalities. Direct financial incentives are promising, but the cited observational evidence does not establish causal effectiveness. Interventions combining availability, affordability and demand may address multiple barriers, without necessarily outperforming single structural measures. To reduce dietary disparities, local policies should form part of a coherent multilevel strategy, address economic as well as physical access, and be durably funded, coupled with rigorous, equity-focused evaluation of implementation, dietary outcomes and, where feasible, longer-term health outcomes.

items.title: Preparing for the future, feeling better now: Old-age financial preparation and psychological well-being in pre-old-age Korean adults.
items.abstract: Objectives Population aging has made old-age financial preparation increasingly consequential, yet it is typically indexed by a single measure that does not distinguish among the forms it takes. Drawing on Conservation of Resources theory and the institutional and normative structure of retirement in Korea, we examined associations between within-person changes in financial preparation and two distinct dimensions of subjective well-being among pre-old-age Korean adults. Methods Using seven biennial waves (2011-2023) of the Korean Retirement and Income Study (9,887 person-waves; 2,389 individuals), we estimated individual fixed-effects regressions examining associations between old-age financial preparation and depressive symptoms, measured using the Center for Epidemiologic Studies Depression Scale (CES-D), and life satisfaction, adjusting for key time-varying covariates. Results Within-person transitions into preparation were associated with a 1.02-point lower CES-D score and a 0.11-point higher life-satisfaction score on a 5-point scale (both p Discussion Old-age financial preparation appears to function as a within-person psychosocial resource related to both evaluative and affective dimensions of well-being. These divergent patterns suggest that the scope and adequacy of preparation matter differently for depressive symptoms and global life evaluations, potentially informing pension policy and financial-planning interventions in aging societies.

items.title: Analyzing epigenetic modifications at sample-specific CpG loci in long-read data using a likelihood-based framework in bsseq.
items.abstract: Summary DNA in CpG context is often epigenetically modified in vertebrate genomes which increases their mutation rate. However, it remains challenging to identify sample-specific CpG loci for analysis of epigenetic modifications. Here, we present a read-based likelihood framework for identifying reference and non-reference CpG loci with high precision and sensitivity in single-molecule long-read sequencing data from Nanopore and PacBio platforms. Including all sample-specific CpG loci increases the number of analyzable loci and reduces bias in modification level estimates, both critical factors for accurate analyses of epigenetic modifications. Availability and implementation The likelihood framework is implemented in the R package bsseq with the source code available on github https://github.com/hansenlab/bsseq. Installation instructions and a user guide for long-read analysis and likelihood-based filtering of CpG loci are available on Bioconductor https://www.bioconductor.org/packages/release/bioc/html/bsseq.html. Supplementary information Supplementary data are available at Bioinformatics online.

items.title: Estimated Usual Nutrient Intakes and Nutrient Inadequacy Among Schoolchildren in Rural Communities in the Philippines.
items.abstract: BackgroundPost-COVID data on nutritional status or dietary intake of school-aged Filipino children are limited but needed to inform interventions.MethodsWe conducted a cross-sectional study among a non-representative sample of 342 school-aged Filipino children aged 5 to 10 years in high-risk rural communities in the Philippines in 2022. Dietary data were collected using a single 24-hour dietary recall ( n = 342). Estimated usual intakes and the prevalence of inadequacy were calculated using the National Cancer Institute 1-day method with external variance ratios (between-person and within-person) from the 2018 Filipino National Nutrition Survey. Foods were grouped using the Food and Agriculture Organization regional food composition tables for analysis.ResultsThe median energy intakes were 1516 (boys) and 1304 (girls) kcal/day for children < 6 years, and 1420 (boys) and 1404 (girls) kcal/day for ages 6 to 10 years, resulting in 38% to 48% of children having energy intakes below estimated energy requirements across age and sex groups. Prevalence of inadequacy ranged from 65.8% to 78.1%, 35.2% to 43.5%, 32.6% to 58.6%, and 33.1% to 76.6% for calcium, iron, vitamin A, and vitamin C, respectively, across groups. Commonly consumed foods included rice, bread, cookies/cake (fillings), coconut oil, powdered milk, moringa, bananas, and coffee. Intakes of meats, fruits, and vegetables were low.ConclusionThe prevalence of micronutrient inadequacies was concerningly high among children in this post-COVID population. Diets were mostly refined rice with minimal fruit and vegetable consumption. While powdered milk and chicken egg were consumed, the intakes were insufficient to meet nutrient requirements. This dietary pattern suggests incorporating nutrient-rich, locally available food for future intervention.

items.title: Awareness of a National Tobacco Prevention and Cessation Campaign and E-Cigarette Quitting Stages: Findings From Truth Initiative's Mass Media Campaign (September 2024 to May 2025).
items.abstract: PurposeTo examine associations between awareness of a national tobacco prevention and cessation campaign and stages of readiness for quitting e-cigarettes.Design, Setting, and SampleData were obtained from a repeated, cross-sectional online survey of United States youth and young adults (aged 15-24 years), who reported past 30-day e-cigarette use, and provided survey responses between September 1, 2024 to May 31, 2025 (N = 3486).Measures and AnalysisMultinomial regression models were used to determine associations between awareness level (no awareness, low awareness, high awareness) of Truth Initiative's mass media campaign and stages of quitting e-cigarettes (precontemplation, contemplation, and preparation/action, based on expressed quit intentions), adjusted for the effects of age, sex assigned at birth, ethnicity and race, parental educational attainment, sexual orientation, current use of other tobacco products, and time of survey aligning with ad campaign.ResultsCompared to those with no campaign awareness, those with low and high campaign awareness were more likely to be in contemplation (relative risk ratio, RRR = 1.78 and RRR = 2.64) and preparation/action (RRR = 1.63 and RRR = 2.77) stages, respectively. Older age, female sex, Non-Hispanic Black ethnicity and race, and later time interval of survey aligning with ad campaign were associated with further quit stage, while bisexual identity was associated with earlier quit stage.ConclusionHigher levels of campaign awareness were associated with more advanced stages of quitting. Results suggest that campaign awareness may be particularly salient among youth and young adults who are considering or actively preparing to quit e-cigarettes.

items.title: Heart Failure in Anthracycline Cardiotoxicity: From Mechanisms to Clinical Management.
items.abstract: Anthracyclines remain a cornerstone therapy for haematological malignancies and solid tumours, but their use is limited by cardiotoxicity, ranging from asymptomatic left ventricular dysfunction to overt heart failure (HF). The risk increases with cumulative doxorubicin-equivalent exposure exceeding 250-300 mg/m2, although susceptibility varies substantially according to patient characteristics, pre-existing cardiovascular disease, genetic predisposition, and modifiable risk factors. Clinically overt HF occurs in ∼6-9% of patients, while subclinical cardiac dysfunction develops in up to 18%. The pathophysiology is multifactorial, involving interconnected mechanisms that disrupt cardiomyocyte homeostasis and promote endothelial dysfunction, inflammation, fibrosis, and adverse remodelling. Yet evidence connecting molecular mechanisms with long-term HF outcomes in humans remains incomplete. Risk stratification, incorporating clinical variables, cardiac biomarkers, echocardiography and, when appropriate, cardiac magnetic resonance enables earlier recognition of cardiac dysfunction. Trials of preventive neurohormonal treatment and statins have produced heterogeneous results, often relying on imaging rather than clinical HF endpoints. Once cardiac dysfunction develops, prompt initiation of foundational HF treatment and multidisciplinary decisions on cancer therapy are essential. Early detection and prompt initiation of HF therapies may reverse myocardial dysfunction, whereas delayed recognition is associated with a poorer treatment response and prognosis. This narrative review integrates current evidence on the mechanisms, risk stratification, surveillance, prevention, and management of anthracycline cardiotoxicity and HF, while highlighting gaps in knowledge, emerging therapeutic strategies, and future directions for clinically meaningful, risk-guided research.

items.title: Work-Caregiving strain among family caregivers of burn survivors: Occupational sacrifice and positive occupational appraisal.
items.abstract: BackgroundFamily caregivers are often working adults whose unpaid care responsibilities can disrupt paid work, yet occupational impact is rarely examined beyond employment status or financial burden. Burn caregiving provides a high-demand traumatic-injury context in which prolonged rehabilitation, family reorganization, and support needs may conflict with caregivers' work lives.ObjectiveTo examine the occupational impact of burn caregiving over a 24-month recovery period and characterize two theory-informed patterns of caregiver occupational experience: occupational sacrifice and positive occupational appraisal.MethodsWe analyzed baseline and 24-month occupational follow-up data from 256 family caregivers in a burn survivor-caregiver cohort. Follow-up outcomes captured work participation, job change, caregiving-attributed workforce detachment, perceived career impact, and work-related barriers and facilitators post-baseline. Occupational sacrifice was operationalized as caregiving-attributed workforce detachment or adverse career appraisal among employed caregivers; positive occupational appraisal was defined as favorable perceived career impact. Baseline demographic, survivor-injury, and psychosocial characteristics were examined descriptively and in logistic regression models.ResultsAt 24 months, 71.5% reported ongoing work participation, 20.7% caregiving-attributed workforce detachment, and 7.8% other changes. Among employed caregivers, 32.2% reported job change, of whom 42.4% reported negative career appraisal. Occupational sacrifice was identified in 35.2% and was accompanied by functional, appearance-related, family-caregiving, workplace, rehabilitation-support, and financial barriers. Positive occupational appraisal was reported by 31.3% and was associated with lower baseline distress and higher posttraumatic growth.ConclusionsThese findings extend injury-related occupational health to family caregivers and support a theory-informed framework for studying work-caregiving strain, occupational sacrifice, and positive appraisal prospectively.

items.title: From Isolated Work to a Team-Based Approach in Home Care Services: Impact on Labor Conditions and Physical Health.
items.abstract: Background Barcelona's municipal Home Care Services (HCS) have undergone a teamwork- and proximity-based reorganization aimed, among other goals, at improving workers' labor conditions. Although team-based home care has been commonly studied in relation to job satisfaction and autonomy, evidence on workers' physical health is limited. Objective To assess the impact of HCS reorganization on workers' employment conditions, ergonomic hazards, and physical health outcomes. Methods Mixed-method quasi-experimental pre-post design (2022-2024). Quantitative data included 1288 survey observations from intervention and comparison groups across three waves (pre: 550 workers; post1: 397 workers; post2: 341 workers). Qualitative data comprised 27 longitudinal interviews with intervention group workers at two time points, with one participant lost to follow-up. Results Quantitative descriptive results showed increased full-time employment and shorter travel times between users' homes in the intervention group. Ergonomic risk exposure was high across groups, but lifting or moving people augmented only among intervention workers. These workers also reported higher levels of fatigue and poorer self-rated health over time. Multivariable analyses confirmed results on travel times, exposure to lifting or moving people, and fatigue. Qualitative findings suggest sustained exposure to ergonomic hazards and indirect effects of the reorganization as potential mechanisms behind fatigue. Conclusions Among intervention workers, three main changes were associated with the HCS reorganization: shorter travel times between users' homes, more frequent lifting or moving people, and higher fatigue levels. Further strategies are needed to reduce physical strain and safeguard workers' health in this essential care sector.

items.title: Child grant receipt and birth registration in Nepal: evidence from the 2022 Nepal Demographic and Health Survey.
items.abstract: Background In Nepal, a child grant program was introduced in 2009 to improve education and nutrition among disadvantaged children under the age of five while linking grant eligibility to birth registration as part of efforts to strengthen civil registration and vital statistics systems. Objective This study examined whether child grant receipt was associated with birth registration. Methods We conducted a cross-sectional analysis of data from the 2022 Nepal Demographic and Health Survey. The outcome was whether a child's birth had ever been registered with civil authorities. The main explanatory variable was whether the child had ever received a child grant. Child age, sex, maternal education, ethnicity, household wealth quintile, and province were included as covariates in multivariable logistic regression models. Results Among 5,064 included children, 72.8% had a reported registered birth. Registration was higher among children reported to have received a grant than among nonrecipients (93.6% versus 65.9%). Children reported to have received a grant had higher adjusted odds of registration than nonrecipients (adjusted odds ratio [aOR] 6.75; 95% CI 5.14 to 8.85). Registration was 71.8% among children whose mothers had no education, 68.3% for grades 1 to 8, and 77.0% for education above grade 8. Conclusions Child grant receipt was strongly associated with reported birth registration. Links between social protection and birth registration should be accompanied by accessible registration services and support for families facing documentation barriers.

items.title: Photovoice as contributing to resiliency among trans women experiencing individual and intersecting HIV and anti-trans stigma in madhesh province, Nepal.
items.abstract: Trans women in low-income countries face high risk for HIV and poor care outcomes, often due to pervasive anti-trans and HIV-related stigma. We implemented a Photovoice intervention to explore how intersecting forms of stigma shape the lives of trans women in one of the Terai districts of Nepal and to examine how participation in the project influenced social support and community connectedness. Using a participatory mixed-methods design, fourteen trans women participated in two Photovoice workshops, completed pre- and post-intervention surveys, and engaged in photo documentation, journaling, group discussion, and interviews. Participants described experiences of internalised and familial stigma, economic exclusion, diminished family support, and social marginalisation, with photographs illustrating how stigma influenced daily life, livelihood, mobility and well-being. Following the intervention, most participants reported greater community connectedness, defined as increased feelings of interpersonal connection, emotional support, and engagement with other trans women and peer networks. These changes were reflected in participants reporting greater outreach to peers, increased emotional openness, and stronger support from relationships developed during the project. Photovoice effectively fostered social support and collective resilience, highlighting the need for structural interventions to improve HIV prevention, treatment, and wellbeing outcomes.

items.title: Arousal state fluctuations destabilize speech intelligibility in older adults
items.abstract: Understanding speech in noisy, multi-talker environments is fundamental for social communication but becomes increasingly challenging as we age. Age-related hearing loss reduces audibility and degrades speech encoding, yet these deficits do not fully explain the momentary lapses in speech understanding that frustrate real-time communication. Here, we tested whether brain state fluctuations immediately before speech onset predict forthcoming speech recognition errors in older listeners. We measured the accuracy, speed, and consistency of speech recognition in 183 adults aged 18-76 years (103 female) using a brief, trial-based multi-talker listening task while tracking pupil dynamics before and during speech presentation. Prestimulus pupil-linked arousal predicted trial-level speech recognition in older, but not younger, adults, independent of hearing status, cognitive load, and task accuracy. In adults over 50 years of age, lower and higher extremes of prestimulus pupil size were associated with less accurate and slower responses, producing a striking inverted-U relationship between prestimulus arousal and forthcoming behavioral performance. Older adults exhibited lower extremes of pupil-linked arousal that were specifically associated with greater self-reported difficulty listening in everyday life. By contrast, stimulus-evoked pupil dilation during speech encoding, a measure of listening effort, did not predict trial-level performance at any age. These findings identify prestimulus pupil-linked arousal as a hidden marker of forthcoming lapses in speech intelligibility in older adults. When considered alongside conventional measures of peripheral hearing status in mixed-effects regression models, these measures provide a more complete accounting of biological changes underlying speech intelligibility deficits that frustrate social communication in older adults . Significance statement As we age, following a conversation in crowded environments becomes more difficult and frustrating, even when hearing tests appear normal. This study shows that fluctuations in arousal level (measured through prestimulus pupil size) are tightly linked to fluctuations in the speed and accuracy of speech processing in adults over 50 years of age. Changes in arousal state regulation uniquely accounted for the moment-to-moment variations in speech intelligibility and were more closely associated with self-reported listening challenges than other conventional measures. These findings highlight the contribution of brain-wide arousal systems to real-world listening challenges and identify a straightforward measure that could be used to more comprehensively assess and potentially improve speech understanding in social settings.

items.title: A concurrent working memory task disrupts motor performance but preserves adaptation during dexterous object manipulation
items.abstract: Abstract Dexterous everyday actions such as grasping and lifting objects rely on precise sensorimotor control and are often performed under concurrent cognitive demands. This study examined how cognitive load induced through a verbal working memory task affects sensorimotor integration in anticipatory adaptation during object manipulation. Participants adapted to an asymmetrical mass distribution by generating compensatory moments at object lift onset, with the aim of minimising object roll. Sensorimotor adaptation performance and grip force modulation were assessed under both single-task (motor only) and dual-task (motor plus working memory) conditions. Results showed that cognitive load led to longer reaction times and increased grip forces, indicating cognitive-motor interference consistent with previous literature. Crucially, however, the trajectory of the adaptation to the novel object dynamics remained robust even under high cognitive load. This resilience suggests that the core processes of error-driven, trial-by-trial motor adaptation which hinge on salient, task-relevant visual and haptic feedback, are relatively immune to the disruptive effects of concurrent working memory demands.

items.title: Symmetry as a common origin of hierarchical emergence and abstraction
items.abstract: Many systems of interest exhibit nested emergent layers with their own rules and regularities, and our knowledge about them seems naturally organized around these levels. How do such hierarchical structures arise, and why should observers track these hierarchies so closely? This paper proposes symmetry as an answer to both questions. By combining principles from information theory, group theory, and statistical mechanics, it is shown that dynamical processes that are equivariant with respect to a symmetry group give rise to multiple emergent macroscopic levels arranged according to the algebraic structure of the symmetry. The same symmetries shape the Bayesian beliefs of an observer with only partial access to the system, yielding a matching hierarchy of “abstract” beliefs that can be updated autonomously at different levels of resolution. These ideas are illustrated in Hopfield networks, where familiar macroscopic quantities emerge from known symmetries, and in Boolean models of gene regulation, where symmetries are instead found from the dynamics. The computational advantages provided by symmetry are showcased in Ehrenfest diffusion and epidemic modeling, where abstract beliefs enable Bayesian inference over exponentially large state spaces. These results identify symmetry as a sufficient mechanism for hierarchical emergence and—at the same time—for the capacity of abstract beliefs to mirror the systems they track, making feasible inferential problems that would otherwise be intractable.

items.title: Children with developmental language disorder show selective impairments in low-frequency neural tracking of speech
items.abstract: Neural tracking of slow temporal modulations in speech supports extraction of the prosodic and syllabic structure thought to be critical for language acquisition by Temporal Sampling (TS) theory, yet whether these automatic cortical tracking mechanisms are altered in children with developmental language disorder (DLD) remains unclear. We recorded MEG while children with and without DLD listened to a story, and quantified source-level lagged speech-brain coherence and frequency-specific cortical functional connectivity across bilateral cortical regions. As expected a priori by TS theory, children with DLD showed significantly reduced coherence in the 0.9–2.5 Hz range associated with prosodic information in the story, spanning bilateral auditory and speech-related cortex. The strongest regional group differences were in left supramarginal gyrus ( p < 0.001) and right inferior frontal gyrus ( p = 0.001). In the 2.5–5 Hz range, linked to syllabic-rate modulations in the story, children with DLD showed reduced coherence in right temporal regions (all p < 0.02). Stronger low-frequency speech-brain coherence was associated with better language performance, indicating that individual differences in cortical speech tracking were behaviourally meaningful. No reliable differences were observed at higher modulation rates (5–9 Hz or 12–40 Hz). Exploratory functional connectivity analyses did not reveal network-level group differences that were robust across ROI time-series extraction methods. These findings indicate that atypical low-frequency neural tracking of speech is functionally relevant to language outcomes in DLD.

items.title: Theory of mind predicts conversational success in early right hemisphere stroke recovery
items.abstract: Those living with right hemisphere damage (RHD) often struggle with engaging in aspects of conversation that require understanding what a speaker means. There is growing evidence that conversation relies on deducing the speaker’s perspective, an ability known as theory of mind (ToM). However, whether individual differences in conversation after RHD relate to ToM deficits is unknown. Here, we related individual differences in conversational success to ToM in 31 speakers during the early stages of RHD (median 5 days post-stroke) in comparison to 16 age- and education-matched controls. We measured conversational success as the number of differences identified between two images while participants conversed with study coordinators. A non-verbal false belief task measured ToM abilities. Baseline cognitive tasks assessed visual inattention, inhibitory control/visual selective attention and working memory. Linear mixed-effects modeling revealed that the ToM ability to explicitly infer others’ perspectives while managing conflict with one’s own reliably predicted conversational success (β = 0.42, p = .023; β’s = 0.44 − 0.64 across sensitivity models). Adding false belief ToM substantially increased model fit (ΔR 2 = 0.115, Cohen’s f 2 = 0.15), independent of baseline cognitive abilities and demographic factors. These findings provide the first empirical evidence in unilateral RHD that the ability to reason about a partner’s knowledge and manage conflict with one’s privileged perspective is critical for successful conversation. Results support theoretical models of ToM as a cognitive basis for everyday conversation. The clinical implications underscore the importance of socio-cognitive screening and ToM-based interventions to enhance communication outcomes in stroke rehabilitation.

items.title: Day-to-Day Variation in Perceived Causal Networks: A Feasibility Study in Two Psychiatric Settings
items.abstract: Abstract Purpose The network approach conceptualizes psychopathology as a system of causally interacting problems of living. Longitudinal Perceived Causal Networks (L-PECAN) is a self-report method designed to capture day-to-day variability in patients’ perceived causal relations between problems. We examined the feasibility of an L-PECAN procedure in two clinical settings and explored within-person variability in perceived causal network structures. Methods Patients in two psychiatric clinics first completed an L-PECAN training week using a generic item list. Personalized items, including contextual factors, were then formulated and used subsequently for a minimum of three weeks. Feasibility was evaluated via recruitment rates and adherence. Within-person variability was examined using saturation and drift analyses. Results Eight patients completed the protocol. Median daily completion times ranged from one to eight minutes. Participants largely perceived their personalized problems as being caused by their other problems. Some causal relations were perceived consistently across days, but overall network structures showed substantial day-to-day variability. Conclusions An L-PECAN procedure incorporating a training week and personalized nodes appeared feasible in the university clinic, whereas uptake and adherence indicated greater implementation challenges in specialist psychiatric care. The method provides a structured way to examine day-to-day variability in perceived causal problem networks. Further research is needed to establish feasibility across clinical populations and to evaluate validity and clinical utility.

items.title: Personalized to Persuade: The Effects of Contextualization and Warmth on Trust and Reliance in Conversational AI
items.abstract: Conversational agents tailor explanations to users’ backgrounds and interests, a strategy we refer to as contextualization. While personalization is an established persuasive lever in politics and marketing, its effect in everyday tasks, where users lack prior knowledge, remains unclear. We report a 2 × 2 between-subjects experiment (N = 380) testing how contextualization and conversational warmth shape the persuasiveness of, and reliance on, an AI assistant that argues against expert recommendations. Contextualization and warmth each reduce persuasiveness, yet their combination restores it through a crossover interaction. Behavioral reliance is high in every condition and invariant to conversational design. Trust predicts both outcomes but mediates neither. AI literacy decouples attitude from behavior: more literate users report lower trust, yet are more persuaded and more likely to abandon the expert position.

items.title: Enacting Constructive Conflicts with AI Agents to Enhance Reconsideration among Novice Interaction Designers
items.abstract: Generative AI agents are increasingly used in interaction design to facilitate ideation, often following their own internal reasoning. These interactions tend to expand the design space. Our work explores an antagonistic role for design agents, prompting designers to engage with stakeholder tension. We built an antagonistic AI agent and examined the agent’s influence in a between-subjects experiment with 45 design students across three conditions: Self Reflection (unsupported review of the design proposal), Stepwise Guidance (written prompts that walk designers through a constructive-conflict framework), and Interactive Engagement (an AI agent that enacts the constructive-conflict framework interactively by synthesizing stakeholder pushback). The latter two conditions share the framework but differ in whether it is self-enacted or agent-enacted. Results show that, compared with Self Reflection, both the Stepwise Guidance and Interactive Engagement groups reported significantly higher self-reconsideration and made more improvements to their design proposals. Compared with Stepwise Guidance, the antagonistic agent introduced more conflictual perspectives, and participants in the Engagement condition generated and discarded more ideas. These findings suggest that an interactive agent that surfaces stakeholder pushback can support concrete design revision while keeping designers engaged with divergent perspectives.

items.title: Neighborhood Exposome at Birth and Trajectories of Epigenetic Age Acceleration Across Childhood
items.abstract: Importance Epigenetic age acceleration (EAA) has been linked to increased disease risk in adults, yet its developmental trajectories and early-life neighborhood determinants remain poorly understood. Objective To examine whether there are associations between the neighborhood exposome at birth and EAA trajectories from early childhood through adolescence. Design, Setting, and Participants This longitudinal cohort study used data from Project Viva, a prebirth cohort that enrolled pregnant women in eastern Massachusetts from April 22, 1999, to July 31, 2002. Participants included 570 children with available peripheral blood DNA methylation data, complete neighborhood characteristics, and complete covariates. Data were analyzed from August 19, 2024, to August 21, 2026. Exposures Neighborhood exposome profiles at birth derived from 22 census tract–level characteristics across 4 domains (area deprivation, social fragmentation, population density, and environmental quality) using self-organizing maps. Main Outcomes and Measures EAA was calculated at 3, 8, and 13 years of age using the Horvath, Skin & Blood, and Wu epigenetic clocks. Trajectories were identified using latent class linear mixed models. Associations between neighborhood profiles and EAA trajectories were estimated using multinomial mixed models. Results Among 570 children (mean [SD] age at early childhood, 3.2 [0.4] years; 305 [53.5%] male), 3 EAA trajectory groups (stable, increasing, and decreasing for the Horvath and Skin & Blood clocks or low-baseline for the Wu clock) and 3 neighborhood profiles were identified. Compared with profile 1 (suburban, lowest adverse exposures [n = 278]), children born into profile 2 (urban, high residential instability and single-person households, and highway proximity [n = 168]) had greater odds of increasing EAA for the Wu clock (adjusted odds ratio, 1.67 [95% CI, 1.03-2.69]). Profile 3 (urban, high socioeconomic deprivation and pollution [n = 124]) showed no associations. Conclusions and Relevance In this longitudinal cohort study, birth into neighborhoods characterized by high residential instability and single-person households and highway proximity was associated with increasing Wu EAA trajectories across childhood. These findings suggest that early-life neighborhood conditions, encompassing both social and physical environmental factors, may represent targets for interventions aimed at reducing long-term disease risk. Further research is needed to clarify the implications of these findings for later health and prevention.

items.title: Fairness, agency, and algorithms: AI in Greek higher education linguistics
items.abstract: The swift expansion of AI in higher education has not been matched by a clear understanding of its effective application within linguistics education, especially in Greece, where the technology is viewed as a means to advance social and economic development. This research undertakes a thorough exploration of AI integration in Greek higher education linguistics through a utilitarian perspective, centering on the experiences of instructors. It aims to shed light on the advantages and obstacles linked to AI adoption, with particular emphasis on issues of fairness and student agency. The study’s goals include examining educators’ experiences with AI tools, identifying perceived contributions to fairness and student empowerment, and uncovering the limitations and difficulties involved. Drawing on semi -structured interviews and focus group discussions, insights will be collected from fourteen technologically adept language educators. The ensuing thematic and discourse analyses will engage with these issues and highlight strategies to strengthen teaching practices. Ultimately, the study seeks to inform policymakers, practitioners, and stakeholders of the profound influence of AI on education, while enriching the academic conversation on this subject and proposing actionable ways to enhance teaching and learning in Greek higher education linguistics.

items.title: Believability and conditional inference in mathematics undergraduates: a replication and extension
items.abstract: Abstract This paper replicates a study in which Alcock et al. (2026) found that content influences first-year mathematics undergraduates’ evaluations of conditional inferences . Alcock et al. reported that these students responded more normatively to inferences from highly believable (true) mathematical conditionals than from conditionals with other mathematical, everyday, or abstract content. We replicated this work with a larger and more diverse sample, finding a similar overall believability effect and evidence that some individual differences in the original study were due to recent teaching. We extended the work by relating conditional inference responses to prior performance in mathematics and to students’ cultural backgrounds, finding that better mastery of more mathematics is associated with better rejection of invalid affirmation of the consequent inferences and that students with English as a first language responded more normatively than students with Chinese as a first language, especially for modus tollens inferences. We consider limitations to generalisability, and argue for the importance of replicating effects of all kinds, not only those linked to teaching interventions.

items.title: Predominance of viral core functions over auxiliary metabolism among carbohydrate-active enzymes annotated in the global soil virosphere
items.abstract: Soil viruses are increasingly recognized as components of microbial communities with the potential to alter ecosystem functioning, yet the frequency and functional distribution of virus-encoded metabolic genes in soils remain poorly understood. Here, the Global Soil Virus Atlas gene catalog, comprising 1,432,147 viral genes from 1,223 samples across 12 ecosystem types, was searched against KEGG, Pfam, and CAZy for functions related to carbon cycling, nitrogen cycling, and antimicrobial resistance. Annotations associated with host entry or cell-wall lysis were separated from putative auxiliary metabolic functions. Of 5,020 initial gene-level functional annotations across the three categories, 3,322 (66.2%) were classified as peptidoglycanases. Their exclusion left 1,698 genes (0.14% of the gene catalog restricted to contigs ≥10 kb), and carbon-cycling functions represented 96.7% of the enzyme-resolved annotations. Chitinase-associated genes formed the largest carbon category, but 78.0% belonged to GH19, a family containing both chitinases and phage endolysins. Among GH19 genes on contigs encoding detectable holins or spanins, 84.2% occurred within three genes of these lysis components, a distribution comparable to that of canonical phage lysozymes. Across six matched metagenomic studies, estimated viral contributions to the targeted functions ranged from 0.00% to 8.45% (mean: 2.27%). Two of the three estimates exceeding 2% were GH19-associated chitinase estimates from rhizosphere soils and were therefore treated as upper estimates. Thus, the putative soil viral metabolic inventory was sparse and concentrated in carbon-degradation functions, whereas much of the initial carbohydrate-active enzyme signal reflected core viral lysis functions rather than auxiliary metabolism. IMPORTANCE: Soil microorganisms drive decomposition and nutrient cycling, and the viruses that infect them may alter these processes by carrying genes that affect host metabolism. However, genes annotated as carbohydrate-degradation enzymes may instead help viruses enter cells or break host cell walls when new virus particles are released. In a worldwide catalog of soil viruses, approximately two-thirds of the initial functional assignments represented these infection or release activities. After their removal, putative viral auxiliary metabolic genes were uncommon and concentrated mainly in carbon degradation. Genes potentially involved in chitin degradation were most frequent, but many occurred near viral genes used to break host cells; their estimated contribution should therefore be viewed as an upper limit. Distinguishing core viral functions from host metabolic modification is essential to avoid overestimating viral contributions to soil processes and to identify the strongest candidates for experimental testing.

items.title: Novel insights into the specialized metabolism of the extremophile black yeast Hortaea werneckii and its modulation, unlocking its potential for compound discovery
items.abstract: Hortaea werneckii is a halotolerant yeast, found in various habitats and which specialized metabolism remains largely unexplored. Moreover, its chemical response to high salinities has not been thoroughly investigated. To address this gap, a large-scale metabolomic study based on HPLC-HRMS/MS was conducted on 64 strains, collected from different habitats worldwide, and cultivated both on saline and non-saline media. The culture media salinity significantly modulated the strains metabolomes, suggesting the yeast exhibits a specific chemical response to high salt concentrations, potentially linked to halotolerance mechanisms. Additionally, the metabolomes were influenced by the ecological origin of the strains, with opportunistic pathogenic isolates producing distinct metabolites. Molecular networking revealed that H. werneckii synthesizes various chemical classes, including potential cytotoxic compounds, making this yeast a potentially interesting source of bioactive compounds. Hortein was detected as dominant and ubiquitous, emerging as a potential chemical marker for the species. This study highlights several compounds of interest, related to the chemical ecology and pathogenicity of H. werneckii . As most of them remain unidentified, future research should prioritize their isolation and identification, to improve our understanding of this extremophile organism and harness its potential in natural product discovery.

items.title: TaxoAttention: fusing semantic and hierarchical taxonomic models with attention-guided augmentation for mosquito identification
items.abstract: Accurate species-level identification of mosquitoes remains a critical bottleneck in vector surveillance, particularly when dealing with morphologically similar taxa or field-damaged specimens. In this study, we introduce a deep learning framework that integrates hierarchical taxonomic structure with attention-based feature learning to improve classification performance under real-world imaging conditions. The model combines a semi-fixed, taxonomy-informed feature stream with a fully trainable semantic stream. It further employs dynamic attention-guided augmentation, designed to focus training on diagnostically relevant regions, such as wing venation, tarsal banding, and palpal morphology, and to reduce the influence of the background. Evaluated on a standardized, predominantly field-collected dataset (MosquitoTax-200) representing 32 species across Aedes, Anopheles, and Culex with 200 images per species, our approach achieves 84.6% macro-averaged precision (mAP), 5.0 percentage points above an Xception baseline trained with standard cross-entropy loss and used as a control. This work highlights the potential of biologically grounded AI tools to scale species identification in vector control operations and to support training and quality assurance in entomological diagnostics.

items.title: Lynx reintroduction from a bottlenecked source exposes a lethal genetic defect
items.abstract: Abstract Conservation programmes worldwide use reintroductions and translocations as management tools to support endangered species. However, such efforts often result in small and isolated populations that face genetic challenges associated with reduced gene flow and inbreeding. Inbreeding depression is a well-known risk in such programmes, as increased homozygosity can expose recessive deleterious alleles, compromise fitness and threaten population persistence. Yet, no causal variant for a lethal disease has previously been identified in a wild population. Here we combine long-term health and population data with genomic analyses to identify a recessive loss-of-function allele causing lethal organ mineralization in young Eurasian lynx ( Lynx lynx ) from a reintroduced population in Switzerland. Spatio-temporal analyses revealed that the allele was introduced from one of the source populations and increased in frequency through founder effects and inbreeding. Our findings establish the first direct link between reintroduction history and a lethal genetic disease in the wild, illustrating how population genetic processes interact to shape the fate of a recessive deleterious allele and emphasize the vulnerability of small, isolated populations following reintroduction.

items.title: Declining environmental predictability erodes reproduction in a tropical seabird
items.abstract: Seasonal breeders often depend on predictable resource pulses, yet climate change may alter reliability without shifting average timing. Here, using satellite chlorophyll records and two decades of individual breeding data for a tropical seabird, we show that weakened breeding synchrony and declining and less consistent reproductive success were associated with increasingly variable bloom timing without a consistent directional shift. Focusing on average timing alone could mean that climate impacts on species are overlooked. The authors show that, for a tropical seabird model species, winter–spring phytoplankton blooms kept a stable mean timing but became more variable between years. Breeding synchrony weakened and reproductive success declined and became less consistent over the same two decades.

items.title: Species-rich and genomically diverse: Comparative genomics reveals how fusions, fissions, and sex chromosomes have shaped beetle evolution
items.abstract: Chromosome evolution in animals reflects a balance between long-term conservation of ancestral linkage groups and lineage-specific chromosomal rearrangements that reshape genome structure. Beetles (Coleoptera), the most species-rich animal order, exhibit extensive diversity in karyotype, yet the extent to which their chromosomes retain deep ancestral structure remains unclear. Here, we analyzed 190 chromosome-level genome assemblies spanning 39 families and 16 superfamilies to characterize genome diversity, evaluate the conservation of ancestral linkage groups (Stevens elements), identify neo-sex chromosomes, and explore the role of repetitive elements in driving karyotypic change. Our results reveal that beetle genomes are highly diverse, varying substantially in genome size, chromosome number, GC content, and transposable element (TE) composition. Despite this diversity, Stevens elements appear conserved across much of the radiation, with several superfamilies maintaining strong chromosome synteny over more than 200 million years of evolution. In contrast, some clades, and specifically the leaf beetles (Chrysomelidae), have undergone extensive genomic changes including numerous chromosomal fusions and fissions and changes in genome size. Using synteny-based approaches across beetles, we identified 37 species (approximately 19.5%) having patterns consistent with neo-sex chromosomes, a substantially higher frequency than previous estimates. These putative X-autosome fusions vary in complexity and age, often clustered within lineages that are prone to chromosomal instability. The ancestral X chromosome appears conserved for over 300 million years, with stable gene content and reduced TEs relative to autosomes. These findings help establish beetles as a promising system to uncover the evolutionary forces that maintain and disrupt ancestral linkage groups and drive the formation of neo-sex chromosomes.

items.title: Recent thermohaline shifts in the Adriatic Sea and their potential consequences
items.abstract: The Adriatic Sea has warmed and salinified rapidly over the past two decades, and the changes are not uniform with depth. We combine 33 664 quality-controlled shipboard and Argo temperature and salinity casts from 1950–2025 into two climatologies, test the individual casts for regime shifts, and use the Argo profiles from the Southern Adriatic Pit to quantify the vertical structure of the changes. Between the 1950–1999 and 2000–2025 climatologies the southern Adriatic salinified at every depth and season, by 0.11–0.53, and warmed by up to 1.6 °C everywhere except at the uppermost levels in summer and autumn, where the sampling differs between the two periods. Amplification relative to the rest of the Mediterranean is strongly depth-dependent: below 700 m the southern Adriatic warms at 6.2 times the median rate of the other Mediterranean sub-basins, whereas above 200 m its warming is not amplified. The occurrence of near-surface salinity maxima (“surface saline lakes”) rises abruptly after 2014, in both ship and float records, from a few per cent of warm-season casts to about 40 %; this regime shift is only provable if vertical resolution and platform are accounted for. The intermediate salinity maximum has lost its dominant band: the detected maxima no longer cluster in one depth interval. Where two maxima coexist they have moved apart and diverged in density, so they are not one migrating core. Over 2014–2024 the steric contribution in the Southern Adriatic Pit is negative, dominated by halosteric contraction, so that local sea level rise must be mass-driven. Salt fingering has intensified below the classical intermediate core, allowing salt transport towards deeper layers. Three consequences follow, set out here as hypotheses. First, deep ventilation may persist under milder winters, because water that is already saline needs less cooling to sink, but each ventilation event may then deliver less oxygen, because the water that sinks is warmer. Second, exchange of oxygen, nutrients and carbon between the surface and intermediate layers may be either suppressed or enhanced beneath more frequent surface saline lakes, depending on whether stratification or double diffusion prevails. Third, Adriatic ecosystems, in which warming-linked mortality and species redistribution are already documented, face a basin changing faster at depth than at the surface. Testing these hypotheses requires sustained high-resolution observations.

items.title: Edukasi Konservasi Mangrove dan Pemanfaatan Potensi Lokal sebagai Upaya Pemberdayaan Masyarakat Pesisir Desa Sungsang, Banyuasin
items.abstract: Mangrove ecosystems play a vital role in maintaining coastal ecological balance and providing social and economic benefits. Sungsang Village, Banyuasin II District, Banyuasin Regency, has mangrove resources that can be developed through conservation and sustainable utilization. These efforts require greater community knowledge and awareness of mangrove preservation. This community service program aimed to improve community knowledge, awareness, and skills in mangrove conservation and value-added product development. Activities included education on mangrove functions and benefits, demonstrations and practical training in local material processing, packaging and marketing training, and community mentoring. Evaluation involved pre-tests and post-tests to assess knowledge improvement. The results showed increased understanding of mangrove ecological functions, conservation, and sustainable resource utilization. Participants also improved their skills in product development and gained knowledge of packaging and marketing strategies. Integrating conservation education with local product is expected to strengthen community participation in mangrove preservation and promote sustainable resource utilization while integrating ecological, social, and economic dimensions.

items.title: Physicochemical gradients shape zooplankton and bivalve communities along the Sô River–Lake Nokoué continuum in Benin: implications for environmental health monitoring
items.abstract: Tropical river-lagoon systems are dynamic environments in which physicochemical variability can influence aquatic community structure. This study characterized the composition, taxonomic richness, occurrence, and spatiotemporal variation of zooplankton and bivalve communities along the Sô River-Lake Nokoué continuum in southern Benin. Monthly biological sampling was conducted at 11 stations from August 2024 to March 2025, including four stations in the Sô River (S1-S4) and seven in Lake Nokoué (S5-S11). A total of 24 zooplankton families and nine bivalve families were recorded. Eurotatoria dominated the zooplankton community, accounting for 56% of total relative density and exhibiting the highest taxonomic richness. Bivalves showed lower family-level richness but were recorded across the study area. Principal component analysis revealed a marked physicochemical gradient associated primarily with salinity, electrical conductivity, and total dissolved solids, distinguishing riverine from lagoonal conditions. Redundancy analysis identified associations between zooplankton community composition and dissolved oxygen and salinity, whereas bivalve community composition was associated with pH and temperature. These results highlight the environmental heterogeneity of the Sô River-Lake Nokoué continuum and provide an ecological baseline for future aquatic monitoring. Because pathogens, human exposure, and disease outcomes were not assessed, the findings do not establish a direct relationship between the observed community patterns and waterborne disease risk.

items.title: A comprehensive benchmark and dual-encoder baseline for terraced field extraction in complex mountainous regions
items.abstract: Terraces play a vital role in mitigating runoff and intercepting sediment. Large-scale, high-precision extraction of terraces from remote sensing imagery is essential for environmental monitoring and soil erosion control. However, accurate spatial identification of terraces still presents significant challenges, including scale variability, shadow interference, and complex geometric configurations. To address these issues, we propose DETS-Net, a dual-encoder network that integrates CNN and Transformer architectures. The network employs ResNet-34 as the CNN encoder for local feature detail extraction, utilizes a Transformer encoder to strengthen long-range dependency modeling, and incorporates an adaptive feature fusion (AFF) module for the dynamic integration of the two feature branches. We develop the THDIR dataset, which covers four typical terrain types, namely, plateau mountains, hills, and mountain-basin transition zones, and contains 9,336 standardized 256 × 256 pixel images. We conduct systematic comparisons with eight representative deep learning models. Experimental results demonstrate that DETS-Net achieves an overall accuracy (OA) of 89.91%, a mean intersection over union (MIoU) of 81.28%, and an F1-score of 87.99% on the THDIR dataset, outperforming current mainstream methods in segmentation precision. We apply the optimized model to 2023 remote sensing imagery of Luotian County in the Dabie Mountains, Hubei Province, and generate a high-precision county-level terrace spatial distribution map. This framework supports the assessment of soil and water conservation benefits through area statistics, slope distribution data, and high-precision boundary extraction and provides a reproducible technical pathway for automated terrace mapping using high-resolution remote sensing imagery in complex mountainous regions.

items.title: Molecular, chemical, and conventional fisheries methods reveal early invasion dynamics and range expansion of an invasive fish in a large North American estuary
items.abstract: Abstract Round Goby (Neogobius melanostomus) have quickly expanded throughout the Hudson River Estuary since their initial detection in 2021, yet patterns of establishment, dispersal, and population status remain poorly understood. We studied Round Goby distribution, relative abundance, establishment, and natal origins in the Hudson River Estuary from 2022–2024 using environmental DNA (eDNA), beach seining, and otolith microchemistry. These approaches provided complementary information on spatial expansion and connectivity between the Hudson and Mohawk rivers, where hydrological and anthropogenic connections can influence aquatic organism movement across river networks. Concurrent eDNA sampling and seining showed agreement in detections, supporting eDNA as a complementary monitoring tool in large tidal rivers. Throughout the study period eDNA detections increased spatially and temporally in the lower Hudson River Estuary, with most positive detections in 2024 occurring across approximately 70 km of brackish habitat, indicating downstream range expansion and likely establishment in brackish waters. Despite continued range expansion, cumulative captures during 2022–2024 were lower than in 2021, suggesting the population has not undergone rapid exponential growth. Otolith microchemistry revealed overlapping but distinguishable natal signatures between Hudson and Mohawk River fish, demonstrating demographic connectivity and indicating that the expanding Hudson River Estuary population is supported by both local recruitment and downstream immigrants from the Mohawk River. Together, these results identify the Hudson–Mohawk connection, facilitated in part by the NYS Canal system, as an important invasion pathway and highlight the value of combining detection and provenance approaches to resolve invasion dynamics across connected freshwater and estuarine habitats.

items.title: Public Spatial Perceptions from PPGIS Studies Using Qualitative Content Analysis in Existing, Candidate, and Outside Protected Areas
items.abstract: Pre-designation stakeholder spatial perceptions remain underexamined despite their relevance to protected area (PA) designation. Using Public Participation Geographical Information System (PPGIS), by convenience sampling, 97 participants (69 locals and 25 visitors) mapped 377 open-ended values and concerns statements across existing PA (EPA), candidate PA (CPA), and outside CPA (OCPA) in eastern Hokkaido, Japan. Inductive coding yielded 1042 code instances organized into 122 codes, 17 sub-themes, and four themes. Gi* hotspot values (n = 719) and concerns (n = 323) were compared to identify value–concern zones, and a participant-based location quotient identified distinctive themes. Values (69%) concentrated on ecology, landscape, recreation, and conservation; concerns concentrated on energy infrastructure, ecological loss, human–wildlife conflicts, and facilities. Potential conflict zones (overlapping value and concern hotspots) were concentrated on the Notsuke Peninsula and Shunkunitai within the EPA, combining shared values with habitat loss. Concern-dominant zones, marked by energy infrastructure and habitat loss, lay mainly outside the EPA. Locals and visitors shared values but differed in concerns; only locals raised human–wildlife conflicts. Codes related to all six elements of the Intergovernmental Science-Policy Platform on Biodiversity and Ecosystem Services conceptual framework, though abiotic elements fell outside its contribution categories. Pre-designation PPGIS provides spatial evidence for boundary delimitation, zoning, and identifying potential conflicts.

items.title: Climate Change and Governance Gap in South Asia
items.abstract: Abstract Climate Change is one of the most concerning non-traditional security threats which is affecting the world at an unprecedented pace. South Asia is the most vulnerable region in terms of climate change with countries across the region are facing challenges like sea-level rise, biodiversity loss, uneven patterns of rainfall, global warming, climate-induced migration, food scarcity, extreme floods and much more which are further responsible for the critical nexus of food and water security. This research paper provides critical analysis on how these problems creates a governance gap in South Asia and requires the need for a comprehensive regional governance framework which is a major gap in this research. This paper also analyzes the various protocols, declarations and reports related to Climate Change which are not responsive towards the specific vulnerabilities of South Asia. Ineffectiveness of South Asian Association for Regional Cooperation i.e. SAARC- major regional grouping of South Asia- particularly due to political disputes and conflicts between countries is also the major factor in governance gap. This paper adopts Qualitative research methodology which includes the analysis of both primary and secondary sources. Finally, this paper proposes the need for a Polycentric governance framework for the effective coordination and cooperation in South Asia.

items.title: The Ecology of Open Science Landscapes
items.abstract: This repository contains the materials from the Unconference 5 of the 2026 SORTEE Conference, held on October 13-14, 2026. This unconference discussed how and if we can use ecological diversity metrics to help us understand states of open scholarship culture. We discussed whether components of ecological diversity metrics (richness, evenness, turnover) can inspire ways to describe openness in research. Prompts included: what are meaningful dimensions of open science? Can they be measured or compared without oversimplification? Where does the ecological analogy break down? The goal was to map candidate metrics, identify shared definitions, and outline potential empirical or conceptual follow-up work. items.title: Perceived priorities, experiences and provision gaps in urban green spaces: evidence from university students in Pécs, Hungary
items.abstract: Urban green spaces play a vital role in enhancing the liveability and sustainability of cities, particularly for university students. This study applies a socially differentiated importance–experience framework to the evaluation of urban green spaces by university students in Pécs, Hungary. The sample was not representative of the target population, primarily because foreign students were overrepresented. Post-stratification weights were therefore applied to align the sample with the composition of the student population at the University of Pécs. Using these weights, Multiple Factor Analysis identified three dimensions for both the importance and experience measures, as well as six dimensions representing the gap between the corresponding importance and experience ratings. Each dimension was subsequently modelled using post-stratification-weighted linear regression. The explanatory variables describing patterns of green-space use were preselected using the Boruta feature-selection algorithm. The findings reveal substantial importance–experience gaps for several basic attributes, including public toilets, accessibility for people with reduced mobility, benches, cleanliness, waste bins and vegetation. Associations with citizenship and patterns of green space use were dimension-specific rather than indicating consistently less experiences among respondents with foreign citizenship. The results suggest that the students’ evaluations of urban green spaces reflect a multidimensional interplay of practical, environmental, and social attributes. Future research should examine comparative settings and incorporate qualitative methods to explore variation among more precisely defined user groups and across urban contexts. Given the non-representative sample and the aggregation of respondents with foreign citizenship into a single group, the results should be interpreted cautiously, particularly regarding gender-specific patterns and heterogeneity within the foreign-citizenship group.

items.title: Population Diversity of Tecomella undulata across South Asia: Diversity identification Markers, Possible Causes, and Potential for Conservation
items.abstract: Tecomella undulata (Sm.) Seem., the sole species of its genus in the family Bignoniaceae, is a keystone tree of the arid and semi-arid tracts of South Asia, valued equally for its ecological role in desert stabilization and its long history of use in traditional medicine. Habitat fragmentation, unsustainable timber and herbal extraction, weak natural regeneration, grazing pressure and a warming/drying climate has together pushed the species toward endangered status in the Thar Desert of Sindh, Pakistan. Since there is a lack of such study which integrate anatomical, phytochemical, and molecular analysis as diversity identification markers, this review explores and summarizes the available information on population diversity identification using molecular (chiefly ISSR and RAPD), anatomical structure and the phytochemical profile as markers to understand variations in T. undulata populations. Published marker-based work shows substantial genetic diversity retained within populations despite geographic isolation, while anatomical and phytochemical surveys, though comparatively sparse, point to xeromorphic adaptations and stress induced shifts in secondary metabolism that likely track local aridity and soil conditions. We argue that combining molecular, anatomical and phytochemical data is not simply additive but necessary though other approaches like common garden experiment may also be needed to fully distinguish genetically fixed divergence from environmentally plastic response, and thereby to identify populations that are both genetically distinct and ecologically or medicinally valuable. This information would give conservation planners, across South Asian range, an evidence based strategy for prioritizing germplasm collection, in situ protection, and restoration efforts before further population decline erodes the genetic resources

items.title: Contrasting local responses but similar regional turnover in phytoplankton and rotifer assemblages in saline–alkaline wetlands, Northeast China
items.abstract: Freshwater salinization and alkalization are emerging threats to global biodiversity, particularly in arid and semi-arid regions. Although ecological impacts of freshwater salinization and alkalization on local biodiversity have received increasing attention, it remains unclear how diversity patterns of organisms in different trophic levels respond at a regional scale. Here, we investigated rotifer and phytoplankton assemblages across 61 wetlands spanning a broad saline–alkaline gradient in the Songnen Plain, Northeast China. We quantified local (alpha) diversity, partitioned beta diversity into turnover and nestedness components, and evaluated how saline–alkaline conditions are associated with assemblage and diversity. Our results showed salinization in wetlands was often associated with high pH, nutrient enrichment, shallower surface water and lower macrophyte coverage, association with a significant decline in local phytoplankton diversity but no significant effect on rotifer diversity. Rotifer assemblages were mainly shaped by water depth, and macrophyte coverage, while phytoplankton assemblages were more influenced by TOC, NH 4 + -N, water temperature, and macrophyte coverage. Phytoplankton diversity in local wetlands was negatively associated with pH and inorganic nitrogen concentrations, whereas rotifer diversity was associated with water temperature, water depth, and nutrient concentrations. Despite these contrasting local responses, both groups exhibited high spatial compositional dissimilarity among investigated wetlands. Mean total beta diversity reached 0.89 for rotifers and 0.91 for phytoplankton, with turnover accounting for 74.16% and 67.03% of the assemblage dissimilarities, respectively. These findings reveal the profound impacts of freshwater salinization and alkalization on wetland organisms. We highlight the importance of integrating both alpha and beta diversity dimensions in monitoring biodiversity response to these emerging threats in freshwater ecosystems under global environmental change.

items.title: Comparative assessment of bacterial diversity in small water bodies of the Eastern Pamir mountains using amplicon-based and metagenomic approaches
items.abstract: Microbial diversity in remote extreme environments remains poorly understood. We investigated sediment microbial communities in small water bodies of the Eastern Pamir cold desert using V3–V4 16S rRNA gene amplicon sequencing and metagenomics, to assess taxonomic and functional diversity. Amplicon data showed high Pseudomonadota abundance and taxa overlooked in the 2019 analysis, including Vampirovibrionaceae. Reanalysis of the amplicon data increased taxonomic assessment from 54% to 93% without changes in the number of unique sequences. Comparison of amplicon and metagenome-derived 16S profiles revealed limited overlap: only 15% of metagenomic V3–V4 sequences were detected in amplicons. Fourteen of 37 phyla were exclusive to ASVs, whereas three (of 20) to MAGs. Metagenomics recovered 86 MAGs spanning 26 classes, predominantly from Bacteroidota. Sulfur oxidation and sulfate reduction pathways occurred mainly in Pseudomonadota. Phototrophic potential was identified in 25 MAGs, largely Bacteroidota and established phototrophic lineages; most possessed complete nitrogen-fixation pathways. Eight genera detected with all methods belonged to halophilic or halotolerant lineages. These findings highlight salinity as an important driver of bacterial community composition in Eastern Pamir benthic communities and identify differences between methods. Integrating amplicon sequencing and metagenomics provides complementary insights into microbial diversity and metabolic potential in remote extreme environments.

items.title: Phylogenetic conservatism of dietary niches in Neotropical leaf-nosed bats
items.abstract: Abstract The tendency of lineages to retain their ancestral niche over time is known as phylogenetic niche conservatism (PNC ). Studies considering Eltonian niche characteristics (i.e. biotic interactions) have increased in recent years. However, the question of whether Eltonian niches are conserved remains largely unexplored. The aim of this study was to test for PNC in the Eltonian niches, namely the dietary niches of phyllostomid bats. More specifically, we look for PNC patterns at three phylogenetic scales: family, subfamily and species levels; and in two features of Eltonian niche: dietary breadth and position. We used phylogenetic comparative methods to test the PNC at family and subfamily levels; for species level, we used an approach that compares the dietary niche similarities between species pairs. Our results are largely consistent with PNC of dietary niches, but different patterns emerged when we assessed dietary niche position or breadth, and at different phylogenetic scales. At family level, we found evidence for PNC in dietary niche breadth, but not for dietary niche position. Conversely, at subfamily level we found evidence for PNC in dietary niche position but not for dietary niche breadth. At species level, we found that dietary niches of sister species resemble each other more than non-sister species do, providing evidence of PNC. Our findings highlight the importance of considering that Eltonian niche do not evolve in the same way over time, nor among subclades. Therefore, not assuming but testing PNC is fundamental for understanding the processes underlying the evolution of dietary niches.
