items.title: Enhancing diagnostic and intervention-related skills with adaptive feedback: Study protocol for a simulation-based learning study on symptoms of learning and behavioural difficulties.
items.abstract: This project uses simulated digital case scenarios to analyse diagnostic and intervention-related skills of teacher, school psychology, and medical students concerning primary school children's difficulties in mathematics and their hyperactive, inattentive and impulsive behaviours. Here, the conditions for an effective use of macro- and micro-adaptive feedback - powered by natural language processing (NLP) methods - compared to static feedback will be the focus. The aim is to identify effective types of feedback for students who differ in their prior diagnostic and intervention-related knowledge. We compare three groups of university students (medical students, school psychology students, and pre-service teachers) with varying professional specialisations and corresponding knowledge bases as learning prerequisites using simulated digital case scenarios. In validation study 1a, we analyse students' case processing and validate our measures for students' prior knowledge. Furthermore, the results are used for informing the design and refinement of micro- and macro-adaptive feedback. Validation study 1b investigates static, macro-adaptive, and micro-adaptive feedback. In Study 2, by using "think aloud"-methods and trace data, we investigate to what extent learners benefit differently from the processing of digital case scenarios in the absence of any feedback and what kind of cognitive, metacognitive, motivational learning processes occur. In study 3, we investigate how the form of feedback in the digital case scenarios affects students' acquisition of new diagnostic and intervention-related skills and how students process the different forms of feedback. Finally, Study 4 examines the extent to which different forms of feedback are helpful for students with low vs. high prior knowledge. This project will analyse which benefits feedback with different degrees of adaptivity can provide for learning diagnostic reasoning and the planning of related interventions, especially when considering potential interaction effects with learners' varying prior professional as well as diagnostic and intervention-related knowledge and diagnostic processing.

items.title: People know who to ask for favors despite underestimating compliance.
items.abstract: Whether and how people approach social interactions hinges on how they expect others to respond. Extensive social psychology research suggests that people are inaccurate interpersonal perceivers, overestimating negative responses (e.g., discomfort) and underestimating positive responses (e.g., appreciation) across a variety of social situations. However, this conclusion is based almost exclusively on mean-level bias analyses that obscure the dyadic nature of interpersonal judgment and rely on a narrow conceptualization of interpersonal accuracy. Leveraging research on favor-asking and anticipated compliance as an exemplar, we demonstrate that interpersonal accuracy takes multiple theoretically distinct forms, and that the prevailing conclusion that people misunderstand their influence over others-because they tend to underestimate compliance-is likely overgeneralized. Across four studies (13,196 directed dyadic ratings), we show that people accurately differentiate between who will comply with their favor requests (dyadic meta-accuracy) despite the average tendency to underestimate compliance (mean-level bias). This pattern emerged for specific and general favor requests, among well- and newly-acquainted individuals, and beyond what could be expected due to self-projection. Through this dyadic lens, people are highly adept judges of their influence over others, as they are able to target their requests toward individuals who are uniquely likely to acquiesce to them-and can avoid wasting time on those who are not. Thus, our research refines existing implications for how people approach asking for favors. More broadly, by aligning theory, measurement, and level of analysis, our studies elucidate the need for greater theoretical precision and empirical breadth in interpersonal accuracy research.

items.title: Mutations in antimicrobial peptides differently affect sleep and plasticity.
items.abstract: Molecules implicated in host defense can, independent of their roles as immune mediators, regulate sleep. In mammals, cytokines such as Tumor Necrosis Factor α (TNF α) and Interleukin1β (IL1β) promote sleep. In Drosophila, infection stimulates the systemic release of a battery of antimicrobial peptides (AMPs). These fly immune effectors have been understudied as sleep modulators. We obtained mutants in different AMPs and characterized their functions in sleep and plasticity. AMP mutants slept less with a longer sleep latency, and lowered arousal thresholds. Group C mutant flies, doubly mutant for the anti-fungal peptides Metchnikowin (Mtk) and Drosomycin (Drs), showed the greatest impairments. These Group C mutants also showed an exaggerated sleep rebound, sleep rebound was unaltered in other mutants. While many classes of AMPs showed sleep deficits, different sets of AMP mutants exhibited specific disruptions in socialization and rocking induced sleep. To determine whether sleep amount and sleep functions were dissociable, we evaluated memory and quantified synapse abundance. Group C mutants uniquely exhibited normal learning and memory, and lower synapse abundance, despite sleeping the least. Group C mutants are thus able to carry out some sleep functions without sleeping much. Glial knockdown of Metchnikowin and Drosomycin mimicked the sleep phenotypes of the null mutants, these genes thus act from glia. While Group C mutants retained normal cognitive function, other AMP mutants showed impairments in sleep and memory. Sleep and memory defects in these AMP mutants were reversible - enhancing sleep of Bomanin mutants pharmacologically or behaviorally improved learning and memory. Together, these data suggest that AMPs are potent sleep modulators and that different classes of AMPs differently affect sleep and sleep dependent outcomes.

items.title: The missing Nobels: Mapping the landscape of prestigious scientific prizes.
items.abstract: Prestigious recognition prizes, like the Nobel Prizes, can shape scientists' career decisions and how science is seen. Yet the landscape of such prizes is not well understood. We screen roughly 2,700 international scientific prizes and rank the 99 most prestigious using a novel prestige index. Recognition is unevenly distributed across fields: physics, life sciences, and mathematics are heavily recognized relative to field size, while computer science, engineering, psychology, and the social sciences are under-served. Only three of the 99 prizes target early-career scientists.

items.title: Slow- Versus Normal-Paced Breathing During an Emotional Task: Limited Evidence for Greater RMSSD Change or State-Affect Benefits.
items.abstract: Slow-paced breathing (SPB) is widely promoted for stress regulation, but its incremental benefit over an active paced-breathing control across age groups remains uncertain. We compared SPB (prescribed 6 cycles/min) with normal-paced breathing (NPB; prescribed 12 cycles/min) during an emotional picture-rating task in 82 younger and 84 older adults. Outcomes were baseline-to-task changes in heart rate variability indexed by the root mean square of successive differences (RMSSD) and mean heart rate, and pre-post changes in state anxiety and affect. The primary RMSSD analysis included 162 participants after the ± 3 median absolute deviation exclusion rule. RMSSD was higher during the task than during the preceding baseline in both protocols. The primary Time × Breathing condition interaction did not establish a larger change under SPB, β = 0.090, 95% CI [- 0.022, 0.203], p = .116, and was sensitive to outlier handling. A secondary task-period contrast showed higher RMSSD under SPB than NPB (ratio = 1.23, p = .009). Mean heart rate decreased without a reliable protocol difference in change. State anxiety and affect showed no robust advantage of SPB. Mixed-model sensitivity analyses likewise did not establish overall protocol differences in change. No reliable age moderation was detected. Respiration was not recorded directly, and adherence to 6 cycles/min or comparable respiratory exposure across ages could not be verified. Overall, the primary analyses provided no reliable evidence of a greater RMSSD change or of an acute state-affect benefit under SPB in this task context; they neither establish equivalence nor isolate the effect of breathing frequency.

items.title: Cluster analysis based on alexithymia in young women: exploring addictions, psychological symptoms and relational vulnerability factors.
items.abstract: Alexithymia has been identified as a transdiagnostic risk factor for addictive behaviours. It has also been widely linked to various psychological risk factors related to addictions. (I) to explore clusters of young women based on alexithymia and; (II) to examine differences between clusters in terms of addictive behaviours (gambling, alcohol, drugs and compulsive buying) and associated psychological symptoms. The sample consisted of 239 women aged between 18 and 35 years. Three clusters were found based on the three subscales of alexithymia (TAS-20). Cluster 1 was characterised by lower scores on alexithymia and low scores on all variables. Cluster 2 was characterised by intermediate levels of identifying and describing emotions and high scores on hopelessness. Cluster 3 showed the highest levels of alexithymia, addictive behaviours and all other study variables except for hopelessness. Young women with addiction risk or problems may benefit from different preventive and therapeutic approaches depending on the alexithymia subscales.

items.title: Biomimetic Optically Encoded Hydrogel Fiber Enables Simultaneous Olfactory-Mechanosensory Perception for Robotic Plume Tracing.
items.abstract: Dynamic odor plumes encode gas identity and airflow transport as coupled spatiotemporal cues, requiring olfactory-mechanosensory fusion perception for intelligent robotic navigation in vision-denied environments. Yet current olfactory-mechanosensory systems typically rely on separated sensing units, limiting co-localized mechanochemical discrimination. Here, we report a biomimetic flexible optical fiber (BFOF) comprising a coaxial hydrogel fiber with distributed, self-assembled odor-sensitive metal-organic frameworks (MOFs) on its exterior, enabling simultaneous decoding of wind vectors and olfactory cues within a single compact optical architecture. Inspired by the spatially integrated mechanoreceptors and chemoreceptors in ant antennae, the BFOF employs conformal MOF-hydrogel interfaces to enhance evanescent-field coupling without compromising receptor activity or waveguiding, partitioning multidimensional airflow attenuation and odor fluorescence into separable optical channels for low-crosstalk olfactory-mechanosensory fusion. Therefore, it achieves high sensitivity, fine directional selectivity, and fast temporal response across a wide range of airflow conditions. It identifies 16 individual gases, 96 mixtures, and the physiological states (unripe, ripe, overripe, and rotten) of 8 fruits with high accuracy. Coupled with a lightweight machine-learning framework, this work establishes rapid, precise, and closed-loop anemotactic navigation and multi-target odor tracing in complex three-dimensional (3D) spaces, offering a compact optical sensing platform for embodied robotic olfaction beyond static gas classification.

items.title: The social gradient in adolescent unintentional injuries demands policy attention.
items.abstract: Unintentional injuries are a leading cause of morbidity and mortality in adolescence, yet they remain underprioritised within adolescent health and equity agendas. Recent Danish studies reveal substantial socioeconomic inequalities in unintentional injuries. Injury risk and injury-related mortality follow a clear social gradient, with adolescents from less advantaged backgrounds experiencing higher rates of both outcomes. Despite these disparities, evidence on effective and equitable prevention strategies remains limited, and current policy efforts largely focus on road traffic injuries while overlooking other important causes. Furthermore, existing injury surveillance systems inadequately capture adolescent-specific contexts and activities, limiting opportunities for targeted prevention. Unintentional injuries are an important but overlooked source of health inequality in adolescence. Reducing the burden of injury requires greater policy attention, stronger research and surveillance, and a focus on the social determinants that drive injury risk. Addressing these upstream factors may improve both injury outcomes and adolescent health more broadly.

items.title: Extreme Heat Events and Increased Risk of Motor Vehicle Crashes, Injuries, and Fatalities: Exploring Differential Impacts across California Census Tracts.
items.abstract: Motor vehicle crashes are a leading cause of death in the USA, killing approximately 120 people daily. California led the nation in motor vehicle deaths for seven consecutive years (2016-2022), with fatalities climbing overall. Extreme heat events (EHEs) have intensified with climate change, potentially increasing crash risk and severity, but this link remains understudied. This study assessed the relationship between different EHE definitions and the risk of crashes, and the associated number of injuries and fatalities in California census tracts across May-October of 2010-2020. Twelve EHE definitions were calculated using high-resolution gridded daily temperature data based on various metrics, thresholds, and duration. A time-stratified case-crossover approach quantified EHE impacts on property-damage-only (PDO) crashes, non-PDO crashes, injuries, and fatalities. Effect modification was explored by climate type, crash-related factors, traffic exposure, road network design, and urbanicity. Compared to non-EHE days, EHE exposure increased crash risk across all outcomes for same-day and 2-day durations and for most 3-day definitions. The largest effects were generally observed for the most extreme EHE threshold (99th percentile maximum temperature), where PDO crashes showed the largest increase for 2-day exposure (OR = 1.07, 95% CI 1.05-1.09). At the same threshold, we estimate a statewide average of 115 excess PDO crashes, 66 excess non-PDO crashes, and 102 excess injuries annually, while the corresponding fatality estimate (3 excess fatalities annually, 95% CI -1-7) was imprecise. Heterogeneity was observed across climates, crash-related factors, traffic volumes, and urbanicity. This study provides insight into the increased risk of crashes due to heat and the magnitude of impact across EHE definitions in California, supporting the need for heat-responsive traffic-safety measures.

items.title: High Per-capita Area of Accessible Urban Green Space and Lower Self-reported Anxiety/Depression Problems among Older Adults in Korea: A Nationwide Multilevel Study ​.
items.abstract: Although a growing body of literature has linked urban green space to better mental health, less is known about population-normalized area-level green-space provision intended for everyday use, particularly among older adults. This study examined the association between district-level per-capita living-area urban forest area and self-reported anxiety/depression problems among older adults in South Korea. We analyzed data from 79,931 participants aged 65 years or older in the 2024 Korea Community Health Survey. Anxiety/depression problems were assessed using the anxiety/depression dimension of the EQ-5D-3L. Exposure was measured using the 2023 Korea Forest Service per-capita living-area urban forest indicator, assigned to each participant's district of residence, and categorized into quartiles. Associations were examined using two-level random-intercept logistic regression models accounting for clustering within public health center areas and adjusting for individual-level covariates, including the urban-rural residential classification. Overall, 17.5% of participants reported anxiety/depression problems. Compared with the lowest exposure quartile (< 9.7 m2/person), the highest quartile (≥ 31.8 m2/person) was associated with lower odds of anxiety/depression problems (adjusted odds ratio, 0.74; 95% confidence interval, 0.63-0.87), whereas no statistically significant associations were observed for the intermediate quartiles. These findings suggest that a high level of district-level living-area urban forest provision may be associated with lower odds of anxiety/depression problems among older adults, with potential implications for age-friendly urban planning.

items.title: Greenness, Air Pollution, and Insulin Resistance in a Latin American Megacity: A Longitudinal Mediation Analysis of the ELSA‑Brasil Cohort ​.
items.abstract: Studies examining the relationship between greenness and insulin resistance may elucidate the distal association between greenness and type 2 diabetes. The role of air pollution on this association remains unclear. We investigated whether air pollution mediated the association between greenness and insulin resistance, among non-diabetic participants (N = 2715) from the Brazilian Longitudinal Study of Adult Health (ELSA-Brasil) in São Paulo megacity, Brazil, followed-up for approximately 8 years (2008-2010, 2012-2014, 2017-2019). Neighborhood greenness (NDVI, in quartiles), air pollution (PM2.5 and PM10), and insulin resistance (HOMA-IR) were examined using mediation analysis, allowing for exposure-mediator interaction. Total, natural direct, and natural indirect effects were estimated, using mixed-effects models, stratified by the neighborhood socioeconomic status (NSES) and adjusted for individual age, sex, education and income. In PM10 analysis for participants from low NSES, higher neighborhood greenness was associated with lower insulin resistance, in a dose-response pattern, as indicated by the total (β = -0.49, 95% CI -0.91, -0.05; β = -0.20, 95% CI -0.54, 0.16; and β = -0.07, 95% CI -0.38, 0.27, for the 4th, 3rd, and 2nd NDVI quartile vs 1st quartile, respectively) and natural direct effects (β = -0.59, 95% CI -1.06, -0.09; β = -0.32, 95% CI -0.67, 0.03; and β = -0.05, 95% CI -0.37, 0.27, for the 4th, 3rd, and 2nd NDVI quartile vs 1st quartile, respectively). The natural indirect effect indicated no mediation by PM10. Similar results were found for the PM2.5 analysis. Greenness was associated with lower insulin resistance among adults living in low NSES areas. However, no evidence of air pollution mediation was found. These results suggest that greater neighborhood greenness may be associated with better cardiometabolic health in socioeconomically disadvantaged areas.

items.title: A unified framework for defining and analyzing spatial niches in spatial omics data analysis.
items.abstract: The term 'spatial niche' is widely used in spatial omics analyses but is inconsistently defined across studies. We survey the literature and find that it most commonly refers to the following three distinct concepts: (1) a proximity-based neighborhood around an anchor cell or spatial spot; (2) a computationally derived spatial domain comprising spatially proximal spots or cells with shared molecular features; and (3) a biologically grounded ecosystem comprising cellular and noncellular components that support resident cells. We organize existing studies under this taxonomy and distinguish two main analytical roles-niches as spot-level covariates for modeling local context, and niches as spot clusters for within-niche and between-niche compositional and molecular analyses. To reduce ambiguity, we recommend reserving 'niche' for biological ecosystems while using 'spatial neighborhood' and 'spatial domain' for the corresponding computational constructs. We also provide a practical decision framework to help researchers align niche definitions and analytical strategies with the biological questions at hand.

items.title: Community-based (midstream) approaches to improving child oral health across the UK.
items.abstract: As health is a devolved matter in the UK, each of the four countries has developed a unique approach to improving the oral health of children in order to meet the needs of their population. Public health interventions can be classed into three main categories: national level (upstream) policy initiatives, community-based (midstream) interventions, and individual level (downstream) interventions. Midstream interventions aimed at improving child oral health have been implemented to varying degrees across all four countries of the UK. This article presents a descriptive overview of the main midstream child oral health improvement programmes in each of these four countries, identifying key challenges and opportunities presented around each approach and the policy framework in which they are operating. Common facilitators across all four countries included cross-party political support and integration with early years services, while sustainability of funding and workforce capacity were identified as challenges to implementation. Robust long-term monitoring and evaluation frameworks are needed to inform effective resource allocation and sustain the improvements achieved.

items.title: Modelling future dental workforce need for adults with special care needs within the UK.
items.abstract: Aims Special care dentistry (SCD) in the United Kingdom (UK) provides care for a range of adults with complex needs, including physically and mentally disabled people, older adults with dementia, adults with medical, emotional, sensory, mental or social impairment, or a combination of these factors, who require care in a range of settings. The aim of this research was to establish a needs-based workforce planning model and tool that focuses on assessing SCD's workforce capacity and capability to deliver tailored dental services for the UK's disabled populace.Methods A predictive analytics tool using Python and HTML was developed to integrate multiple large national datasets to identify key variables for long-term workforce planning and model future SCD demand through 2050. There are currently 13 million disabled adults, 5.9 million of whom are 'disabled; limited a lot'. National and regional population demand projections for SCD were calculated until 2050 using data mainly from the Office for National Statistics and the 2021-2022 Family Resources Survey. National data on the specialty were obtained from registration and survey data. National and regional resource supply projections for SCD were calculated until at least 2040 recursively from 2018 taking into consideration multiple factors.Results A detailed analysis highlighted several key findings. Under the present scenario, supply aligns with demand only when 5-8% of the 'disabled; limited a lot' category require complex dental care, suggesting that only a small proportion of needs is currently met by specialists. Planning for the future, for the baseline scenario, where 50% of the 'disabled; limited a lot' population is considered to have complex needs, even adding 150 specialty trainees per year will not meet projected need until 2040 due to the length of training. If the other half of the 'disabled; limited a lot' population is assumed to have moderate needs, then upskilling and adding 0.2% of the primary care dentists' pool, or about 80 primary care dentists to the dentists with extended skills (DES) pool per year, would allow this level of moderate need to be met as early as 2034. Strategic workforce redirections, such as even transitioning just 0.1% or 40 primary care dentists into the DES pool per year, could begin to significantly alter the supply-demand dynamics, together with a modest increase in specialty training numbers.Conclusions This study highlights the immense and growing need for SCD and the upskilling of frontline practitioners in caring for adults with additional needs. In essence, while the challenge before us is monumental, it is not insurmountable. Strategic planning, focused training initiatives, and nimble workforce reallocation are pivotal to ensuring that the UK's vulnerable populations receive the specialised dental care they deserve.

items.title: How commerce influences health and oral health.
items.abstract: There is increasing recognition that commercial factors can influence health and oral health both negatively and positively. This narrative review summarises the tactics used to market sugar, tobacco and alcohol, products that can be harmful to oral health. This article considers options open to governments and official agencies to combat the adverse influence of commerce on oral health. It also examines the role of the dental care system itself as a commercial determinant. Finally, it also reviews how commercial determinants can positively influence oral health.Dental professionals need to be aware of the influence of commercial actors on oral health. Such knowledge can enable them to act as advocates for health and oral health improvement and to engage meaningfully in wider societal debates.

items.title: MRI measures of oxygen extraction fraction in the subacute phase of mild neonatal hypoxic-ischemic encephalopathy.
items.abstract: Early identification of newborns with mild encephalopathy at risk of clinical progression is critical. Our group has previously demonstrated regional quantification of oxygen extraction fraction (OEF), a noninvasive MRI-derived measure of cerebral oxygen utilization in newborns with encephalopathy receiving therapeutic hypothermia (TH). This study evaluates whether regional OEF measured between 2 and 7 days of life distinguishes newborns with mild encephalopathy who are not treated with TH and subsequently exhibit clinical progression within the first day of life from those who remain clinically stable. Vessel-specific OEF maps of the brain were obtained using the accelerated T2-relaxation-under-phase-contrast (aTRUPC) MRI technique from full-term newborns with mild encephalopathy and healthy controls. OEF was quantified across six predefined venous drainage regions. Fifty-three full-term newborns (28 with mild encephalopathy, 25 healthy controls) were enrolled. Seven newborns with mild encephalopathy showed clinical progression on the first day of life and received TH (TH group); the remaining did not receive TH (non-TH group). OEF was significantly lower in cortical regions in the TH group compared with healthy controls and the non-TH group. Cortical OEF represents an innovative imaging biomarker. Prospective studies are needed to determine its value for risk stratification during the therapeutic window. Early identification of newborns with mild encephalopathy at risk of progression remains challenging during the therapeutic window. Cortical oxygen extraction fraction (OEF) measured between 2 and 7 days of life was significantly lower in newborns who progressed within the first day of life than in newborns with mild encephalopathy who did not progress and healthy controls. Regional OEF may provide a noninvasive biomarker for early risk stratification and treatment decision-making in newborns with mild encephalopathy.

items.title: Measuring Quality in Assisted Living: The Oregon Way.
items.abstract: Assisted living (AL) is the largest residential long-term care provider for dementia specific services in the United States (US), but no nationally accepted standards exist for measuring AL quality in the US Oregon's legislatively mandated Quality Measurement Program (QMP) requires all licensed AL communities to report five quality indicators annually: direct care staff retention, training compliance, falls with injury, prescriptions for nonstandard antipsychotic medication use, and resident satisfaction scores as measured by CoreQ. We linked the 2024 QMP quality measure data to administrative data for all licensed Oregon AL communities with 25 or more beds (n = 450). We examined whether these indicators differ by organizational characteristics. We used ordinary least squares regression models to examine the associations between these quality metrics and memory care (MC) endorsement, profit status, Medicaid contract, size, and rural location. MC communities reported a higher rate of falls with injury (11.6% vs. 7.3%) and double the rate of nonstandard antipsychotic prescriptions (18.6% vs. 9.1%) compared to standalone AL, with no statistically significant differences in staff retention, training compliance, or overall resident satisfaction scores. Nonprofit communities had higher staff retention (+11.5 percentage points) and higher resident satisfaction scores across all CoreQ domains compared to their for-profit counterparts. Finally, communities with a Medicaid contract reported higher nonstandard antipsychotic prescription rates (+4.7 percentage points) and lower overall CoreQ scores compared to non-Medicaid communities. Performance on some QMP measures differed by MC endorsement, ownership structure, and Medicaid contract. Because QMP does not capture measures of resident acuity, these differences should not be read as differences in overall care quality. Future work should examine whether and how contextual information such as payer-mix and case-mix adjustment and ownership data could make public reporting more informative.

items.title: Clade I and Clade II monkeypox virus in Barcelona, 2025-2026: More similarities than differences in a case-case study.
items.abstract: Clade I is becoming more predominant in Europe and may differ epidemiologically from Clade II. This case-case study (N=100) compared Clades I and II detected in Barcelona between September 2025 and June 2026. Crude and adjusted odds ratios (aOR) with 95% confidence intervals (95%CI) were estimated using logistic regression models. While the overall epidemiological profile and clinical severity were similar, Clade I cases were more likely to reside in lower-income districts, less likely to be migrants (aOR=0.34, 95%CI 0.25;0.47), and more frequently reported sexual activity during leisure activities(aOR=7.55, 95%CI 3.93;14.53), attendance at large-scale events(aOR=18.78, 95%CI 7.40;47.67). Clinically, Clade I cases showed higher odds of fever (aOR=1.55, 95%CI 1.05;2.28), odynophagia (aOR=5.13, 95%CI 2.98;8.85), oral rash (aOR=42.60, 95%CI 12.11;149.88) and generalized rash, whereas generalized lymphadenopathy (aOR=0.33, 95%CI 0.15;0.71) and anogenital rash (aOR=0.55, 95%CI 0.36;0.83) were less frequent. These findings suggest that Clade Ib circulation in urban settings currently mirrors the epidemiological patterns established by Clade IIb.

items.title: Digital Tools for the Detection of Dermatitis: A Systematic Review.
items.abstract: Contact dermatitis (CD) plays a significant role in occupational health due to its frequent occurrence and environmental triggers and is among the most common occupational diseases in Western countries. Despite its prevalence, occupational contact dermatitis (OCD) is often overlooked by occupational physicians, largely due to limited knowledge and a lack of validated detection tools. Advances in digital technologies and artificial intelligence (AI) offer promising opportunities for improving early detection, yet an overview of available digital tools and their effectiveness in dermatitis detection is lacking. A systematic review was conducted in PubMed, Embase, Cinahl, and Scopus. The search focused on original studies published in peer-reviewed journals between 2014 and 2024. Forty-three studies evaluating digital tools for dermatitis detection were included, categorized as models (n = 31) or devices (n = 12). Models represent AI algorithms not yet in practical use, while devices are tools already implemented. Convolutional Neural Networks (CNNs) were the most commonly used computational technique. Median sensitivity and specificity were 0.84 and 0.97 for all tools, 0.85 and 0.97 for models, and 0.78 and 0.97 for devices. The results provided in this review will serve as valuable input for the development of new tools to enhance early OCD detection.

items.title: A Bibliometric Analysis of Body Donation Research (2006-2025): Perspectives From Medical Education, Ethics, and Policy.
items.abstract: Body donation is fundamental to anatomical education and biomedical research. The field has expanded from technical dissection to include ethical, regulatory, and educational dimensions, yet a systematic bibliometric analysis of its evolution is lacking. This study maps the knowledge structure, collaboration patterns, and research frontiers of the English-language body donation literature (2006-2025), focusing on the interplay among anatomical education, cultural ethics, and institutional governance. Publications were retrieved from the Web of Science Core Collection on August 5, 2026; 419 English-language articles met the eligibility criteria. CiteSpace (v6.2.R3) and VOSviewer (v1.6.18) were used to analyze collaboration networks, cocitation structures, citation bursts, and keyword co-occurence. Annual output increased steadily across three phases. The retrieved literature is concentrated in a small number of countries and institutions, a pattern inseparable from the language and database boundaries of the corpus, and collaboration is denser within regions than between them. Keyword co-occurence produced five clusters, mapped onto three analytical domains: anatomical education, cultural ethics, and institutional governance, the last with no cluster of its own. Organ donation concepts are still frequently conflated with body donation, and research frontiers have shifted from gross anatomy pedagogy toward legal regulation and public willingness. Body donation research has evolved from a technique-driven paradigm into a multidisciplinary field integrating humanistic care, legal frameworks, and educational innovation. Remaining gaps include the uneven representation of world regions in the indexed literature and the conflation of body and organ donation; both constrain culturally adaptable governance and anatomical education.

items.title: Genome-wide DNA methylation study uncovers epigenetic markers associated with early life stress in individuals with major depressive disorder.
items.abstract: Early life stress (ELS) is a significant risk factor for major depressive disorder (MDD); however, the epigenetic mechanisms underlying this association remain poorly characterized, partly due to the lack of trauma-stratified control groups in previous studies. We performed genome-wide DNA methylation profiling using Reduced-Representative Bisulfite Sequencing (RRBS) on whole blood samples from 90 adults divided into four groups: MDD with ELS (n = 30), MDD without ELS (n = 30), controls with ELS (n = 15), and controls without ELS (n = 15). Differentially methylated regions (DMRs) were identified employing MethylKit and DMRcate (≥5 CpGs, FDR < 0.05) and annotated via FUMA GENE2FUNC and clusterProfiler. Our analysis revealed 551, 581, and 479 DMRs in comparisons of MDD vs. control, MDD + ELS vs. control + ELS, and MDD non-ELS vs. control non-ELS, respectively. Core genes SELENOO, FASN, and THOC7 were consistently differentially methylated across all groups, reflecting shared mitochondrial, metabolic, and RNA-processing mechanisms. The MDD + ELS group demonstrated a higher DMR burden, particularly in regions associated with active promoter chromatin, with ELS-specific genes HIVEP3 and NRL exhibiting GWAS evidence linked to treatment-resistant depression and ADHD. Conversely, DMRs in MDD non-ELS were enriched in repressed chromatin states, with hypermethylation in loci within CAMK4 and CALM1 suggesting constitutive silencing of calcium-dependent neuronal signaling pathways. Our findings underscore the significant contribution of ELS to specific epigenetic changes associated with MDD, particularly in neurodevelopmental and stress-response pathways. In contrast, MDD without ELS exhibited a distinct methylation profile that affected synapses and synaptic plasticity. Our study, therefore, emphasizes the necessity of trauma-informed approaches in psychiatric research.

items.title: Assessing occupational exposure to imidacloprid among animal shelter workers using human biomonitoring.
items.abstract: Imidacloprid (IMI) is a neonicotinoid insecticide used as an ectoparasite treatment for pets in professional and home-use settings. Animal shelter workers apply these treatments to pets in their care and often use multiple ectoparasite treatments per day, resulting in a potential for occupational IMI exposure. To assess IMI exposures among animal shelter workers, human biomonitoring approaches were adopted, with multiple individual spot urine samples collected over 24- or 48-hour periods from eight full-time animal shelter workers. Samples were analysed for IMI and its metabolites, IMI-olefin and OH-IMI, to assess occupational exposure to IMI. Study results show that animal shelter workers had elevated urinary concentrations of IMI and metabolites compared to a previous general population study, with concentrations comparable to pet owners using the same products. However, all urinary concentrations were below 1.4% of the Acceptable Operator Exposure Level, indicating low-level exposures among the study cohort.

items.title: Childhood Metabolomic Profiles of Phthalate and Phthalate Replacement Exposure in the Project Viva Cohort.
items.abstract: Metabolomics, the systematic characterization of the wide array of small molecules present in a biological sample, can provide critical information on the physiological response to complex environmental exposures. Phthalates are a group of endocrine-disrupting chemicals with wide-ranging reported impacts on human health and development. We quantified concentrations of 19 phthalate and phthalate replacement compounds in mid-childhood spot urine and performed untargeted endogenous metabolomic profiling in fasting plasma in mid-childhood (N = 212, mean age = 7.95 years, 53.3% female) and early adolescence (N = 417, mean age = 12.91 years, 50.8% female) among children in the Project Viva birth cohort. We examined associations of mid-childhood phthalate concentrations with endogenous metabolomic profiles in mid-childhood and in early adolescence (253 and 538 metabolites at each timepoint, respectively), using multivariable linear regression for individual phthalates and quantile g-computation for the mixture of phthalates, adjusted for sex, race/ethnicity, maternal education, household income, and age at blood draw for metabolomic assays, with further models stratified by sex. Individual phthalate metabolites were cross-sectionally associated with five endogenous metabolites, and the phthalate mixture was associated with six endogenous metabolites during mid-childhood. Additionally, mid-childhood exposure to individual phthalates was associated with five metabolites in early adolescence, including associations between detectable mid-childhood 1,2-cyclohexane dicarboxylic acid diisononyl ester (DINCH), a phthalate replacement, and higher 2-hydroxylaurate levels in the overall sample and associations between MCPP and lower levels of three polyunsaturated fatty acids among female participants. Identified metabolites were involved in biological functions and health outcomes including inflammation and cognitive function.

items.title: Prenatal exposure to heavy metal(loid)s and essential elements and infant sleep: A metabolome-wide analysis in the Shanghai Birth Cohort.
items.abstract: Prenatal exposure to heavy metal(loid)s is associated with impaired neurodevelopment, but its relationship with infant sleep outcomes remains unclear. We investigated associations of prenatal exposure to metal(loid)s and essential elements with these outcomes and explored metabolic links. This prospective cohort study analyzed Shanghai Birth Cohort data from 2,148 infants at 6 months and 1,853 at 12 months. Eleven elements were measured in early pregnancy. Sleep were assessed using the Brief Infant Sleep Questionnaire. Associations were examined using multiple linear regression, multinomial logistic regression, g-computation for mixtures, and generalized estimating equation (GEE) models. A meet-in-the-middle approach, followed by exploratory mediation and pathway enrichment analyses, identified candidate metabolites linking maternal element concentrations with sleep outcomes and explored potential metabolic pathways. After FDR correction, copper (Cu) was associated with longer sleep latency at 6 months, whereas cadmium (Cd) showed inverse associations with daytime sleep duration; while Cu and calcium (Ca) were associated with increased nighttime awakenings at 12 months. Cu, Ca, magnesium (Mg), were associated with greater risk and severity of parent-reported sleep problems, whereas arsenic (As), lead (Pb) mercury (Hg), showed inverse associations with severity. Cu was associated with increased snoring risk across infancy. Longitudinal GEE analyses supported persistent associations of Cu with longer sleep latency and multiple sleep disturbances, and of Ca with increased parents-report sleep problem. In mixture analyses, the essential-element mixture was associated with shorter nocturnal sleep duration, whereas the heavy metal(loid) mixture was associated with shorter total sleep duration. Candidate intermediary metabolites were primarily enriched in lipid metabolic pathways, particularly glycerophospholipid metabolism and unsaturated fatty acid biosynthesis. Higher maternal concentrations of selected elements, particularly Cu and Ca, were associated with caregiver-reported infant sleep disturbances. Exploratory metabolomic findings highlighted lipid-related signatures associated with maternal element concentrations and infant sleep outcomes, suggesting candidate pathways for further investigation.

items.title: Sertraline disassembles the mitochondrial transduceosome and disrupts testosterone biosynthesis.
items.abstract: The widespread use of the selective serotonin reuptake inhibitor (SSRI) sertraline is limited by its frequent side effect of sexual dysfunction, yet the underlying mechanisms remain poorly understood. This study aimed to elucidate how sertraline directly disrupts testicular testosterone synthesis. Using an integrated approach combining network toxicology, molecular docking, in-vivo mouse model, and in-vitro Leydig cells experiments, we identified that clinical doses of sertraline significantly suppressed testosterone synthesis. Mechanistically, sertraline downregulated the protein level of the steroidogenic acute regulatory (StAR), the rate-limiting enzyme for testosterone synthesis, without affecting its mRNA level. Molecular docking and thermal shift assays revealed that sertraline specifically binds to the outer mitochondrial membrane protein VDAC1 with high affinity. This binding site spatially overlapped with the StAR-VDAC1 interaction interface. Consequently, sertraline disrupted the formation of the StAR-VDAC1 transduceosome, as validated by co-immunoprecipitation analysis. This led to StAR destabilization and degradation, thereby blocking mitochondrial cholesterol import and subsequently testosterone biosynthesis. Crucially, VDAC1 overexpression rescued sertraline-induced downregulation of StAR and restored testosterone synthesis. In conclusion, our findings demonstrate that sertraline disrupts testosterone synthesis by binding to VDAC1, disrupting the essential StAR-VDAC1 interaction and leading to StAR degradation. This mechanism provides a new perspective for understanding the clinical reproductive-related side effects of sertraline and for developing intervention strategies targeting the VDAC1-StAR interaction.

items.title: Entangled stoichiometric objectives shape microbial catabolism
items.abstract: The understanding of fundamental relationships between energetic and biosynthetic parameters of catabolism and anabolism is a central challenge in microbiology. The large diversity of microbial metabolisms can be compared on the basis of our current definitions of catabolism and anabolism. Catabolism has two functions: synthesising charged energy carriers and carbon precursors. Energy carriers, however, are also involved in precursor synthesis, complicating the analysis. We introduce an unbiased method to quantify stoichiometric relationships between catabolism and anabolism in genome-scale metabolic models. We compare catabolic strategies across diverse (heterotrophic) microbial species and growth conditions, focusing on states of maximal biomass yield per unit of energy source. Catabolic networks turn out to vary greatly, due to variation in the energy and carbon source for growth and the requirement to make suitable precursors for anabolism. We find that the ATP requirement for 1 gram biomass ranges between 72.8 and 148.0 mmol, precursor sets range between 4 and 14 in size, and acetyl-CoA is the only universal precursor across species. An important varying factor is the amount of ATP that is produced or consumed during precursor synthesis. This causes the remaining ATP demand, which is produced in catabolism, to vary. We conclude that the diversity of heterotrophic catabolism results from entanglement between charging of energy carriers and precursor synthesis. The state of maximal energetic efficiency is reached by maximizing the yield of charged energy carriers during precursor synthesis and simultaneously minimizing the demand for charged energy carriers in the conversion of precursors into macromolecules. Our formal analysis of catabolic diversity using a rigorous definition of catabolism's two functions shows that microbial metabolism cannot be simplified in this manner; it rather shows that these two functions are intertwined due to the precise biochemistry.

items.title: Nitrogen and Phosphorus Losses in a Rural Watershed Under no Tillage System in Southern Brazil
items.abstract: ABSTRACT Intensive production is sought by farmers but may compromise sustainability depending on management. No‐Tillage System (NTS) is a conservation system and paradigm in Brazilian grain production; however, the quality of its adoption is questioned as water erosion regained importance and remains underestimated. This study quantified nitrogen (N) and phosphorus (P) concentrations and losses and evaluated the seasonal contribution of soluble and particulate fractions to nutrient export in a rural watershed under long‐term NTS without terraces in southern Brazil. A 118.8‐ha watershed comprising 13 agricultural fields was monitored from December 2022 to November 2023. Streamflow was continuously monitored at the watershed outlet, while daily streamwater samples were collected and analyzed for total, soluble, and particulate N and P. Nitrate (N‐NO 3 − ) and ammonium (N‐NH 4 + ) concentrations remained below the Brazilian critical environmental limit (CEL), whereas TP frequently exceeded the 0.10 mg L −1 threshold. Particulate N (PN) accounted for 70.20% of total N (TN) export, while particulate P (PP) accounted for 97.65% of total P (TP) export, demonstrating the predominance of particulate pathways. Nutrient losses increased markedly during intense precipitation and high streamflow, particularly in October and November. Annual losses reached 30.80 kg N ha −1 and 4.91 kg P ha −1 , corresponding to monetary losses of US$ 22.58 ha −1 and US$ 4.85 ha −1 , respectively. Overall, long‐term NTS alone was insufficient to prevent substantial nutrient losses under high‐flow conditions, particularly in particulate form. Integrating NTS with mechanical runoff control practices and effective soil cover is therefore essential to improve soil and water conservation in agricultural watersheds.

items.title: Board NGO Experience and Corporate ESG Performance: The Moderating Role of Organizational Psychological Capital
items.abstract: ABSTRACT This study examines the association between directors with non‐governmental organization (NGO) experience and firms' environmental, social, and governance (ESG) performance, as well as the moderating role of organizational psychological capital (OPC). Using 1659 firm‐year observations from UK FTSE 350 companies between 2012 and 2021, we combine manually collected board data with natural language processing to measure OPC from annual‐report narratives. The results show that NGO‐experienced director representation is positively associated with ESG performance, particularly its environmental and social dimensions. We find limited evidence suggesting that OPC may strengthen the positive association between NGO‐experienced director representation and ESG performance. The study extends emerging research on NGO‐experienced directors by examining overall ESG performance and identifying OPC as a complementary organizational resource that may condition this association. The findings contribute to corporate governance, sustainability, and organizational psychology research and offer implications for boards, investors, and policymakers.

items.title: Green Entrepreneurship as a Catalyst for Local Environmental Management in South Africa: Opportunities, Barriers, and Policy Implications
items.abstract: ABSTRACT Building on the question of how environmental management can be addressed at the local level, the transition from a linear “take–make–dispose” model to a circular economy ( CE ) has become central to sustainable development, particularly in emerging economies facing intertwined environmental and socioeconomic challenges. In South Africa, high unemployment, energy security, and escalating waste generation intensify the urgency for systemic restructuring. This study examines green entrepreneurship (GE) as a catalyst for CE development within environmental management, focusing on Limpopo Province as a contextually rich case of resource potential and developmental vulnerability. Using a qualitative design grounded in thematic analysis, data were collected from 40 green entrepreneurs and 10 policymakers across recycling, renewable energy, sustainable agriculture, green manufacturing, and governance sectors. Findings reveal a layered circular ecosystem comprising downstream resource recovery (recycling and waste management), midstream production transformation (renewable energy and regenerative agriculture), and upstream systemic enablers (consultancy and ecodesign services). These activities represent distinct circular business model innovations through which firms create environmental value by recovering resources, extending product life cycles, substituting fossil‐based inputs, and redesigning production processes. Findings indicate that green entrepreneurs implement a range of CE practices, including resource recovery, renewable‐energy provision, composting, and environmentally oriented manufacturing. Participants reported that these activities contributed to waste reduction, resource efficiency, and environmental sustainability. However, these reported outcomes reflect participant experiences and perceptions rather than independently verified environmental performance measures. However, scaling remains constrained by limited access to finance, high upfront technology costs related to waste management infrastructure, technical skills shortages, policy fragmentation, and weak institutional coordination. The study argues that GE is not peripheral but central to South Africa's circular transition. It concludes that strengthening green finance mechanisms, technical capacity development, gender‐inclusive support systems, coherent policy integration, and value chain coordination is essential for unlocking sustainable investment growth. By situating entrepreneurial agency within provincial socioeconomic realities, the paper contributes to debates on implementing CE in the Global South.

items.title: Unintended positive and negative consequences of climate adaptation interventions for Australia's native species
items.abstract: Climate adaptation interventions aim to reduce the vulnerability of biodiversity to climate change, but could have unintended consequences in agricultural landscapes where conservation and production goals intersect. We employed expert elicitation to complement a systematic search of peer-reviewed literature, identifying unintended consequences from climate adaptation interventions implemented for Australian native species in agricultural landscapes. We documented 158 unintended consequences spanning ecological, agricultural, governance and management processes, occurring within and outside intervention sites. 52% were positive co-benefits and 48% were negative consequences. Interventions generated on-site benefits by enhancing habitat or food availability for non-target native species, although this sometimes facilitated invasive species colonisation, competition and predation. Co-benefits for agricultural production included improved soil health, reduced agricultural weeds, and greater resource availability for livestock, although negative impacts on farmland such as native herbivore competition with livestock were also reported. Providing food and water was significantly less likely to generate positive co-benefits, and experts also noted that insufficient control of invasive species could exacerbate risks of intervention failure. Governance and implementation challenges such as management burden, limited knowledge of, sharing of, or adherence to, recommended practices, and insufficient funding to complete required tasks, often underpinned the emergence of unintended consequences. As only 22% of reports included monitoring of unintended consequences outside intervention sites but, when reported, these consequences could be severe, we recommend increased attention to off-site impacts. Our results highlight the importance of sustained financial support and strong governance to ensure the long-term effectiveness of climate adaptation interventions and to strengthen monitoring capacity.

items.title: Termite mounds as fertility islands and their benefits for raised-field agriculture in the floodplain of the Bangweulu Basin, Zambia
items.abstract: Termite mounds are conspicuous features in tropical savannas, where the role of termites as ecosystem engineers is widely acknowledged. Among the many impacts of termites on the environment, modifications of the physicochemical properties of the soil are prominent, to the point that termites have influenced the agricultural and cultural practices of local communities. However, most studies have focused on dry savannas. We investigated the role of termite mounds as fertility islands, and their role in subsistence agriculture, in one of the world’s most extensive floodplain savannas, the Bangweulu basin in Zambia. First, based on inspection of satellite images, we showed that termite savannas and areas of raised-field agriculture (the main type of subsistence agriculture in the region) covered respectively 14 % and 23 % of the studied surface area, and overlapped. Second, investigating more specifically the area near the village of Yongolo, we evidenced two superimposed patterns of spatial distribution of termite mounds, one involving large mounds (mean height 1.7 m) and one involving small mounds (mean height 0.6 m), both regularly spaced with an average inter-mound distance of 68 m and 8 m, respectively. The two types of mounds differed in their termite communities, the large ones each hosting one nest of Odontotermes , the small ones hosting mostly nests of Trinervitermes and Cubitermes . Both mound types had soil properties that differed from those of the basin soil, leading to an expected increase in soil fertility on mounds (higher contents of N, C, organic matter and clay). Woody plants, including trees, occurred only on large mounds. On small mounds, the epigeal structure of termite nests was higher where depth of flood water was higher, showing plasticity in nest construction in response to environmental constraints. Termite mounds were extensively used by local people, in particular as preferred plots for building raised fields for cassava cultivation. Raised fields on termite mounds were richer in nitrogen and clay, but had a thinner layer of dark soil, than those off termite mounds. The main benefits of building raised fields on termite mounds appeared to be a longer duration of the cultivation period (allowing cultivation during the inundation period) and increased soil fertility through weathering of termite nest structures. Termite mounds (as fertility islands) and raised fields (built by piling up topsoil) both result in nutrient concentration. In addition, both termite nests and raised fields are built taller where flooding is deeper. Thus, termites and humans rely on analogous strategies to mitigate constraints in seasonally flooded savannas, showing convergence in niche construction.

items.title: High‐Frequency Stimulated Brillouin Scattering in Suspended Thin‐Film Lithium Niobate Waveguides
items.abstract: ABSTRACT Stimulated Brillouin scattering (SBS) enables photonic filtering at gigahertz center frequencies with narrow linewidths at megahertz‐range, making it a key building block for integrated microwave photonics. Accessing radio‐frequency bands beyond 15 GHz with SBS requires high frequency shifts and high gain coefficients, a combination that yet remains a challenge. Here, we show that SBS in suspended Z‐cut thin‐film lithium niobate (TFLN) waveguides satisfies these demands, exhibiting Brillouin frequency shifts exceeding 15 GHz when pumped at telecom wavelengths, nearly twice the highest values previously reported in TFLN. We observe gain coefficients up to 23.8 , among the largest achieved for such high Brillouin frequency shifts in any integrated Brillouin platform to date. For the first time, we apply spontaneous Brillouin microspectroscopy to suspended TFLN waveguides and confirm the high‐frequency acoustic mode observed in our SBS experiments. Our results unlock TFLN as a compelling material platform for scalable microwave photonics, with future applications spanning communication, sensing, and information processing.

items.title: One year of broadband radio monitoring of the enigmatic transient GRB 250702B reveals the evolution of the relativistic jet
items.abstract: Abstract We present an extensive radio monitoring campaign of the unique extragalactic transient GRB 250702B, associated with unprecedentedly long duration gamma-ray emission, lasting over 3 hr. Our observations span 0.65–233 GHz from 6–356 d (observer frame) post-discovery. The radio emission shows a smoothly evolving peaked synchrotron spectrum consistent with an adiabatic shock expanding into a stratified ambient medium (ne∝R−k; k = 1.5 − 2). We detect significant variability in the low frequency (≤3 GHz) light curves which we interpret as interstellar scintillation, placing an approximate bound on the blast wave image size of 1.2 × 1016 ≲ R⊥ ≲ 5 × 1017 cm. The temporal evolution of the flux density and critical synchrotron frequencies suggest the shock that powers the radio emission is potentially a wide-angle θj ≳ 15 deg, low Lorentz factor (Γ ≲ 10) jet, or a narrow θj ≲ 2 deg (Γ0 > 50) highly relativistic jet. A narrow jet is expected for a stellar-mass black hole engine, such as a helium star merger, and the beaming-corrected kinetic energy in this scenario is consistent with the known distribution for long GRBs (EK ~ 1051 erg). The wide-angle jet scenario would instead require a progenitor involving prolonged accretion. We derive and show an intermediate or stellar-mass black hole tidal disruption event are viable possibilities. The beaming-corrected kinetic energy in this scenario is on the low end of the known distribution for relativistic SMBH TDEs (EK ~ 1050 erg). We disfavour an SMBH TDE due to lack of compatibility with the observed timescales. The detection of a jet shut off within the next year would favour a WD-IMBH TDE due to the shorter theoretical duration of super-Eddington accretion than the main-sequence TDE channels.

items.title: Investigating the coincidence problem with Interacting Dark Energy Models
items.abstract: Abstract Interacting dark energy (IDE) models within the framework of general relativity (GR) provide a possible extension of the standard $\Lambda$CDM model and may alleviate the coincidence problem. In this paper, we investigate three phenomenological interacting dark energy models using a combination of cosmic chronometer $H(z)$ measurements and two standard cosmic rulers: baryon acoustic oscillations (BAO) and quasars (QSO). The observational constraints indicate a mild preference for energy transfer from dark energy to dark matter, a scenario that may help alleviate the cosmic coincidence problem. However, the standard $\Lambda$CDM model, corresponding to the absence of interaction, remains fully consistent with the observational data, as the no-interaction case lies within the $1\sigma$ confidence interval of the inferred interaction parameter for all three IDE models. Model comparison, using Akaike Information Criterion (AIC) and the Bayesian Information Criterion (BIC), further indicates that the current data do not provide statistically significant evidence favouring any IDE model over the standard $\Lambda$CDM scenario. These results suggest that, while a weak dark-sector interaction is permitted by the data, present observations do not provide compelling evidence for departures from the standard $\Lambda$CDM model.

items.title: Re-evaluating the sidereal zodiac zeropoint: A critique of Spica and Zeta Piscium, horizon-based astral reference plane, Shaula as a practical naked-eye reference, and the 232 CE Kali
items.abstract: Background: Traditional sidereal zodiac frameworks rely heavily on the fixed stellar anchors Spica (Chitra) and ζ Piscium (Revati), under the historical assumption that they represent diametrically opposite coordinate markers (180° and 360°/0°, respectively). High-precision modern astrometry breaks down this paradigm, revealing a 3° 57' 51'' longitudinal error away from true axial symmetry at epoch J2000.0. This spatial discrepancy forces an irreconcilable mathematical paradox where anchoring one star inherently distorts the position of the other, introducing systematic error into modern sidereal calculations. Methodology: This study executes a rigorous astronomical, historical, and statistical metaanalysis across 20 classical Indian texts, incorporating modern Western astrometry, Sæmundsson’s atmospheric refraction formula, and Aryabhatiya mathematical frameworks to resolve these structural inconsistencies. Results : Horizon-based analysis demonstrates that ancient coordinate models were driven by a local horizontal plane where ζ Piscium rose in the east simultaneously as Spica set in the west. Correcting for systemic naked-eye atmospheric refraction (29.0' at the horizon) reveals the true geometric separation between the stars and refines Spica's actual historic longitude to 179° 19'. Applying the Aryabhatiya's macro-epoch parameters invalidates the traditional 3102 BCE Kali Yuga date due to a structural weekday contradiction (Friday vs. the textually mandated Wednesday sunrise). Instead, astronomical back-calculations and Swiss Ephemeris data pinpoint a rare planetary conjunction within 17° of Aries Zero on Wednesday, March 21, 232 CE, identifying this zero-precession juncture as the true historical anchor point for the zero-ayanamsha epoch. Conclusion: While Shaula (λ Scorpii) aligns closely with the 240° marker and exhibits minimal proper motion displacement—making it an exceptionally practical empirical marker for naked-eye observers—absolute mathematical anchorage for precise modern calculations must be exclusively anchored to the vernal equinox point of 232 CE. Shifting the Kali epoch to 232 CE and reinterpreting the Aryabhatiya's timeline consequently places Aryabhata’s redefined birth year at 569 CE.

items.title: Genetic Structure, Cytonuclear Discordance and Cryptic Biodiversity in the Rare Hawaiian Plants Schiedea stellarioides and Schiedea spergulina.
items.abstract: The endemic Hawaiian plant genus Schiedea (Caryophyllaceae) represents an adaptive radiation of 36 species. Schiedea species exhibit a wide range of morphologies, breeding systems, and habitats, making it an excellent model group for understanding insular evolution, including evolution of breeding systems in plants. Previous cytonuclear discordance in genealogies inferred for Schiedea species suggests multiple instances of past introgression. For example, two rare para- or sympatric species ( S. spergulina and S. stellarioides ) endemic to Kauai, which are placed in separate clades based on nuclear genealogies, were resolved as sister to each other in the reconstruction of chloroplast histories, suggesting chloroplast introgression. We examined the population structure of both species using nuclear and chloroplast microsatellites for three extant populations of S. spergulina and two extant populations of S. stellarioides , representing the remaining populations known of these species. Genetic variation in both species was low, and inbreeding coefficients are consistent with past population bottlenecks in both species. The nuclear microsatellite dataset indicated strong interspecific structuring ( F ST = 0.57) that is consistent with their divergence in previous nuclear phylogenies, with S. spergulina exhibiting significant population divergence ( F ST = 0.21), primarily due to isolation by distance. In contrast, the chloroplast microsatellite dataset indicated that the S. spergulina Waimea Canyon populations appear more similar to populations of S. stellarioides than to the conspecific Lawai Valley population. Approximate Bayesian Computation with Random Trees strongly supports a model of introgression from S. stellarioides into S. spergulina over incomplete lineage sorting for this pattern. These results indicate that the Lawai Valley population of S. spergulina is likely on a distinct evolutionary track relative to conspecific populations and may represent an ancestral lineage for this species. Given the divergence found in this study, continued protection of all populations for both species is important to preserve their genetic ancestry.

items.title: High-Resolution Insights Into Genetic Diversity and Population Structure of Raja clavata Across the Northeast Atlantic and Mediterranean Sea.
items.abstract: Understanding genetic population structures is crucial for stock assessment, fisheries management and the effective conservation of marine species. This is of particular relevance for elasmobranchs that are vulnerable to fishing pressure due to late maturation and low fecundity characteristics. Raja clavata , a commercially exploited skate species is one such elasmobranch. This study investigated the genetic diversity and population structure of R. clavata across the Northeast Atlantic and the Mediterranean Sea, on large (between ecoregions) and small (within ecoregions) geographic scales. Ecoregions covered are the Aegean-Levantine Sea, Azores, Bay of Biscay and the Iberian Coast, Celtic Seas and Greater North Sea. A panel of 4793 single-nucleotide polymorphisms was used across 6902 individuals, collected between 2001 and 2023, to assess genetic diversity and population structures of R. clavata in the Northeast Atlantic and the Mediterranean Sea. The analyses include principal component analyses, discriminant analysis of principal components, admixture, isolation by distance and genetic diversity indices. Evidence for at least five subpopulations is presented. Population differentiation is demonstrated between and within ecoregions, with clear genetic differentiation of a coastal subpopulation in the Bay of Biscay, revealing genetic structure on a relatively small geographic scale for elasmobranchs. Significant isolation by distance patterns were observed in the Greater North Sea and the Bay of Biscay and Iberian Coast ecoregions, while genetic diversity estimates differed substantially between ecoregions, with lower levels observed around the Azores, suggesting potential past genetic bottlenecks. This study highlights the importance of utilising updated genetic approaches to inform conservation and fisheries management strategies. Its sampling effort places it among the largest of its kind for an elasmobranch species and provides unprecedented high resolution genetic insights into the population structure of R. clavata .

items.title: The 'Sandalwood Leopard': A Rare Colour Morph of the Indian Leopard (Panthera pardus fusca) From Southern India.
items.abstract: We report a female Indian leopard ( Panthera pardus fusca ) exhibiting a rare 'Sandalwood' colour morph from a camera-trap survey conducted in southern India between December 2025 and January 2026. The study area comprised dry deciduous and scrub habitats. Among five individuals identified in the study area, this individual was recorded on nine occasions across six camera-trap locations. Across a long-term dataset comprising 926 individually identified leopards from 148,853 camera-trap days collected over 14 years of surveys across Karnataka, this represents the only scientific record of this phenotype. The individual displayed a distinctive combination of traits, including lighter pelage, pale brown rosettes, and reduced pigmentation in exposed skin. Although these features are clearly distinguishable from the typical phenotype, the underlying genetic basis remains unknown and would require molecular analysis from non-invasive samples. In the absence of such evidence, we conservatively classify this individual as a rare colour morph. As the first scientifically documented record of this phenotype from Karnataka, we propose the term 'Sandalwood leopard' as a regionally contextualised descriptor reflecting the state's natural and cultural heritage.

items.title: An Unusual Canopy Ascent by a Grass Snake (Natrix natrix) to a Crow Nest.
items.abstract: Grass snakes ( Natrix natrix ) are a semi-aquatic colubrid species that are seldom observed beyond ground level. While previous notes have reported the species occasionally climbing shrubs and small trees to either bask or prey on arboreal species, we present evidence of a live individual that was identified at a height of 16.7 m in an empty crow nest in an oak tree during a drone survey. This presents a substantial increase on the previous record for the species of 6 m and we discuss potential sensory, morphological, and behavioral explanations for why the snake was so high in the tree. Our observation highlights the individual flexibility that may be overlooked by standard surveys, guiding future behavioral and ecological studies.

items.title: Extrafloral Nectaries of Passiflora Species: Nectar Composition and Secretion, Visitors and Interactions With Herbivores.
items.abstract: The extrafloral nectaries of Passiflora have different location and morphology; though widespread in this genus, little is known about their functioning and interaction with visitors and, thereafter, with herbivores. The ecology of the extrafloral nectaries of three Passiflora species from Argentina was studied with respect to nectary types, nectar chemistry and secretion, as well as occurrence and behavior of nectarivores, folivores, florivores and frugivores in different sites. Sucrose, glucose, fructose and 15 proteinogenic amino acids occurred in all three species. The total sugar amount did not differ between species. The sucrose/hexose proportion was high in all species. The amino acid quantity and quality of P. caerulea differed from those of P. suberosa and P . misera (which belong to a different subgenus), thus amino acid traits might contribute to taxonomic differences. Nectaries in all three species were active only in young leaves. The glands of P. suberosa (larger than the ones of the other two species) housing Acari and detritus during the post-secretory stage might function as incidental domatia. Due to their color, shape and distribution, P. caerulea and P. misera extrafloral nectaries probably mimic lepidopteran eggs. Nectar production did not vary with varying ant exclusion time in any species but P. caerulea secreted again and faster after experimental removal. The assembly of nectar feeders differed between species; co-occurring specimens of different plant species shared only some consumers, and not all insect taxa were associated with each plant species in every locality. Ants (the most frequent visitors) and wasps seemed to protect Passiflora spp. from Heliconiinae caterpillars and Coreids; other hemipterans and flies were nectar thieves.

items.title: The Use of Palaeoecology in UK Peatland Restoration: Perspectives From Practice.
items.abstract: Extensive degradation has necessitated high-priority restoration of UK peatland ecosystems. Palaeoecology has great potential to support peatland restoration, offering a long-term perspective of environmental change that can help determine baseline conditions, restoration targets, and intervention success. However, it is suggested by palaeoenvironmental researchers that palaeoecology is underutilised in practical settings, with few examples of applied palaeoecological studies within academic literature. This study uses a practice perspective to evaluate the extent to which palaeoecology is incorporated into UK peatland restoration and identifies barriers and opportunities for integrating long-term ecological research into restoration practice. A desk-based study of 68 UK peatland restoration projects and survey of 32 peatland practitioners were used to explore the use of palaeoecological research as part of UK peatland restoration projects. A total of 10 instances of applied palaeoecology in UK peatland restoration were found between the desk-based study and practitioner survey. The findings indicate that palaeoecology is rarely utilised in UK peatland restoration practice, with limitations in funding, time, and academic input identified as key barriers. Cases where palaeoecology has been considered primarily utilised pollen analysis and radiocarbon dating, with practitioners largely involved in fieldwork and research design. This study makes two recommendations to facilitate the incorporation of palaeoecological research into UK peatland restoration practice: (i) better dissemination and documentation of case studies to provide greater evidence of how palaeoecology may be used to support UK peatland restoration and clearer insight into the use of palaeoecology in practice; (ii) better two-way knowledge transfer between palaeoecologists and practitioners to identify restoration challenges and knowledge gaps where palaeoecology could contribute.

items.title: Ungulate Loss and Rewilding Drive Rapid Changes Across Multiple Trophic Levels in an African Savanna.
items.abstract: Although the ecological roles of large herbivores in savannas are well studied, the indirect impacts that cascade through community processes remain underexplored, especially during the early stages of reintroducing large herbivores to restore ecological processes or rewilding. In a Kenyan savanna, we used an eight-year ungulate exclusion experiment with a recent rewilding treatment to test how loss and restoration of ungulate assemblages alter vegetation structure, plant communities, litter, soil conditions, and arthropod communities. Complementing these broader impacts, we used a focal grass species to examine shifts in herbivores and pathogens associated with buffelgrass ( Cenchrus ciliaris ), a common palatable C4 perennial bunchgrass used by a wide range of herbivores. Three key patterns emerged from ungulate exclusion and rewilding. First, ungulate exclusion increased buffelgrass volume by 200% (from 2.4 L to 7.5 L m -2 ), but rewilding reversed this effect within 9 months. Second, ungulate exclusion tripled total and pathogen-associated leaf damage on buffelgrass and increased the number of damage types. Third, ungulate exclusion increased litter and simplified litter arthropod communities, while rewilding increased litter arthropod abundance by 2.4-fold alongside a partial recovery in litter depth, indicating a rapid detritivore response to rewilding. Additional analyses show treatment-specific shifts in herbaceous and woody plant communities across precipitation regimes and increased soil compaction with ungulate access. Together, these results show that ungulate exclusion restructures plant communities, increases litter with downstream changes in arthropod communities, and elevates natural enemy pressure on an important native bunchgrass. Meanwhile, rewilding can rapidly reverse many of these biotic effects, even after 8 years of exclusion, though some abiotic legacies persist.

items.title: Long-Term Stability of Aboveground Biomass and Productivity Without Anthropogenic Management in Subtropical Coniferous Forests: Insights From the Ecosystem Demography Model.
items.abstract: Understanding the long-term stability of forest ecosystems is essential for predicting the sustainability of forest carbon sequestration under climate change. However, the temporal dynamics of stability in subtropical coniferous forests during natural succession remain poorly understood. Filling this knowledge gap is necessary to establish a baseline for disentangling the combined effects of anthropogenic and natural disturbances. Using the process-based Ecosystem Demography model (ED-2.2), we simulated multi-decadal dynamics of aboveground biomass (AGB), productivity, and their stability in coniferous forests of subtropical China under a scenario excluding anthropogenic management. Our results indicated that the temporal stability of simulated forest productivity was generally higher in the early development period (i.e., 1-50 simulation years, 0.647 ± 0.574) than in the late development period (i.e., 51-97 simulation years, -0.061 ± 0.168), with negative stability values reflecting periods of net AGB loss. Forest plots with lower stability of simulated productivity (-0.187 to -0.131) also exhibited reduced stability of simulated AGB (1.812-3.024) in the late period. It was likely associated with seasonal precipitation stress between summer and autumn according to model simulations and subtropical climate features. Seasonal precipitation stress may trigger a cascade of effects, ranging from reduced water availability and leaf photosynthesis to elevated tree mortality risk. These changes ultimately alter forest composition and structure, destabilizing annual productivity. Our findings highlight that precipitation played a key role in shaping the long-term stability of productivity in subtropical coniferous forests.
